column1: # HOTD2 function names — the committed source of truth for the Ghidra database.
# Addresses are virtual, lower-case hex, no 0x prefix.
# Regenerate from a live database with:   ./ghidra/run.sh export-annotations
# Replay onto a fresh import with:        ./ghidra/run.sh apply-annotations
# ApplyAnnotations only renames a symbol whose current name is still a Ghidra
# default (FUN_/SUB_/LAB_/DAT_/UNK_), so re-applying is idempotent and never
# clobbers a name a human chose in the GUI.
# Names recovered by Ghidra's own analysers (CRT, D3DX, Catch@/Unwind@) are
# deliberately NOT listed: auto-analysis recreates them on import.#
# **Rows are sorted by address, and every writer must keep them that way.**
# tools/annotate.py inserts in order; ExportAnnotations.java re-sorts on write.
# The file used to be append-only and grouped into topical sections, and both
# workstreams appending at the tail is where every TSV merge conflict came
# from -- two branches adding unrelated rows to the same last line. Sorted
# insertion puts them in different parts of the file instead. The sections
# went with it: each one spanned nearly the whole segment, so address order
# broke the twelve of them into 149 fragments.

column3: SoundStopGroup(group) -- 0: SoundChannelStopAndRewind(0xF) + SoundChannelsRelease(0xF,0xF,0), the BGM stream; 1: the same on channel 0x10, the voice; any other: stop and rewind every channel 0..0x14 that is playing. Reached through SoundStopGroupThunk with g_bgm_stop_group (0) / g_voice_stop_group (1). [proved]

walks the region tables; the engine's only table-driven draw path. Only the CURRENT region's list: 0x0059C980 + region*0x18 is a -1-terminated s16 list of indices into 0x0059C984's {s16 slot, s16 draw_mode}. Ghidra's body stops at 0x0040143E; the loop tail 0x00401443..0x0040145F (next index, JNZ 0x0040129B) sits outside it, which is why the decompile shows one entry. A slot opcode 0x50 loads is not drawn here -- something else must AssetDrawSlot it, as WaterSurfaceUpdate does the canal. [proved]
writes BAMS pitch/yaw; yaw = atan2(dx, dz)

A direction to the BAMS pair that carries +X onto it as MatrixRotateY(ry) then MatrixRotateZ(rz): ry = (s16)trunc(atan2(-dz, dx) * 65536/2pi) into the 4th argument, rz = (s16)trunc(atan2(dy, dx/cos(ry) or -dz/sin(ry)) * 65536/2pi) into the 5th, the divisor picked by (ry + 0x2000) & 0x4000. FLD [ESP+0x10]; FCHS; FLD [ESP+8]; FPATAN at 0x00401721. [proved]

The same question for the other order: rz = atan2(y, x) into the 5th argument and ry = -atan2(z, x/cos(rz) or y/sin(rz)) into the 4th, which is what MatrixRotateZ(rz); MatrixRotateY(ry) carries +X onto. MatrixToEulerZYX's first half. [proved]
The BAMS pair that carries +Y onto (x,y,z) for MatrixToEulerBams: rx = s16(atan2(z, y)); h = y/cos(rx) or z/sin(rx) by which is larger; rz = -s16(atan2(x, h)).

A direction to the BAMS pair that carries +Y onto it as MatrixRotateZ(rz) then MatrixRotateX(rx) -- VecAimXAxisYThenZ's counterpart for the up axis: rz = (s16)trunc(atan2(-x, y) * 65536/2pi) into the 5th argument, rx = (s16)trunc(atan2(z, y/cos(rz) or -x/sin(rz)) * 65536/2pi) into the 4th, the divisor picked by (rz + 0x2000) & 0x4000. FLD [ESP+8]; FCHS; FLD [ESP+0xC]; FPATAN at 0x00401871. [proved] from the listing; the order is checked numerically against the port's MatrixRotateZ/MatrixRotateX. One caller, ThrowerEmitGroundDust's 0x46 arm, which hands it g_coli_hit_normal.

Decompose the matrix stack's top rotation into a BAMS {pitch, yaw, roll} triple. Transforms (0,0,1) and hands it to VecToAngles for pitch and yaw; then transforms (1,0,0), cancels Rx(-pitch).Ry(-yaw) off it and takes fpatan of the result for roll. Read by RescueTargetHeldState (on the rescue) and by the stage-2 car rig FUN_00452320, whose wheels hang off a roll-limited copy of the body frame built from this triple.

Reads the top of the matrix stack back as three BAMS angles for MatrixRotateZ(rz); MatrixRotateY(ry); MatrixRotateX(rx): VecAimXAxisZThenY on the image of +X gives ry (param_2) and rz (param_3), then the image of +Y is taken back through MatrixRotateY(-ry); MatrixRotateZ(-rz) and rx (param_1) = atan2(z, y) of it. Push/pop balanced, so the stack is untouched. [proved]
matrix -> (rx, ry, rz) BAMS decomposition
atan2(|a x b|, a.b) for two vec3s, returned in BAMS. ComputeLookAtAngleError uses it to index the camera turn-rate curve, and TurnLookAtToward to size its slerp step.

dot(a,b)^2 / (|a|^2 * |b|^2), negated when the dot is negative -- the square of the cosine, never rooted. The camera hooks' `> 0.99999` convergence tests are against this value, so the threshold is about 0.18 degrees, not 0.26.
(num * b + den * a) / (num + den). CameraEaseBlockEyeToPathPose and CameraEaseEyeToPath call it with (1, 15) -- one sixteenth of the way from a to b per frame.

LerpWeighted for a BAMS angle, the short way round, all integer: u = (b - a) & 0xFFFF; u < 0x8000 ? a + (u*num)/(den+num) : a - ((0x10000-u)*num)/(den+num), IDIV truncating, result not masked. Callers: CameraFollowPlayerMidpoint (three) and RescueTargetFreedDrift (one). [proved]
Returns the largest of its three float arguments. RingEffectSpread and RingEffectFadeOut hand the result straight to NoOpStub, the same dead pattern as MaxOfThreeToNoOpStub. [proved]

UpdateSceneViewAndLight() -- the per-frame scene update, run before anything draws. Three jobs.  1. For each of the two player camera blocks (base 0x009A6000, stride 0x69 dwords): build the view matrix from the block's position and its Y-then-X rotation, hand it to FUN_004A9BD0/FUN_004A8CA0, write the settled position back, then build the INVERSE (negated roll, X, Y, translation) into the block's second matrix slot. For the active player (g_current_player_view, DAT_009C6F00) it also transforms (0, DAT_009CA0E4, -1000) by that matrix and passes it to FUN_00403AC0.  2. MatrixStackSetTopFromArray(active view), then BuildSceneLightDirection(g_scene_light_pitch_bams, g_scene_light_yaw_bams, &g_scene_light_block0, &g_scene_light_dir_view) and SetRenderLightDirection(&g_scene_light_dir_view) -- note the VIEW-space vector is what reaches the device. FUN_0040E160 then rebuilds it again for the shadow/projection copy at 0x009A21E0.  3. **Latches the scene state**: g_scene_state_major_entered = g_scene_state_major and the same for minor. That is the pair IsPlayerAttackable reads, so 'entered' means 'as of the start of this frame's update', one frame behind a state change made during the frame. Finally bit 0 of DAT_009A5900 is set unless (major == 1 && DAT_009C8E98 != 5 && !(DAT_009A5900 & 0x30)).  The colour and ambient are NOT pushed here -- FUN_0040AD90 does that, with SetRenderLightColour/SetRenderAmbient, and SetLightingDefaultSingle turns them into the D3DLIGHT7.

Resets the four camera blocks' eye/target to the default at 0x0059C990, g_camera_index = 0, EvtEnterSceneState(0, 0), clears g_camera_free and the hand-back and override latches, and re-inits both light blocks. [proved]

The camera actor's scene init, called by CameraActorCreate on the task it just allocated: CameraBlocksReset, a full EvtEnterSceneState(1, 1), the action ring's two cursors (0x009CA108, 0x009A34D0) and g_queued_events_pending to 0, g_evt_action_advance = 2, and the four evt-action handler slots (g_evt_action_handler, stride 0x1A4) from the table at 0x00576CA4. [proved]

The camera actor's task (CameraActorCreate allocates it third in every scene's list). Clears g_camera_settled and seeds g_camera_is_tracking to 1, dispatches g_camera_actor_major_hooks[g_scene_state_major_entered] -- rows 1 and 2 both reach EvtRunQueuedActions, which calls the slot-0 action handler (CamAdvancePathFrame, a starter, CameraDriverSelectMode, CameraDriverFromDeferredPose...) -- then calls the handlers of evt-action blocks 1..3 (0x009A62B0, stride 0x1A4) with their index, then UpdateSceneViewAndLight, which builds this frame's view from the block. So every camera driver, and the view that is drawn, runs before CameraUpdateTick's hook and before any player or actor. [proved]

ActorAlloc(CameraActorTick, 0x34) then CameraActorInit on it. The third call of the scene's task-list builder at 0x00460710, after EvtLoadBlockProgram (the interpreter task) and the light push, so the camera actor -- and EvtRunQueuedActions inside it -- runs before the camera update hook, the players, UpdateCameraEnemySlots and every actor. [proved]

EvtRunQueuedActions()  Drains the 16-slot ring of actions pushed by evt opcode 0x30 (queue_event). Each queued record is {?, selector, operand[...]}; the operands are copied to the scratch block at DAT_009A6184 (8 dwords) and the handler is fetched from a TWO-LEVEL table:      handler = table[selector >> 4][selector & 0xF]      /* table = 0x005776EC */  The high nibble is BOTH the group index and the operand count -- the instruction is `2 + (selector >> 4)` dwords -- so the groups are organised by arity. The index table has 7 slots, four of them null; the sub-tables are laid out immediately BEFORE it:      group 1 @ 0x005776C4  6 handlers  selectors 0x10 .. 0x15     group 2 @ 0x005776DC  2 handlers  selectors 0x20 .. 0x21     group 4 @ 0x005776E4  1 handler   selector  0x40     group 6 @ 0x005776E8  1 handler   selector  0x60  TEN handlers in total. An earlier note in the docs claimed "100+ scripted actions"; that was an overestimate and is wrong.      0x10  EvtActionSetPlayerFlag10      DAT_009A5EBC bit 0 = op0     0x11  EvtActionSceneState11         EvtEnterSceneState(cur_major, op0)     0x12  EvtActionSetUpdateRoutine12   DAT_009A5CE0 = PTR_FUN_00579E90[op0]     0x13  EvtActionSetContinuation13    per-player continuation = op0 ? .. : FUN_00420810     0x14  EvtActionSetGlobal14          DAT_009C6F00 = op0     0x15  EvtActionSetFlag15            DAT_009C6F33 = 1     0x20  EvtActionHoldCameraPreset20   op0 = frame countdown; each frame copy                                         6 dwords from 0x00576CF0 + op1*0x18                                         into the player's camera block     0x21  EvtActionFinishSequence21     EvtEnterSceneState(2, op0); DAT_009A5900 |= 1     0x40  EvtActionCamPlay40            PLAY A cam/ PATH -- see below     0x60  EvtActionStoreSixOperands60   copies 6 operands to DAT_009C6FD8..  Measured across stages 1-6: the only selectors that occur are exactly those ten (0x10 x3, 0x11 x4, 0x12 x2, 0x14 x2, 0x15 x6, 0x20 x1, 0x21 x418, 0x40 x751, 0x60 x13). 0x13 is defined but never used.  --- selector 0x40, the evt -> cam link -------------------------------------      queue_event 0x40, start_frame, end_frame, path_index, flags  EvtActionCamPlay40 -> CamStartPathPlayback -> CamAdvancePathFrame, which calls CamEvalPath7(DAT_009A2D78, (float)frame, &eye, &lookat, &roll, &_) once per frame and increments the frame counter until it passes end_frame.      start_frame == -1   resume from the current frame instead of seeking     flags & 2           defer: stash into DAT_009C70AC/B0 for a later 0x40     flags & 4           consume the stashed values instead of the operands  path_index is a GLOBAL index across every loaded cam/ file, not a per-file one. DAT_004C479C maps global index -> cam file id, and its run lengths are exactly the per-file path counts, cp_* first then op_*:      0..17 cp_demo(18)  18..28 cp_demo2(11)  29,30,31 (1 each)  32..54 cp_st1(23)     55..120 cp_st2(66) 121..162 cp_st3(42)  163..202 cp_st4(40)     203..216 cp_st5(14) 217..232 cp_st6(16) ... then the op_* files  VALIDATION: all 751 selector-0x40 instructions in stages 1-6 name a path inside their own stage's global range -- 751/751. A wrong operand order would scatter those indices across the whole 233-path space. See tools/verify_evt_cam.py.

g_camera_actor_major_hooks[1]: EvtRunQueuedActions, then while g_scene_state_minor_entered (0x009C6F10) is 3 either copies camera block 0's eye and angles (0x009A60C0, 6 dwords) and target (0x009A60D8, 6 dwords) into block 2 (0x009A6408/0x009A6420) and CamBlockSetAnglesFromLookAt(block 2, block 2's target, block 0's roll) when 0x009C6F1C is 0, or re-derives block 2's angles from its own eye/target/roll when it is 5. 0x009C6F1C is written only by CameraBlocksReset (0x0040220E) and ResetSceneOnEnter (0x0045EE2F), both an EBX they zeroed, so the copy is what runs. Ported in web/src/game/camera/actor.ts, for the frog's read of block 2's yaw. [proved]

g_camera_action_starters[4]. When g_camera_starter_reseats is set (always, after the first checkpoint): CameraResetForPathShot; g_camera_eye = the block eye with y - 15.0 (0x004C4398), g_camera_pitch/roll_bams = 0, g_camera_yaw_bams = (block yaw - 0x8000) & 0xFFFF; and g_cam_path_target = T(block eye) Ry(block yaw) Rx(block pitch) * (0, 0, -30). Then -- the MatrixStackPop at 0x0040254F is not a return -- g_camera_starter_reseats = 1, g_evt_action_handler = CameraDriverSelectMode, and CameraDriverSelectMode(0). EvtRunQueuedActions reaches it the frame AFTER the finish_sequence, because the dequeue loop does not re-call a handler EvtActionFinishSequence21 installed. [proved]

g_camera_action_starters[6]. CameraActionStartWithEyeSnap without the g_camera_eye write: when g_camera_starter_reseats is set, CameraResetForPathShot and g_cam_path_target = T(block eye) Ry(block yaw) Rx(block pitch) * (0, 0, -30); then g_camera_starter_reseats = 1, install CameraDriverSelectMode and call it. [proved]

Minors 4 and 6's driver. busy = any of g_enemy_slots[0..3] occupied. With variant 0/1 (g_enemies_alive) or 2 (g_enemies_present): count != 0 -> mode 3, else 2 unless busy. g_camera_driver_held == 1 forces 6. Unless the mode is 2, g_camera_free and g_camera_hand_back_started are cleared. 0x009C6F30/32 force 7 -- unreachable: those two bytes are written only by the mode-7 routine FUN_00402A40 itself and zeroed by CameraResetForPathShot (byte search). Dispatches g_camera_mode_hooks[mode], THEN g_cam_path_frame = __ftol(g_rail_frame) (FLD at 0x004026F7, after the call). [proved]

g_camera_mode_hooks[2]: one jump through g_camera_hand_back_hooks[g_camera_hand_back_variant]. Variant 0 and 2 are CameraTurnOntoPathTarget (0x00402740), variant 1 is CameraHandBackToPath (0x00402860); CameraResetForPathShot only ever writes 0, so the other two are unreachable in the shipped game.

g_camera_hand_back_hooks[0]/[2]. switch ((free?2:0)|(started?1:0)): 0 sets started and falls into 1; 1 calls CameraArmStashedPath(block 0) whenever g_evt_cam_override_valid is set -- no frames-left test, unlike CameraTrackEnemiesTick -- then CameraEaseEyeToPath, StepCameraLookAtDamped, and on |VecCosSquaredSigned(lookat-eye, blockTarget-eye)| > 0.99999 clears started and raises g_camera_free and g_camera_settled; 2 and 3 (already free) CamEvalPath7(g_active_cam_path, (float)g_cam_path_frame) straight into the block's eye and target. Every arm ends CamBlockSetAnglesFromLookAt(block, 0). [proved]

Camera mode 2's sub-handler 1. NOT what the old name CameraStartTurnOntoPathTarget claimed: the bytes at 0x00402867 are C6 05 2D 6F 9C 00 01, which writes g_camera_free = 1 -- the *path* branch -- along with 0x009C6F2C = 0. It abandons the turn after one damped step and hands the camera back to the path. It is also unreachable: its only reference is entry 1 of the sub-table at 0x00576CE0, selected by byte 0x009C6F2E, whose sole writer (0x0040322D) stores 0.

The gameplay camera. Calls SelectCameraLookAtTarget, eases the block's look-at onto the result with TurnLookAtToward, and takes the turn rate from ComputeLookAtAngleError while enemies are registered or a flat constant when none are.

g_camera_action_starters[7]. When g_camera_starter_reseats is set: CameraResetForPathShot, g_camera_free = 1, g_camera_mode = 0. Then g_camera_starter_reseats = 1, g_evt_action_handler = CameraDriverFromDeferredPose, and calls it. No seat of g_cam_path_target, unlike 4 and 6. [proved]

Minor 7's driver. g_camera_free = 1, cleared if any of g_enemy_slots[0..3] is occupied; then memcpy(0x009A60C0, g_cam_path_eye, 24) -- eye and the pitch/yaw/roll words -- and memcpy(0x009A60D8, g_cam_path_target, 24) -- target and the three words after it -- and g_cam_path_frame = __ftol(g_rail_frame). No turn and no counter test. [proved]

The hand-back's eye: CamEvalPath7(g_active_cam_path, (float)g_cam_path_frame) into the scratch eye at 0x009C6F90 (target and roll into locals), then each of the block eye's three words = LerpWeighted(block, path, 1, 15) -- a sixteenth of the way a frame. [proved]

CameraTrackEnemiesTick's first call after the arm. With g_camera_ease_eye set, each block eye word = LerpWeighted(block, g_cam_path_eye, 1, 15), a sixteenth a frame; clear -- the reset value, and what goto_scene_state writes -- the block eye is simply assigned g_cam_path_eye. [proved]

CamEvalPath7(g_active_cam_path, (float)g_cam_path_frame) with the target going into g_camera_lookat_target, then TurnLookAtToward(block eye, lookat, block target, out, 1, (s8)*[0x00576C0C] = 12) and block target = out. [proved]

Picks what the camera looks at. Walks g_enemy_slots; an enemy holding an attack permit (obj+0x121 != -1) is focused ALONE, otherwise the midpoint of two registered enemies is used, and with no enemies registered it falls back to the cam/ path's own target channel. This is the gameplay tracking camera.

Clears the camera's hand-back state at the first tick of a camera action. Zeroes g_camera_free (0x009C6F2D), g_camera_hand_back_started (0x009C6F2C), the two mode-7 request bytes 0x009C6F30/0x009C6F32 and 0x009C6F31, and g_camera_hand_back_variant (0x009C6F2E); sets g_camera_index = 0, g_cam_path_frames_left = 0x7FFFFFFF and g_camera_turn_rate = 0x200; clears bit 0 of 0x009A5EBC and 0x009A5D8C and copies g_cam_path_frame into the float at 0x009C70BC. Called from all three camera-action starters -- 0x00402475, 0x00402595, 0x00402DBE -- and nowhere else. **It is the only writer of g_camera_hand_back_variant and it writes 0**, so every shot in the shipped game takes variant 0: CameraDriverSelectMode therefore tests g_enemies_alive rather than g_enemies_present, and CameraDispatchHandBack runs CameraTurnOntoPathTarget.

queue_event selector 0x20, a persistent handler: every frame g_camera_free = 1 and the camera block's eye and pitch/yaw/roll (6 dwords) = g_camera_preset_table[operand 1]; operand 0, when non-zero, counts down and retires the action at zero. Writes the angles and not the target. [proved]

EvtActionCamPlay40's flags & 2 branch: stash rather than play. g_active_cam_path from the action's path; g_stashed_path_frame = operand 0, or g_cam_path_frame + 1 when it is -1; g_stashed_path_end_frame = operand 1; DAT_009C70B8 from the action block; then retires the action (queue 0) or parks its handler on NoOpStub. Scene state (2,6)/(2,7)'s hooks play the range later. [proved]

One frame of a non-deferred cam_play, and the action handler EvtRunQueuedActions calls once per frame while the play is queued. Read from the instruction stream at 0x00403605..0x0040368D: cur = g_cam_path_cursor (+0x104); g_cam_path_frame (+0xD0) = cur; CamEvalPath7(g_active_cam_path, (float)cur, &g_camera_block_eye, &g_camera_block_target, &roll, &_); CamBlockSetAnglesFromLookAt(...); g_cam_path_frames_left = end - cur; if (cur >= end) { slot 0: g_queued_events_pending--, g_evt_action_advance = 1, cur++, return; else park the handler on NoOpStub } cur++.  **The publish, the curve evaluation and the block write all happen BEFORE the 'cur >= end' test that retires the action**, so the block holds the pose of the frame a shot ends on -- start..end inclusive, one frame each -- and only the frame AFTER the end is left unwritten. CameraPlayStashedPath (FUN_0040C8A0) and CameraStepRailTick (FUN_0040C790) are the deferred twins and increment first instead.

queue_event selector 0x21 (finish_sequence). Its first two stores FREE BOTH ATTACK PERMITS -- MOV [g_attack_permits], 0 at 0x00403714 and MOV [g_attack_permits+4], 0 at 0x0040371E (c705a02b9a0000000000 / c705a42b9a0000000000) -- without touching any actor, so the holders keep obj+0x121 until their next TryClaimAttackSlot voids it. Then g_camera_mode = 3, FUN_00403BB0(2, operand) (EvtEnterSceneState without the 0x009C6F08/10 stamp), g_screen_furniture_flags |= 1, g_evt_action_handler = g_camera_action_starters[g_scene_state_minor], g_evt_action_advance = 0 -- it does not retire itself; goto_scene_state does. The permit clear is what releases a ZombieStateHoldForCameraCue captor that graduated on its cue frame still owning a permit: all three held spawns in the game (stage 2 0xA030 cue 75:660, 0x51F4/0x5250 cue 66:430) have a finish_sequence queued right after their cue frame. [proved]

queue_event selector 0x15: g_camera_ease_eye = 1, then retires (slot 0: advance = 1, pending--; else the slot's handler = NoOpStub). Its whole effect is on CameraEaseBlockEyeToPathPose. 12 sites in the shipped scripts. [proved]
g_scene_state_table[0][0]: g_camera_update_hook = NoOpStub and nothing else. [proved]

g_scene_state_table[1][1]. Installs CameraFollowPlayerMidpoint as the camera update hook, and both players' camera hook (+0x7C) = PlayerHookDrawBody -- the per-player draw helper -- so under the follow camera a hit spawns no damage overlay. One of eight installers that write g_camera_update_hook. [proved]

g_scene_state_table[1][2]. g_camera_update_hook = NoOpStub, and BOTH players' camera hook (0x009A5CDC + p*0x130) = PlayerHookDrawBody and their +0x80 hook = 0x00415960. So under this state a hit spawns no damage overlay. [proved]

g_scene_state_table[1][3]. g_camera_index = 2, g_camera_update_hook = CameraFromViewAngles, both players' +0x80 hook = 0x00415970. Does NOT write the camera hook at +0x7C, so whatever the last installer put there survives. [proved]

g_scene_state_table[2][4]. g_camera_update_hook = CameraSnapToPathEye; both players' camera hook (+0x7C) = PlayerHookSpawnDamageOverlay and +0x80 = 0x00415980. All four row-2 installers write the same +0x7C hook, so under every cam/ path camera a hit shows its damage overlay. [proved]
g_scene_state_table[2][5]. g_camera_update_hook = CameraPathWithImpulseShake; camera hook (+0x7C) = PlayerHookSpawnDamageOverlay, +0x80 = 0x00415990, both players. [proved]
g_scene_state_table[2][6]. Installs CameraStepDeferredRailWithFrameExport as the camera update hook; camera hook (+0x7C) = PlayerHookSpawnDamageOverlay, +0x80 = 0x00415990, both players. [proved]
g_scene_state_table[2][7]. g_camera_update_hook = CameraPlayStashedPath; camera hook (+0x7C) = PlayerHookSpawnDamageOverlay, +0x80 = 0x00415990, both players. [proved]

CamBlockSetAnglesFromLookAt(float *block_eye, float *block_target, float roll). Turns the camera block's eye/look-at pair into the block's own orientation words: VecToAngles(eye - target, &block[+0x8C], &block[+0x90]) then block[+0x94] = roll. Note the delta is eye MINUS target. CamAdvancePathFrame calls it immediately after CamEvalPath7 and before the end-of-path test, so the frame a shot ends on gets its angles written like any other.

Angle between the camera's current look direction and the desired one, clamped to 0x1FFF (45 deg) and used to index PTR_DAT_00576C04 -- the turn-rate curve, so a bigger swing turns at a different rate.

g_camera_turn_curve = 1 and RET: MOV word ptr [0x009C6F38], 0x1 at 0x00403BA0 (66c705386f9c000100). Its one caller is CameraBlocksReset (0x00402207). With ResetSceneCombatState's MOV word ptr [0x009C6F38], SI at 0x0045EEF9 -- SI = 1 from MOV ESI, 0x1 at 0x0045EEC2 -- these are the only writes of the curve index: a byte search for 386f9c00 finds exactly these two and ComputeLookAtAngleError's read at 0x00403B73. So curve 1 is the only curve ComputeLookAtAngleError ever indexes. [proved]

EvtEnterSceneState without the _entered stamp: g_scene_state_minor/major = args, then JMP g_scene_state_table[major * 9 + minor]. Called by EvtActionFinishSequence21, ResetSceneCombatState, EvtOpGotoSceneState31 and EvtOpGotoSceneStateWhenPlayersAlive32 -- the last two stamp major_entered = 1 and minor_entered themselves. [proved]

EvtEnterSceneState(int major, int minor)  The scene state machine. Records the state and immediately runs its installer:      DAT_009C6F14 = DAT_009C6F10 = minor;     DAT_009C6F0C = DAT_009C6F08 = major;     goto g_scene_state_table[major * 9 + minor];     /* 0x00576C14 */  The *9 is confirmed from the disassembly (LEA ECX,[ECX+EAX*8]; ADD EAX,ECX), not from the decompiler. FUN_00403BB0 is the same without the DAT_009C6F08/10 backup copies.  A cell does not do work -- it INSTALLS the hooks for that phase:      _DAT_009C7080              camera update, run each frame by CameraUpdateTick     _DAT_009A5CDC/_DAT_009A5E0C   per-player update  (P1 / P2, 0x130 apart)     _DAT_009A5CE0/_DAT_009A5E10   per-player sub-routine                                (also writable from script: queue_event 0x12)  6 rows x 9 columns. Bind one loaded cam/ file's paths into the global 0..417 path-slot space.  Walks the file's offset table and the EXE slot list in lockstep, so path k of a file is global slot slot_list[k]:      slot = *psVar3++;                                   // s16[] at 0x004C470C     *(int *)(&DAT_0059C9F8 + slot * 8) = *piVar4++ + DAT_0059C9EC;     (&DAT_0059C9FC)[slot * 4] = 2;  i.e. descriptor_ptr = file_base + offset_table[k]. Count comes from the u16 table at 0x004C476C. The 0x10-byte per-file record at 0x0059D708 gets its state word (+8) set to 2; its +0 is the raw allocation and its +4 the curve base, both filled by the loader at 0x00403F75/0x00403F9E as file_base + 4 + path_count*4.  NOTE FOR THE FORMAT: this performs NO fixup, relocation or decode of the curve payload. The file arrives by a plain CreateFileA / GetFileSize / ReadFile / CloseHandle into a 32-byte-aligned buffer, and CamEvalHermiteCurve then reads those bytes as floats. So the bytes on disk are the bytes the game evaluates -- which is what establishes that the smashed 0xFF bytes in cp_st1/cp_demo/cp_title/cp_st3 are a data defect and not a misparse. See docs/re/anomalies.md.  CamEvalPath7 takes the descriptor pointer from this table but the curve base from SLOT_TO_CAM (0x004C479C) instead; the two tables agree for all 418 slots.

Evaluate one cam/ Hermite curve at time param_2.  param_1 is the curve header as a ushort*: [0] = key_count (always a power of two), [1] = search_steps (its log2). Keys follow at byte +4, 16 bytes each.  The indexing pins the layout beyond doubt. *(float *)(param_1 + i*8 + 2) is byte i*16 + 4 -- key i's first field -- and it is what the binary search compares against, so field 0 is TIME. With pfVar1 = &key[i].field0:      pfVar1[ 1]  key[i].value           -> weight  3s^2/h^2 - 2s^3/h^3     pfVar1[-3]  key[i-1].value         -> weight  2s^3/h^3 - 3s^2/h^2 + 1     pfVar1[ 3]  key[i].tangent_in      -> weight  s^3/h^2 - s^2/h     pfVar1[-2]  key[i-1].tangent_out   -> weight  s^3/h^2 - 2s^2/h + s     pfVar1[-4]  key[i-1].time  so the key is {time, value, tangent_out, tangent_in} at a 16-byte stride, and tangents are in value-per-unit-time. Textbook cubic Hermite.  There is no masking, no sentinel test and no integer path: whatever bytes are in the file are read as floats. Combined with the loader doing a plain ReadFile and CamBindPathSlots doing no payload fixup, that is what proves the smashed 0xFF bytes in cp_st1/cp_demo/cp_title/cp_st3 are evaluated by the shipped game too. See docs/re/anomalies.md.  The search cannot leave the key array, so times outside the curve extrapolate along the end segments rather than clamping.

Algorithm: ActorAlloc(LAB_00407A70, 0x68); position from params[0..2]; facing from params[3..4], recomputed toward g_camera_block_eye when params[10] != 0; kind byte params[9] stored at +0x5C; a switch on the kind fills the texture range [+0x60, +0x64] and the base scale +0x50. Kinds 1/2/3/5/6 are the collision materials (sand, metal, other, water, wood); 0x53 also seeds +0x4C from rand(); 0x5A recurses twice to spawn kinds 0x5B and 0x5C. Then a distance-based scale law (kind 'S' out to -35, everything but 'c' out to -15) and PlayImpactSoundForMaterial(kind).  Parameters: params -- 12 floats, built by the caller. Returns: nothing.  Named SpriteEffectSlotRange in ghidra/annotations until 2026-09-03, which described only the switch; docs/formats/combat.md called this address SpawnImpactSprite, which described only the material cases and collided with the wrapper's own name. It spawns, and impact is one of its kinds.
Collision material -> ricochet sound. The filenames it resolves to are what name the materials: 1 sand, 2 metal, 3 other, 5 water, 6 wood.

The per-frame body of the object SpawnSpriteEffectFromParams allocates, and the whole of what a sprite effect is. Draws AssetDrawSlot(+0x60) under translate(+0x38..+0x40) * RotY(+0x48) * RotX(+0x44) * RotZ(+0x4C) * scale(+0x50/+0x54/+0x58) in draw layer 0xE, then +0x60 += 1 and dies once it passes the last slot at +0x64 -- so the flipbook is one asset slot per frame at 60 Hz and its length is last - first + 1. Kind 'P' (0x50) draws under light colour (1.0, 0.3, 0.0) and kind 'S' (0x53) under (0.85, 0.85, 0.75) at three quarters scale until its cursor reaches 0x129.

SpawnSpriteEffectsTowardEye(pt, kind): one SpriteEffectDrawAndTick object (ActorAlloc 0x68) at pt, pitch/yaw from VecToAngles(g_camera_block_eye - pt), roll +0x4C = 0. Kind 0x5A spawns 0x5B, 0x5C, 0x5D and keeps no slots of its own; 0x5B runs slots 0xAA4..0xAB6 at scale 4.0 roll 0xC000, 0x5C 0xA87..0xAA3 at 2.0 roll 0xC000, 0x5D 0xAB7..0xAD3 at 2.0 (boss1q.bin). Scale law: view z > -30.0 -> scale = z * -0.0333333 * scale, floored at 0.25. Only callers: Class23TakeShots (0x0049161C 0x5A, 0x00491630 0x5C) and itself. [proved]

SpawnGroundRingEffect(obj). Only in g_app_state 6: ActorAlloc(RingEffectSpread, 0x13F4) at obj+0x100/+0x108 (the tracked bone's world x/z, NOT the origin) and y = (obj+0x1F8 & 4 ? QueryGroundHeightAt(x, y + 20, z) : obj+0x44) + 0.05; +0x68 = obj+0x68, +0x1330 = 0x78, +0x118 = 1.0. Nine call sites, every one a body on its way out: class 0x30's and 0x31's corpse states, OneHitTargetPlayDeathClip, FrogStateDieTumbleAndSink, RescueTargetFreedState. The task then runs RingEffectSpread (120 frames), RingEffectHold (30) and RingEffectFadeOut (39), each installing the next into obj+0x00. SpawnRingEffectAtPose (0x00408370) is the other spawner of the same task. [proved]

The ring task's first handler, shared by SpawnGroundRingEffect (0x00407DA0) and SpawnRingEffectAtPose (0x00408370): obj+0x1330 -= 1 and at zero obj[0] = RingEffectHold; then, in draw layer 0xC, T(obj+0x40/44/48) RotY(obj+0x68) and two draws: slot 0x1A38 (common.bin 371) under Scale(r, s, r) with r = cos(ftol(n * 136.5333) BAMS) * s * 4.0 and s = obj+0x118, so the ring opens from nothing to 4s over 120 frames; and four copies of the splash strip 0x15E4 + (g_blink_frame_counter + 0/8/0x18/0x10) % 30 at T(+-D, 0, +-2D) Scale(s/2) with D = 2s * sin(ftol(n * 136.5333) BAMS), converging on the centre. The tail past the first no-return MatrixStackPop is the whole second half. [proved]

The ring task's second handler: obj+0x1330 += 1 and at 30 obj[0] = RingEffectFadeOut, obj+0x1330 = 0, obj+0x1370 = 1.0 -- then draws THIS handler's frame anyway: layer 0xC, T(pos) RotY(obj+0x68), slot 0x1A38 at Scale(4s, s, 4s) and one strip 0x15E4 + g_blink_frame_counter % 30 at Scale(0.3s). [proved]

The ring task's last handler: obj+0x1320 += 1 and at 40 ActorKill without drawing; else obj+0x1370 -= 0.025 and, layer 0xC under T(pos) RotY(obj+0x68), AssetDrawSlotWithAlpha(0x1A38, alpha) at Scale(r, s, r), r = cos(ftol(m * 409.6) BAMS) * s * 4.0 -- the ring closes again as it fades -- and the strip 0x15E4 + g_blink_frame_counter % 30 at Scale(0.3s) with the same alpha. [proved]

SpawnGroundRingEffect's sibling that takes a six-word pose and a scale: in g_app_state 6 only, ActorAlloc(RingEffectSpread, 0x13F4), ActorClearGameFields, obj+0x40 = p[0], +0x44 = p[1] + 0.05, +0x48 = p[2], +0x68 = p[4] (the pose's yaw), +0x1330 = 120, +0x118 = scale. SeveredHeadUpdate passes its own yaw; the three class-0x51 callers (FishCheckShot, FishStateFlung twice) build only x, y, z on the stack and p[4] is an unwritten local. [proved]
obj+0x1390 is a PARENT ACTOR here, not a descriptor tail

Event opcodes 0x01-0x04: run the spawn only in a one-player game.    if (g_max_attackers == 1) jmp g_evt_spawn_gated_handlers[g_evt_opcode];   else                      skip the -1-terminated operand list;  g_evt_spawn_gated_handlers (0x00577650) is indexed by the *opcode*, so 0x01 -> EvtOpSpawnPlaced09, 0x02 -> EvtOpSpawnSimple0A, 0x03 -> EvtOpSpawnObj0B,    0x04 -> EvtOpSpawnObjC0C. The descriptor list is therefore identical to the ungated opcode it forwards to; only the gate is new. EvtOpSpawnIfTwoPlayers (0x00408860) is the same routine testing 2.  g_max_attackers is the count of players currently in play (raised in FUN_00414770 for a player state flagged 0x20, lowered in FUN_00414280), so "mode" here means the live player count, not a difficulty or game mode.  Only 0x03/0x04 and 0x07/0x08 are ever encoded by a shipped script.

Event opcodes 0x05-0x08: run the spawn only in a two-player game.  Identical to EvtOpSpawnIfOnePlayer (0x00408820) but testing g_max_attackers == 2. The forward table g_evt_spawn_gated_handlers repeats the same four entries at indices 5-8, so 0x05 -> EvtOpSpawnPlaced09, 0x06 -> EvtOpSpawnSimple0A, 0x07 -> EvtOpSpawnObj0B, 0x08 -> EvtOpSpawnObjC0C.  Stage 1 block 0 step 2 pairs them: 0x07 lists three class-0x30 zombies and 0x03 lists the last two of the same three, so the second player adds one zombie to the stage's opening encounter.

alloc 0x13F4; reads desc+0x24/+0x25 inline; does NOT set obj+0x1390. Copies the record's position and all three orientation dwords whole, desc+0x14/+0x18/+0x1C to obj+0x64/+0x68/+0x6C (0x00408925..0x00408934), after the byte tail -- the same three the other two allocators copy. [proved]

obj+0x34 = the spawn record's flags word | 1, and obj+0x38 = 0. Run by SpawnFromDescriptor BEFORE the class's own Init, which then ORs its bits on top. This is where the descriptor's flags become the actor's: bit 15 takes it out of the shot test and the crowd push, bit 17 skips the per-frame ground snap in ZombiePushOutOfWorldAndActors so a spawn placed on a ledge stays on it (95 spawns), bit 18 tells EnemyZombieInit not to compute the aim angles, bit 27 picks between row[2] and row[3] (155 spawns), and bit 14 freezes the pose. Bits 1 and 2 are consumed rather than kept: EnemyZombieInitByCharType (0045300B, 00453045) clears each and raises obj+0x38 bit 0x10 or 0x20 in its place, which it has to, because bits 1 and 2 of obj+0x34 are what MarkActorShot writes to name the player who fired. Bit 1 is the stationary thrower's do-not-walk-away and EXACTLY TWO shipped records set it, stage 3 block 2's two axe men (evt 0x3078 and 0x30BC, 0x20002); bit 2 is set by three stage-2 class-0x30 records. Bit 23 (0x800000) is a read-only spawn bit: NOTHING in .text writes it -- an exhaustive scan of every encoding that can set bit 23 of the dword at +0x34 finds no site -- and its five readers all ask the same question, skip the NoCameraTrack raise and the g_enemy_slots clear when this actor is the last enemy. Six shipped spawns carry it, all class 0x30 initial state 18: three in stage 1 (char type 7) and three in stage 3 (char type 11, 0x8800000). Bit 3 (0x8) is class 0x30's ride-the-carrier bit: EnemyZombieInitByCharType (0045301D) reads it and re-reads the descriptor's position and yaw as an offset on g_carrier_object, see ZombieAttachToCarrier. EXACTLY FOUR shipped records set it, all class 0x30, all st5evtbl block 2 step 2 op 38 (0x1D44, 0x1D74, 0x1DA4, 0x1DD4; init_flags 0x20008 and 0x60008). Unlike bits 1 and 2 it is NOT cleared, so it stays readable on obj+0x34.

Event opcode 0x0A, and its operands are NOT the 0x24-byte placement descriptor the other spawn opcodes use: each points at a two-word record {class, hp}. The object is allocated from g_class_handlers[class] at 0x13F4 bytes, initialised by FUN_00408970, and both obj+0x11C and obj+0x11E take the second word as a SIGNED 16-BIT store, so the shipped 0xFFFF0000 is a zero. Nothing writes a position, so this is the opcode for objects that place themselves. All four records the shipped scripts name live in comevtbl.bin -- classes 0x60 (chapter card), 0x61 (result card), 0x62 (its tally) and 0x63 (the subtitle gate) -- which is why every stage names the same four addresses 0x00977234/3C/44/4C; stage 6 adds three stage-local records. Ported: script/ops/spawn.ts places them and game/class60/, game/class61/ run the two that raise a script flag.

opcodes 0x0B/0x0D; alloc 0x13F4; obj+0x1390 = descriptor + 0x24. Also copies the u16 at descriptor+0x20 into obj+0x1316 (MOV word ptr [ESI + 0x1316], AX -- 66898616130000 at 0x00408A77), which EnemyThrowerInit and EnemyZombieInit both read as their class's second flag word. tools/hod2lib/evt.py calls that word 'unused in every shipped file'; it is not -- 23 of 51 class-0x31 and 76 of 345 class-0x30 spawn descriptors set it, including five stage-6 class-0x31 spawns that carry surface bits 0x40/0x80/0x100. The record's position and orientation go on unmodified: descriptor+0x08/+0x0C/+0x10 to obj+0x40/+0x44/+0x48 and descriptor+0x14/+0x18/+0x1C to obj+0x64/+0x68/+0x6C (0x00408A61..0x00408A70), all three angles, whole dwords, for every class. [proved] Stage 2 block 21 step 2's two class-0x31 zstin (descriptors 59548 and 59600 in st2evtbl.bin) carry (0, 0xC000, 0xC000) -- on their sides against a wall -- and are the only character placements in the six stages whose pitch or roll is not zero; the port dropped both words until the exporter emitted them as the placement's pitch and roll.

opcode 0x0C; alloc 0x1314; obj+0x130C = descriptor + 0x24. Before that: ActorClearGameFields, ActorInitFlags(desc+0x04), the position desc+0x08/+0x0C/+0x10 to obj+0x40/+0x44/+0x48 and all three orientation dwords whole, desc+0x14/+0x18/+0x1C to obj+0x64/+0x68/+0x6C (0x00408C01..0x00408C10), then desc+0x22 into obj+0x11E and obj+0x11C. No obj+0x1316 store, which SpawnFromDescriptor has. [proved] Class 0x13 is spawned here: five stage-2 static props carry a non-zero pitch (evt 48896/48952/49008/49064, komono_st1.bin[3] at block 17 step 1, and 84232, etc_1.bin[63] at 15x) and ScriptedPropUpdate13 draws it.

Allocates the UpdateCameraEnemySlots task (ActorAlloc(0x00408DD0, 0x34)), then zeroes the 14 {key, actor} candidate pairs at g_camera_candidates, g_camera_candidate_count, and the 16 {u8 occupied; void *actor} entries of g_enemy_slots. The twelfth call of the task-list builder at 0x00460710: the slot fill runs every frame, BEFORE any actor, so it consumes the candidates the actors registered on the frame before. [proved]

A task (ResetCameraEnemySlots allocates it). SortCameraCandidates, then clears all 16 g_enemy_slots, then walks the sorted candidates: one holding an attack permit (obj+0x121 != 0xFF) takes the first free of slots 0 and 1 -- or nothing, if both are taken -- and anything else goes to slot rank+2; either way obj+0x120 = the slot. Then g_camera_candidate_count = 0. So a non-permit candidate's slot is its distance rank plus two, and slots below it can be empty. [proved]
Takes the first free general slot, 2..13; slots 0 and 1 are reserved for enemies holding an attack permit. The slot index is kept in obj+0x120.

Adds an actor to the camera candidate list unless obj+0x34 bit 0x10000 is set -- which ZombieStateApproach sets while walking and clears when the actor wins an attack permit, so only committed enemies are ever tracked. Key is (int)(|actor - camera eye| * 10.0). ITS XREF LIST IS INCOMPLETE IN GHIDRA AND THE MISSING CALLER IS THE IMPORTANT ONE: get_xrefs_to 0x00408ec0 returns eleven sites and not one of them is an enemy class, which reads as proof that class 0x30 and 0x31 are never camera candidates. They are. ActorRegisterCameraPoint (FUN_00409B70) ends PUSH ESI / CALL 0x00408ec0 at 0x00409bec..0x00409c03, AFTER the JMP to MatrixStackPop that Ghidra has marked no-return -- so the function body, the decompilation and the xref all stop at the tail call, and disassemble_bytes past 0x00409bec is what finds it. EnemyZombieUpdate (FUN_004533F0) makes that call every frame with a 4.0 lift.
LSD radix sort, two 8-bit passes, over the {distance key, actor} candidate list -- nearest first.
Adds a live, not-yet-dead actor to the distance-ranked enemy list, at most 14.

ActorAlloc(RankEnemiesByDistance, 0x34), then zeroes the 14-pair registration list at 0x005A4D58 and its count at 0x005A4D50. The thirteenth call of the task-list builder at 0x00460710, directly after ResetCameraEnemySlots. [proved]

Once a frame: sorts the registration list by distance to the camera and writes **two** different ranks. Pass one: obj+0x131D gets the raw distance rank, nearest first, and obj+0x131E is set to 0xE. Then entries that are not live, or that carry obj+0x34 bit 0x20000000 -- which ZombieStateBackOff sets while it retreats -- are dropped, and pass two numbers the survivors 0, 1, 2 into obj+0x131E. So the compacted rank is the queue with the retreating actors taken out, and it is what the '< 3' cap tests, while the ring allowance tests the raw one. The list holds fourteen; a fifteenth enemy is never ranked and keeps 0xFF, which reads as -1 and passes every test.

A radix sort over the distance-rank registration list: two 8-bit passes on the u16 key at DAT_005A4D58, moving the {key, actor} pairs through the scratch at DAT_005A4E38 and back. Called by RankEnemiesByDistance and nothing else; it only orders, it does not move anyone.
14-slot table at g_hit_slots; sets obj+0x38 |= 0x40
Frees this actor's camera slot: g_enemy_slots[obj+0x120] = 0, obj+0x120 = 0xFF.

The one and only caller of ResolveHit (FUN_00409430) in the image -- one xref -- and the gate on it. ChooseHitPlayerOrder first, then for each player in g_hit_player_order whose bit is up in obj+0x34: g_hit_bone[p] = (s8)obj+0x190+p, and ResolveHit runs ONLY if obj+0x34 bit 0x100 is clear (00409336 8b4834 MOV ECX,[EAX+0x34] / 00409339 f6c501 TEST CH,0x1 / 0040933c 750e JNZ 0040934c, which lands past the CALL at 0040933f). So an actor the class has made shot-immune -- a thrower down or getting up, a zombie emerging or frozen on a cue -- takes NO damage at all: not reduced damage, and not a hit resolved and then discarded. The shot still marks the actor and still gets feedback, which is where ThrowerShotFeedback's forced g_hit_result = 5 comes from. It then clears bit 3 of the bone record's +0x280 and both the per-player bit and obj+0x34 bit 3.

Picks which players' marks a shot handler resolves this frame, and in what order: g_hit_player_order[0] = [1] = -1; then g_active_player 0 -> [0] = 0, 1 -> [0] = 1, 2 -> rand() % 2 ? {0, 1} : {1, 0}. The rand() is drawn only with both players in. DispatchHit opens with it; FrogAwardKillAndEnterDeath calls it on the kill and never reads the order. [proved]

body-part and damage tables indexed by actor type. Reads g_app_state (0x009C8E98) TWICE, and both reads are about being out of play. At 0x00409495, when g_app_state != 6 it raises obj+0x34 |= 0xE00 on the actor being hit (a1988e9c00 / 83f806 / 7409 / 8b4734 / 80cc0e / 894734) -- three bits with three readers: 0x200 makes ActorSwapDamagedPart return before it does anything (f6c502 at 0x00409916), 0x400 skips both the sever arm (f6c604 at 0x004095BD) and the torso death-wound arm (f6c404 at 0x004096C0), and 0x800 forces g_hit_result to 0 (f6c508 at 0x004096F9). At 0x00409741 the 1-in-4 head pop on the killing shot is gated on g_app_state == 6 (833d988e9c0006 / 756c), so the head only comes off in play. Neither read fires during ordinary play; both hold in the attract demo, which is g_app_state 5.
per-bone, per-difficulty addend from g_pBoneDamageByRank
decrements obj+0x11C only

writes the effect slot into record[0] -- the slot the bone DRAWS -- so a hit replaces that body part. Refuses outright when g_cur_actor's obj+0x34 bit 0x200 is set: 00409913 8b4834 MOV ECX,[EAX+0x34] / 00409916 f6c502 TEST CH,0x2 / 00409919 757f JNZ (the epilogue), which skips the swap, the obj+0x78 clear and the obj+0x1318 zone bit. Only ResolveHit's out-of-play OR of 0xE00 raises 0x200; no shipped spawn record carries it. Past the refusal: rec+0x00 = slot; slot 0 or 1 -> rec+0x78 = 0 (0x00409973) and no search; any other -> ResolveDamagedPartSphere(rec, slot, type) then ResolveDamagedPartSphere(rec, slot, type == 0xD ? 0xB : 7), both always, since the first returns 0. The zone bit is raised when effect[type][(rec+0x8C) + bone*6 + 1] -- the current step's code, read at 0x004098ED before the refusal -- is 0 or 1. Five callers, all in ResolveHit (a byte scan for CALL rel32 agrees with the xrefs); the headshot's is (rec, 0, 2) at 0x004097AA. [proved]

ResolveDamagedPartSphere(rec, slot, type): walks g_character_part_tables[type] from row g_character_bone_counts[type]-1 while row.slot != -1, and on the first row whose slot equals rec+0x00 -- the slot the caller has just written; the pushed slot is never read -- copies row.radius to rec+0x78 UNSCALED (MOV EDX,[ECX+0x10]; MOV [ESI+0x78],EDX at 0x004099DB) and the centre to rec+0x7C..+0x84, and stops. A search that finds nothing writes nothing. Returns 0 on every path (XOR EAX,EAX at 0x004099D7 and 0x004099F7), so ActorSwapDamagedPart's TEST EAX,EAX at 0x00409943 never skips its second call: every swap to a slot above 1 searches the actor's own type and then type 7 (0xB for type 0xD), and a row in the second overwrites the first -- the shipped rows both find agree (verify_combat check 17). Three callers, all in ActorSwapDamagedPart. [proved]
Search g_character_skeletons[char_type] for the node whose bone index (+0x14) is the argument. Starts at the root's children, so the root itself is never returned.
Recursive half of FindSkeletonNodeForBone. Node layout: +0x14 u16 bone, +0x16 u16 child count, +0x18 child pointers.

Run when a bone reaches its sever step (effect-table next == 1, or a torso hit that kills). Calls RemoveBoneSubtree on every CHILD of that bone -- the bone itself keeps the stump model ActorSwapDamagedPart just gave it, and everything below it disappears.

Sets the destroyed-zone bit in obj+0x1318, zeroes the bone's draw slot (rec+0x00) and rec+0x78, then recurses into its children. A zero draw slot is both invisible and unshootable: ShotTestBoneTree tests `if (rec[0] != 0)`.

Transforms obj+0x100 into view space for the shot test, runs RegisterForShotTest, then **raises obj+0x104 by its float argument** -- 4.0 for a class-0x30 zombie, 0 for a class-0x31 thrower -- and registers the actor for camera tracking. So the point the camera follows is the tracked bone lifted by four. The RegisterForShotTest call is at 0x00409BED, past the MatrixStackPop Ghidra marks no-return, so it is in no xref list (L35) and none of the callers' updates appears among RegisterForShotTest's callers. obj is g_cur_actor (0x009A26A0), not an argument. [proved]

Projects the actor's tracked view-space point at obj+0x70/74/78 by g_projection_distance_px and asks whether it lands inside the frame -- half-width g_projection_distance_px * 0.5, half-height a literal 240; no sign test on z. Both claim routines call it only AFTER a pick has survived, and not to refuse: an off-screen grant also raises the claimant's latch bit and g_attack_committed, which the next claim anywhere reads first. ZombieStateHoldAtRange calls it to drop that latch again (0x00455750). Ported in game/combat/permits.ts.

Which half of the screen the actor's tracked view-space point projects to: FLD g_projection_distance_px; FMUL [obj+0x70]; FDIV [obj+0x78]; FCOMP [0x004C436C] (0.0); TEST AH, 1 -- returns 1 when P*x/z < 0 (or unordered) and -1 otherwise (0x00409C90..0x00409CB6) [proved]. ActorScreenX (0x0043EF30) is the same product, truncated to an int. No sign test on z, like ActorIsOnScreen. Three callers: TryClaimAttackSlot and ThrowerTryClaimAttackSlot, in the two-attacker arm when g_players_in_play != 1 and g_enemies_present != 1, where -1 offers player 0's permit and 1 player 1's -- so an enemy goes for the player on its own half of the screen [likely: that reading of the halves assumes the engine's -Z-in-front view convention] -- and FUN_0047FE90. Ported in game/combat/permits.ts.

Writes one byte -- 0 or 1, and nothing else is accepted -- into every vertex-blended part of a skinned-model record: model+0x3C parts, the byte at model+0x40 + i*8 - 7 for i from 1, which is +1 of record i-1, the byte SkeletonDrawWalk's part loop tests. It does not reach the skeleton's nodes, whose gate is model+0x64 bit 0, and every caller that hides an actor writes that too. Ten calls, two of them missing from Ghidra's xrefs (state 28 at 0x004586E0 has no function): ZombieStateCorpseBlink, ZombieStateEmerge, ZombieStateWaitForCameraFrame and state 28 twice each, 0x0045DBC0 and class 0x32's 0x00480810 once. [proved]

Traces a vertical segment from (x, y-1000, z) up to (x, y, z) and returns g_coli_hit_surface -- the surface-type id, 0 for a miss. The sibling of QueryGroundHeightAt, which returns the height. Callers test 0x35, 0x37, 5 and 0x5A.

May an enemy commit an attack on this player? Three clauses, in order: g_scene_state_major_entered (0x009C6F08) must be 2 -- the cam/ path camera row, so no attack lands during the follow camera or a scripted view-angle turn; then g_app_state == 5 returns TRUE unconditionally, which is the ATTRACT-MODE override (the demo has no real player, so its g_player_state is never 5 and the demo would otherwise never be attacked); otherwise g_player_state[player * 0x98] must be 5. It does NOT test g_player_invuln_frames: the 90-frame window after a hit stops the damage and nothing else, so enemies keep taking their turns through it. Called with -1 by TryClaimAttackSlot and the scripted attackers, which in the engine reads g_player_state - 0x130 bytes and relies on that not being 5.

TurnAngleToward(cur, want, rate): step an angle toward another by at most rate BAMS and return it. Both angles are masked to 16 bits; three distances are formed -- direct |a-b|, up through the seam b-a+0x10000, down through it a-b+0x10000 -- and if the rate is >= any of them the result is want & 0xFFFF. Otherwise a + rate or a - rate, the short way (ties at 0x8000: up when a < b, down when a > b). All comparisons signed, and the result is NOT wrapped: callers store a + rate past 0xFFFF or a - rate below 0 as it is and the next call masks it. A NEGATIVE rate never lands (no distance is <= it) and steps the long way, so the angle runs to the opposite heading at |rate| a frame and then dithers +-|rate| about it -- ZombieStateBackOff (-0x40, +0x40 when obj+0x136C bit 0x400000 is up), ThrowerStateLeapAside and ThrowerStateWithdraw (-0x100) use that. Callers: TurnActorTowardCameraEye, TurnActorTowardCamera, TurnActorAwayFromPoint, TurnActorAwayFromPointTestArrival, ZombieStateDragTarget (obj+0x68 to 0x2000 at 0x1A0), ThrowerStateDelayedPounce (obj+0x6C to 0 at 0xCCC), and eight calls Ghidra has no xref for, from the undefined bone-2 aim routines at 0x00453BE0 and 0x00485BA0 (rate 0xC0) that ZombieDrawBonePart, ThrowerDrawBonePart and ScriptedHumanoidBoneDrawHook call. [proved]

(obj, rate): obj+0x68 = TurnAngleToward(obj+0x68, VecToAngles(obj+0x40 - g_camera_eye_x, 0, obj+0x48 - g_camera_eye_z).yaw, rate). A rate limit, not an ease. ZombieStateHoldAtRange and ZombieStateWaitTurn pass 0x40, ZombieStateDelayedStrikeInPlace and ZombieStateRideCarrier 0x1A0. [proved]

The flying head's per-frame routine, three sub-states at +0x194. LZSS decompressor. Returns the number of bytes written to dst.  Called by every pol/ and tex/ asset loader. On disk a compressed file is a u32 uncompressed-size header followed by the bitstream; callers read that header themselves and pass src = file + 4.  Format ------ Flag bits are read LSB-first from the same byte stream that carries the literal and match payload bytes, so a payload byte may be fetched while a flag byte is still partly consumed. A fresh flag byte is loaded only when its 8-bit budget is exhausted.    while flag bit == 1:        emit one literal byte   flag bit == 0, a match follows:       next bit == 1  -> long form           u16 w           w == 0                -> END OF STREAM           offset = (w >> 3) - 8192      (13-bit, always negative)           n      = w & 7           length = n + 2                if n != 0           length = u8 + 1               if n == 0       next bit == 0  -> short form           two bits, MSB first   -> n           offset = u8 - 256             (8-bit, always negative)           length = n + 2  Window is 8192 bytes. Matches are copied one byte at a time from dst+offset, so overlapping copies are intentional and an offset of -1 is a legal run fill.  Verified: reimplemented in tools/hod2lib/lz.py and run against all 793 compressed assets. Every one produces exactly the byte count its header declares. Spec in docs/formats/lz.md.

PushSceneLightStateToDevice() -- the object entry point FUN_0040AE60 installs with ActorAlloc(FUN_0040AD90, 0x34), so it runs once a frame. It pushes the whole scene light state to the device: the nine per-channel setters FUN_0040B0A0..FUN_0040B390 for light block 0 and again for block 1, then PushSceneFogFromLightBlock(&DAT_009A357C, &DAT_009A357A, g_scene_fog_near, g_scene_fog_far), SetRenderLightColour(g_scene_light_colour_r/g/b) and SetRenderAmbient(g_scene_light_ambient). This and SetupSceneProjection (through FUN_0040C2E0) are the only two callers of the fog push, and neither transforms the near/far -- they are eye-space depths and the view matrix that draws a triangle is what they are relative to.
evt opcode 0x20's dispatch entry: ApplyLightChannelOperand(0), i.e. the every-frame light block. Opcode 0x24 is the block-1 twin and 0x21/0x23 (and 0x25/0x27) are the rate and time tween forms.

ApplyLightChannelOperand(block) -- the body of evt opcodes 0x20/0x24 (set a light-block channel). **This switch is the authoritative channel map**, and it is dword offsets into the block, not inference from a seeding function:  case 0 -> block[0x0C] = g_scene_fog_near        (+0x30)  case 1 -> block[0x0D] = g_scene_fog_far         (+0x34)  case 2 -> block[0x09] = g_scene_fog_r           (+0x24)  case 3 -> block[0x0A] = g_scene_fog_g           (+0x28)  case 4 -> block[0x0B] = g_scene_fog_b           (+0x2C)  case 5 -> writes [9] and [10] then FALLS THROUGH into case 4, so it is the  all-three-fog-components alias  case 6 -> block[0x90] = g_scene_light_colour_r  (+0x240)  case 7 -> block[0x91] = g_scene_light_colour_g  (+0x244)  case 8 -> block[0x92] = g_scene_light_colour_b  (+0x248)  case 9 -> writes [0x90], [0x91], [0x92]: the all-three-light-colour alias  case 10 -> block[0x93] = g_scene_light_ambient  (+0x24C)  Each case also writes the parallel tween block (g_light_tween_block0/1) at indices 1,5,9,0xD,0x11,0x15,0x19,0x1D,0x21 -- stride 0x10 with the value at +4, but only NINE slots for eleven channel numbers, because the aliases 5 and 9 have none. So the tween block index is a COMPACTED index (0,1,2,3,4,6,7,8,10 -> 0..8) and coincides with the channel number only for 0..4. Reading the channel map off that array instead of off this switch gets channels 6+ wrong by one slot.  block == 0 selects g_scene_light_block0 (the one pushed every frame); 1 selects g_scene_light_block1, which nothing reads. Operands for the float channels are POINTERS resolved through FUN_0045EBB0; the fog RGB channels take their value inline.
SetSceneAmbient(f) -- writes g_scene_light_ambient (0x009A378C, light block 0 channel 10) and DAT_009C8A64, then SetRenderAmbient(f). ChapterCardInstall's sub 0 calls it with 0.7.

PushSceneFogFromLightBlock(a, b, near, far) -- SetFogRange(near, far), and nothing else. **The first two arguments are dead**: both callers pass them and this routine forwards only param_3 and param_4, so the scene fog range reaches D3DRENDERSTATE_FOGSTART/FOGEND untouched. Two callers, and that is the whole of the fog-range path in the binary: PushSceneLightStateToDevice (0x0040AD90) once a frame with g_scene_fog_near/far, and FUN_0040C2E0 from SetupSceneProjection with the scene light block's +0x30/+0x34 -- the same two words. No camera position, eye or transform appears anywhere on either path, which is what makes FOGSTART/FOGEND eye-space depths measured from whatever view matrix draws the frame.

JMP [g_camera_update_hook]. The task CameraUpdateTaskCreate allocates -- fifth in the scene's list, after the camera actor and before the player tasks -- so the scene state's hook (the rail, the held eye, the view angles) runs after this frame's driver and view and before anything that measures to g_camera_eye. [proved]

g_scene_state_table[1][3]'s hook (CameraInstallViewAngles). The gameplay eye is fifteen units below the camera in its own frame. [proved]

g_scene_state_table[2][6]'s hook, installed by CameraInstallDeferredRail. Stores g_stashed_path_frame into 0x009C709C -- a word nothing reads (no other xref, byte search) -- re-points g_camera_update_hook at CameraStepRailTick and falls into it. [proved]

Steady-state body of CameraStepDeferredRailWithFrameExport. Advances the stashed path frame, evaluates eye and target as independent channels, takes yaw from (eye - target) and forces pitch and roll to zero, and exports the frame it drew. The guard is 0040c79e CMP ECX,EAX (cur, end) / 0040c7a0 JGE 0040c889 -- it stops once cur >= end -- and like its twin it increments (0040c7cb INC dword ptr [0x9c70ac]) BEFORE it publishes (0040c7d1 FILD dword ptr [0x9c70ac]). So a stashed 351..384 publishes 352..384 here and 352..385 under CameraPlayStashedPath (FUN_0040C8A0), state (2,7), whose guard is JG. The pair differ in that one byte and in nothing else that matters to a cue. [proved] Neither writes g_cam_path_frame (0x009A6110).

The camera hook scene state (2,7) installs -- the second of the two that play a range EvtActionCamPlay40's `flags & 2` branch (FUN_00403490) stashed into g_stashed_path_frame/g_stashed_path_end_frame. It re-points g_camera_update_hook at itself, so it is both the installer and the steady body. **It increments before it evaluates**, and its guard is one byte different from the (2,6) twin's: 0040c8be CMP ECX,EAX (cur, end) / 0040c8c0 JG 0040c9a9 -- stop only once cur > end -- then 0040c8eb INC dword ptr [0x9c70ac] and 0040c8f1 FILD dword ptr [0x9c70ac], so the increment carries the last comparison ONE FRAME PAST the end. A stashed 351..384 publishes 352..385; a stashed 581..660 publishes 582..661. (This row said 582..660 until stage 2 block 9 was played, which is the (2,6) answer.) CameraStepRailTick (FUN_0040C790) is the (2,6) twin: 0040c79e CMP ECX,EAX / 0040c7a0 JGE, so it stops ON the end frame. CamAdvancePathFrame (FUN_004035E0), which drives the ordinary non-deferred play, publishes the cursor and increments after, so it holds start..end inclusive. NEITHER stashed routine writes g_cam_path_frame (0x009A6110): it keeps whatever CamAdvancePathFrame last published for the whole of a stashed play. [proved] The browser port had modelled both as CamAdvancePathFrame and so lost the last frame of every deferred shot; stage 2 block 16's captor cue (path 75 frame 660) and its civilian's killed-script cue (frame 650) are both timed to that tail. It then modelled both as the (2,6) twin, and stage 2 block 9's civilian -- class 0x10 stream 18, op 0x0D cue (66, 385) against a stashed 351..384 -- could not raise g_script_flags[3], so wait_script_flag 3 held that block for ever. g_scene_state_table[1][1]'s hook. g_camera_eye and pitch/yaw/roll from the player bodies (g_player_body +0x40..0x48, +0x64..0x6C): the LerpWeighted(1,1) midpoint of both when g_players_in_play != 1, else the active player's body. [proved]
