Per player: g_player_input_is_gun = 1 when the bound maple device's flag byte has 0x80 (a gun), else 0 with g_player_pad_kind = MapleDeviceKind; both -1 with no device. [proved]
The kind of an emulated maple device from its capability word (+4): 0xF06FE a standard controller -> 0, 0x7FF -> 1, low byte 0xFE or 0xFF -> 2, anything else -> -1. [proved]

Which of the four binding sets in g_player_input_bindings a player's device uses: -1 no device; 0 when g_player_input_is_gun is 1 (a gun: the PC mouse or light gun); else by g_player_pad_kind -- 1 a standard controller (the PC keyboard), 2 kind 1, 3 kind 2. [proved]

The per-frame transform of one effect node: MatrixTranslate from EffectFrameTranslations, then RotZ/RotY/RotX from EffectFrameRotations, indexed by the node's bone - 1. g_effect_interp_mode[effect] selects the rate: 0 is one key per frame, otherwise the animation runs at half rate and odd frames blend the two neighbouring keys (mode 2 slerping through matrices when any axis differs by more than 0x3000).

Draws an animated effect through EffectDrawTree with AssetDrawSlot. The argument is a 4-int state block {effect id, motion id, frame, prev frame} living inside the owning object -- obj+0x324 for a class-0x41 prop.

Wraps the frame counter (to 0 at g_motion_play_length[motion]-1, and to the end when it goes negative) and then walks g_effect_trees[effect id]'s children with EffectDrawNode. The descriptor IS a node: same {u32 slot; s16 bone; u16 children; u32 child[]} struct, with slot 0 and bone 0 so the root itself never draws.

One effect node: push, EffectPoseNode, AssetDrawSlot(node->slot), recurse into the children, pop. A node with bone < 1 is a pure transform and draws nothing. Slot 0x10CE gets a random 0.27-0.37 scale each frame, which is how the smoke puffs vary.
As EffectDrawUnlit but routes each part through SubmitSlotWithSceneLightArray instead of AssetDrawSlot. KindedPropUpdate picks this one for item set 4 and for scene 3.

EffectDrawUnlit with two extras, and the entry point both class 0x44 selector 0 and FUN_00474120 use. EffectDrawWithCapture(state, capture_bone, slot_override): DAT_007C1789 = capture_bone + 1, so EffectDrawNode copies the matrix of the node whose bone equals capture_bone into state+0x14 (obj+0x338); DAT_007C178C = slot_override, and a value >= 0 makes every node draw THAT slot instead of its own. EffectDrawUnlit passes 0xFF and -1 for the two, which is why it captures nothing. DAT_007C1788 = 0 either way, so the parts are unlit.

Address of one frame's translation array inside the motion buffer: g_motion_slots[motion].base + 4 + frame * align4(bones * 0x12 - 0xF), then bone * 0xC for three floats. The effect's animation is an ordinary motion; only the node tree is its own.
Address of one frame's rotation array, the same stride as EffectFrameTranslations offset past the translations; bone * 6 for three BAMS shorts in X, Y, Z order.

BuildSceneLightDirection(pitch_bams, yaw_bams, world_out, view_out)  Turns the scene light block's +0x18 / +0x1C angle pair into a direction vector, in both world and view space:      v = (0, 0, 1)     MatrixStackPush; MatrixLoadIdentity();     MatrixRotateY(yaw); MatrixRotateX(pitch);     TransformVector(v) -> world_out            ; block +0x00     MultiplyByViewMatrix(g_view[player]);     TransformVector(v) -> view_out             ; block +0x0C     MatrixStackPop  MatrixRotateY/X PRE-multiply (M <- R x M) and the vector transform is D3D's row-vector form, so pitch is applied first and yaw second. Working it through with the matrices as those rotators actually store them:      dir = ( cos(pitch) * sin(yaw), -sin(pitch), cos(pitch) * cos(yaw) )  The caller (FUN_00401F40, the per-frame scene update) passes **view_out** to SetRenderLightDirection, which negates it into g_render_light_dir_*. So the D3DLIGHT7 direction -- the direction light travels -- is -dir, and `dir` itself is the direction the light comes FROM.  Both angles are BAMS: MatrixRotateX/Y multiply by 9.58738e-05 = 2*pi/65536.  Written by evt opcodes 0x18 (set) and 0x17 (slerp over N frames).

LightBlockSetDirection(block, pitch, yaw) -- block+0x18 = pitch, block+0x1C = yaw; the angle pair BuildSceneLightDirection turns into a vector. ChapterCardInstall's sub 0 points light block 0 along camera block g_camera_index (DAT_009A60CC and g_camera_block_yaw_bams, stride 0x69 dwords).

The per-tick frame: steps g_frame_counter, g_blink_frame_counter and g_scene_tick_counter; then, when g_ini_autoreload is set, refills any player whose input mode has bit 31 and whose g_player_ammo is 0 (6, or the Original magazine), clears g_player_magazine_empty and plays 0x3E16A9 while the firing gate is open -- an inline PlayerRefillMagazine; then projection, AppStateDispatch, CommitAppState. [proved]
g_app_state_pending = -1. Drops a pending state change without committing it. Called by ResetGameOnStart's teardown path (FUN_0040A920 -> 0x0040E840).

g_app_state_pending = the argument. Does not change g_app_state; CommitAppState applies it at the end of the frame. Fourteen call sites, requesting 3, 4, 6, 7, 0x0C and 0x0F. Start-with-a-credit (FUN_00414FC0) requests 6, which is what makes 6 the in-play state.

The only writer of g_app_state, run at the end of the per-frame tick FUN_0040E730. Does nothing while g_app_state_pending is negative. Otherwise it tears the old screen down (AssetDrainAllJobs when the pending state is 0x0E, three other teardowns otherwise), sets DAT_009C71C4 = (pending == 5) -- the attract flag -- clears the per-player counters, then g_app_state = pending and g_app_state_pending = -1. The line that fixes what 6 and 7 mean: if (pending < 6 || pending > 7) g_player_state = 9 for both players, so 6 and 7 are the ONLY states that leave a live player alone.

RequestAppState(g_app_state_next_table[g_wCaptionMode][g_app_state]) -- the scripted advance out of a screen that has finished. Callers: RunAttractDemo when the demo scene runs out while g_app_state is 5, and the name-entry screen FUN_00481400 when g_GameMode is not 3.

The lightweight skeletal model a 0x504 side block carries at +0x70, used only by class 0x40's horde member (HordeMemberInit) and class 0x47's lone member (LoneHordeMemberInit47). Zeroes the clock (+0x00 frame, +0x04 play frame, +0x0C blend length, +0x0D flags), sets mode +0x20 = 3 (SubModelWalkBonesHalfRate), poses the rest frame into the per-bone records at side+0xA4 (0x70 bytes a bone) and installs SubModelDrawBoneHook at obj+0x12EC.
SubModelInit's pose: frame 0 of the clip at model+0x08, object transform T(pos) Ry Rx Rz, root translation, and SubModelStoreRestBone down the skeleton.

Per bone of SubModelPoseRestFrame: bone record +0x00 = g_submodel_bone_slots[bone + obj+0x1350*10] (the slot SubModelDrawBoneHook draws), +0x68 = 0x21, +0x04..0x0C the frame-0 rotations, +0x1C the matrix.

One bone of the half-rate walk. Blending (model+0x0D bit 1): slerp the bone's snapshot toward the clip frame by frame/blendLen. Else odd play frames average the new rotation with the previous one (half the wrapped delta). THEN, for character type 0x1D with g_app_state 6 and obj+0x34 bit 0x10000000 (the dive): bone 8's X = 0xFFFF - ftol(obj+0x1344*16384) and bone 9's X = ftol(t*20480) - ftol(t*-16384) - 0xFFFF -- the jaw opens as the dive runs (0x0040EF15..0x0040EF6D, constants 0x004E1FB0/B4/B8).

The root of SubModelPoseAndEmitBones: MotionFrameAddress(type, clip, play/2), odd play frames averaged with the next, then SubModelApplyObjectTransform. While blending, lerps the root from the snapshot at model+0x10..0x18 and slerps the root rotation.

T(obj pos) then Ry(yaw) Rx(pitch) Rz(roll) when obj+0x133C is 0 (Rz Ry Rx otherwise), MatrixScale(obj+0x134C), and when obj+0x135C is set MatrixScale(1, (61 - obj+0x1330)/61, 1) -- the horde corpse flattening. Then the clip root translation as a pose offset (model+0x20 bit 0x10 clear). Records the frame-0 root at obj+0x12F4.
The per-bone draw hook SubModelInit installs at obj+0x12EC. AssetDrawSlot(bone record +0x00), or AssetDrawSlotWithAlpha(slot, (80 - obj+0x1330)*0.0125) when obj+0x1338 is set.
MatrixStackPush; SubModelPoseAndEmitBones(model, pos, bones); MatrixStackPop. Called by HordeMemberUpdate and HordeCorpseSinkUpdate.
SubModelAdvanceClock, SubModelPoseRoot, then one of three bone walks by model+0x20 & 3: 2 FUN_0040F680, 3 SubModelWalkBonesHalfRate, else FUN_0040F710. SubModelInit sets 3 and nothing changes it.

The clock half of the draw, run once per SubModelDraw. Not blending: model+0x04 = model+0x00 % g_motion_play_length[clip]. Blending: once model+0x00 reaches the blend length (s8 +0x0C) the frame jumps to the start frame at +0x04 and the blend bit clears. model+0x00 itself is incremented by the CALLER after each draw.
Mode 3's bone walk: each bone's rotation from MotionFrameAddress(type, clip, play/2) at (bone*3+6)*2, through SubModelPoseBoneHalfRate, stored at bone record +0x1C and restored between siblings.
Cut straight to a clip: +0x08 = clip, frame and play frame 0, +0x1D = 0. No blend.

(model, clip, start, blend): snapshot every bone (SubModelSnapshotBone) and the root, then frame = 1, play = start, clip, blend length = blend + 1, flags |= 1. The horde passes start 0 and blend 4: five frames from the frozen pose to the new clip's first frame.
Per bone of SubModelBlendToMotion: copy the bone record's current rotation (+0x38..0x40) to the blend source (+0x44..0x4C).

Builds the skeletal model record embedded at obj+0x194. Writes model+0x116C (the character size, and the factor SkeletonApplyRootMotion scales its root delta by) from the CHARACTER TYPE alone -- MOVSX EAX,[ESI+0x60]; ADD EAX,-0x1e; CMP EAX,0x1a; JA to the 1.0 arm, then the index byte table at 0x00410568 selecting 0x3f19999a / 0x3f333333 / 0x3f666666. And writes model+0x64 = 3 unconditionally at 0x004104C5 -- MOV dword ptr [ESI + 0x64], 0x3, bytes c7466403000000 -- so bit 0, the skeleton's draw gate SkeletonEmitNode tests, and bit 1, the one and only gate SkeletonApplyRootMotion tests before it moves the actor, are SET on every skeletal actor in the game. [proved] model+0x3C = g_pCharacterExtraParts[type]->count and model+0x40 = ActorAllocSub(count*8), each 8-byte record's +0 set to 0 and +1 to 1: every vertex-blended part starts visible. [proved] Through SkeletonBuildAndPose it also raises obj+0x34 bit 0x80 on g_cur_actor, and every Init that calls it points g_cur_actor at itself first, so every skinned actor carries the per-bone bit unless its builder clears it: PlaceBats, SpawnBatWings, CatInit, SpawnGoldenFrog and 0x00463E50 / 0x004641F0 do, with AND 0x7F straight after. [proved]

reads the motion frame, sets the object root pose, then walks the node tree Raises obj+0x34 bit 0x80 on g_cur_actor when g_character_skeletons[model+0x60]->+0x16 (root count) is non-zero: 0x004105CC..0x004105E2, OR CL,0x80 -- the only instruction in the image that sets the per-bone shot bit ShotTestSphere forks on. [proved]

per node: writes the bone's DRAW RECORD at obj+0x20C + bone*0x90 and then Translate(bone offset); RotZ; RotY; RotX from frame+0x0C+bone*6, recursing into the children. ONCE, AT BUILD: its only caller is SkeletonBuildAndPose (0x0041079B), itself called only from ActorBuildSkinnedModel -- an earlier note here said each frame, which is wrong. rec+0x00 comes from the NODE's own slot. The record fields it writes are +0x00 the asset slot, +0x74 = 0x21, +0x78 the HIT-SPHERE RADIUS and +0x7C..+0x84 its centre, from PTR_DAT_004D032C[char_type][bone-1] with the radius scaled by obj+0x1300 -- but ONLY when that table entry's own slot equals the slot just written. Otherwise all four go to zero. The comparison is MOV EDX,[EAX-0x14]; CMP EDX,[EDI]; JNZ 0x00410876 at 0x00410830 -- the row's slot against the NODE's -- and it runs once, so it refuses the rows that name another model than the skeleton does: zsass's hands (rows 4 and 7 name the armed 0x1FA2/0x1F9E, the nodes the bare 0x1F9F/0x1F9B) and every row of a type whose table is a stub read on past its -1; tools/verify_combat.py's GATED holds the whole list against the exe. A later swap does not re-run it: a damaged part's sphere is ResolveDamagedPartSphere's, and the hands' are SpawnThrownWeapon's and ZombieThrowHandWeapon's (zero), ThrowerStateRearm's and ThrowerStateRestoreBothHands' (rows 4 and 7). This row used to say a swapped bone loses its sphere through this test, which a routine that runs once at build cannot do. [proved]

Per-frame root pose, and it emits NO MatrixTranslate of its own. Opens with SkeletonResolveTrackFrames (FUN_00410BD0); takes track 0's root translation -- the current frame's three floats from FUN_00412F50, or model+0x44..0x4C lerped towards model+0x50..0x58 by g_motion_fade_weight when model+0x37 & 0x21 is up; writes it to model+0x6C/0x70/0x74; and hands a POINTER to it to SkeletonApplyRootMotion (FUN_00410C50), which is the only consumer of it. All this routine then puts on the matrix stack is BONE 0's rotation, MatrixRotateZ(rz); MatrixRotateY(ry); MatrixRotateX(rx) from frame+0x0C/0x0E/0x10, which it also stores at g_skeleton_node_out+0x04/0x08/0x0C. The blended arm interpolates the two tracks' angles the short way round against 65536.0 (0x004E1FDC) and 32768.0 (0x004E1FE0) and converts with FUN_004ACF50. So the composed transform for a skinned actor is T(obj+0x40) R(obj+0x64..0x6C) S(model+0x116C) T(the pose translate FUN_00410C50 chose) Rz Ry Rx(bone 0), and every bone hangs off that. [proved]

The per-track pre-pass SkeletonPoseRootFrame opens with, and it touches no matrix. For each track i in 0..model+0x36 it either caches that track's frame pointer -- FUN_00412F50(char_type, model+0x20+4i, model+0x18+4i) into g_motion_frame + 4i -- or, when that track's cross-fade bits are up (model+0x37+i & 0x21), computes its fade weight into g_motion_fade_weight + 4i instead. [proved]

Takes a POINTER to the frame's root translation and is the only consumer of it, both as world movement and as the pose offset -- which is what makes the two mutually exclusive. model+0x1160..0x1168 is the BASELINE, the root translation the last delta was taken at, and four things write it: the wrap damper (when |model+0x10 - model+0x18| > g_motion_play_length[model+0x20]/4 it sets baseline = root + (root - baseline)/play_length, so the wrap frame contributes very nearly nothing), the fade reset (model+0x37 & 1 and not & 0x20 -- the state ActorSetMotionBlended leaves -- sets baseline = root outright), ActorSetMotion (seeds it from the NEW clip's frame 0), and this routine's own gated arm. So no clip change ever turns a clip's ABSOLUTE root into a step: the delta is strictly frame to frame. The gate is model+0x64 bit 1, tested at 0x00410D2F. SET: delta = root - baseline goes through MatrixTranslate(obj+0x40..0x48); RotZ/RotY/RotX(obj+0x6C/0x68/0x64); MatrixScale(model+0x116C) and the transformed point is written back to obj+0x40 and obj+0x48 -- and to obj+0x44 as well when bit 0x10 is also set (TEST at 0x00410DB0) -- then baseline = root. CLEAR: nothing moves. L37: the SET arm DOES NOT RETURN. Ghidra ends it at MatrixStackPop(1) and shows a return; the bytes at 0x00410E5F-0x00410E93 write the baseline and fall into the shared tail, which calls the pose hook at model+0x115C, copies model+0x18 to model+0x10, and pushes MatrixTranslate(obj+0x40..0x48), the actor's rotation in one of six orders chosen by model+0x68, MatrixScale(model+0x116C) and THEN the pose translate: MatrixTranslate(0, root.y, 0) with bit 1 set (TEST/JZ at 0x00411005) and MatrixTranslate(root.x, root.y, root.z) with it clear (0x00411020). So a clip's root translation either moves the OBJECT or offsets the POSE -- never both, and never neither. [proved]
draws record[bone].slot; record base obj+0x20C, stride 0x90

MatrixStackPush(0), SkeletonDrawWalk, MatrixStackPop(1) -- and then ActorDrawShadow(g_cur_actor): 004110b2 MOV EAX,[0x009a26a0] / 004110b8 CALL 0x0040a590, past the MatrixStackPop Ghidra marks no-return, which is why the decompilation (and this row, until it was disassembled) showed no shadow (L35). Note the shadow is g_cur_actor's, not the model's owner's. [proved]

The body of DrawSkinnedModelAndShadow: parks the track and bone records in g_motion_track/g_motion_bone_records, walks g_character_skeletons[type] emitting each node (whose draw SkeletonEmitNode gates on model+0x64 bit 0), then draws the vertex-blended parts and runs the actor's attachment list. The part loop is the parts' DRAW GATE: for i in 0..model+0x3C, it draws part i only when the byte at model+0x40 + i*8 + 1 is non-zero (0x00411146) -- the same byte ActorSetPartVisibility (FUN_00409D10) writes for every part at once, and the one ZombieStateAwaitCivilianOrder (FUN_0045BAD0) clears for part 0 alone to hold a captor off screen. The parts are g_pCharacterExtraParts' waist and skirt, not bones. The byte at +0 of the same record is a lazily-filled 'this part has a model' cache: zero asks BuildCharacterPart and, if that answers, latches 1. The attachment call (model+0x1174 on model+0x1170) has no gate at all. [proved]

The motion sampler's clock arm. model[2] = model[0] % (g_motion_play_length[model[8]] + 1) -- the play cursor, which WRAPS at play_length + 1 and so takes every value from 0 to the play length inclusive; model[6] = model[2] / 2 is the authored frame, and an odd cursor blends the two neighbours on tracks 1 and 2, which is the 60 Hz over 30 Hz interpolation. Sets model+0x5D when the cursor has reached the play length and model+0x5E when it has reached play_length - 1. Nothing here advances model[0]: the owning class does, and a class holds a clip on its last frame by simply not incrementing it. WHILE A CROSS-FADE IS UP (model+0x37 bit 0, raised by ActorSetMotionBlended) the cursor is NOT recomputed, so the incoming clip is held on its start frame; when model[0] - model[10] reaches model+0x30 + 1 (fade + 2) it rewrites model[0] = model[2] + 1 and drops the bit, and the clip plays on from the frame after its start. [proved]

Emits one node of the skeleton. The node's draw -- the per-class hook at model+0x1158, unless SkeletonNodeDrawSuppressed vetoes it -- runs only when the node's draw record holds a slot (MOV EAX,[ESI] / TEST / JZ at 0x004114F2) AND model+0x64 bit 0 is set (TEST byte ptr [ECX+0x64],0x1 / JZ at 0x00411505, ECX = g_skeleton_model): with either clear it skips straight to the recursion at 0x004116CC, so model+0x64 bit 0 hides every node of the skeleton while the walk goes on. The skipped block also holds the rest: when the node's bone index matches the tracked one, it records that node's **world position** into obj+0x100/104/108 -- which is what SelectCameraLookAtTarget aims the camera at, never obj+0x40. The bone is 1 for an ordinary humanoid (character types 0..0x14), 2 when obj+0x136C bit 0x10000000 is set, and 9 for body condition 5 or the g_camera_block_target case; obj+0x10C..114 gets the same point in the other space. A further -3.5 is applied to the height in the two-player attacker case. Otherwise, unless obj+0x34 has 0x8000, it writes the bone's world sphere centre. Recurses into the node's children. [proved]

One node's pose, called by SkeletonEmitNode before it stores the node's matrix at record+0x28 (record = g_skeleton_node_out + bone*0x90). MatrixTranslate(node+0x04/08/0C, the node's offset); then the node's three angles from its track (record+0x8E): unfaded and on a whole frame (model+0x37+track & 0x21 clear), the frame's s16s at g_motion_frame[track] + (bone+2)*6; fading (bit 1), or on a half frame (bit 0x20) with model+0x64 bit 8, MatrixInterpolateSwingTwist of slot A (record+0x10..0x18) towards slot B (record+0x1C..0x24) by g_motion_fade_weight[track], read back through MatrixToEulerZYX; a half frame without model+0x64 bit 8, a per-angle lerp A->B of the s16 difference. Every arm then rotates RotZ RotY RotX and STORES the three angles at record+0x04..0x0C (0x004118ED..0x00411923), so every draw overwrites the current angles a state may have written -- they survive only if a MotionLoadPoseSlot mode-0xC snapshot takes them first (FrogStateHopWithinScreenWedge, Boss4StateTurnClipThenApproach). The decompiler shows the interpolated arm returning early; the listing falls through to the store. [proved]

Start a clip at frame zero with **no cross-fade**: writes the motion id to track+0x20, zeroes the frame counter (track+0x00), the play cursor (track+0x08), track+0x10 and track+0x18, and clears the two fade bytes at +0x36/+0x37, so nothing of the outgoing clip is left to blend from. ActorSetMotionBlended (FUN_004119A0) is the fading half of the pair; this one is for the scripted cues that are meant to cut, and ZombieStateMotionCue21 is one of them. It ALSO seeds SkeletonApplyRootMotion's baseline when model+0x64 bit 1 is up -- TEST AL,2/JZ at 0x00411966, then FUN_00412F50(char_type, motion, 0) and three stores at 0x0041197B/0x00411984/0x0041198D -- so the baseline starts at the NEW clip's frame 0 and a cut can never turn that clip's absolute root into a step. [proved]

Start a motion on the track with a **cross-fade**: the fourth argument is the fade length in frames, stored at track+0x30 as length+1, alongside the start frame at +0x08 and its half at +0x18. Every class-0x30 state passes one -- 5 for ZombieStateApproach's walk and ZombieStateStrike's swing, 10 for the attack run, the hold's idle, ZombieStateBackOff's retreat, the lunge and ZombieStateWaitTurn. ActorSetMotion (FUN_00411930) is the one that does not fade, and it is used for the scripted cues that are meant to cut. It also writes track+0x37 = (track+0x37 & 0xDF) | 1 at 0x004119C5-0x004119D7, which is exactly the bit-0-set-bit-5-clear state SkeletonApplyRootMotion tests before it resets the root-motion baseline to the current root -- so a faded clip change cannot produce a step either. [proved]
Start a motion on one of the actor's two motion tracks; the track index is the last argument (0 the looping motion, 1 the one-shot the hit reaction uses).
MotionCrossFadeTo with a different flag pair (block+0x38 |= 9); used by the alternate hit reaction indexed by the last-hit zone.
Start a motion on track 1 cross-fading from what is playing. block+0x33 = fade + 1 -- ActorPlayHitReaction passes 20 when the hit severed something and 10 otherwise.

Loads one pose into one of the skinned model's three pose slots, for the root (model+0x6C current / +0x44 slot A / +0x50 slot B) and, through SkeletonWalkBoneAngles, every bone on the given track (bone record +0x7C current / +0x88 A / +0x94 B). Mode 0 = current from (motion, authored frame), 1 = slot A from it, 2 = slot B from it, 0xC = SNAPSHOT: copies the current (last drawn) pose into slot A and reads no motion data. ActorSetMotionBlended's MotionStartOnTrack calls mode 0xC then mode 2 with the new clip's start frame, which is what makes a cross-fade dissolve from a still of the outgoing pose rather than from a clip that keeps running. [proved]

One bone's half of MotionLoadPoseSlot: when the bone's track byte (record+0x8E, i.e. model+0x106 + bone*0x90) equals the track argument, writes its three s16 angles from frame+(bone*3+6)*2 into record+0x7C (mode 0), +0x88 (mode 1) or +0x94 (mode 2), or copies +0x7C into +0x88 (mode 0xC). [proved]
Recursive walk of MotionLoadPoseSlot: MotionWriteBoneAngles for this node's bone (node+0x14), then itself for every child (node+0x16 count, node+0x18 pointers). [proved]

MotionStartOnTrack's arm for a start on an odd play cursor: loads slot A from authored frame f and slot B from f+1 (MotionLoadPoseSlot modes 1 and 2), then poses the skeleton between them under a pushed matrix -- the 60 Hz-over-30 Hz interpolation, applied at the moment the clip starts. [proved] for the two loads; the two posing calls (FUN_00411F80, FUN_004120C0) are unread.

Writes a track index into the bone records of one subtree: for the node of the given bone (the character's root skeleton when 0) calls FUN_00412290 on every child and stores the track in the node's own record+0x8E. MotionWriteBoneAngles tests exactly that byte, so this is what decides which bones a track (0 the loop, 1 the hit reaction) drives. [likely] -- FUN_00412290 is unread; the +0x8E write and its reader are [proved].

Per-node veto, consulted by SkeletonEmitNode before it calls the node draw hook at obj+0x1158. Read from the disassembly rather than the decompiler's switch: for character type 0x17 it is CMP word[node+0x14],0x10 / SETGE, so every bone from 16 up is suppressed -- exactly the eight BuildCharacterPartSubparts replaces. Otherwise it suppresses BONE 9 alone, and only when the slot bone 9 is CURRENTLY DRAWING -- g_motion_bone_records[9].slot, so a swap would change the answer -- is one of ten literals: 0xE3C 0xE4D 0xEA2 0xEB6 0xEC6 0xED6 0xEF6 0xF06 0xF83 0x15B0, enumerated out of the jump table at 0x00412360 and its byte map at 0x00412368. Those ten are exactly the ten character types whose g_pCharacterExtraParts part 1 draws that same slot, 1:1 with no strays either way: 0x21 0x22 0x26 0x28 0x29 0x2A 0x2C 0x2D 0x35 0x3B. The rule is: when a part is drawn soft, do not also draw it rigid. It never ADDS a draw.

Bind the attachment list at obj+0x1170: for every id in the s16[] up to the terminating negative, look up g_actor_attachment_table[id] = {s32 bone; s32 slot}. An id BELOW 0x24 overwrites bone_records[bone].slot -- the bone draws that model instead of the one its skeleton node names, which is how a civilian gets one of the 60 interchangeable hito_kao_* faces. An id of 0x12 or above also asks the asset system to load the slot. Ids of 0x24 and above are drawn as extra models by ActorDrawAttachedParts and are not bound here. CivilianInit calls this straight after writing the list pointer from the spawn tail's +0x08.
The undo of ActorBindPartList's loads: walks the same s16[] and releases every slot whose id is 0x12 or above. It does not put the overwritten bone slots back -- the object is being torn down.

Draw the actor's attachment list: the s16[] at obj+0x1170, terminated by a negative. SkeletonDrawWalk calls this last, through the hook at obj+0x1174, so attachments are drawn after every skeleton node. Ids above 0x23 index g_actor_attachment_table; the record is {s32 bone; s32 slot} and the draw is MatrixStackSetTopFromArray(bone_records[bone].matrix at +0x28) then AssetDrawSlot(slot) -- an EXTRA model on a bone, not a replacement. In Original Mode (g_GameMode == 1) with DAT_009C88AC set, bone 2 is scaled 1.5x in X and Z and bones 5/8/12/15 by 2.0x. Ids 0x23 and below are handled by ActorBindPartList at build time instead, which overwrites the bone's own drawn slot. Every class-0x10 civilian's hair, hat, bag and shoes come through here: 52 of the 65 class-0x10 spawns in the shipped evts carry a list.

ActorDrawAttachedParts submitting through the scene light array instead of AssetDrawSlot. CivilianInit installs it at obj+0x1174 in place of the plain one when g_scene_light_array (0x009A2BB4) is non-null, and raises obj+0x38 bit 8 at the same time. Same list, same records, same 1.5x/2.0x Original Mode scales.

MatrixInterpolateSwingTwist(A, B, t): leaves A . Rot(c, trunc(a*t)) . RotY(trunc(b*t)) on the stack top, the rotation part of A turned t of the way to B. R = A^-1 . B (MatrixSetTop3x4 of A's rotation, MatrixInvert, MatrixMultiply by B's rotation); v = R.(0,1,0); a = (s16)__ftol(atan2(sqrt(vx^2+vz^2), vy) * 32768/pi) is the SWING of the Y axis, about c = (vz, 0, -vx) -- or (1,0,0) when a is exactly 0x8000; the twist is what is left, Rot(c,-a).R, and b = (s16)__ftol(atan2(-w.z, w.x) * 32768/pi) of w = twist.(1,0,0). When a is 0 the swing is skipped: MatrixStackSetTopFromArray(A) then RotY(trunc(b*t)). Translation is dropped throughout (the rows are rebuilt with a zero one). Its one caller is EffectPoseNode's interpolation-mode-2 arm, with t = 0.5, when all three key angles differ by more than 0x3000 -- effect 0x13's break reaches it.
motion job sub-step 0: builds "mot\%s", CreateFileA, allocates size+0x20
sub-step 1: one ReadFile of the whole bank -- mot/ is NOT compressed
sub-step 2: the entire parse -- one int32 offset per motion id in the bank
asset job kind 8; dispatches the sub-step at job+0x0C
asset job kind 9
asset job kind 10
((bones*6+15)&~3)*frame + 4 + slot.base; bones from the CHARACTER type

Walks a -1-terminated s16 list of asset ids through FUN_0041D750, choosing the list by app state and g_GameMode. Not in play (g_app_state != 6): g_preload_lists_by_scene[g_scene_index]. In play: g_GameMode 2 (Training) takes g_preload_lists_training_by_block[g_evt_block_index], except block 3 which takes g_preload_lists_training_by_lesson[g_training_lesson]; g_GameMode 3 (Boss) takes g_preload_lists_boss_by_scene[g_scene_index]; g_GameMode 0 and 1 (Arcade and Original) share g_preload_lists_by_scene[g_scene_index]. That 0 and 1 share the ordinary per-scene table while 2 and 3 do not is one of three independent witnesses that 0 and 1 are the two full-game modes.
PadStartPressed(player): off the title g_pad_state & 8 (player 0) or & 0x80000 (player 1); on it (app state 4) & 0xC or & 0xC0000. [proved]

True in app states 5, 9, 0x0A and 0x0B, and in 6 only at run phase 8; false otherwise. PlayerUpdateInPlay polls for a start press only then, and ResetDamageRank uses rank 2 then. What 9 and phase 8 are is [open]; 5 is the attract demo and 0x0A/0x0B its scenes. [proved]

DrawBackdropDome -- the game's sky.  Ghidra had left this block undefined, so it appeared in no xref listing by name. Selected by evt opcode 0x1B (preset, DAT_009A2C34) and gated by 0x1C (mode, DAT_009CA090: 0 off, 2 drawn but frozen, else drawn and animating).  Preset table at g_backdrop_preset_table (0x00579968), 12 x 16 bytes:      +0x00  s16  slot_a   the dome that is drawn     +0x02  s16  slot_b   a second slot, used by the 8/10/11 variant paths     +0x04  f32  dy       Y offset from the camera, 0 .. -3000     +0x08  s32  spin     BAMS added to the angle every frame     +0x0C  s32  angle0   BAMS the angle resets to when the preset changes  Main path:      esi = &g_camera_pose[g_camera_player];     /* 0x009A60C0 + player*0x69 */     if (preset != DAT_007C2118) {              /* preset changed */         state->angle = table[preset].angle0;     }     if (backdrop_mode == 0) return;      MatrixStackPush(0);     MatrixTranslate(esi->x, esi->y + table[preset].dy, esi->z);     if (backdrop_mode != 2) state->angle += table[preset].spin;     if (preset == 5) { MatrixRotateZ(0x8000); MatrixRotateY(-angle); }     else               MatrixRotateY(angle);     MatrixScale(1.2f, 1.2f, -1.2f);     AssetDrawSlot(table[preset].slot_a);  TWO DETAILS THAT MATTER:    * It follows the camera in ALL THREE AXES, not just horizontally, so the     dome can never be approached.   * The Z SCALE IS NEGATIVE. The dome is turned inside out -- it is modelled     to be seen from within.  Presets 8, 10 and 11 branch to separate paths at 0x004133FB / 0x004133F3 / 0x00413441; those also call FUN_00413560, which scrolls texture V by -0.005/frame and wraps at -2.995.  The call at 0x004133D3 is to FUN_0041EBB0, the empty stub -- a dead call.  Every dome lives in st1_1, etc_1 or st5_01b regardless of which stage uses it; the sky is shared geometry. No region draws these slots, so the script pulls them in with opcode 0x50 like any other prop.  See docs/formats/evt.md.

DrawBackdropDome's preset-10 and preset-11 path (called at 0x00413432 and 0x00413442). slot = g_backdrop_preset_table[g_backdrop_preset].slot_a (+0x00, 0x00579968 + preset*16); unless the backdrop mode (0x009CA090) is 2 it calls FUN_00413560 (the V scroll); then MatrixLoadIdentity -- so the draw is in VIEW space --, MatrixTranslate(0, -500.0, -50.0) (0xC3FA0000, 0xC2480000 pushed), MatrixRotateX(0xDE00), MatrixRotateY(-g_camera_block_yaw_bams[g_camera_index]) (0x0041367C, NEG), AssetDrawSlot(slot). Turned by the camera block's heading negated, so what it draws keeps a world heading while it follows the view. Not ported: render/backdrop.ts says these presets' own paths are not reproduced. What the model looks like is [open]. [proved]

DrawRainParticles -- evt opcode 0x1D's effect, gated on DAT_009C8E50 == 1.      SetDrawLayerNibble(0xE);     for (p = g_rain_particles; p < 0x007C2114; p += 3 floats) {         p.y -= 2.0;         if (p.y <= -7.0) {                    /* respawn */             p.x = rand() % 0x14 - 10.0;       /* [-10,  9] */             p.y = rand() % 0x32 - 25.0;       /* [-25, 24] */             p.z = rand() % 0x19 - 35.0;       /* [-35,-11] */         }         world = RotY(g_camera_pose[player].yaw) * p               + g_camera_pose[player].eye;         yaw = angle_of(world - eye, with dy passed as a LITERAL 0);         Translate(world); RotateY(yaw); RotateZ(0x100);         Scale(1.5, 3.5, 1.0);         AssetDrawSlotAlpha(0x53, 0.5);     }     SetDrawLayerNibble(8);                    /* back to the default layer */  THE COUNT IS NOT STORED. The particle array runs 0x007C1EB8 .. 0x007C2114 at 12 bytes each, which is 50. The loop bound is the end of the array.  Three details that are not what a from-scratch particle system would do:    * The volume is rotated by the camera's YAW ONLY before the eye is added,     so it follows where the camera looks horizontally while staying     world-vertical. Rain never tilts when the camera pitches.   * The spawn box is 20 x 50 x 25 sitting IN FRONT of the camera (z from -35     to -11), so drops are only ever created ahead of the view.   * The per-drop yaw is computed with the vertical component passed as a     literal 0, so a drop's facing does not change as it falls.  RotZ(0x100) is 1.40625 degrees -- the streaks are very slightly off vertical.  Asset slot 0x53 is stage1.bin[0]. No region draws it and no asset opcode loads it: the routine names the slot as a literal, so anything reconstructing the scene must pull it in explicitly or the effect has no model.  The call at 0x00413704 is FUN_0041EBB0, the empty stub -- a dead call, the same one DrawBackdropDome makes.  [measured] Only stage 1 ever turns rain on: 18 `enable_rain 1` in st1evtbl, and every other stage's uses are all 0.  See docs/formats/evt.md.

Draw the HUD letterbox shutter and drive the firing gate. evt opcode 0x1F selects the state in DAT_009CA0F4.  Geometry: the bars are asset 0x93E, which is common.bin model 129 -- a single four-vertex quad spanning x -0.515..0.515, y -0.05..0.05. MatrixTranslate positions its ORIGIN, so a bar placed at y = 0.35 occupies 0.30..0.40. At the game's 41.100 degree vertical FOV the frustum half-height at |z| = 1 is tan(20.55 deg) = 0.37477, so a closed shutter's inner edge sits at 80 % of the half-height: a 10 % band top and bottom. The quad's 0.515 half-width just covers the 0.4997 half-width of a 4:3 frustum, i.e. the artwork is cut for a 4:3 screen exactly.  States (DAT_009CA0F4):   0  draw closed at +/-0.35, -> 4, gate ON   1  opening: counter 0 -> 0x28, y = 0.35 + counter*0.0025, -> 2, gate ON   2  nothing drawn -- fully open (y = 0.45 clears the frame at counter 30)   3  closing: counter 0x28 -> 0; at 0 draw closed, -> 4, gate OFF   4  draw closed unless (DAT_009A5900 & 0x30)   5  draw closed, -> 4, gate OFF   6  gate ON, -> 2   7  restore the previous state (DAT_009C8E9C)   8  one bar at (0,0,-1) scaled (1,8,1) -- half-height 0.4, a full blackout  The gate is g_nFiringGate (0x009C8E00). It is not "the shutter is open": states 0 and 5 both draw a closed shutter and set it 1 and 0 respectively. It is also what gates the Start poll for a cutscene skip -- see g_nEvtSkippableRegion.

Body: if (g_trigger_down) { if (!g_aim_on_screen || ammo == 0) { if (g_player_input_is_gun == 1 && !g_aim_on_screen && ammo != 6) PlayerRefillMagazine; } else if (g_nFiringGate) { unless attract (app 5), g_player_infinite_ammo or an Original magazine of -1: ammo -= 1; at 0 raise g_player_magazine_empty and zero g_player_reload_prompt_timer; g_nPlayerFired = 1; g_player_shot_count++ unless 0x009A5C48; BuildShotRay; PlayerShotEffectSpawn; PlaySoundId(g_gunshot_sound_ids[player]); } } then if (g_pad_state & the binding set's reload mask && g_player_input_is_gun == 0 && ammo != 6) PlayerRefillMagazine; then the skip poll (g_nFiringGate 0 and g_nEvtSkippableRegion: pad 0x2 / 0x20000 sets g_nSkipRequested). So: an EMPTY gun pointed at the screen does nothing at all -- no refill, no sound (the RELOAD voice is HudDrawAmmoAndReloadPrompt's); a gun reloads only by a pull with the aim OFF the screen; a pad only by its reload button. Neither reload is behind the firing gate. [proved]

Four conditions, all required: g_app_state == 6 (in play); the player is either holding a live gun (DAT_009A5D85[p*0x130] != 1 and DAT_009C8FD0[p*0x14] != 0) or in input mode 5 or 6 as FUN_0041E260 reports it; g_player_lives > 0; and g_nFiringGate != 0 (the read at 0x00416A65). So the crosshair is HIDDEN whenever the shutter's firing gate is down -- the same flag that makes the trigger do nothing. Position: modes 5/6 take it from FUN_0041E280, everything else from (g_crosshair_x + 320, 240 - g_crosshair_y), i.e. the 640x480 screen with the origin at the centre and y up. The sprite id is a s16 from the table at 0x00579F58 indexed by (DAT_009C9F60[p*0x7c] + player*4); the record at 0x009A5D44 + player*0x130 is handed to FUN_0041C630.

Draws and steps the three 6-record rings one player's shots leave, in draw layer 0xC. The muzzle flash (g_shot_flash_ring) runs 9 frames from g_muzzle_flash_slots[player] at scale 0.1 with a second draw from g_muzzle_smoke_slots[player] at 0.75 for weapon kind 4 and 0.5 otherwise, and is skipped entirely for kind 3. The tracer (g_shot_tracer_ring) advances by its velocity, billboards through MatrixClearRotation, spins +0x1000 BAMS a frame and draws g_muzzle_smoke_slots[player] + 2; it lives 60 frames, or dies on its second frame when g_shot_hit_something says the shot landed. A kind-5 tracer (CMP EAX,0x5 at 0x00416CBE) takes the other arm instead, 0x00416D2B..0x00416DB2: Translate(record), CamEvalObjectPath6(0x194, (float)(frame % 0x18)), Translate(that xyz), MatrixClearRotation, RotZ(rz) RotY(ry) RotX(rx), AssetDrawSlot(0x109D) -- no spin; PUSH 0x109D at 0x00416DA1 is the only draw operand in .text naming that slot (the other two are AssetQueueLoadSlot's). The third ring is Original Mode weapon kind 4 only: 24 frames from slot 0xA6F at scale 0.05. Every record's frame counter steps whether or not it is live. The loop tail past the first draw's return is in the listing, not the pseudocode (L35).

Fills one slot of all three per-player effect rings, once per trigger pull, hit or miss. The muzzle point is the crosshair at camera-space z = -1: (g_crosshair_x / g_projection_distance_px, g_crosshair_y / g_projection_distance_px, -1.0), with the flash angles from FUN_004016B0 and then yaw += 0x8000 and pitch negated. The tracer takes that point through the camera matrix into world space and flies normalize(point - eye) * 20.0, or * 10.0 for Original Mode weapon kind 5, which also routes its draw down the object-path arm. The ring cursor g_shot_effect_cursor advances after the flash and the tracer are written and BEFORE the Original Mode third record, so that one lands in the NEXT slot.

DamageOverlayClear(player_task): g_damage_overlays[player].active = 0 and .frames = 0. Called by DamageOverlayUpdateAndDraw on expiry and by g_player_state_handlers[1] (0x00413DE0) when the overlay is live. [proved]

Per player, last-but-two call of PlayerUpdateInPlay (0x00413F87), also from FUN_00414280. If active: frames -= 1; clear when it reaches 0 or g_max_attackers has risen above the count latched at spawn; if still active draw: SetDrawLayerNibble(0xA), push, identity, MatrixTranslate(g_damage_overlay_offsets[kind].x + rec.x, [kind].y, -1.02 = 0xBF828F5C), MatrixScale(g_damage_overlay_scales[kind] x3), NoOpStub, AssetDrawSlot(dword [0x579F7C + (count + kind*2)*4]) -- CALL 0x00418560 at 0x004173B5, the plain draw and not AssetDrawSlotWithAlpha --, pop, SetDrawLayerNibble(8). No alpha, colour or scale ramp: the sprite is drawn unchanged for 59 frames. Its opacity is therefore the model's own: the eleven common.bin models 116..126 are one mesh each, TSP 0x9400041B (0x9404041B for 123/124, U flip): SRCALPHA/INVSRCALPHA, UseAlpha and IgnoreTexAlpha clear so the translucent pass with the alpha test on, shading mode 0 so ALPHAOP MODULATE (texture x diffuse), base colour ARGB (1,1,1,1); textures 26..33 are ARGB4444 VQ, alpha 0 around each mark and 255 over most of it with a 4-bit soft edge -- the marks draw opaque, not translucent. THEN, whether or not it drew (the decompiler's early return is wrong -- the draw arm falls into 0x004173CC, L37): if frames == 0x37 play the hurt voice, player 0 rand()%2 ? 0x1EA9 : 0x11EA9 (DAMEGE_JMS 184/185), player 1 rand()%2 ? 0x11DA9 : 0x1DA9 (DAMEGE_GA 187/188). [proved]

DamageOverlaySpawn(player_task, kind): only if g_damage_overlays[player] is not already active -- a hit during a live overlay shows nothing new and plays no sound. active = 1, frames = 60, count = g_max_attackers, x = g_damage_overlay_x_by_players[(count-1)*2 + player] (read as 0x004ECB54 + (player + count*2)*4), kind = kind; PlaySoundId(g_damage_overlay_sounds[kind]). The kind is PlayerTakeDamage's third argument. [proved]

The lives readout, one player, from PlayerUpdateInPlay's HUD branch (lives > 0, app state not 5/9) -- NOT gated on g_nFiringGate, unlike HudDrawAmmoAndReloadPrompt. Shutter state 2 only: player 0 draws DrawScreenSprite(0x5B9 '1P', 28, 412) and one lamp per life at x = 60 + 32*i, y = 412, sprite 0x6C2 + ((g_frame_counter + i*4)/3) % 7 -- a seven-cel flame whose phase is staggered 4 frames per lamp; player 1 draws 0x5BA '2P' at 584 and lamps 0x6CA.. at x = 548 - 32*i. Original Mode (g_GameMode 1) with more than 5 lives draws one lamp, 'x' (0x65) and the digit 0x59 + lives instead. Shutter state 4 with g_screen_furniture_flags bit 0x10 clear: 'HOLD YOUR FIRE!' (0x5B8) at (32, 422) or (416, 422), scale (1.5, 1.0), depth 0.98, on the low 45 of every 60 g_frame_counter frames. Any other shutter state draws nothing. [proved]

The ammo readout and the RELOAD prompt, one player. Called from PlayerUpdateInPlay only while g_nFiringGate is non-zero. Draws nothing unless g_bHudShutterState is 2 (fully open, full size) or 1 (opening, scaled by (40 - counter)*0.0125 + 1 from the per-player float at 0x007C2120); any other shutter state zeroes that counter and skips the readout. Arcade draws one bullet sprite per round left, stepping (spacing + 24) px from x=24 for player 1 and back from x=592 for player 2, at y = 364 + the per-weapon dy. Original Mode draws the same sprite once plus a two-digit count when g_player_ammo >= 7, and 'oo' (sprites 0x65, 99) when g_player_magazine_size is -1, i.e. unlimited; the sprite and the two offsets come from the 12-byte rows at 0x004ECA20 indexed by the weapon at DAT_009A2247. Then the RELOAD prompt, which needs the empty latch DAT_009A5C7E set AND g_nFiringGate again (0x00418001): sprite 0xA27 blinks on the low 45 of every 60 frames of the counter at 0x009A5C80, joined after 120 frames by 0xA28 or 0xA29, and the same counter plays a nag sound while the trigger is held. The counter counts up and re-arms at 120 rather than overflowing.

Loads the shared pol/common.bin and tex/common.bin asset banks.  The clearest example of the asset load path in the binary; every other loader is a variation on it.    wsprintfA(path, "pol\%s", "common.bin")   CreateFileA / GetFileSize / ReadFile into the staging buffer at 009c8e54   size = *staging                     <- u32 uncompressed size header   LzDecompress(staging + 1, dst)      <- src skips the header  The pol bank decompresses to a fixed .data buffer at 00811720. The tex bank is allocated at run time: alloc(size + 0x20), then aligned up to 32 before use.  The registration loop that follows walks 0x175 (373) entries of a table at 004e3110, using the sign bit of each container word as a present/absent flag.

SetupSceneProjection()  The game's one 3D projection setup. Called from the per-frame scene update (FUN_0040E730) and from FUN_00460030.      SetMatrixMode(3);                       /* PROJECTION            */     MatrixLoadIdentity();     MatrixTranslate(DAT_009C7300, DAT_009C7304, 0);   /* screen offset, both 0 */     BuildPerspectiveProjection(0x1D3B, 4.0/3.0, 0.8, 8000.0);     SetMatrixMode(1);                       /* commits it via SetTransform */     MatrixLoadIdentity();     ...     DAT_009A2D70 = 240.0 / tan(0.35866388296751145);   /* = 640.16 */  So, for the whole game:      vertical FOV   0x1D3B BAMS = 41.100 degrees = 0.7173277659 rad     horizontal FOV 53.127 degrees     aspect         4:3     near / far     0.8 / 8000.0  DAT_009A2D70 = 640.16 is the projection distance in pixels for a 480-tall viewport -- (480/2) / tan(fovY/2) -- and is an independent confirmation of the same FOV.  Not to be confused with the projection built once in InitD3DDeviceAndTextureStages (0x004A4DA0) with fov DAT_00598778 = 60 degrees, aspect 0.9, near 1.0, far 6000.0 into DAT_007DE5C8. That matrix is never handed to the device -- DAT_007DE5C8 has exactly one xref, the call that fills it -- and DAT_00598778 has exactly one read. It is stock d3du sample scaffolding and is dead. The 60 degrees there is a red herring.

AssetDrawSlot(slot): slot 0 calls NoOpStub(1.0f) and returns; otherwise, when the slot record (0x009A66A0 + slot*0x10: model pointer at +4, flags word at +0xC) has both 0x8000 and 1 set, RenderSubmitModelDefaultLight(model). It takes no alpha and adds none: the model is drawn in each mesh's own pass with each mesh's own material (WalkMeshChainAndDraw's SetMaterial from the header), so a translucent-pass mesh's on-screen alpha is its texel alpha times its base alpha (+0x2C) -- the faded path is AssetDrawSlotWithAlpha (0x004185A0). [proved]

AssetDrawSlotWithAlpha(slot, alpha): AssetDrawSlot's twin with a draw alpha -- slot 0 calls NoOpStub(1.0f); otherwise the same resident test on the slot record (0x9A66AC & 0x8000 and & 1), then RenderSubmitModelFadedDefaultLight(model, alpha), which queues the command faded (key bit 29) so DrawModelWithForcedAlphaBlend draws it -- whatever the alpha, 1.0 included. [proved]
lit variant of AssetDrawSlot, same slot

AssetDrawSlotWithAlpha under the scene light array: the same resident test on the slot record (0x9A66AC & 0x8000 and & 1), then RenderSubmitModelFadedSceneLights(model, alpha). Slot 0 calls the empty stub. [proved]

Resolves an asset slot like AssetDrawSlot (slot 0 does nothing; the record at 0x9A66A0 + slot*16 must have +0xD bit 0x80) and hands its model to ModelUVsFromViewNormals (FUN_004AA400); draws NOTHING. Every caller calls it just before drawing the same slot: DrawCharacterPartSlot's type-9 arm (0x00419C0D) and types 0x4C..0x52's arms, ZombieDrawBonePart's 0x1C71..0x1C80 arms (not 0x1C73/0x1C7C), class 0x2D's node hook at 0x00429040 and FUN_0042BF30's orbs. So those models are drawn with UVs made from their normals this frame. [proved] for the body; not ported -- the port draws the twin (type 9) and znele's cels with their exported UVs.

ModelFlipStripCullingParity(model)  Walks a loaded NL1 model's mesh chain and XORs bit 0 of every *strip* control word, flipping culling 2 <-> 3 (backface <-> frontface) and 0 <-> 1 (both "no cull", so a no-op there).  Applied ONLY to the four asset slots listed at g_ModelFixupSlotList (0x0057A280) -- it is a per-asset content patch, not a general load step. Paired with ModelForceFogControlNone, called immediately before it.  This is the canonical statement of the NL1 chain walk. Three rules, nothing else -- no parameter_control bit, no shading mode, no 16-bit-UV flag:    chain word bit 31 set  -> mesh header, 0x50 bytes, skip geometry with                             (mesh_data_size & ~3)   chain word bit 31 clear-> strip header {flags, count}, 8 bytes;                             count is a TRIANGLE count when flags & 8   vertex record          -> 8 bytes when bit 0 of its first dword is clear                             (a back-reference), 32 bytes when set  Verified against all 9,112 models: the walk lands exactly on every declared mesh end, zero desyncs (tools/verify_walk.py).

ModelForceFogControlNone(model)  Walks a loaded NL1 model's mesh headers and rewrites each mesh's tsp_instruction:      tsp = (tsp & 0xFFBFFFFF) | 0x00800000;  Bits 22-23 are PowerVR2 fog control (0 LUT, 1 per-vertex, 2 none, 3 LUT mode 2). Clearing 22 and setting 23 forces fog control to 2 = NONE, so these meshes never take the fog path in TranslatePvr2StateToD3D.  Only reached for the four slots in g_ModelFixupSlotList. Mesh stride here is (mesh_data_size & ~3) + 0x50 -- the size field is masked down to a 4-byte boundary, as it is in WalkMeshChainAndDraw.  Note the walk assumes every chain word at this level has bit 31 set; if one does not it falls into an infinite loop, which is a second confirmation that a top-level chain word is always either a mesh header or the zero terminator.

ModelSetMeshAmbientScale(model, k): writes k into every mesh header's +0x28 along the chain (stride (mesh_data_size & ~3) + 0x50, the same walk ModelForceFogControlNone makes). +0x28 is the scale WalkMeshChainAndDraw and DrawModelWithForcedAlphaBlend multiply the diffuse RGB by to build the D3DMATERIAL7 ambient colour, so this sets how much of the scene ambient a model takes. One caller, FUN_004193B0. [proved]

Build the runtime record for one of g_pCharacterExtraParts' parts, lazily, the first time SkeletonDrawWalk wants to draw it. Refuses while the part's asset slot is not resident. The 0x54-byte record holds four {count, source verts, index list, bone matrix} groups plus the drawn slot at +0x44 and the matrix the draw happens in at +0x50; the five bone indices come from g_character_part_bones[part], with per-character-type overrides for 0x0E, 0x1F/0x46/0x4E, 0x41, 0x4C and 0x53. Character type 0x17's part 1 goes to FUN_00419EB0 instead, which builds eight sub-parts. The vertices are a private copy of the loaded model's, so the deform writes into geometry only this actor draws.
Part drawer: deform all four groups -- which=1 for k in 0,1 then which=0 for k in 0,1 -- then draw. Every part 1 in the game takes it, and so does type 0x4C's whole 18-part list.

The part's 0x54-byte runtime record, or 0 if it has none yet. Rebuilds it through BuildCharacterPart when the asset slot has moved -- it compares rec+0x48 against the slot's current base -- and drops the old vertex map with FreeCharacterPartVertexMap.

The deform, and it is a HARD PARTITION rather than a blend. One call per vertex group: it composes inverse(draw bone matrix) * (group bone matrix), then walks the part's rows -- one signed byte per row in the group's assign array -- and for every row the byte claims (>= 0) transforms that group's source point and normal, at rec+0x04/+0x24 with stride 0x18, into the draw bone's space and writes them over every copy of that vertex in the loaded model. A negative byte means the row belongs to another group. Measured across three parts: 0 rows claimed by two groups and 0 claimed by none, so every vertex has exactly one bone and weight 1. The source arrays are in the GROUP BONE's local space, so the net effect after the draw re-applies the draw bone's matrix is simply world = group_bone_matrix * source_vertex.

Draw the deformed part: set the matrix from rec+0x50, the FIFTH bone of the part's g_character_part_bones row, and draw rec+0x44. Skipped when the part's visibility byte at model+0x40 + part*8 + 1 is clear. The character-type switch (type - 9 through the byte map at 0x00419DE8 into the jump table at 0x00419DCC) draws types 9, 0x12, 0x17 and 0x18 AT obj+0x138C -- AssetDrawSlotWithAlpha or FUN_00418620, with no test of obj+0x136C bit 2; type 9 runs FUN_00418660 first -- types 0x4D-0x4F, 0x51, 0x52 run FUN_00418660 and draw solid, type 0x4C's parts 0-5 draw two slots from DAT_004EDA50 at obj+0x1370 and its others one, and every other type draws solid through AssetDrawSlot or SubmitSlotWithSceneLightArray. [proved]
Part drawer: deform group 2 only, then draw. g_character_part_drawers gives it to types 0x1F/0x46/0x4E parts 1 and 2.
DeformCharacterPartGroup for one group, then DrawCharacterPartSlot. The which argument picks the pair of group slots: 1 is groups 0 and 1, 0 is groups 2 and 3.

Part drawer: deform group 0 only, then draw -- the commonest by far, and every humanoid's part 0 (the waist). The part's other groups are left holding what the loaded model stores, which is correct because a group whose bone IS the draw bone deforms to the identity: measured, the exe's source vertices for such a group equal the pol model's stored ones to within the low mantissa bit that WriteCharacterPartVertexPos sets.
Byte-for-byte the same as DrawCharacterPartGroup0 -- push 1, call DeformAndDrawCharacterPart -- as a second copy. g_character_part_drawers gives this one to character type 0x17's part 0.

Character type 0x17's part 1 alone, and a different mechanism: instead of one slot with four vertex groups it builds EIGHT sub-parts from g_class17_subpart_records, each with its own bone, asset slot and vertex map, into a 0xD0 record. Gated on DAT_009C7A78 == 4. Its eight bones are 16 and above, which is exactly the range SkeletonNodeDrawSuppressed vetoes for this type.
The drawer for character type 0x17's eight sub-parts. Unread beyond its shape.

Dispatch one of the character's non-skeleton parts: g_character_part_drawers[char_type][part](part). Every humanoid's part 0 is FUN_00419E90, which deforms one vertex group; the types with two parts draw part 1 through FUN_004198B0, which deforms all four. SkeletonDrawWalk's tail loop is what calls it, once per part that has a model and is not hidden.

Per part, the map from a logical vertex to every copy of it in the loaded model. Copies two blobs out of the mesh-info block in .rdata and relocates the second by adding the loaded model's base. The result is a 0x1C record: +0x04 the row count, +0x08 the head size in bytes, +0x10 the row stride, +0x18 the rows. A row is {s16 head[n]; u32 vertex_record_pointers[m]} with the pointer list terminated by -1, and a row is one logical vertex: measured, hito_gal's waist has 20 rows and 24 pointers onto 24 distinct vertex records, its skirt 24 rows and 28 pointers onto 28. The head is read by nothing in this build.
Frees the two blobs BuildCharacterPartVertexMap copied and then the record.

Write one deformed position over every copy of a logical vertex. It ORs bit 0 into the x coordinate's bits first, which is the PowerVR2 vertex control word: bit 0 of a record's first dword is what tells the chain walker this is a 32-byte vertex and not an 8-byte back-reference, so the write must not clear it. That costs the low mantissa bit of x, about 6e-4 at these magnitudes.
The normal half of WriteCharacterPartVertexPos, at +0x0C of the vertex record. It ORs bit 0 into the normal's z for the same reason the position half does it to x.
WriteCharacterPartVertexPos, writing the same position a second time 0x82C0 bytes further on. Used only for character type 0x4C's parts 0-5, whose model has a twin at that fixed offset.
WriteCharacterPartVertexNormal writing a second copy 0x82C0 bytes on, NEGATED -- the twin is mirrored, so its normals point the other way. Character type 0x4C only.

DrawScreenSprite's worker: draws only while the sprite's texture bank g_screen_sprite_bank[id] is loaded (state byte 4 in the per-bank record at 0x009C7328, stride 0xC), then SubmitScreenSpriteQuad(record, g_screen_sprite_tex_slot[id]). [proved]

DrawScreenSprite(sprite, x, y, depth, sx, sy, rot, flags): builds the 14-dword record SpriteDrawCheckedBank reads -- UVs (0,0)-(1,1), alpha 1.0, -1 at +0x30 -- and calls it. x, y are the sprite's top-left corner in the 640x480 screen with y down (the corner table g_sprite_quad_corners puts (x,y) at offset 0); the quad is texture width*sx by height*sy pixels; depth goes to z and rhw; rot is BAMS about the corner; flags 0x10/0x20 flip U/V, the low nibble picks the anchor. Every HUD readout goes through it. [proved]

ScreenSpriteQueuePush(rec): DrawScreenSpriteLayered's worker. Copies the 14-dword sprite record into the next 0x40-byte cell of the queue buffer (cursor 0x007C21A4, refused once it reaches 0x007C29A8), ORs 0x700 into the flags word at +0x34, marks the cell live (+0x3A = 1) and links it in right after the header of layer rec+0x38 (the four headers at 0x007C21A8, stride 0x40; next pointer at +0x3C) -- so within a layer the newest record is drawn first. [proved]

DrawScreenSpriteLayered(id, x, y, depth, sx, sy, rot, flags, layer): DrawScreenSprite's record (UVs 0..1, alpha 1.0, -1 at +0x30) with the layer as a ninth argument at +0x38, handed to ScreenSpriteQueuePush instead of drawn. ScreenSpriteQueueFlush draws the queue at the end of the frame, layers 0..3 in order. Callers: BossHpBarUpdate (four, layer 2) and the two player-panel routines at 0x00416880/0x004168C0 (layer 2). [proved]

TexBankPaletteIndex(bank, texture): which of the 16-colour palettes a PAL4 texture of a tex/ bank is bound with. A switch on the bank index: 0x147 (scr_common) reads the s16 table g_scr_common_palette_index, other banks their own tables or constants, default 0. [proved]
Reverse of g_screen_sprite_tex_slot: the first sprite id whose global texture slot is the argument, or -1; scans the 2979 entries up to 0x005802D4. [proved]
Asset job kind 7: release every texture of a tex/ bank through TextureSlotRelease and mark the bank's state byte 0. [proved]

Empties the layered sprite queue: four header cells at 0x007C21A8 (stride 0x40) each marked not-live (+0x3A = 0) and chained through +0x3C to the next, the last's next 0; cursor 0x007C21A4 = the cell after the fourth header. Called once a frame from SetupSceneProjection. [proved]

Draws the layered sprite queue: walks the chain from the first header through +0x3C and hands every live cell (+0x3A != 0) to SpriteDrawCheckedBank. The headers are not live, so the order is layer 0's records newest first, then layer 1's, 2's, 3's. Only caller FUN_00418550, which the frame tick runs after the task walk. [proved]

PlaySoundId -- the single entry point for every sound in the game.  One id space, split by the TOP NIBBLE (id >> 28):    0  SE       linked list at g_se_name_list (0x005845F8), stride 0x34 = {u32 id; char[0x30]}, walked linearly; name appended to "Sound\SE\"; terminated by id == 0xFFFF. id 0 early-outs -- that is how a script says "no sound". 0x000100A0 goes to SoundCommand(0, 0x100A0), which does nothing. 0x21A9 / 0x121A9 go to channel 0x11 unlooped. Otherwise the g_looping_se_ids / g_looping_se_stop_ids walk sets the loop flag or stops every loop.   1  BGM      (id & 0xFFF) indexes a table of char* filenames prefixed "Sound\BGM\": plain (0x005803F8, char*[20]) when g_app_state == 6 && g_GameMode == 0, else _AR (0x00580354, char*[41]). The tables are CONTIGUOUS, which is what fixes their lengths. A null entry (2, 4, 7) breaks out and changes nothing. Otherwise SoundPlayOnFreeChannel(name, loop, 0xF, -1) -- channel 0xF, the one STREAMED channel -- with loop = 0 for exactly 0x10000009, 0x10000025, 0x10000014 (CMPs at 0x0041D1FB/0x0041D205/0x0041D20D -> PUSH 0 at 0x0041D241) and 1 for every other id (PUSH 1 at 0x0041D21D); then g_current_bgm_id = id. The channel is released and the file reopened from its first byte EVERY time, so playing the track already playing restarts it. See SoundStreamThread for the loop: [dataStart, EOF) end to end, no loop points.   2  voice    (id & 0xFFF) * 0x24 into records at 0x0058044A; a s16 of -1 marks an empty slot. Name at +2, prefixed "Sound\Voice\"; channel 0x10, unlooped.   8  control  PlaySoundControl(id): 0x80000001 the SE channels, 0x80000002 the voice, anything else the music; then g_current_bgm_id = 0 for exactly 0x80000000.  Reached from evt 0x5F via BgmStopThenPlay and from se_play 0x38-0x3B, which is how the stage scripts start their own tracks (step 2 of each entry block; stage 5 uses 0x5F). See docs/formats/sound.md.

g_current_bgm_id = 0; SoundStopGroup(g_bgm_stop_group) and (g_voice_stop_group); SoundCommand(1..7, 0x1100A0) releases SE channels 0..14. Called by MarkSceneOver, ResetGameOnStart, GameOverRunPhase, TitleMenuRunPhase and the attract screens. [proved]

PlaySoundId's namespace-8 arm. 0x80000001: SoundCommand(1..3, 0x1100A0), every SE channel; 0x80000002: SoundStopGroup(g_voice_stop_group), the voice; ANY OTHER value: SoundStopGroup(g_bgm_stop_group), the music. PlaySoundId then zeroes g_current_bgm_id for exactly 0x80000000. [proved]
evt 0x5F's target: OutputDebugString("SS_Event_ENTRYBGM_BG_core"); PlaySoundId(0x80000000); PlaySoundId(param_3). Only the third operand is used. [proved]
Tail call to SoundStopGroup(group). [proved]

Enqueue an asset LOAD job for one slot id on the ring AssetQueueUnloadSlot uses (0x007DA220, 16-byte records, 64 deep, cursor DAT_007D9E1C & 0x3F): +0x08 the slot, +0x0C the state 0, +0x00 the kind = (slot_to_pol[slot] (s16 at 0x004E83B4) != 0xE7). Job table 0x00588C20 sends kinds 0 AND 1 to 0x00418B80, which steps the per-state loader through 0x0057A29C; kind 2 is AssetUnloadSlot. EvtOpAssetLoadSlot50 is its script caller. LoadSceneAndReset (0x0046012E) and the unfunctioned site at 0x0048A1D5 queue slot 0x109D -- the Original Mode weapon-5 round PlayerShotEffectsThink draws -- behind a byte test of the per-player Original Mode block (0x009A225D). [proved]
Enqueue asset job kind 2 for a slot id (ring at 0x007DA220, 64 deep, cursor DAT_007D9E1C); job table 0x00588C20 entry 2 is AssetUnloadSlot (0x00418BA0).

Enqueue asset job kind 7 for a texbank id (same ring as AssetQueueUnloadSlot); job table 0x00588C20 entry 7 is FUN_0041CD00, which frees the bank's textures. PROVED the texbank free: evt op 0x55 asset_free_texbank (EvtOpAssetFreeTexbank55) is this call on its operand. ChapterCardInstall frees its chapter texbank (0x18C..0x191, e.g. 399 = scr_chapter_st4.bin) with it.

Enqueues asset job kind 0xB with a cam file index. Kind 0xB's handler (0x00404080) dispatches job.state through 0x005773C0 = {0x00403E70, 0x00403FB0, 0x00404000}, the cam file open/read/resolve steps. GameOverRunPhase passes 5, cp_gmovr.bin. [proved]
