Class 0x46's handler, and a placer: every path ends in ActorKill. THE BAT, settled twice over -- character type 0x1E is zabat.bin (one node, slot 6913) and every death plays COMMON2\KOUMORI1_22.wav or KOUMORI2_22.wav, koumori being the bat. obj+0x130C (from desc+0x25 on the opcode-0x09 path) picks one of three flights, and each member is a 0x13D8-byte actor with clip 0x407, a 4.0 shot sphere at obj+0x124, obj+0x120 = 0xFF, BatDrawBoneSlot at obj+0x12EC, a wing actor from SpawnBatWings, and a slot in g_bat_members[obj+0x1374 * 0x19 + obj+0x1377]. Sub-type 0 (24 spawns) is ONE bat per descriptor running BatDiveUpdate: obj+0x1377 = +0x11C - 1 is the member index, obj+0x1375 = desc+0x24 the flight group, and a one-player game DROPS members 5 and 6 (the guard is 1 < g_players_in_play || +0x11C < 5). Sub-type 1 (1 spawn) builds 25 members running BatScatterUpdate, with no counters at all. Sub-type 2 (2 spawns) builds 6, or 8 with two players, running BatSwarmUpdate -- ((1 < g_players_in_play) - 1 & 0xFFFFFFFE) + 8, which reads like 8-or-10 and is not. Sub-types 0 and 2 increment BOTH g_enemies_present and g_enemies_alive and take a RegisterEnemySlot slot; sub-type 1 does neither.

The uniform quadratic B-spline basis the bat's flight path is evaluated with: w0 = (1-t)^2/2, w1 = (1-t)t + 0.5, w2 = t^2/2, which sum to 1. Its first argument, the segment index, is UNUSED here -- the caller adds it to the control-point index instead. PlaceBats calls it with t = 0 to seat a bat at 0.5*p0 + 0.5*p1.

The bat's per-bone draw callback, installed at obj+0x12EC by PlaceBats and SpawnBatWings. It reads the node's resolved record in g_skeleton_node_out at node_index * 0x90 and draws its slot if it is not -1. The call to NoOpStub(65536.0) that precedes it does nothing -- a bare RET -- so this hook is the plain drawer with no cel substitution of any kind, unlike class 0x30's and class 0x31's.

Builds the bat's WING actor and returns; PlaceBats calls it once per member. A second 0x13D8-byte skinned actor of character type 0x1F = zabat_wing.bin, six nodes in two three-segment chains (bones 1-2-3 and 4-5-6), running BatWingUpdate. It carries the body's obj+0x1374/obj+0x1377 so it can find its body in g_bat_members, and nothing else -- no position, no counter, no shot sphere. Its clip comes from BatWingUpdate, not from here.

Class 0x46 sub-type 0: the bat that flies a scripted path and then takes a life. Three states in obj+0x1376. State 0 counts obj+0x13D0 down from member*0x14, so the six members of a flight launch 20 frames apart. State 1 walks g_bat_spline_points[group*3 + member%3] as a 4-point quadratic B-spline, two segments, t at obj+0x13D4 stepping 0.05 a frame -- 20 frames a segment, 40 in all -- with obj+0x204 * 5.0 added to y and the yaw eased an eighth of the way to the heading each frame; past the last segment it latches the end point into obj+0x130C/0x1310/0x1314 and homes on g_camera_block_eye, obj+0x13A4 running 0 to 1 at 0.015 a frame (about 67 frames) with a sideways sine wobble of amplitude obj+0x13A8, which is 1.0 until t passes 0.8 and then (1-t)*5 so it damps to nothing on arrival. At t > 1 it calls PlayerTakeDamage(player, 1, 9) if either g_player_state is 5, gives both counters back and despawns -- THERE IS NO RANGE TEST AND NO ATTACK PERMIT: an unshot bat always connects. A hit (obj+0x34 bit 8) is only taken in states 1 and 2, so a bat is invulnerable for its whole launch delay; it pays 80, plays KOUMORI1 or KOUMORI2 at random, sprays blood, and falls in state 2 -- obj+0x131C dropping 0.02722 a frame, pitch and yaw spinning 0x200 and 0x800 -- for 0x50 frames before despawning.

Class 0x46 sub-type 1: 25 bats that burst away from the placer and are gone. Same three states in obj+0x1376, staggered obj+0x13D0 = member*2. State 1 has no path at all -- the velocity PlaceBats randomised (x = ((rand%101)*0.001 - 0.05)*0.8, y = (rand%11)*0.001 + 0.01, z = 2.0) is scaled by 1.05 and 1.08 every frame, so they accelerate away -- and the actor despawns the moment its z passes -3500. Shootable for 80 points on the same KOUMORI death sound, but it TOUCHES NEITHER ENEMY COUNTER, so no wait_enemies gate can see it. A shot one bounces its x and z velocity by -0.3 and falls until y < -25, where it spawns the SpawnBatSplash cel run and plays COMMON\SIBUKI8_16.WAV -- the water, which is where its one spawn is: stage 3 block 2 step 4.

Class 0x46 sub-type 2: 6 bats, or 8 with two players, that circle and then take a life. State 0 is not a wait but the ORBIT -- obj+0x135C turns 0x400 a frame about the point PlaceBats scattered into obj+0x130C/0x1310/0x1314 (the placer's position plus up to +-2 on each axis), at a radius of 12 + 5*sin(obj+0x1360) where obj+0x1360 advances by rand()%0x201 + 0xE00 a frame -- and it runs for obj+0x13D0 frames, seeded 0x3C + member*0x14 so the swarm peels off one at a time. State 1 is BatDiveUpdate's homing arm with obj+0x13A4 stepping 0.01 instead of 0.015 (100 frames) and the yaw eased a quarter rather than an eighth; it ends the same way, PlayerTakeDamage(player, 1, 9) and both counters back. UNLIKE sub-type 0 the hit test is only gated on obj+0x1376 != 2, so a swarm bat is killable while it is still orbiting.

The wing actor SpawnBatWings built. It has no state: every frame it looks its body up in g_bat_members[obj+0x1374 * 0x19 + obj+0x1377] and despawns if the slot is empty, then seats itself on the camera matrix times the body's bone matrix at obj+0x2C4, translated (0, 1, 2), takes the body's yaw + 0x8000 and a fixed pitch of 0xE800, copies the body's motion frame counter from obj+0x194, and draws. Its clip comes from a paired lookup: walk the five s16 of g_bat_body_motions for one equal to the body's obj+0x1B4 and take g_bat_wing_motions at the same index. Both tables ship all-identical, so the answer is always 0x406.

The per-frame routine of the 0x50-byte object SpawnBatSplash allocates (ActorAlloc(0x0042F930, 0x50)); Ghidra had it as a bare label until this was read. MatrixStackPush(0); MatrixTranslate(obj+0x38, obj+0x3C, obj+0x40) -- the caller's x and z and a literal y of -25.0 -- and nothing else, no rotation and no scale; AssetDrawSlot(0x1339 + obj+0x44); MatrixStackPop(1); then obj+0x44 += 1 and ActorKill once it passes 0x1D. So it draws common.bin 307..336 once each, the first on the frame it is made (ActorAlloc appends to the list the bat is walking, and TaskRunTree reads +0x1C afresh), and is gone after the thirtieth. [proved] Ported as game/class46/splash.ts (the step) and render/bat_splash.ts (the draw).

The water splash a shot bat leaves when its corpse falls past y = -25: BatScatterUpdate (0x0042EAC7) and BatSwarmUpdate (0x0042EF73) both call it, with (x, y, z) of the corpse. A 0x50-byte object running BatSplashUpdate (0x0042F930): obj+0x38 = x, obj+0x3C = -25.0 (0xC1C80000 -- the y argument is NOT read), obj+0x40 = z, obj+0x44 = 0, the frame. No skeleton; it draws asset slot 0x1339 + frame for 30 frames and then kills itself -- common.bin entries 307 to 336. The sound is the caller's, PlaySoundId(0x4616A9) = COMMON\SIBUKI8_16.WAV, and the swarm plays it only in g_scene_index 2. [proved]

Class 0x42's placer: one loop that builds a batch of objects and dies. How many is obj+0x130C and the player count (0x009C8E80 > 1), computed with SETG/DEC/AND rather than a branch: sub-type 0 gives 6 or 8 (0042f9c4-0042f9d3) and sub-type 2 gives 10 or 15 (0042f9e3-0042f9f1). Each member takes its asset slot from the dword table at 0x0055D74C plus 0x7800 into obj+0x1E4, rand() %% 0x3C into obj+0x1E8 as a phase, 0xFF into obj+0x120, g_ground_plane_y (0x009C8E58) into obj+0x224 and 0 into obj+0x192, then FUN_00408E80 makes the object; the object is recorded in the array at 0x007DCA4C and the running count at 0x007DCA49. The mechanism -- they fall under gravity and break into halves, one member flagged special at random -- is in docs/formats/spawns.md, and what they ARE is still [open]. Do not read the slot table's extent off this routine (L6): its index is the loop counter and its end is unestablished. **Each member is counted as an enemy**: 0042fbbf INC word ptr [0x009c7006] (g_enemies_present) and 0042fbc6 INC word ptr [0x009c904a] (g_enemies_alive), both INSIDE the loop, so one batch puts 6 to 15 into the counters a wait_enemies_alive gate reads. [proved] The browser player has no module for class 0x42, so nothing increments either counter and the gate in the same step comes down without them: stage 2 block 21 step 4 spawns two batches at op 29 and waits at op 34, block 26 step 2 spawns one at op 12 and waits at op 19.

The object SpawnBloodSprayAtPoint allocates, and the whole of it: MatrixLoadIdentity, MatrixTranslate(obj+0x38/0x3C/0x40), MatrixScale(0.3, or 0.15 with g_wCaptionMode == 1), AssetDrawSlot(obj+0x54), then obj+0x54++ and FUN_004A7040 -- free -- once it passes 0x52. Slots 0x3A..0x52 are the SAME twenty-five-cel flipbook SpawnBloodSpray (FUN_00407310) glues to a bone, pol/common.bin entries 0..24, which is what says this is blood and not some other sprite: it is the bone-stuck spray with a fixed point instead of a bone.

Blood at a point rather than on a bone. ActorAlloc(BloodSprayAtPointDrawAndTick, 0x98) with eff+0x38/0x3C/0x40 = the CALLER's obj+0x70/0x74/0x78 -- it takes obj+0x40 and reads +0x30 past it -- and eff+0x54 = 0x3A, the first cel. BodyCreatureUpdate calls it on the frame the creature is shot.

Class 0x53's Init -- the cat: g_character_skeletons maps its character type 0x1A to eighteen nodes that all land in cat.bin. obj+0x1F4 = 0x1A, obj+0x1FC (model+0x68, the object rotation order) = 1; sub = ActorAllocSub(0x24) at obj+0x1310 with +0x10 = the tail's first s16 (the animation set), +0x12/+0x1C/+0x1E = 0; obj+0x1B4 = g_cat_motions[set*5]. The tail's second s16 is the subtype. Subtypes 0 and 1 go to CatMotionListUpdate -- 1 additionally raises obj+0x38 bit 3, drawn through the scene light array -- and subtype 2 and up go to CatBranchTriggerUpdate with motion 0x305, obj+0x124 = 4.0 and sub+0x10/+0x12 = 0, but ONLY while g_GameMode == 1; in arcade the actor despawns at once. Both arms clear obj+0x34 bit 0x80 after ActorBuildSkinnedModel, so a cat is shot whole. Four spawns, all stage 2, in blocks 3, 5, 8 and 11. [proved]

Class 0x53 subtypes 0 and 1 (CatInit installs it): the cat that plays its set's playlist and leaves. Draw (LightsUseSecondarySet, DrawSkinnedModelAndShadow(obj+0x194, obj+0x40, obj+0x20C), LightsRestoreScene), then model[0] += 1 and sub+0x12 += 1 (life). When model[0] == g_motion_play_length[g_cat_motions[set*5 + sub+0x1C]] - 1 the counter goes back to 0 and sub+0x1E (passes) += 1; when g_cat_motion_repeats[set*5 + sub+0x1C] is not -2 and equals the passes, sub+0x1C steps (wrapping to 0 on a -1 entry), obj+0x1B4 = the new clip WRITTEN DIRECTLY (no ActorSetMotion, no fade), model[0] = 0, passes = 0. ActorDespawn once sub+0x12 > 1000. Writes no position: the cat moves only by its clips' root motion (SkeletonApplyRootMotion, from the draw). Set 5 (stage 2 block 11): 0x305 x2, 0x2FC x1, then 0x2FD for ever, which is the run. sub+0x10 is the animation set here. [proved]

Class 0x53 subtype >= 2: a shootable route-branch trigger. First, g_script_flags[0x83] == 1 despawns it (stage 2 sets flag 131 in block 8 right after freeing cat.bin). sub+0x10 is the state here. State 0 counts sub+0x12 and, while obj+0x1B4 is 0x305 and the count is past 199, ActorSetMotionBlended(0x2FA, 0, 10). If obj+0x34 bit 3 is set (shot) AND g_script_branch_var is still 0 AND g_evt_block_index == 8, it writes g_script_branch_var = 2, blends to 0x2FD and latches state 1 -- so this trigger answers the branch only in block 8, and only if nothing else has answered it already. That gate is load-bearing: of the four shipped spawns only block 8's route record has a slot 2 to go to, and tools/verify_branches.py fails if the gate is dropped. States 0 and 1 then test obj+0x40 < -478.0 and, past it, blend to 0x305 and set state 2: 0x2FD's root motion is what carries it there, along -x. Nothing clears bit 3. Ends with the draw, model[0] += 1 and ActorRegisterOriginInViewSpace. Reached only in original mode; see CatInit. [proved]

Class 0x2C's handler (g_class_handler_pairs entry 24 at 0x0059341C). Zeroes g_script_branch_var at 0x00432D55, obj+0x34 = 1, obj+0x11C = 0, obj+0x1310 = g_evt_block_index (0x009A2BC0), obj+0x124 = radius, and installs Class2CBranchToggleUpdate. A writer of g_script_branch_var the globals.tsv inventory had missed (found by a byte-pattern sweep for a4889c00, L32). No shipped stage places class 0x2C, so it is unreachable. [proved]

Class 0x2C's update. Despawns (ActorDespawn) the frame g_evt_block_index differs from obj+0x1310. On obj+0x34 bit 8 (shot) it TOGGLES obj+0x11C 0<->1 and writes the same value to g_script_branch_var (0x00432DF4 = 0, 0x00432E08 = 1), then clears bit 8; draws a camera-facing two-state billboard from the table at 0x00589D78 indexed [obj+0x130C * 2 + obj+0x11C]. A shootable route switch; unreached by any shipped spawn. [proved]
class 0x33, switch on obj+0x11C

The update ScriptedSceneryDispatch33 installs for class 0x33 selector 1 -- obj+0x11C is the sub-type selector, not hit points (L3), so the evt's hp field picks it. This is the object g_carrier_object (0x009A5C34) points at: 004331e1 MOV [0x009a5c34],EBP writes it every frame, so the global is live for as long as one of these exists. It raises TWO bits on its OWN obj+0x34, and they are different ends of the ride. 0x10000000 at 00433203, when g_script_flags[tail+0x20] == 1 or (s32)tail+0x18 == obj+0x1370 -- that is what ZombieStateRideCarrier (class 0x30 state 29) leaves on. 0x40000000 at 00433280, once tail+0x14 is not -1.0f and obj+0x1370 has passed it, together with obj+0x1334 = 0 and an effect spawned from the six dwords at tail+0x24 -- and THAT is the bit ZombieStateDelayedStrikeInPlace reads at 0045eafe to give up to state 10 after 0x14 frames. Twenty frames after raising it the routine also sets obj+0x34 bit 0x200000, plays 0x723A9 and swaps the drawn slot to 0x1AAB..0x1AD2. Stage 5 block 2 step 2 op 37 spawns one (evt 7396, hp 1).

Class 0x33 selector 1's mover. One caller, ScriptedCarrierUpdate33 at 004333EC, and only on the frames that routine does not despawn or detonate. obj+0x1312 is its own two-step cursor. 0 seats the object from the descriptor tail: obj+0x13F0 = tail+0x00 (draw slot); tail+0x04 == -1 ORs 0x80000001 into obj+0x34 and copies tail+0x08 into BOTH obj+0x124 and obj+0x128 (the shot sphere), otherwise it ORs 0x80000051 -- bit 0x10 is the mesh shot volume -- and puts tail+0x04 in obj+0x14C; obj+0x1350 = tail+0x0C (the op_ path slot); obj+0x1374 = tail+0x10 (the last frame); obj+0x1354/0x1358/0x135C = 0x24A/0x260/0 (the sprite cursors the draw tail cycles). obj+0x1370 starts at (float)(g_cam_path_frame - 1) via FILD, so the path cursor is seeded from the CAMERA's frame at the spawn instruction and is its own counter thereafter. Cursor 1 runs; 2 and up return at 00433881, which is what freezes obj+0x1370 for good. Every running frame adds 1.0 (0x004C4380) to obj+0x1370; if obj+0x1374 <= it the cursor goes to 2, otherwise CamEvalObjectPath6(obj+0x1350, obj+0x1370) writes obj+0x40/0x44/0x48 and obj+0x64/0x68/0x6C -- the three rotations MASKED to 16 bits -- and obj+0x118 = 1.0. Draw slot 0x1A35 and 0x1A36 override the scale to 2.5, 0x1A36 also adds 0x4000 BAMS to obj+0x68, and 0x1B0E subtracts 5.0 (0x0055D2B4) from obj+0x40. Slot 0x1B0E also plays 0x423A9 on the seating frame. Three shipped spawns: st2evtbl 20432 (0x1A36, path 336) and 75152 (0x1A35, path 338), st5evtbl 7396 (0x1B0E, path 382).
class 0x33 selector 2: draws params[0] until params[3] == cam frame or g_script_flags[params.u8(0x11)]. The stage-2 van bodies are these

Class 0x33 sub-handler 4, off ScriptedSceneryDispatch33's obj+0x11C switch. A piece of scenery an actor shoves out of its way. Reads the descriptor tail at obj+0x1390: +0x00 the draw slot (stage 1's two are 4196 = komono_7.bin part 0, a chair); +0x04 a shot mesh, and when it is -1 obj+0x124 = obj+0x128 = the f32 at +0x08 (3.5) so the object gets a body sphere instead; +0x0C a script flag that CLEARS obj+0x34 bit 0x8000; +0x0D a script flag that calls ActorDespawn. Bit 0x8000 is the freeze and it is the same bit ColiTestSphereAgainstActors skips on (0x80008000), so a frozen one is not a push target either: the two chairs spawn with descriptor flags 0x8000 set and stage 1 block 1 step 3's set_script_flag 32 is what arms them. While the bit is clear it runs ScriptedPushableApplyPush33, then draws AssetDrawSlot(obj+0x13F0) at obj+0x40..0x48 / obj+0x64..0x6C. L35: Ghidra ends the body at 0x00433C5C, on the MatrixStackPop call, and the real tail runs to 0x00433CD3 -- a second matrix push that writes the transformed origin to obj+0x70..0x78 and then PUSH ESI / CALL 0x00405160 at 0x00433CC6, RegisterForShotTest, which is what puts the object in the per-frame dynamic list a zombie's push can find. The decompilation shows neither, and the xref list of RegisterForShotTest does not name this function.

The move half of ScriptedPushableUpdate33 (class 0x33 selector 4), and it is class 0x30's push arithmetic on a scenery object. If obj+0x138 is non-zero -- the pusher ColiTestSphereAgainstActors recorded there -- it steps obj+0x40/0x44/0x48 by obj+0x13C * 0.1 along obj+0x140..0x148, times 1.8 when the PUSHER's obj+0x34 holds either bit of 0x18000000 (TEST ECX,0x18000000 at 0x00433D11): Committed 0x10000000, a zombie in its strike, or 0x8000000, the sprint bit a spawn record sets and ZombieOnShot raises on every landed shot, clears obj+0x138, and re-resolves against the actors. Then it always resolves against the full collision set at the full hit depth. ScriptedPushableSyncSphere33 re-seats the collision sphere after every one of the three moves. Same fraction (0.1) and same 1.8x multiplier as ZombiePushOutOfWorldAndActors, so an enemy walking into one of these shoves it aside at exactly the speed it would shove another enemy.

Three stores: obj+0x12C = obj+0x40, obj+0x134 = obj+0x48, obj+0x130 = obj+0x44 + obj+0x128 -- the collision-sphere centre from the position, with y raised by the body radius. Called only by ScriptedPushableApplyPush33, once before the push and once after every move it makes, which is why a shoved object's sphere never lags its model. The class-0x33 selector-4 counterpart of ActorUpdateBoundingSphere (FUN_00454AC0) and ThrowerPlaceCollisionSphere (FUN_00449E80).

g_class_handler_pairs class 0x60, and the actor every stage's block 0 step 1 places with spawn_simple just before its wait_script_flag 0xF8. An installer first: if g_GameMode == 3 (boss rush) it ORs 0x20 into DAT_009A5900 (0x004342FA), calls BossModeChapterCardUpdate (FUN_00434920) and writes it into obj+0x00; else if g_app_state == 0x0B it ORs the same bit (0x00434328), calls FUN_00434DA0 and installs that; otherwise it runs the chapter card inline. Both variants clear the bit themselves (0x00434CE7, 0x00434ED6). The card is a two-sub machine on obj+0x1312. Sub 0 (0x00434360) ORs 0x20 into DAT_009A5900, seats the scene light block through FUN_0040E140 with g_scene_index's entry of DAT_009A60CC/D0, calls FUN_0040C2C0(0.3f), runs a per-scene setup arm from the jump table at 0x004348D8 (each fills the eight u16 text slots at 0x007DCBA0..AE), then at 0x004345A4 INCs the sub to 1 and sets obj+0x11C = 0xB4 -- 180 frames -- and falls straight into the sub-1 body. Sub 1 draws the card per scene from the table at 0x004348F0 and every arm falls into the countdown at 0x00434802: a pad skip (g_pad 0x009C9028 bit 2, only once obj+0x11C < 0xA0, or bit 0x20000 unconditionally) forces obj+0x11C = 1; then DEC obj+0x11C, and while it is above 0 the routine returns. At zero it plays the per-scene exit sound (0x18C/0x18D/0x18E through FUN_0041D710), calls FUN_0041D970, sets g_script_flags[0xF8] = 1 at 0x004348C1, clears DAT_009A5900 bit 0x20 and ActorKills itself. That flag write is the whole reason wait_script_flag 0xF8 opens.

The chapter card's update in Boss Mode: ChapterCardInstall installs it instead of the story card when g_GameMode == 3 (MOV [ESI], 0x434920 at 0x00434308). Sub 0 loads texbank scene+0x160, drains the asset jobs and seeds the damage rank from g_initial_damage_rank; sub 1 draws the scene's 5x4 backdrop of 128x128 sprites from 0x0055DD50 until g_script_flags[0x0055DD5C[scene]] is 1; sub 2 frees the bank and clears g_screen_furniture_flags bit 0x20; sub 3 waits for g_boss_engaged and starts the clock (BossModeClockStart); sub 4 reads the clock into 0x009C7060 while g_boss_engaged holds and moves on when it drops; sub 5 blinks the time for 120 frames. The time is drawn from sub 3 on as mm:ss:hh in sprites 0xACF+digit. [proved]

g_class_handler_pairs class 0x61 -- the stage-clear card, placed by spawn_simple 0x0097723C in the last step of every result block and gated by the wait_script_flag 0xFE two instructions later. Reads g_civilians_rescued_by_scene[g_scene_index] and the per-scene tables at 0x0055DF50 / 0x0055E044 / 0x0055E04B, then dispatches on obj+0x1312: sub 0 at 0x00434FB1 calls FUN_0041D3A0(0,0,-1) and FUN_0041CFD0(0x10000003), zeroes g_nFiringGate, ORs 0x10 into DAT_009A5900 and sets obj+0x11C = 0x1A4 -- 420 frames, seven seconds; sub 1 at 0x00435107 advances the sub once obj+0x11C has fallen to 0x78 or below, which is when the score tally at 0x00434F4D starts adding up; every sub then falls into the common tail at 0x00435118, which draws the rescue list and ends DEC obj+0x11C / JG return. At zero it sets g_script_flags[0xFE] = 1 at 0x0043567C, clears DAT_009A5900 bit 0x10 and ActorKills itself. Nothing else in the image writes 0x009C72FE -- a whole-image byte search for the address finds exactly this instruction -- so this actor is the only thing that can open a 0xFE gate.

g_class_handler_pairs class 0x62 -- the result card's companion, placed by spawn_simple 0x00977244 immediately before class 0x61 in the same step. Loads texbank 0x16A (FUN_0041D6D0) and sound 0x7C (FUN_0041D650), then reads g_civilians_rescued_by_scene[g_scene_index] and walks the per-scene rescue list at 0x0055DF50 until a 0xFFFF terminator. Writes no script flag: a whole-image sweep of g_script_flags puts every writer outside 0x00435930..0x00435F20.

Per-frame task started by evt opcode 0x2D (play_dialogue). Draws the subtitle line the countdown is currently on.  Task fields: +0x34 variant id, +0x36 frames remaining, +0x38 line index.      frames -= 1;     if (frames == 0 || g_nEvtSkipFlag || DAT_009A2230) { task_end(); return; }     if (DAT_009C911E != 1) {         id = lines[variant * 4 + line];              // u16[] at 0x005919A8         if (frames < line_rec[id].end_frame) line++;         DrawTextCentred(line_rec[id].x_offset, 384.0, line_rec[id].text);         return;     }     FUN_0041C6D0(rec.sprite, rec.x, rec.y, 1,1,1, 0, 7);  THE SPRITE BRANCH IS DEAD. DAT_009C911E has exactly one writer in the binary (FUN_0040AC60, which stores 2) and the global is BSS, so the == 1 test is never true. The game always draws text, which makes the script's dialogue recoverable: "We're meeting G over there.", "Get him!" and so on.  Lines advance on a countdown, not a timer: end_frame (line record +0x3E) is "frames still remaining when this line gives way", so the last line of a variant stores 0 and holds to the end.  Line record, 0x40 bytes at 0x0058BC68:     +0x00  f32   x_offset    added to the centred position     +0x04  char  text[0x3A]  NUL-terminated ASCII     +0x3E  u16   end_frame  The early return on g_nEvtSkipFlag means a skipped cutscene drops its subtitles -- a third live consumer of the skip flag beyond 0x40/0x41/0x42 and 0x2E.

evt opcode 0x2D, play_dialogue. Picks a line by player configuration, plays its voice and starts the subtitle task.      variant = u16[0x0058B6B8 + (group * 3 + player_cfg) * 2];     if (variant == 0) return;                   /* nothing for this config */     if (g_nEvtSkipFlag || DAT_009A2230) return; /* skipped cutscene */     rec = 0x00589DA8 + variant * 0x10;     if (rec.voice) PlaySoundId(rec.voice);     task = start(DrawDialogueSubtitleTask, 60);     task.variant = variant; task.frames = rec.frames; task.line = 0;  player_cfg is DAT_009C7000: 0 = 1P/player 1, 1 = 1P/player 2, 2 = 2P. Scene states 10 and 11 take the other branch, which always uses configuration 0. The split is real content, not a duplicate: group 5 is "Get him!" for one player and "Get them!" for two.  Record, 0x10 bytes at 0x00589DA8:     +0x00  u16  sprite    only the dead sprite path reads this     +0x02  u16  frames    the whole line's duration     +0x04  f32  x         only the dead sprite path reads these     +0x08  f32  y     +0x0C  u32  voice     PlaySoundId id, or 0  Neither the variant table nor the record table stores a count; the record table is bounded by the variant table that follows it, giving 401 records.

The boss health bar, one frame. Kills itself at once if g_boss_hp_fraction is exactly -1.0 (0x004C4C64). The shown fill +0x40 rises 0.01 a frame (double 0x0055D190) while below the global, clamped to it, with the trail +0x44 pinned to it; otherwise it equals the global. The trail then falls 0.001 a frame (double 0x0055E180), never below the fill. A global of exactly 0.0 starts the blink counter +0x48; from then the bar is hidden when counter % 10 < 5 and kills itself when the counter was 0x78. Draws four sprites of tex/scr_bosmater.bin through DrawScreenSpriteLayered, layer 2: 0xB6 (the empty track, from x - (1 - 2*trail)*144, sx (1 - trail)*18, depth 0x3F804189), 0xB7 (the trail, from x - (1 - 2*fill)*144, sx (trail - fill)*18, depth 0x3F8020C5), 0xB5 (the fill, from x - 144, sx fill*18, depth 1.0) -- all sy 0.8, flags 0x29 -- and 0xB8 (the 256x32 frame at (x, y), 1.2 x 0.8, depth 0x3F80624E, flags 10). The one reader of g_boss_hp_fraction in the image. [proved]

BossHpBarSpawn(x, y): ActorAlloc(BossHpBarUpdate, 0x4C), +0x34 = x and +0x38 = y (the frame's centre in the 640x480 screen), +0x40 = 0 (the shown fill), +0x44 = 1.0 (the trail), +0x48 = 0 (the blink counter), and g_boss_hp_fraction = 1.0. g_class_handler_pairs class 0x63, and the commonest spawn_simple record (0x0097724C), placed at the top of most steps in every stage -- installs CheckCutsceneSkipRequest from the task table at 0x005934E4. The standing task that turns a Start press into a cutscene skip. THIS IS THE LINK that makes the whole skip feature work.      if (g_nEvtSkippableRegion == 0) { task_end(); return; }     if (g_nSkipRequested) {         if (cam_end != cam_frame) cam_end = cam_frame;   // end the move here         g_nSkipRequested = 0;         g_nEvtSkipFlag   = 1;         DAT_009A2230     = 1;         AssetDrainAllJobs();         *task = FinishCutsceneSkip;                      // clears 2230, ends     }  Note what the camera line is NOT: DAT_009A6148 is the end frame and DAT_009A6144 the current one (see CamAdvancePathFrame), so this ends the current camera move where it stands rather than fast-forwarding it to the end of the path. That retires the queued event, which is what lets wait_queued_events_done fall through.  AssetDrainAllJobs is there because the waits that would have covered the streaming are about to be skipped past.  Installed from the task table at 0x005934E4 via InitCutsceneSkipWatcher, so nothing calls it directly. That is why Ghidra had not disassembled this block and why an xref search on g_nEvtSkipFlag appeared to show only writers storing 0 -- which led an earlier revision of these notes to the wrong conclusion that the feature was one assignment short of working. It is not; it ships working.
clears DAT_009A2230 one frame later and ends the task

Draw one line of dialogue text, centred, as a run of glyph sprites.      void DrawTextCentred(float x_offset, float baseline_y, char *text)  Measures the string, then starts at x = 320.0 - len * 5.6 + x_offset and advances 11.2 px per character across the game's 640x480 screen. Callers pass 384.0 as the baseline, i.e. subtitles sit near the bottom.  Lowercase letters get a per-glyph baseline nudge for descenders and x-height:      g          +4     p q y      +5     b i l      +1     f j t      +2     d h k      +0     everything else in a-z  +3  Characters map to sprite ids through the u16 table at 0x0055E054, indexed by character code; '~' is a literal 0x62D. Each glyph is drawn by FUN_0041C6D0 with colour (1.0, 0.8, 0.8).  Sole caller is DrawDialogueSubtitleTask, the per-frame task evt opcode 0x2D starts.

Allocate the boss-name banner: ActorAlloc(BossIntroBannerUpdate, 0x1314), ActorAllocSub(0xE0) into +0x1310, the caller's 0x40-byte record into +0x130C, and the block's step word cleared. The boss-name banner, HOTD2's tarot-card intro. Record: +0 flag, +2 cp_ path, +4 end frame (300), +6 the boss's card slot, +8 card x/y/z, +0x14 the boss card's end x/y, +0x20/+0x30 two name sprites {id, x, y, depth}. Step 1 sets g_camera_driver_held = 1, stashes the camera block's eye/target at +0xC8/+0xD4, lays out eight cards 0.01 apart in z at scale 0.03 (card 0 slot 0x7ED, card 6 the record's slot, the rest 0x7EE). Each card is drawn after FUN_004759C0(yaw), identity, translate, RotateY, scale, AssetDrawSlot. [proved]

Class 0x51's handler -- THE FISH, settled by asset name: its draw slots 0x1156..0x1169 are fish.bin entries 3 to 22 and the death slots 0xB6F/0xB70/0xB71 are entries 0, 1 and 2. Reads the descriptor tail at obj+0x130C. tail+0x0E == 6 means the record is NOT a fish: it is a GROUP HEADER, which clears the four g_water_attack_slots, copies tail+0x00 into g_water_level and ActorKills itself -- seven of the twenty-eight shipped descriptors are these, and they sit at the world origin. Otherwise: obj+0x124 = 2.1, an 0x84-byte ActorAllocSub at obj+0x1310 holding the whole class, both enemy counters up, sub+0x76 = -1, obj+0x120/0x121 = -1, RegisterEnemySlot, sub+0x1C/0x24 = tail+0x00/+0x04 (the per-axis closing speed), FishBeginRise, then tail+0x0C as the entry mode (0 raises sub+0x6A bit 2 and draws solid, 1 zeroes the alpha to fade in), tail+0x0E the sub-type, tail+0x10 the rise frames, tail+0x12 the bob cycles, tail+0x14 the lunge frames and tail+0x08 the bob amplitude. Installs FishUpdate.

Allocates one class-0x51 FISH at a point -- ActorAlloc(FishUpdate, 0x1314) plus an 0x84-byte sub-block -- with a lifetime at sub+0x7E (0 means 0x50) and a sub-type at sub+0x6C, incrementing both enemy counters. REFUSES while ANY of the four dwords at g_water_attack_slots is non-zero, which is what paces a summoning round to one fish at a time. Writes g_water_level = -24.9 itself. Skips FishBeginRise entirely and calls FishClaimSlotAndLunge, so a summoned fish has no rise and no bob. Class 0x14's two summoning rounds are its only callers.

Class 0x51's per-frame routine: g_cur_actor = obj, then FishCheckShot, FishRunState, FishDraw, FishProjectToScreen and FishRegisterForCameraTracking. The shot is checked BEFORE the state runs, so the frame a fish is hit is the first frame of its death state.

What a PLACED class-0x51 fish starts from. Puts the actor back on sub+0x00..0x08, turns sub+0x1C/0x24 (the tail's per-axis speeds) into a velocity toward g_camera_block_eye by scaling them with the UNIT direction, faces it that way (atan(dx/dz) in BAMS), and zeroes the rest of the block into state 0 with a full alpha and the strip at 0x1156..0x1169. Its sub+0x78 = 1 is a default FishInit overwrites one line later.

The class-0x51 leap begins, or it does not. Claims one of the four g_water_attack_slots -- a random index first, then the lowest free one, -1 if all four are taken -- and the index decides the attack permit: slots 0/1 are player 0 and 2/3 player 1 in a two-player game, and in one player it is (g_active_player == 0) ? 0 : 1. The slot is ALSO where the fish leaps to: a point in the camera's own space at x = +/-1.5, z = -6.0, y = 0 (or 1.0 for sub-type 2) less 2.0 again for the odd slots. dx is forced to 1.0 when it is exactly zero. Writes the whole displacement to sub+0x28/0x2C/0x30, the yaw atan(dx/dz) to sub+0x50 and the pitch atan(dz/dy) to sub+0x58, draws sub-type 2's +/-2 sideways swing into sub+0x80, divides the displacement by sub+0x7E into sub+0x1C/0x20/0x24, records the origin at sub+0x10/0x14/0x18, resets the strip and enters state 2.

Class 0x51's whole damage model, and it has no hit points: it fires only in states 0 to 3 with obj+0x34 bit 3 set, so a fish is only ever shot once. 80 points to whichever of bits 1/2 is set, or to rand() & 1 when both are, and g_player_hit_count only for sub-type 0. PlaySoundId(0x716A9) = COMMON\\BLOOD07_16.WAV. Then the fork on sub+0x6A bit 0: NOT submerged goes to state 4 with a 0.4 kick, a velocity directly away from the camera at half the distance and a tumble drawn on both axes; submerged surfaces to g_water_level + 0.04, splashes, drops g_enemies_present and goes to state 5. Both arms end with the hit bit cleared, SpawnFishBloodCloud, obj+0x34 |= 0x10000, one off g_enemies_alive and the enemy slot, and the permit and attack slot released.
Class 0x51's six-arm switch on sub+0x62. State 2 is the only arm with two calls -- FishStateLunge then FishLungeTestBite, in that order, so a fish that arrives this frame bites this frame.

Class 0x51 state 0. Closes on the camera at sub+0x1C/0x24, keeps sub+0x6A bit 0 in step with g_water_level every frame, winds the alpha up by 0.02 toward 1.0, advances the strip, and hands to state 1 once the timer reaches sub+0x7C.

Class 0x51 state 1, the surface ride: y = sin(sub+0x68) * sub+0x44 + sub+0x04, floored at the home height, with the phase stepped 0x333 a frame and reset every 0x50 frames -- each reset counting a cycle into sub+0x7A. The splash is fired on the CROSSING, not on the state: 0.3 coming out of the water, 0.5 going in, only when the bit is about to change. The pitch snaps to 0xE000 on the first frame of each cycle and winds up 0xCC a frame to a 0xFFFF stop. When sub+0x7A reaches sub+0x78 it calls FishClaimSlotAndLunge; on -1 it retires from both counters, releases everything and FishBeginSwimAway(0x3C).

Class 0x51 state 2. The arc is a sine of the STEP over the duration, not of a clock: sub+0x74 is clamped at sub+0x7E - 1 while the timer runs on to twice that, so a fish that has not connected hangs at the top of its leap for a second duration before FishEndLunge takes it. Sub-type 0 rides its velocity in x and z and takes y from one sine; sub-type 1 adds a second sine at twice the rate and six units of amplitude; sub-type 2 leaves x to the sines -- sub+0x28 plus the +/-2 at sub+0x80 -- and steps y and z linearly. Splashes once, at timer 2.

Ends a class-0x51 leap: state 3 with the timer restarted, the camera slot cleared and the attack permit released -- but NOT the attack slot, which FishStateFallBack holds for another 0x20 frames so the next fish cannot leap through the one still coming down.

Class 0x51 state 3. Thirty-two frames of nothing, then the g_water_attack_slots entry goes back; from 0x20 to 0x3F it falls 0.4 a frame at half its lateral speed; past 0x3F it takes one off each enemy counter, clears its g_hit_slots entry and the permit, and ActorDespawns.

Class 0x51 state 4 -- shot above the water. A ballistic arc at 0.03266 a frame with a tumble on sub+0x50/0x58. SUB-TYPE 1 IS THE ONLY ARM THAT ASKS THE WORLD FOR A FLOOR (QueryGroundHeightAt ten units above itself), and g_coli_hit_surface == 0 means the trace found nothing, so that sub-branch is the WATER case and the other is solid ground, which plays COMMON\\ENE_WALK3_16.WAV and pins the corpse. Every other sub-type waits to fall back through g_water_level, or gives up at 0x1900 frames. All routes drop g_enemies_present and enter state 5.

Class 0x51 state 5 -- dead on the water, or on a floor. y = sin(sub+0x40) * sub+0x2C + sub+0x0C with the centre sinking 0.005 a frame, for 300 frames, then ActorDespawn. sub+0x40 is a FLOAT BAMS phase accumulating sub+0x3C and converted by __ftol masked to 16 bits; the decompiler drops that argument. A corpse that landed on solid ground has a rate of zero, so it lies still and still sinks. Fires two surface rings at timer 1 unless sub+0x6A bit 1 says it is on the ground.

Runs beside class 0x51 state 2 every frame. One distance to g_camera_block_eye, three answers: under 8.0 it calls PlayerTakeDamage(obj+0x121, 1, 9) if it holds a permit and ends the lunge either way; over 200.0 it ends the lunge without a bite; between the two, nothing.

Class 0x51's draw. States 2 and 3 and the default share an arm that, when sub+0x6A bit 2 is set and the fish is below g_water_level, draws a FLATTENED SILHOUETTE at the surface instead -- scale (0.4, 0.01, 0.4) at g_water_level + 0.07 -- and otherwise translates, yaws by sub+0x50 and pitches by the lunge progress or by sub+0x58. Bit 2 also picks AssetDrawSlot over AssetDrawSlotWithAlpha(slot, sub+0x48). State 5 half-turns before pitching.

Writes obj+0x70/0x74/0x78 for a class-0x51 fish in states 0, 1, 2 and 3 by transforming its position through the camera matrix at g_camera_blocks + player * 0x1A4. FishDraw writes the same three fields for the other states from the matrix stack.

The way out for a class-0x51 fish that wanted to leap and found all four attack slots taken. Zeroes the timer, puts a frame count in sub+0x7C, sets sub+0x28 = 0.4 as the silhouette scale and installs FishSwimAwayTick. NOTHING EVER REMOVES THE OBJECT: the frame count is never read and the installed update has no despawn.

The update FishBeginSwimAway installs. Holds the fish at sub+0x04, drifts it along sub+0x1C/0x24 and draws -- the surface silhouette at sub+0x28 scale when sub+0x6A bit 2 is set, the model otherwise. No despawn and no state test; see FishBeginSwimAway.
Offers a class-0x51 fish to the camera in states 0, 1 and 2 only: copies its position to obj+0x100 and calls RegisterForCameraTracking.

Allocates a 0x68-byte task running BloodCloudTickInScreenSpace at the dying fish's camera-space point obj+0x70/0x74/0x78 with the slot cursor +0x54 = 0x3A, in g_app_state 6 only. NOT SpawnBloodSpray despite the shared first slot: this one draws with an identity matrix at a fixed point, at scale 0.1. Called once, from FishCheckShot. [proved]

SpawnFishBloodCloud's update: identity, T(+0x38/3C/40), Scale(0.1, or 0.05 with g_wCaptionMode == 1), AssetDrawSlot(+0x54) and +0x54 += 1 -- then, past the no-return MatrixStackPop the decompiler stops at, ActorKill once +0x54 > 0x52 (0x00439E81..0x00439E8D). So twenty-five frames, slots 0x3A..0x52, the last one drawn. [proved]

Allocates a 0x68-byte task running WaterSplashUpdate at (fish.x, g_water_level - 0.4, fish.z) with the slot cursor +0x54 = 0x1339, the caller's scale at +0x58 and kind at +0x64. Not gated on g_app_state. Kind 0 plays COMMON\\SIBUKI3_16.WAV and anything else COMMON\\SIBUKI2_16.WAV -- shibuki, a splash. Called on the surface crossing in state 1 (0.3 out, 0.5 in), at lunge frame 2 (0.6), and on the three deaths that meet water (0.8, kind 1). [proved]

FishSpawnWaterSplash's update: T(+0x38/3C/40), Scale(+0x58), RotY(g_camera_block_yaw_bams), AssetDrawSlot(+0x54) and +0x54 += 1 -- then, past the no-return MatrixStackPop, ActorKill once +0x54 > 0x1356 (0x00439F7D..0x00439F8B). Thirty frames of common.bin 307..336, the same strip OwlWaterSplashFlipbookStep draws. [proved]

Allocates a 0x68-byte task running SurfaceRingDrawAndFade at (fish.x, g_water_level - 0.2, fish.z) drawing slot 0xB71 -- fish.bin entry 2 -- with the caller's scale at +0x58, a growth of 0.02 at +0x5C, alpha 1.0 at +0x60 and a count of 0 at +0x66. Silent. Its only callers are FishStateSink's two, on its first frame (0.6 then 0.3) unless the corpse is on solid ground; the deaths that meet water call SpawnRingEffectAtPose instead. [proved]

FishSpawnSurfaceRing's update: T(+0x38/3C/40), Scale(+0x58, 0.2, +0x58), AssetDrawSlotWithAlpha(+0x54, +0x60) -- then, past the no-return MatrixStackPop, +0x58 += +0x5C (0.02), +0x66 += 1, +0x60 -= 1/60 (0x0055DCF4), and ActorKill when +0x66 reaches 60 (0x0043A04D..0x0043A071). Sixty frames, the ring widening while it fades. [proved]

g_class_handler_pairs class 0x11, and the only creature in the game built on frog.bin. Spawned by evt opcode 0x0C, so the descriptor tail arrives at obj+0x130C and there is no obj+0x1390. Seeds three file-scope globals that every routine in the class uses instead of an argument -- 0x009A26A0 = obj, 0x007DCBC4 = obj+0x194 (the skinned model), 0x007DCBCC = obj+0x40 (position/velocity), 0x007DCBC8 = the 0x38-byte sub-block it allocates through ActorAllocSub and parks at obj+0x1310 -- which means only one class-0x11 object can be mid-update at a time. Reads the tail through FrogArmScriptFromDescriptorTail, snaps y to g_ground_plane_y, writes gravity -0.0272222 to obj+0x5C, takes the CHARACTER TYPE from tail+0x00 (0x1B = frog.bin, 15 bones) into obj+0x1F4 and the motion id from tail+0x02 (0x141 in all four shipped spawns) into obj+0x1B4, zeroes the counter part[0] and the cursor part+0x08, builds the skeleton with ActorBuildSkinnedModel, then ORs part+0x64 (obj+0x1F8) with 4 -- the trace-the-floor bit SpawnGroundRingEffect and ActorDrawGroundShadow read (0x0043A170) -- writes the rotation order part+0x68 = 1 (0x0043A17C), copies obj+0x40..0x48 into obj+0x12C..0x134 (the published sphere, at the feet), sets obj+0x124 = g_actor_radius_by_char[0x1B] = 10.0 and obj+0x128 = 3.0, raises g_enemies_present and g_enemies_alive, sets obj+0x121 = 0xFF and installs 0x0043A1E0. Four spawns exist in the whole game, all st1evtbl block 3 step 1. [proved] from the listing 0x0043A080..0x0043A1D0.

Class 0x11's per-frame body; Ghidra had no function here. Re-seeds the four class globals, writes the 2-D camera distance to sub+0x14, then g_frog_bone1_on_entry = translation(g_camera_blocks[g_camera_index] * part+0x130) -- bone 1 as the last draw left it, through this frame's camera -- then runs FrogAwardKillAndEnterDeath, FrogReadNextScriptCommand, g_class11_states[sub+0x04] (the ten-entry table at 0x00592660), FrogIntegrateVelocityAndGravity, FrogDrawAndCycleBone2Slot, ActorRegisterCameraPoint(1.0f) -- 1.0, against 4.0 for a class-0x30 zombie -- and FrogPushOutOfActorCollision. The shot flag is consumed before the state runs and the actor-vs-actor push happens after the draw. [proved]

The class-0x11 shot path, and there is no hit-point arithmetic in it: obj+0x11C is stored 0 as a u16 (obj+0x11E untouched) and never compared, so the first shot that raises obj+0x34 bit 3 kills. Latches obj+0x34 bit 0x4000000, sets sub+0x04 = 8 and sub+0x05 = 0, clears sub+0x00 bit 0, ORs obj+0x34 0x8000 (OR DH,0x80 -- RegisterForShotTest stops filing the corpse, so a shot passes through it; NOT 0x100), calls ChooseHitPlayerOrder (a rand() draw with both players in, and the order is never read here), writes part+0x108 = 0xB91 (bone 1's draw slot, frog.bin 3, the corpse), part+0x198 = 0 (bone 2's slot, the croak run) and part+0x210 = 0 -- records are 0x90 apart from part+0x78, so that is bone 2's record +0x78, its HIT-SPHERE RADIUS, not bone 3's slot: bone 3 keeps its model -- then SpawnBoneHitSprite(obj, 2), after the radius is zero, so the blood sits on the sphere's centre. Picks the shooter from obj+0x34 & 6 (2 -> player 0, 4 -> player 1, else rand() % 2), ScoreAddForPlayer(p, 0x50) -- 80 points -- increments g_player_hit_count at 0x009A5C86 + p*0x130, and plays 0x716A9 = COMMON\BLOOD07_16.WAV. [proved] from the listing 0x0043A2E0..0x0043A3C7.

Class 0x11's integrator. Adds obj+0x4C/0x54/0x50 to obj+0x40/0x48/0x44 in that order, then adds obj+0x5C (-0.0272222) to the y velocity only while the actor is above g_ground_plane_y AND sub+0x00 bit 3 is clear. Bit 3 is raised on the frame FrogStateLeapAtPlayer connects and cleared again when the leap's recovery ends, which is what holds the frog in the air on the player's face.

Class 0x11's draw, plus the thirty-model cycle on bone 2. While sub+0x00 bit 1 is set it steps sub+0x0A and derives a triangle wave sub+0x08 = ping-pong over 0..29 with period 59, raising bit 2 on the wrap; the draw is SetSceneLight / DrawSkinnedModelAndShadow(part, obj+0x40, part+0x78) / RestoreSceneLight; then, unless obj+0x34 bit 0x4000000 is set, bone 2's draw slot at part+0x198 = 0xB94 + sub+0x08, which is exactly frog.bin entries 6..35 and ends where bone 3's default slot 0xBB2 begins. Finally it advances the motion cursor at part+0x00 unless obj+0x34 bit 0x4000 -- the freeze the death state sets on the penultimate frame of clip 0x13F.

Class 0x11's actor-vs-actor separation, run last in FrogUpdate, after the draw and ActorRegisterCameraPoint. The point is WORLD space [proved]: MatrixStackPush(0); MatrixStackSetTopFromArray(g_camera_blocks[g_camera_index]) -- the block's +0x40, view to world; MatrixMultiply(part+0x130) -- bone 1's draw record (record stride 0x90 from part+0x78, matrix at +0x28), which the draw has just stored in view space; MatrixGetTranslation -- the same chain ActorShiftToHoldBone1Position reads as world. So it is bone 1 where this frame's draw put it. Skipped entirely while sub+0x04 == 6 (the leap), which still writes the point. Otherwise ColiTestSphereAgainstActors(point, obj+0x128 = 3.0); on a hit the push is g_coli_hit_depth times a factor of the xz distance d from g_frog_bone1_on_entry (bone 1 as last drawn, through this frame's camera): 0.05 when d < 0.1 ([0x004C4CC8], [0x004C4C88], which jumps past the next multiply), d * 0.3 when d <= 0.6 ([0x0055E1D4], [0x004C4D10]), 0.3 above. The push is added along g_coli_hit_normal_x/z to obj+0x40/0x48 AND to the point; the point goes to obj+0x12C..0x134 either way -- the sphere RegisterForShotTest publishes next frame. [proved]

Reads class 0x11's descriptor tail (obj+0x130C) into the sub-block: state 0, sub+0x18 = tail+0x04 (trigger camera path), sub+0x1C = tail+0x06 (trigger frame), sub+0x20 = 0x141, sub+0x0C = tail+0x0A (the command cursor). sub+0x10 is the half-width of the wedge in front of the camera the frog may hop into: tail+0x08 when nonzero, else the horizontal half-FOV minus 0x200, computed as -0x200 - ftol(atan2(320.0, g_projection_distance_px) * -10430.378). One caller, FrogInit.

Class 0x11's command reader and, once the list ends, its whole AI. Runs every frame but returns unless sub+0x00 bit 0 is set. While *(s16*)sub+0x0C != -1 it takes the opcode's LOW BYTE as the new state and consumes operands: op 0 takes three s16 (camera path, frame, motion id), op 3 takes one s16 and stores it minus obj+0x68 sign-extended as a relative turn, everything else takes none. At the 0xFFFF terminator the cursor stops for good and the autonomous half takes over: inside 50.0 of the camera it goes to state 6 and CLAIMS g_attack_permits[obj+0x121] -- picking the player from g_players_in_play, g_active_player and which permits are free, and falling back to state 7 if the permit is already held -- and outside 50.0 it rolls a new wander state through the eight-entry jump table at 0x0043A970 (states 0/4/7 -> 1; states 1/3 -> rand()%6 giving 7, 4 or 1; states 2/5/6 unchanged), then downgrades state 1 to 5 inside 53.0 and to 2 inside 76.0.

Two instructions: FLD float ptr [0x009C8E58] / RET. It takes three float arguments -- callers push the actor's x, y and z -- and IGNORES all of them, so it is g_ground_plane_y and not a terrain query, whatever the decompiler's signature says (L1). Four callers, all class 0x11: FrogInit, FrogIntegrateVelocityAndGravity, FrogStateLeapAtPlayer and FrogStateDieTumbleAndSink.

g_class11_states[0]. Substate 0 starts the motion in sub+0x20 (0x141 by default, or op 0's third operand) and falls straight through into substate 1's test: g_active_cam_path == sub+0x18 && g_cam_path_frame >= sub+0x1C raises sub+0x00 bit 0 and the reader takes the next command. Note this reads camera block 0's frame at 0x009A6110, while FrogStateHopWithinScreenWedge's aim reads camera block 2's yaw.

g_class11_states[1], [2] and [3] -- the travelling hop, on clip 0x140 with 0x142/0x143 as the 45-degrees-per-pass turns. GHIDRA DROPS 687 BYTES of this function at 0x0043AAC8-0x0043AD76 and 42 more at 0x0043AF04-0x0043AF2D (L37); the five-arm jump table is at 0x0043B0CC. Substate 0: state 3 uses the absolute turn op 3 already stored; states 1 and 2 compute atan2 to the camera in the actor's frame and take a window from the tracked point obj+0x70/0x78: state 1 is [aim-0x1800, aim] when -z*0.25 < x, [aim-0x1800, aim+0x1800] when z*0.25 <= x ([0x004C4D0C] is -0.25), else [aim, aim+0x1800]; state 2 is [aim-0x1800, aim] for x > 0, else [aim, aim+0x1800]. Class 0x13's update. Despawns when g_active_cam_path and g_cam_path_frame both equal the pair the descriptor named, otherwise runs the behaviour at sub+0x00 and draws: MatrixTranslate(obj+0x40), MatrixRotateX(obj+0x64), MatrixRotateZ(obj+0x6C), MatrixRotateY(obj+0x68) (0x0043FEDE, 0x0043FEE7, 0x0043FEF0, 0x0043FEF9) -- each call pre-multiplies the stack top, so a model point sees RotY first and the product is T.Rx.Rz.Ry, a three.js Euler in order XZY (this row said YZX, which render.test.ts's class-0x13 matrix check fails) -- then MatrixScale(sub+0x14) when the scale is not 1.0, and AssetDrawSlot(obj+0x1F4) or AssetDrawSlotWithAlpha when sub+0x18 is not 1.0. It stores the matrix at obj+0x150, writes the world translation to obj+0x70/74/78, sets draw layer 8 and calls RegisterForShotTest. No motion or root-motion routine is called and the Init leaves obj+0x3C = -1, so the three angles reach nothing but this draw. The behaviour is called at 0x0043FEC9, before the draw at 0x0043FEDE, and the model at obj+0x1F4 is drawn nowhere else (routines 0, 1 and 2 draw their wakes and doors under the same angles, each after its own seat) -- so the angles this draw reads are the record's (SpawnFromDescriptorSmall, 0x00408C01..0x00408C10) only where the behaviour writes none: behaviour 0 (NoOpStub) and carrier selector 3 (0x00440AD0), for life. Class 0x15. Spawns N copies of a prop spaced by a delta vector; each samples the wave field for its height.
Reads {amplitude, wavelength, speed} from the descriptor tail on its first tick, installs WaveEvalTravelling, then advances the source's phase by speed every frame.

One travelling source's contribution. phase = (|cos yaw| > 0.5 ? cos(yaw)*p.z : sin(yaw)*p.x) + src.phase; height = cos(2*pi*phase/wavelength) * amplitude. The 65536 scale and the BAMS cosine make it a plain sinusoid truncated to BAMS resolution. FPU args are dropped by the decompiler -- read from the disassembly.
Same setup with WaveEvalCircular, then walks the source itself along its BAMS yaw at speed -- x += sin(yaw)*speed, z += cos(yaw)*speed.
One circular source's contribution. r = hypot(p.x-src.x, p.z-src.z); height = cos(2*pi*r/wavelength) * amplitude * max(0, 1 - r*0.01), so a ripple dies at 100 units.

Class 0x16. Allocates the 0x2C-byte wave-field manager and records the water plane Y from the spawn descriptor's y -- the descriptor's x and z are ignored, so the field is a global plane height, not a placed object.
Class 0x17. Claims one of eight source slots, copies the spawn position and its three orientation words into it, and picks travelling or circular from g_wave_source_kinds by obj+0x11C.
Sums every active source's contribution at a point. This is a height QUERY for floating objects -- the water surface itself is static level geometry and is never displaced by it.

The carried prop's shot response, run by its flight and roll routines after RegisterForShotTest. On obj+0x34 bit 8: counts the hit into g_player_hit_count[shooter] (bits 2/4, else rand()&1) unless DAT_009A5C48, takes one hit point unless bit 0x100, clears 0x0E. At zero a type other than 2 BREAKS -- sub+0x44/0x48 = the type record's s16[0]/s16[1], sub+0x4C/0x50 = 0, update = CarriedPropBreakUpdate, position taken to the world through g_camera_blocks and its yaw/roll from VecAimXAxisYThenZ -- and type 2 is deflected along the ground (0x0044257C, installs 0x00444F70). [proved]

g_prop_behaviours[1]: the prop in the carrier's hands. Then obj+0x70 = the translation (view space) and RegisterForShotTest -- it is shootable in the hands, but nothing here reads the hit bit. [proved]

The carrier died holding it. The held matrix to the world through g_camera_blocks, MatrixToEulerZYX into obj+0x64..0x6C, sub+0x14 = obj+0x70; VecToAngles of the seat's +Z (g_camera_blocks, RotY/RotZ/RotX of the seat) gives a pitch; carrier not HoldingWeapon and pitch < 1: vel = carrier rotation * (0,0,0.15), spin (-0x200, 0, -0x100); else (0,0,-0.15) and (0x200, 0, 0x100). Axis (0,0,1), CarriedPropFallFree, and g_attack_permits[obj+0x121] = 0. [proved]

The carrier let go (sub[4] != 10). Takes the held matrix into the world through g_camera_blocks, MatrixToEulerZYX into obj+0x64..0x6C, obj+0x100 = pos, RegisterForCameraTracking. Mode 4: aims at g_camera_blocks * (x, 0, -15) with x = 0 for one permit or (obj+0x121*2-1)*3 for two, and sets a ballistic launch -- horizontal speed = distance / obj+0x4C (the flight frames), obj+0x5C = obj+0x50 (gravity), vy = dy/frames - frames*gravity*0.5. Mode 5 rotates obj+0x4C..0x54 by the carrier's facing and sets sub+0x38 = (0,0,1); anything else rotates it the same way. Then installs g_prop_behaviours[sub[4]]. [proved]

Where a carried prop sits: the points param_2 along +Y of bones 4 and 7 (obj+0x474 and obj+0x624, each record +0x28), their midpoint into out[0..2], VecAimXAxisYThenZ of the segment into out[4] (ry) and out[5] (rz), and a roll out[3] = the average of the two bones' up-vector angles about the segment plus 0x8000: a7 = trunc(atan2(z,y)*10430.378), a4 = trunc(atan2(z,y)*-10430.378) (0x0055CB20 is the negative constant), d = (-a7 - a4) & 0xFFFF signed, roll = d/2 + a7 + 0x8000. [proved]

g_prop_behaviours[2]; the stage-4 boss's held prop. Nothing here despawns it. [proved]

The prop (obj+0x70, radius obj+0x128) against a bone sphere (param_2+0x68, radius +0x78), all in view space. Inside the sum of radii: LineSphereIntersect along last frame's position (sub+0x14 through g_camera_world_to_view) to this one's, the crossing nearer the previous position becomes obj+0x40 (to the world through g_camera_blocks); the velocity is damped 0.8/0.8/0.7 in the frame facing the sphere centre (VecToAngles, RotX/RotY), a tumble of MatrixRotateAxis(normal x the prop's +X, 0x200) is read back with MatrixToEulerZYX into the spin sub+0x2C..0x34, and the pivot sub+0x20 = the radius-weighted point between the centres, in the prop's own frame. Returns 1; outside, zeroes the pivot and returns 0. [proved]

g_prop_behaviours[4]: the thrown prop. Integrates obj+0x40 by obj+0x4C..0x54 with gravity obj+0x5C, spins by sub+0x2C..0x34, draws under g_camera_world_to_view (0x009A6000), RegisterForCameraTracking, obj+0x70 = view-space pos, RegisterForShotTest, CarriedPropCheckShot. [proved]

g_prop_behaviours[5], stage 2 block 28's pair: pos += vel, vel.y += obj+0x5C; LoadIdentity; RotZ RotY RotX; MatrixRotateAxis(sub+0x38, sub+0x34); RotX(sub+0x2C), read back with MatrixToEulerZYX; CarriedPropGroundContact (PlaySoundId(0x1916A9) on a contact); sub+0x14 = pos; draw under g_camera_world_to_view; RegisterForCameraTracking; RegisterForShotTest; CarriedPropCheckShot. [proved]

The prop after it hit the player: drawn in view space at obj+0x40 (MatrixLoadIdentity), counting sub+0x98 down; under 0x3D it blinks on odd frames; at zero it gives back g_attack_permits[obj+0x121] and despawns. obj+0x100 = g_camera_blocks * pos (world) for RegisterForCameraTracking. No shot test. [proved]

Ground for a falling or rolling prop, in the frame of the ground under it (QueryGroundHeightAt from +100, g_camera_fixed_eye_y over surfaces 5/0x37, tilted to g_coli_hit_normal when there is one). The prop's two ends (+-record+0x14 along its +X, before and after MatrixRotateAxis(sub+0x38, sub+0x34)) and its centre, dropped by record +0x10 and +0x0C; the lowest is the contact. At or under the ground: lift out along the ground's up, velocity friction 0.105 along and x-0.3 across (0x0056453C, 0x0055D2C4), |vy| < 0.02 zeroed, sub+0x2C *= 0.99; an END contact sets the roll axis from that end's motion and sub+0x34 = (s16)atan2(|r.yz|, halfLength) * 0.975, a flat one sub+0x34 *= 0.85; with an end still in the air the axis is turned toward the ground by angle/256; then pos moves cos(seg rz) * sub+0x2C * (end? +0x10 : +0x0C) * 2^-15 along the segment heading. Returns 1 on a contact. The __ftol operands are all visible in the listing (0x00444A1A-0x00444A83). [proved]

The dropped prop: pos += vel, vel.y += gravity, the same tumble as CarriedPropRollAtCamera, CarriedPropGroundContact, sub+0x14 = pos, the draw under g_camera_world_to_view, and RegisterForShotTest + CarriedPropCheckShot only while CarriedPropIsOnScreen. Never despawns itself. [proved]

The broken prop. While g_motion_slots[sub+0x48].state (0x009A37E4 + m*8) is 2 -- the motion resident -- it halves obj+0x6C and draws effect sub+0x44 with 0x0040DD90 at obj+0x40 (RotY, RotZ); then, in every case (L37: Ghidra ends the draw arm at the pop, the bytes fall through at 0x00444F46), sub+0x4C += 1 and ActorDespawn at g_motion_play_length[sub+0x48] - 1. The routine CarriedPropCheckShot's type-2 arm installs (0x0044257C..0x004426D0): pos += vel; vel.y += obj+0x5C (-0.0 after the deflect); the three spins; draw under g_camera_world_to_view; view point -> obj+0x70; ActorDespawn once FUN_004459C0 says it is off screen.
