obj+0x70..0x78 with radius obj+0x124 projected by g_projection_distance_px against a 640x480 screen; 0 behind the camera. [proved]
Foot of the perpendicular from param_1 to the LINE (not segment) through param_2 and param_3, into param_4; its distance is the FPU return Ghidra drops (L1). [proved]

The line through param_3/param_4 against the sphere (param_2, radius param_1): 2 with both crossings in param_5/param_6 when ClosestPointOnLine's distance is below the radius, 1 with the tangent point twice at equality, 0 otherwise. [proved]

Class 0x43's handler and a PLACER, not the actor: it allocates a 0x2A0-byte object running OwlUpdateAndResolveShot and then ActorKills itself. The species is settled twice over -- OwlDrawBodyChain's sixteen AssetDrawSlot ids all resolve to owl.bin, and the death sound is COMMON2\FUKUROU1/2_22.wav, fukurou being Japanese for owl. In a one-player game it keeps only member 0 of subtype 0 and members 0-1 of every other subtype, killing the rest outright. obj+0x228 = descriptor+0x22 - 1 is the member index 0..3 and obj+0x224 = descriptor+0x25 the subtype 0..3; the fourteen shipped spawns are all opcode 0x09 so there is no obj+0x1390 tail. obj+0x1F0 is bams(atan2(camEyeX - x, camEyeZ - z)) frozen at spawn -- the decompiler drops the whole FPU sequence at 0x00445EB3. Subtype 0 starts in state 4, subtype 2 in state 3, subtypes 1 and 3 in state 0. It stamps four words it owns alone: 0x007DCC64 = 0.03 (read by nothing), 0x007DCC68 = 0.06 (the approach-spline rate), 0x007DCC50 and 0x007DCC54 = 0.

Class 0x43's per-frame entry. obj+0x34 bit 3 is the WHOLE damage model -- the class calls no ResolveHit, no DispatchHit and no ActorApplyDamage, and nothing decrements obj+0x11C -- so one bullet kills. NOTHING IN THE CLASS CLEARS BIT 3 (no AND of obj+0x34 with a mask that drops it anywhere in 0x00445DB0..0x00448F00), so a bullet that lands on a subtype-0 owl while it is invulnerable -- until g_cam_path_frame reaches 682.0 (FILD/FCOMP at 0x004460EA), a guard no other subtype has -- is kept, and kills it on the first frame the guard lets it. Death plays FUKUROU1/2 on a rand() coin, pays 80 to the player named by bits 1/2 (a coin flip when both are set) with g_player_hit_count, releases g_class43_attack_token if the owl was in state 4, raises obj+0x34 0x1000000 (0x004461D6: the corpse bit OwlDrawBodyChain reads, NOT the 0x4000000 of ResolveHit), gives back g_enemies_alive and g_enemies_present, raises 0x10000 and clears the camera slot, raises 0x40000000 in states 0 and 2, damps vx/vz by 0.4, sets state 6 and zeroes obj+0x24C, +0x250 and +0x254 (+0x254 has no other reference in the image; +0x26C is not touched), throws the corpse at unit speed along g_camera_block_yaw_bams + 0x8000 (0x009A60D0, read at 0x0044627B and 0x004462B6 -- the block yaw faces the viewer, so this is away from the camera), spin obj+0x1F8 = -768, sheds 40 feathers and swaps obj[0] for OwlCorpseFallAndSettle -- then FALLS THROUGH into the rest of the frame. Then it dispatches g_class43_states[obj+0x220] (0x00592944, 7 entries used; 6 is a bare RET), steers obj+0x68 toward either the velocity heading or the camera depending on the state with an error in -0x7FFF..+0x8000 (a quarter of it in state 1, a tenth otherwise), draws, files the camera point (the circle centre + 4.0 in state 1) with RegisterForCameraTracking, and publishes obj+0x70/74/78 = view(obj+0x40) for RegisterForShotTest -- ShotTestSphere against a radius of 1.5 at obj+0x124 -- on every frame it is alive, the death frame included. It never writes obj+0x12C, so its actor-versus-actor push entry is degenerate. Last it stores g_class43_members[obj+0x228]. [proved]

g_class43_states[0]. The staggered launch: g_class43_launch_delay (0x00592940, s8[4] = {0,1,2,3}, the four bytes immediately before the state table) times 20 frames per member. Member 0 has no delay and goes straight to state 3 as soon as g_class43_attack_token is -1, g_scene_state_major_entered is 2 and a player is in play; members 1-3 play COMMON2\HABATAKI6_16.wav and go to state 2 toward a HARD-CODED holding circle -- (-640, spawnY+10, -950) radius 6.28 dwell 55 for subtype 1, (-415, 140, -2750) radius 6.28 dwell 88 for everything else. obj+0x240 winds BACKWARDS from 44 while waiting and the member-0 exit does not reset it, so a long wait would underflow the wing-beat slot; in the shipped data the gate opens on the first frame.

g_class43_states[1]. Circles obj+0x1DC/1E0/1E4 at radius obj+0x290 (6.28), obj+0x1F4 stepping +0x3E0 for subtype 1 and -0x3E0 otherwise -- 992 BAMS a frame, a lap in about 66. Steering gain 0.014, pitch eased toward 0x1000 at 5% and obj+0x218 toward 0 at 20%. Leaves for state 3 once obj+0x24C passes obj+0x248 (55 or 88) AND g_class43_attack_token is -1 -- that token is what makes the flock attack one at a time.

g_class43_states[3]. Rides a uniform quadratic B-spline through g_class43_approach_curves (0x00564550, s16[4 subtype][4 member][4 point][3], 384 bytes ending exactly where the float pool begins), advancing obj+0x29C by 0x007DCC68 = 0.06 only while inside 4.0 of the current point and stepping the segment at 0.99. Speed capped at 1.5, steering gain ramping 0.003 a frame to 0.15 (subtype 2) or 0.2. At the end of segment 1 subtypes 0/1/3 take g_class43_attack_token and enter state 4 with obj+0x244 = 1, the arm that homes on the camera eye; SUBTYPE 2 INSTEAD COASTS through obj+0x24C and enters with obj+0x244 = 2, so a stage-2 block-14 owl never homes in on its first pass.

g_class43_states[2]. A straight lerp from obj+0x1C4/1C8/1CC to the holding point obj+0x1B8/1BC/1C0 with obj+0x270 climbing 0.0175 a frame to 1.0, plus a 30-frame vertical bob of 0.15. Pitch eases toward 0x3000 when obj+0x3C is set and 0x1000 when it is not, and NOTHING IN THIS CLASS EVER WRITES obj+0x3C, so the target is always 0x1000. Within 5.0 of the holding point it goes to state 1 if obj+0x230 is set (which state 0 always sets on this path) and to state 3 otherwise.

g_class43_states[4], and the strike. GHIDRA'S FUNCTION BODY SKIPS 395 BYTES: the listing jumps 0x004470EC -> 0x0044727C past a MatrixStackPop it has marked no-return, and those bytes are the entire obj+0x244 != 1 trajectory -- a lerp onto the camera with a lateral sway of sin(obj+0x1FC) * obj+0x294 rotated by obj+0x1F0, a 0.2 bob and a bank eased toward sin(obj+0x1FC + 0x4000) * 4096. Read it with disassemble_bytes. The obj+0x244 == 1 arm is a plain lerp onto the camera eye whose rate obj+0x274 accelerates by 0.005 a frame. Inside 5.0 units of the camera eye it calls PlayerTakeDamage(obj+0x121, 1, 9) if that player is in state 5 -- one life, no clip frame, no attack permit but the token -- then picks an escape direction, builds a retreat circle from a four-arm jump table at 0x00447678, sheds 8 feathers, releases the token and goes to state 5.

g_class43_states[5]. Half an orbit of the retreat circle built by state 4, radius 5/7/6/8 by subtype from a jump table at 0x00447C04, obj+0x1F4 stepping obj+0x234 * 0x1F0. Pitches toward the climb angle by an eighth each frame and floors it at 0. Past 0x8800 (or below 0x7800 going the other way) it coasts, damping 0.9, and on the frame obj+0x240 hits 18 it plays COMMON2\HABATAKI6_16.wav, retakes g_class43_attack_token and re-enters state 4 with obj+0x244 = 2. THE LOOP IS 4 -> 5 -> 4 FOR EVER: an owl only leaves through being shot.

Class 0x43's whole renderer -- a hand-built matrix chain, no skeleton and no character type. GHIDRA'S BODY ENDS AT 0x00447D40 on a no-return MatrixStackPop and the routine really runs to 0x00447FA4, so three of its four limb chains are in no decompilation. Sixteen AssetDrawSlot ids, all owl.bin: 0xBBF/0xBC0 the body alive/dead on obj+0x34 bit 0x1000000, 0xBC1 + obj+0x240 the 30-frame beat, 0xBF8 + a 16-frame ping-pong of the global frame counter for the head (frozen at 0 in state 6), 0xBF1/0xBF4/0xBF2 an inner chain, and 0xBF6/0xBBE/0xC08+n and 0xBF5/0xBBD/0xC18+n for the mirrored outer pair whose 15-frame strip is stepped by obj+0x21C during the dive only. 15 pushes against 15 pops on both the live and the dead path.

Class 0x43's target selection, called on every dive launch. Two players (g_players_in_play == 2): a rand() coin into obj+0x121, and an aim offset obj+0x1E8/1EC of length ftol(hypot(obj+0x40 - eye.x, obj+0x48 - eye.z)) * (1/60) ([0x0055CB80], 0x3C888889; the eye is g_camera_block_eye, 0x009A60C0/C8) along g_camera_block_yaw_bams (0x009A60D0, read at 0x00448050 -- NOT g_camera_yaw_bams) + 0xC000 for player 0 or + 0x4000 for player 1, so the two owls come in on opposite sides. It is NOT obj+0x204 / 60 as this row once said: the routine never reads +0x204. One player: obj+0x121 follows g_active_player when that is 0 or 1 and is LEFT ALONE when it is -1 or 2, and the offsets are not written. [proved]

Evaluates g_class43_approach_curves at (obj+0x298, obj+0x29C) into the steering target obj+0x1AC/1B0/1B4. The control-point index is obj+0x298 + (obj+0x228 + obj+0x224*4)*4, so four points per (subtype, member) and two spline segments; the weights come from FUN_0042DFD0, the uniform quadratic B-spline basis ((1-t)^2/2, (1-t)t + 1/2, t^2/2) shared with class 0x40. Every row's first control point is its descriptor's spawn position, which is what says the indexing is not adrift.

Class 0x43's corpse -- installed into obj[0] by OwlUpdateAndResolveShot, so it replaces the update: no state dispatch, no yaw, and it never registers for the camera or the shot test. Settled (obj+0x26C, written 1 by the four landings and by nothing else): y -= 0.03. Falling: vy -= 0.020415, move, obj+0x64 += obj+0x1F8, then obj+0x1F8 = ftol(obj+0x1F8 * 0.95) ([0x0055CB40]); then a switch on obj+0x224 through the jump table at 0x004487B8. 0 (0x00448397), a stairwell: east of x = -720.60425 each of g_class43_corpse_rails picks the segment whose x span holds the corpse and flips vz on the sign of a 2D cross product -- rail 0 on > 0, rail 1 on < 0, so between the rails both fire and cancel and beyond either one turns it back; x < -739 clamps x, zeroes vx/vz and adds 0x600 to the spin; y < 35.91906 lands (y = 35.91906, ring at 35.93906 with obj+0x68, through the tail at 0x0044870C it shares with 2), otherwise the step n + 45 (n = 0 down to -12, one per 6 in x west of -671) bounces it: y onto the step, vx/vz x0.8, vy x-0.4, spin -0x400, COMMON\DAMAGE5_22.WAV. 1 (0x004482BA): the line (-630.6, -923.8) + (-34.89999999999998, -15.5) in doubles; on its positive side y < 49.16 settles with a ring at 49.3, yaw 0xDC00 (0x00448319) and no thud and no clamp; otherwise OwlTestPositionBelowPlane(0, 0.979029, 0.203721, 140.1687) settles with a ring at y - 1, pitch 0x1000, yaw 0xDC00 (0x00448376) and DAMAGE5. 2 (0x004485BA): inside x (-1136, -1113), z (-1121, -1098.7) an eight-step stair n*3.5 - 33 (n up to 8, one per 3.7666 south of -1102.4666) turns the fall (vy x-0.5) every time and bounces it once (obj+0x250: vx/vz x-0.5, spin +0x600, DAMAGE5); y <= -36 anywhere lands (y = -36, ring at -35.98 with obj+0x68, 0x00448710, DAMAGE5). 3 (0x0044872E): y <= -25 settles with OwlSpawnWaterSplashFlipbook (0x00448758) and COMMON\SIBUKI8_16.WAV, no clamp. Every ring is scale 0.75. Then obj+0x24C++, and past 0x78 ActorDespawn instead of the draw (LightsUseSecondarySet, OwlDrawBodyChain, LightsRestoreScene). [proved]
Allocates the 0x80-byte splash the subtype-3 corpse makes when it reaches y = -25, seeded with the corpse's x and z and a fixed y of -25.0.

The splash's update: AssetDrawSlot(0x1339 + n) -- common.bin 307..336 -- one frame per tick, ActorKill past frame 29. Its tail is past a no-return MatrixStackPop and is invisible in the decompilation.
Returns 1 when a*x + b*y + c*z + d <= 0 for the actor's obj+0x40/44/48. Its one caller is the subtype-1 corpse landing, which tests the plane (0, 0.97903, 0.20372, 140.1687).

The one steering primitive every class-0x43 flight state uses: velocity += ((target - position) - velocity) * gain, componentwise, on obj+0x1A0/1A4/1A8 against obj+0x1AC/1B0/1B4. The gain is the whole difference between the states -- 0.003 gliding to the holding point, 0.014 circling, a ramp to 0.15/0.2 on the spline, obj+0x270 * 0.03 in the dive.

Allocates N 0x80-byte feather tasks running OwlFeatherDriftAndDraw, each ActorClearGameFields'd, and draws nine rand() apiece: x, y, z within +-0.5 of the owl (rand()%11 * 0.1 - 0.5), a drift target x and z within +-3 of the feather (rand()%61 * 0.1 - 3.0), a fall rate (rand()&3) * 0.001 - 0.0215, a phase rate rand()%0x201 + 0x200, a roll amplitude rand()%0x801 + 0x2800, and a yaw rand()&0xFFFF -- which, rand() being 0..0x7FFF, is half a turn. OwlUpdateAndResolveShot passes 40 on the death and OwlStateDiveAtCamera 8 on every strike. [proved]

One shed feather: x eases toward its target by 1 / (0x8000 / rate) a frame and z by 1/32; y = base - sin(phase) * 0.5 with the base falling by the fall rate; the roll is amplitude/2 - ftol(amplitude * sin(phase)); phase += rate. Each time the phase passes 0x7FFF it counts a half turn and re-rolls target, base, fall, rate and amplitude (six rand()), and past eight half turns it ActorKills WITHOUT drawing. Draws AssetDrawSlot(0xBF0) -- owl.bin 51 -- under T(x, y, z) RotZ(roll) RotY(yaw) RotX(0x4000) Scale(0.15). [proved]

Allocates the 0x13F4-byte decal the corpse leaves where it settles, with a 120-frame life at obj+0x1330 and the caller's scale at obj+0x1340. Plays STAGE1_SE\BOBBLE1_22.wav when g_scene_index is 0 and STAGE2_SE\BOBBLE1_22.wav otherwise.

The decal's first phase: obj+0x1330 -= 1 (and at zero obj[0] = OwlGroundImpactRingFadeOut, still drawing this frame), then under T(obj+0x40/44/48) RotY(obj+0x68) RotX(obj+0x64) two draws: AssetDrawSlot(0x1A38) -- common.bin 371 -- at Scale(c, 1, c) with c = cos(ftol(n * 136.5333) BAMS) * obj+0x1340 * 3, opening over the 120 frames, and the splash strip 0x15E4 + g_frame_counter % 30 at Scale(s) with s = sin(same) * obj+0x1340, shrinking to nothing. The second draw is past the no-return MatrixStackPop. [proved]

The decal's second phase: obj+0x1330 counts up from 0 and, once it reaches 30, obj+0x1320 counts up too and at 40 the decal ActorKills without drawing. Otherwise AssetDrawSlotWithAlpha(0x1A38, (40 - obj+0x1320) * 0.025) under T(pos) RotY(obj+0x68) RotX(obj+0x64) Scale(3 * obj+0x1340, 1, 3 * obj+0x1340): 29 frames at full alpha, then 39 fading. [proved]

Class 0x20's handler, and an Init. Everything comes from the parameter tail at obj+0x1390: tail+0x00 (s8) the character type into obj+0x1F4, tail+0x01 (s8) a SUB-TYPE into obj+0x130C, tail+0x02/+0x04 (s16) the removal trigger (g_active_cam_path == tail+0x02 and g_cam_path_frame >= tail+0x04), tail+0x06 (s16) the motion into obj+0x1B4 -- and ZERO there means pick one of g_class20_idle_motions (0x005647A4) with rand() & 3. Sub-type 2 also reads four floats at tail+0x08..+0x14 as an x/z BOX. Then ActorBuildSkinnedModel, obj+0x1F8 |= 2, obj+0x194 = rand() (a random phase), obj+0x12EC = OneHitTargetBoneDrawHook, obj+0x120 = 0xFF (no camera slot), obj+0x3C = -1 (no hit slot), and obj+0x124 = g_actor_radius_by_char[type]. In g_app_state 10 it raises obj+0x34 bit 0x8000 INSTEAD of setting the radius, which takes the actor out of the shot test entirely. Installs OneHitTargetUpdate, or OneHitTargetHoldDrawn when g_GameMode == 2 and g_evt_block_index == 0xD.

Class 0x20's per-frame routine, and the whole of what the class is: a skinned actor that DIES TO ANY ONE HIT. It has no hit points -- nothing subtracts from obj+0x11C anywhere in the class -- so the branch on obj+0x34 bit 3 (MarkActorShot's) is the entire damage model. Not shot: the removal test on the tail's cam path and frame, then g_hit_slots[obj+0x3C] = 0 and ActorDespawn. Shot: walk all 16 bone records at obj+0x280 + bone*0x90, and for each whose +0x00 has bit 3, swap in g_pBoneEffectSlots[type][bone][0] when that slot is > 2, spawn the hit sprite through SpawnBoneHitSprite, and score -- bone 2 pays 120 plus g_head_combo_bonus and then adds 10 to it, any other bone pays 10 and ZEROES the combo, both incrementing g_player_hit_count. Then 80 more to the player named by obj+0x34 bits 1/2 (rand() & 1 if neither), obj+0x34 bit 0 cleared, DAT_009A244A incremented, ActorSetMotionBlended(obj+0x194, 988, 0, 5) and on to OneHitTargetPlayDeathClip. obj+0x130C then selects the idle behaviour: 1 spins the yaw by +0x40 or -0x40 BAMS a frame depending on whether the s16 at obj+0x11C is non-zero, 2 clamps x and z into the tail's box and turns 0x100 BAMS away at each wall, 0 does neither. Ends with DrawSkinnedModelAndShadow, obj+0x194 += 1, obj+0x34 bit 3 cleared and RegisterForShotTest when bit 0 is set.

Class 0x20's death state. Draws, steps obj+0x194, and when the play cursor obj+0x19C reaches g_motion_play_length[obj+0x1B4] it UNDOES that step -- so the clip holds its last frame -- sets obj+0x1330 = 0x78 as a 120-frame countdown, calls SpawnGroundRingEffect and goes to OneHitTargetSinkAndDespawn. In g_GameMode 2 block 0xD with DAT_009C72F2 set it diverts to OneHitTargetHoldDrawn instead.

Class 0x20's corpse. Draws (without stepping the motion, so the pose is held), counts obj+0x1330 down from 120 and sinks obj+0x44 by 0.04 a frame; at zero it clears g_hit_slots[obj+0x3C] and calls ActorDespawn. Two seconds of body, sunk 4.8 units.

Class 0x20's held state, reached only in g_GameMode 2 (arcade) block 0xD. It draws the actor and does nothing else -- no motion step, no shot test, no removal -- until DAT_009C72F2 is clear and DAT_009C72F1 set, at which point it clears obj+0x34 bit 3, calls RegisterForShotTest and returns the object to OneHitTargetUpdate. That pair of bytes is written by FUN_00497640/FUN_00497760 and read by ZombieAdvanceMotion, CivilianUpdate and class 0x31 as well; what they are is [open].

Class 0x20's per-bone draw callback, installed at obj+0x12EC by OneHitTargetInit. Switches on the skeleton node's bone index at node+0x14: bones 4, 7, 11 and 14 draw the node's own asset slot and then a second asset from the node's attachment record at node+0x18, translated by that record's three floats; bone 2 draws at DOUBLE SCALE in g_GameMode 1 when DAT_009C88A8 is set; every other bone draws its slot plainly. Renderer-only -- it writes nothing to the actor.

Class 0x31, subtypes 0x16-0x19. Subtype 0x16 is zsass.bin and puts asset slots 0x1FA2 and 0x1F9E into bone 5 and bone 8's draw slots (obj+0x4DC / obj+0x68C) -- the hands, holding an item, in place of the bare-hand parts 0x1F9F and 0x1F9B. Stage 2 block 5 spawns two of them at y=87 with 130 hit points, out of walking reach, so the item is thrown. Seeds obj+0x136C = (s16)obj+0x1316 | 0x180000 -- the descriptor's +0x20 word, so the starting surface, the draw-path bit and the throw-table bit all come from the spawn record -- then derives the stance as 3*bit8 + 2*bit7 + bit6 and writes obj+0x134C = 0.0/1.0/2.0/3.0 for it, raising obj+0x136C bit 5 for a non-ground stance. obj+0x1320 and obj+0x1324 take the two 16-bit outputs of FUN_004016B0, i.e. BAMS angles, not the frame counters other classes keep there. Installs ThrowerDrawBonePart at obj+0x12EC and ThrowerPushOutOfWorld at obj+0x12F0. Its state machine is g_class31_states (0x00592960), 36 entries, dispatched by EnemyThrowerUpdate. Writes obj+0x1FC (model+0x68, the draw's rotation order) = 1 at 0x004496A2 -- c686fc01000001, MOV byte ptr [ESI+0x1fc],1 -- so a class-0x31 actor is drawn T RotX(pitch) RotZ(roll) RotY(yaw) through SkeletonApplyRootMotion's jump table at 0x00411038; nothing else writes that byte on a thrower (its other writers are the owl's states, EnemyZombieInit, ZombieSplitCopyToHalf, PlaceStoryModeSwitch, Class32Init and FUN_0042FCA0). [proved]
Class-0x31 update: a cooldown, a pre-hook, dispatch through g_class31_states, then velocity += acceleration and position += velocity -- this class integrates ballistically, unlike class 0x30.

Class 0x31's per-frame shot drain, run before the state dispatch. Calls DispatchHit -- which is where ResolveHit actually applies the damage -- then walks g_hit_player_order (0x009C8908; it is NOT g_hit_slots), writes the bone index to obj+0x1368, and runs ThrowerShotFeedback. Unless obj+0x34 bit 0x100, hit result 5, or obj+0x136C bit 0x200000 already latched, it releases the attack permit and picks the reaction: on the killing blow state 2 with voice kind 2 for bone 2 else 1; alive and obj+0x34 bit 0x2000 clear, state 0x21 for character type 0x18, state 1 when already in state 7 and on the ground, otherwise state 2 -- and obj+0x136C bit 0x400000 latches a re-entry when a reaction was already running. It never writes obj+0x1364, which is where ZombieOnShot puts the hit result.  Its voice kinds are the same rule as ZombieOnShot's, which is what makes the reading a rule rather than one function's habit: LEA EBP,[EDI*4+0x9a2d88] (&g_shot_bone[p]) at 004499d4, MOV EAX,[EBP] at 00449a70 and CMP EAX,0x2 at 00449a76 -- kind 2 when the shot bone is 2, the head, kind 1 otherwise (00449A7E and 00449A8B). A later note here said 'on the hit result'; the register is the bone pointer, and the start of this row had it right. [proved]

Class 0x31's copy of ActorShotFeedback. Forces g_hit_result to 5 while obj+0x34 bit 0x100 is set, so a downed thrower only ricochets. Result 1 on bone 2 with head model 0x2002 swaps in 0x2015, sets obj+0x136C bits 0x6000000 -- the knocked-down latch that later routes states 1 and 2 into the get-up -- and shouts voice kind 3; otherwise blood at 0.75, 0.5 for result 2, 1.0 for result 3, and nothing at all for result 4. Result 5 spawns sprite 0x51 for character type 0x18 else 3, and clinks 0x1516A9 for type 0x17, 0x0F16A9 for 0x19, 0x1116A9 otherwise.  Its own kind-0 site is 00449D11, unguarded -- the class's shot feedback plays the hurt voice where ZombieOnShot gates the same kind on the result not being 5.

the per-frame collision hook EnemyThrowerInit installs at obj+0x12F0; class 0x30's slot holds ZombiePushOutOfWorldAndActors. Push out of actors (radius*2/3, depth*0.1, x/z only) on bit 0x100000 -- except that unless this is character type 0x18 (zslman, CMP at 0x00449D7F), a found object (g_coli_hit_object) whose obj+0x34 has 0x200000 (TEST at 0x00449D8F) pushes nothing and instead, if obj+0x136C bit 0x20 (off the ground) is up and the state is not 2, sets state 2 (ThrowerStateFallAndLand) sub 0 [proved]; out of the world (full radius, full depth, all three axes) on bit 0x80000, then ThrowerSnapToSurface in states 7 and 8 only. EnemyThrowerInit seeds both bits

class 0x31's ActorUpdateBoundingSphere. obj+0x12C = pos, with y lifted 1.4*radius on the ground, LOWERED 1.4*radius on the ceiling (bit 0x100) and level on a wall (bits 0xC0). Not class 0x30's radius+constant

Class 0x31's copy of ZombieAdvanceMotion: LightsUseSecondarySet, DrawSkinnedModelAndShadow(obj+0x194, obj+0x40, obj+0x20C) -- the draw, and the per-node hook with it -- LightsRestoreScene, then obj+0x194/0x198 += 1 unless obj+0x34 has 0x4000. In g_GameMode 2 the advance also needs 0x009C72F1 == 1 and 0x009C72F2 == 0, and the hook for the next frame is ThrowerDrawBonePart when it advances and ThrowerDrawNodePart when it does not. Called at 0x0044998A, EnemyThrowerUpdate's last act but the camera point. [proved]

Class 0x31's per-bone draw callback, installed into obj+0x12EC by EnemyThrowerInit and called by SkeletonEmitNode once per drawn node. For bone 2, while obj+0x136C has 0x100 or lacks 0x20 and obj+0x34 lacks 0x40000, it first calls ActorAimHeadAtCamera (FUN_00453BE0), which turns bone 2's own draw toward the camera. Character type 0x18: a node on slot 0x1FED or 0x1FF1 while obj+0x136C bit 0x8000000 is up adds 0.025f ([0x004C4CB0]) to obj+0x1384 and, once that is not below 1.0, pins it at 1.0 and drops the bit -- per NODE, so two bare hands grow twice as fast, and 41 f32 additions, not 40, reach 1.0 -- then draws the slot solid, MatrixScale(1, obj+0x1384, 1) and 0x1FF4; the 0x1FF0 arm is unreachable (the guard admits only 0x1FED and 0x1FF1 but the branch compares against 0x1FEE at 0x0044A1A2). Every other type-0x18 node goes to ThrowerDrawPartAlphaIfBlinking with obj+0x138C. Other types: solid while obj+0x34 has 0x4000000; else slot 0x1FB9 under obj+0x136C bit 2 WRITES obj+0x138C with a 120-frame ramp (g_blink_frame_counter % 0x78 times 1/60, folded back from 0x3C) and draws at it, slots 0x2016 and 0x204A draw 0x2017/0x204B + counter % 0x32, and anything else is drawn at obj+0x138C under bit 2 and solid without. [proved]

Draws one part for class 0x31, choosing the engine entry point: FUN_004185E0 when obj+0x136C bit 0 is set AND the global at 0x009A2BB4 (written by EvtOpSetSceneLighting14) is non-zero, else FUN_00418560. Bit 0 is never written by class-0x31 code -- it is seeded from the spawn descriptor's +0x20 word via obj+0x1316, and 18 of the 51 shipped class-0x31 spawns set it. What the alternate entry point does is [open].
As ThrowerDrawPart, but takes a second argument -- the alpha at obj+0x138C at every call site -- and passes it to FUN_00418620 or FUN_004185A0. Same obj+0x136C bit 0 / 0x009A2BB4 selector.

Picks between ThrowerDrawPartWithAlpha and ThrowerDrawPart on obj+0x136C bit 2 (TEST byte ptr [EAX + 0x136c], 0x4 -- f6806c13000004 at 0x0044A285), which is the bit EnemyThrowerInit, ThrowerStateCorpseBlink, ThrowerStateGrabPlayer and ThrowerStateBlinkInThreeHops raise. That bit is what makes obj+0x138C reach the draw at all.

Class 0x31's plain node draw hook, which ThrowerAdvanceMotion installs in g_GameMode 2 on a frame it holds the clock: the part a skeleton node names -- MOVSX EAX, word ptr [arg+0x14] indexes the 0x90-stride table at 0x009CA0A4 and the part id is that record's first dword. Character type 0x18 goes through ThrowerDrawPartAlphaIfBlinking with obj+0x138C; every other type through ThrowerDrawPart. No regrow, no ramp. [proved]

The alternate obj+0x12EC draw hook, installed by EnemyThrowerInit when g_GameMode and DAT_009C88A8 are both 1 (item code 0x15) alongside doubling obj+0x3A4. Draws nothing while DAT_009C88A8 is clear, and wraps ThrowerDrawBonePart in a 2x scale for bone 2 only.

Class 0x31 state 1, the stumble. Clamps obj+0x1368 -- which ThrowerOnShot set to the bone index -- to 15, looks the group up in g_bone_reaction_group and the motion in g_class31_hit_reactions[set], and cross-fades it over 0x14 frames for bones under 9 or hard-sets it for 9 and above, so a leg shot cuts where an arm shot blends. On the clip's last frame it clears obj+0x34 bit 0x40000000 and obj+0x136C bit 0x400000, then goes to state 17 if obj+0x136C bit 0x4000000 is set -- which only a decapitation sets -- and otherwise asks ThrowerPickNextState.

Class 0x31 state 2, the knockdown and the death fall. Sub 0 clears the surface bits, plays g_class31_motion_sets[set][5] -- the airborne clip, 0x3A6 / 0x3A4 / 0x1BC / 0x3A6 by set -- blended on a first entry and hard-rewound on a re-entry (obj+0x136C bit 0x400000, which also counts obj+0x1328 up), and launches ThrowerBeginKnockbackArc while obj+0x1328 is at most 1. Sub 1 rides the arc, freezing the pose at frame 35/20/44/44 by character type, then sets obj+0x5C = -0.05444444. Sub 2 falls until QueryGroundHeightAt(x, y+4.5, z) catches it or obj+0x1338 reaches 0x78, snaps, records the surface in obj+0x1350, bounces with vel.y *= -0.5 and vel.xz *= 0.5, plays effect 0x46 and sound 0x2716A9, and re-bounces while the vertical speed is over 0.15 -- character type 0x16 never re-bounces. Sub 3 splits: alive and not on surface 0x5A, it lies still for (rand()%10+1)*3 frames, plays 0x11B unless it is character 0x17 and gets up through sub 4 into state 0x11 when obj+0x136C bit 0x4000000 is set or ThrowerPickNextState otherwise; dead, or on surface 0x5A, it waits for obj+0x1F1 -- the motion block's clip-ran-out flag -- and goes to state 3 for character 0x16 or ThrowerEnterCorpseState for the rest, spawning effect 0x61 on a 0x5A landing in scene 3 block 4.

Class 0x31 state 3, reached by character type 0x16 only. Sub 0 hard-rewinds the death clip -- 0x11E for 0x16, 0x1BC for 0x17, 0x11D for 0x18 and 0x19 -- then releases the attack permit and the tracking slot in that order; sub 1 waits for obj+0x19C to reach the clip's length minus one and hands to ThrowerEnterCorpseState. Entered from state 2 sub 3 and from ThrowerStateFallToSurface; the switch still covers the other three character types, which is residue.

Class 0x31 state 4, the corpse for every character but 0x18. Sub 0 spawns the ground ring -- from y+5.5 when the frozen clip is 0x3A6, because the ring is placed from the feet -- sets obj+0x1330 to 0x78 and obj+0x34 bit 0x20000; then 120 frames of y -= 0.04 while obj+0x194, the motion play cursor, is pinned to a pose frame drawn from g_class31_corpse_frames_m11d, _m11e, _m1bc or _m3a6 by rand()%17>>4, so the second entry comes up once in seventeen. On the last frame it frees the tracking slot if this was the last enemy present, frees the hit slot and despawns.

Class 0x31 state 5, the corpse for character type 0x18. The same opening as state 4 -- the ground ring, obj+0x1330 = 0x78, obj+0x34 bit 0x20000 and the same pose-frame pin -- but it does not sink: it flickers, setting obj+0x138C to 1.0 and clearing obj+0x136C bit 2 on an even counter and 0.0 with the bit set on an odd one, testing the parity before the decrement so the first frame is visible, then despawns the same way after 120 frames, leaving obj+0x138C at 0 and bit 2 clear. An alpha, read by ThrowerDrawBonePart per bone and by DrawCharacterPartSlot for the waist -- it writes neither obj+0x1F8 nor the part bytes, unlike ZombieStateCorpseBlink. [proved]

Class 0x31's leave-the-field helper, and the routine sitting in state slot 6. Retires from the alive count and then the present count, releases the attack permit, frees the tracking slot and clears obj+0x34 bit 0 before ActorDespawn. Called directly by ThrowerStrikeConnect and ThrowerStateGrabPlayer; nothing anywhere writes 6 to obj+0x1310, so it is never entered as a state.

Class 0x31's next-state router, called from states 7, 1 and 17. Dispatches on the ground distance to the camera: d <= 30 (15 for character type 0x17 standing on surface 0x35) goes to state 8; otherwise the band is 1 for 40 < d <= 50 and 2 everywhere else, and it draws a candidate state from g_class31_action_picks[set][band][(rand()>>4)%10 + (obj+0x1318 & 7)*10] and offers it to ThrowerTryEnterState, latching obj+0x135C and obj+0x136C bit 0x2000 on success and falling back to state 7 on refusal. Band 0 of the table is never reached and the band != 0 test is dead code.

Gate for a proposed class-0x31 state on the current actor; writes obj+0x1310 and obj+0x1312 and returns 1 only if it is legal. Jump table 0x0044B134 indexed by the byte table 0x0044B160 on state - 7 [proved]: 7 always; 8 only when ThrowerTryClaimAttackSlot FAILS and 9 only when it succeeds; 0xC and 0xD refuse character type 0x18 and then need a permit; 0xE and 0xF need obj+0x136C bit 0x20 clear and a successful ThrowerFindWallBeside at -1.0 or +1.0; 0x10 needs bit 0x20 clear and ThrowerFindCeilingAbove; 0x1D and 0x1E only from state 7 and only when ThrowerHasBareHand; 0x1F needs ThrowerBothHandsArmed and then a permit; 0x20 CLAIMS FIRST (0x0044B0E5) and then needs QueryGroundSurfaceAt(x, y + 4.5, z) == 0x35 -- a refusal on the surface keeps the permit; everything else returns 0. Five ThrowerTryClaimAttackSlot call sites.

Class 0x31 state 7, the hub. Plays the idle for the actor's current stance -- the ground picks a walk variant from g_class31_motion_sets, the three wall and ceiling stances have their own clips 0x138, 0x137 and 0x131 (0x20F, 0x20C and 0x212 for character type 0x18) -- turns toward the camera with TurnActorAwayFromPointTestArrival at 0x200 a frame, then offers state 0x1D (0x1E for character 0x18, the re-arm) to ThrowerTryEnterState and otherwise asks ThrowerPickNextState what to do next. An actor off the ground does not turn. Ends by emitting the movement trail with ThrowerEmitGroundDust(0x5A).

Class 0x31 state 8. Idles in the pose its stance names -- 0x129, 0x124 or 0x134 off the ground, the motion set's own idle pair on it -- until ThrowerTryClaimAttackSlot succeeds, then plays sound 0x2416A9 and goes to state 9, the pounce, for character types 0x16, 0x18 and 0x19. Character 0x17 instead goes to state 0x20 when it is standing on surface 0x35 above the camera, else state 0x18.

Copies the current attack's arc motion script into the actor's slot. The stance row is bit6 + 2*(bit7 + 2*bit17) + 3*bit8 of obj+0x136C, the entry is g_class31_melee_attacks[obj+0x130C] + (obj+0x131A + row*4)*0x10, and the pointer at that entry's +0x00 is copied as 12 dwords into g_arc_scripts at 0x009C8AA0 + obj+0x3C*0x30. It LATCHES NOTHING: the stance is used for this one lookup and obj+0x1364 -- the row ThrowerStrikeConnect reads its hit frame through -- is not written. The only store to obj+0x1364 on a thrower in the image is ThrowerStateLeapDown's at 0x0044B6FB; SpawnThrownWeapon's three (0x0045055F, 0x00450591, 0x004505F9) go through ESI, the projectile, and FUN_00450930's through an object it has just allocated. So states 22 and 23, which call this and never leap down first, connect on whatever row obj+0x1364 already holds. [proved]

Class 0x31 states 9, 12 and 13, the pounce: off the roof, or out of the band picks, and into shot. [proved] from the listing, four arms off the jump table at 0x0044B868 (0x0044B68F, 0x0044B759, 0x0044B7A4, 0x0044B835), each of the first three ending INC obj+0x1312 and running on; JA returns for a sub past 3. Sub 0: ThrowerPickLandingPoint(obj, &p); obj+0x68 = g_camera_yaw_bams; ActorArcBeginToWaypoint(obj, &p, &DAT_007DCC70, 1) -- the sentinel makes that routine draw the attack; obj+0x1364 = bit6 + 2*(bit7 + 2*bit17) + 3*bit8 of obj+0x136C, AFTER the arc is begun and BEFORE the surface clear; obj+0x34 |= 0x10000000 (OR at 0x0044B6F0, not 0x20000000); ActorPlayHitVoice(obj, 3) when the head's draw record obj+0x32C is 0x2002; type != 0x18: obj+0x136C &= 0xfffff61f (0x9E0: 0x800 and the surface bits, NOT 0x200); type 0x18: obj+0x136C &= ~0x800 and obj+0x13D8..E0 = obj+0x40..48, the spot it leaves from. Sub 1: ThrowerStrikeConnect unless obj+0x136C & 0x800 or type 0x18; if ActorArcStep(obj, 1) == 1 return; obj+0x136C &= 0xffe7ffff (both collision bits down). Sub 2: ThrowerStrikeConnect unless 0x800; re-snap obj+0x40.. to ThrowerPickLandingPoint unless g_GameMode is 2 with g_script_flags[0xF2] (0x009C72F2) up; return while obj+0x19C < g_motion_play_length[obj+0x1B4] - 2. Sub 3: obj+0x136C &= ~0x800; obj+0x34 &= ~0x10000000; state 10, sub 0.

Class 0x31 state 10, the leap back out of the player's face after a pounce. [proved] from the listing; Ghidra cuts sub 0 at the MatrixStackPop at 0x0044BA37 (no-return, L35) and the body runs on. Three arms (SUB/DEC/DEC at 0x0044B890), the first two running on, RET for any other sub. Sub 0: obj+0x34 |= 0x20000000; obj+0x136C |= 0x180000; type 0x17 obj+0x34 |= 0x2000. Type != 0x18: MatrixTranslate(g_camera_eye), MatrixRotateY(g_camera_yaw_bams), x = obj+0x136C & 0x10 ? 5.0 : (1 - 2*(rand() % 2)) * 5.0 ([0x0055D2B4]), p = MatrixTransformPoint(x, 0, 50.0); ColiTraceSegmentAllSets(p.x, obj+0x104 - 1000, p.z, p.x, obj+0x104 + 1000, p.z) ([0x004C49C4] = 1000.0) -- a hit puts g_coli_hit into obj+0x13D8..E0, a miss (p.x, g_camera_fixed_eye_y, p.z). Type 0x18 skips all of it and goes back to obj+0x13D8, where ThrowerStateLeapDown left from. Script: obj+0x131A == 3 and type != 0x18 -> 0x00564AF8; type 0x16 -> 0x005649A8; type 0x17 -> nothing copied (JZ 0x0044BAE7 past the MOVSD, so the local is uninitialised stack); type 0x18 by 3*bit8 + 2*bit7 + bit6 -> 0x00564D68/0x00564DC8/0x00564E28 for 1/2/3, 0x00564D08 otherwise; any other type 0x00564AC8. ActorArcBeginToWaypoint(obj, obj+0x13D8, script, 1). Sub 1: unless obj+0x136C & 0x20, TurnActorAwayFromPoint(obj, obj+0x13D8, obj+0x13E0, -0x100); if ActorArcStep(obj, 1) == 1 return; obj+0x34 &= ~0x20000000; obj+0x1338 = 0; ThrowerReleaseAttackPermit; type != 0x18 SetCurrentActorMotionBlended(g_class31_motion_sets[obj+0x130C][4], 0, 1), type 0x18 ActorSetMotionBlended(0x211/0x20E/0x214 for row 1/2/3, 0x20B otherwise, 0, 5). Sub 2: if ++obj+0x1338 < 0x5A and the 2D distance to g_camera_eye < 50.0 ([0x0055D2AC]) return; return while obj+0x19C < g_motion_play_length[obj+0x1B4] - 2; state 7, sub 0.

Class 0x31 state 11. Sub 0 records the start height in obj+0x1388, sets obj+0x34 bit 0x2000 and plays 0x1BC for character type 0x17 and 0x3A5 for everything else; sub 1 falls under obj+0x5C = -0.05444444 until QueryGroundHeightAt(x, y+1.0, z) catches it, then picks a landing clip by the drop measured against g_coli_hit_y -- over 15 units the same long clip again, between 10 and 15 the short 0x1BA for type 0x17 and 0x3A9 otherwise, under 10 none at all -- and zeroes obj+0x1388 whenever it plays one, which is what lets sub 2 exit at once instead of waiting the fall clip out. Sub 2 goes to state 10 when obj+0x34 bit 0x20000000 is set and state 7 otherwise; a dead actor, or any actor whose landing surface is 0x5A, is killed and routed to state 3 for character 0x16 or ThrowerEnterCorpseState for the rest.

The gate on class-0x31 states 14 and 15. Refuses unless the actor is facing the camera within 0x2000 and obj+0x136C bit 1 is clear, then traces horizontally from a point 60 units to the actor's own left (argument -1.0) or right (+1.0), at the ground height under it plus rand()%20 + 9.0, back to the actor. On a hit it stores a point 4.5 units short of the wall in obj+0x13D8..E0 and returns 1 -- so with no wall there, the actor simply does not go.
The gate on class-0x31 state 16. Traces from 1000 units above the actor in its own frame down to the actor, and on a hit stores the contact point in obj+0x13D8..E0 and returns 1.

Class 0x31 states 14, 15 and 16: the leap onto a wall or the ceiling. ThrowerFindWallBeside / ThrowerFindCeilingAbove have already put the destination in obj+0x13D8..E0; this begins the arc with ActorArcBeginToAtSpeed, installs the state's own three-stage arc motion script (g_class31_arc_to_wall_b for 14, g_class31_arc_to_wall_a for 15, g_class31_arc_to_ceiling for 16), plays sound 0x2416A9, and on arrival sets the stance bit its state id names -- 14 sets 0x80, 15 sets 0x40, 16 sets 0x100 in obj+0x136C -- plus 0x20, off the ground. Those bits are the stance that selects every later motion and attack row. Returns to state 7.

Class 0x31 state 17, and it is the decapitation recovery: only ThrowerShotFeedback's head-model swap sets the obj+0x136C bit 0x4000000 that routes states 1 and 2 here. Sets obj+0x34 bit 0x100 -- the window in which shots ricochet -- plays motion 0x127 with a 5-frame fade for every character type, plays sound 0x1C17A9, and on the last frame clears both that bit and the knocked-down latch before asking ThrowerPickNextState. Character type 0x18 can never reach it, since ThrowerOnShot diverts it to state 0x21; and 0x127 is a szom.bin clip, so character type 0x17 -- the only one on kame.bin's skeleton -- asks here for a clip its own rig does not have. [open]

probes 1000 units in (1500 on the ceiling) to a point 4.5 past the actor and returns the hit itself, with NO standoff. Used by the knockdown bounce. ThrowerSnapToSurface does NOT call this -- see ThrowerFindSurfaceUnderfoot at 0x44C640

Calls ThrowerFindSurfaceUnderfoot and, when it answers, moves the actor onto the contact point. Run every frame by ThrowerPushOutOfWorld but only in states 7 and 8, which is what keeps a wall-clinging actor stuck to its wall while it stands and waits -- and what drops it into state 11 when the wall has gone.

what ThrowerSnapToSurface actually calls -- NOT TraceActorSurfaceContactPoint (0x44C370), which looks identical for its first forty lines. Probes 10 units each side of the actor (15 on the ceiling). On a WALL it re-places the actor 6.5 units off the surface it found, keeping the actor's own y; on floor/ceiling it takes y from the hit and keeps x/z. Misses answer (1000,y,1000) for a wall and -1000 for a ceiling so the range test fails and the actor goes to state 8 or 11

Class 0x31's copy of TryClaimAttackSlot, instruction for instruction (0x0044CA40..0x0044CB97) -- the obj+0x121 = 0xFF it opens with (0x0044CA45), the latch read, the same one-player pick with the same two rand() %% 2 calls and the ActorScreenHalfSign arm, the IsPlayerAttackable void -- except the off-screen latch bit: OR AH, 0x80 at 0x0044CB70, obj+0x136C bit 0x8000 rather than 0x20000. No obj+0x34 write; class 0x31 clears NoCameraTrack nowhere. Neither tests the distance queue, so a thrower may claim from any range. Twelve call sites: ThrowerTryEnterState x5 (0x0044B063 states 0xC/0xD, 0x0044B06B state 9, 0x0044B08D state 8, 0x0044B0BF state 0x1F, 0x0044B0E5 state 0x20), 0x0044B3FB ThrowerStateWaitForPermit, 0x0044E683 ThrowerStateRideObjectPath, 0x0044E6DC ThrowerStateLeapStrike, 0x0044E8CA ThrowerStateDelayedPounce, 0x0044EF33 ThrowerStatePathFollow, 0x0044FB36 ThrowerStateThrow, 0x00450BC0 ThrowerStateStrikeOnTheSpot. [proved]

Where a thrower lands, and it is a place on the **screen** rather than in the world: a pixel offset divided by g_projection_distance_px and unprojected at a fixed depth through g_camera_blocks[g_camera_index] (view to world), so the actor always arrives the same distance in front of the camera however the camera is pointing. The switch is on obj+0x1310, the STATE (MOVSX/SUB 0x16/DEC at 0x0044CBB1): state 0x16 vertical -350px at depth -15.5; state 0x17 vertical -350px at depth -6.0 (MOV [ESP+0x10], 0xc0c00000 at 0x0044CBDA); any other state 390px for character type 0x16 (obj+0x1F4) and 320px otherwise, at -15.5. Sideways +160px when obj+0x121 is 0, -160px when it is 1, 0 otherwise, and 0 whenever g_max_attackers is 1. Out is (side*depth/px, vert*depth/px, depth) transformed. Constants [0x00565E00..0C] = 160, -160, -350, 390; [0x004C49CC] = 320; [0x004C436C] = 0. [proved]

Class 0x31's strike connect, run every frame of an attack state. Tests no range at all. [proved] from the listing. With obj+0x136C bit 0x400 up it reads g_class31_throws[obj+0x130C] entry (s8)obj+0x131A: returns unless obj+0x19C == (s16)entry+8; whiffs when ((obj+0x1318 & 7) & (s16)entry+0xC) == (s16)entry+0xC; then PlayerTakeDamage((s8)obj+0x121, kind, (s16)entry+0xA) -- and raises NO 0x800 on this arm. Otherwise g_class31_melee_attacks[obj+0x130C] entry (s8)obj+0x131A + obj+0x1364*4: fires when obj+0x19C == the entry's hit frame -- an exact compare, CMP EDX, ECX at 0x0044CE9F -- or when that frame is -1 and obj+0x1360 == 4; whiffs when (obj+0x1318 & mask & 7) == mask (so mask 0 always whiffs); PlayerTakeDamage((s8)obj+0x121, kind, the entry's overlay) and obj+0x136C |= 0x800. kind is 1 normally and 0 when obj+0x34 bit 0x2000000 is set, in which case ThrowerLeave follows on either arm. It does NOT test 0x800 itself: ThrowerStateLeapDown tests it before calling, ThrowerStateDelayedPounce and ThrowerStateStrikeOnTheSpot do not, ThrowerStateCloseAndStrike gates on the throw entry's own frame. ThrowerStateWaitForPermit raises 0x400 for character type 0x17 only.

class 0x31's ReleaseAttackSlot. Frees g_attack_permits[obj+0x121] and, if obj+0x136C bit 0x8000 is set, lowers g_attack_committed. THE BIT IS 0x8000, NOT 0x20000: FUN_00456520 is the class-0x30 twin and tests 0x20000 of the same word. Calling the wrong one leaves the latch up and no enemy in the scene can claim again. Eight class-0x31 call sites
Decrements g_enemies_alive exactly once per actor, guarded by obj+0x136C bit 0x800000.
Decrements g_enemies_present exactly once per actor, guarded by obj+0x136C bit 0x1000000.

class 0x31, called by every fall state. If obj+0x34 bit 0x4000000 or hp<1: untrack from the camera (obj+0x120, NOT the permit) unless this is the last enemy present, then ThrowerRetireFromAliveCount. So g_enemies_alive falls when the actor is knocked off its feet, not when the body settles

Puts the actor into its corpse state: clears obj+0x136C bits 0x180000, sets obj+0x34 bits 0xC001 (bit 14 freezes the motion advance), retires from g_enemies_present unless obj+0x38 bit 0, steps the motion play cursor back one frame, then enters state 5 for character type 0x18 and state 4 otherwise.

where a shot class-0x31 body flies. t = 15.0/|obj+0x70..0x78| * 10.0, clamped at 0, *1.5 if obj+0x34 bit 0x4000000 (already dead); destination is the view-space tracked point with z REDUCED BY t, transformed back through the view-to-world matrix at DAT_009A6040 + block*0x1A4. The camera space has -z in front (ThrowerPickLandingPoint unprojects at -15.5), so z-t throws the body AWAY from the viewer, keeping its screen x and y. Two callers: FUN_0044A450 and ThrowerStateKnockedTumbling

Thunk to ActorSetMotionBlended on the current actor's motion block. Its first argument is read but never used, so it always drives DAT_009A26A0 + 0x194; every caller passes obj+0x194 anyway. The third argument is a start frame inside the clip, not a blend length.

Class 0x31's ground effects, keyed by a code; cdecl, reads g_cur_actor. 0x46 (ThrowerStateFallAndLand's bounce): once per landing on obj+0x136C bit 0x4000, which it sets; the pose is obj+0x40 with pitch/roll from VecAimYAxisZThenX(g_coli_hit_normal) when obj+0x1350 > 0, else zero; SpawnSpriteEffect kind 0x61 face-camera 1 in rain or on surfaces 0x37/5, else kind 0x46 face-camera 2 -- both re-aim at the camera, so the normal's angles are never seen. 0x50 (ActorArcStep's landing, 0x0044D9FC): when obj+0x34 bit 0x10000000 is clear, 0x20000000 set and the type is 0x16..0x19, SpawnSpriteEffect kind 0x61 at obj+0x40 in rain, else SpawnSpriteEffectFromParamsThunk kind 0x4B scaled (0.4, 2.0, 0.2) face-camera 1; every 0x50 then FALLS INTO the 0x5A arm (the else-if returns only for other codes). 0x5A (ThrowerStateStandAndDecide's every exit) and 0x50: for type 0x16 playing g_class31_motion_sets[1][2 + obj+0x34 bit 27] (PTR_DAT_005929F4 is that row, hard-coded) at cursor 0x19 or 0x32, or in any state but 7: moves the trail point obj+0x13E4..EC to obj+0x40 and spawns two SpawnSpriteEffectFromParamsThunk sprites at the midpoint, pitch and yaw from VecToAngles(now - old), yaw +0x4000 and then +0xC000, scale (distance * 0.05981133, 0.8, 0.2), face-camera 0, kind 0x61 if QueryGroundSurfaceAt(mid.x, mid.y + 5, mid.z) is 0x37 or 5 else 0x4B. [proved] from the listing.

Stretches an installed arc motion script onto obj+0x1334 for every character type but 0x19 (ActorArcStep phase 0; it is passed the step as a second argument and reads only the first). slack = script[5] - script[7] + duration -- stage 1's start minus its threshold plus T, NO fades in it (0x0044D606..0x0044D614; the old note gave FitArcScriptByStartFrame's slack here, which subtracts both fades). slack == 0: nothing. slack > 0: while script[6] + script[10] < slack, both fades +1 (0x0044D638); then if slack < their sum, script[6] -= 1 (0x0044D68F) -- so the odd frame lands on stage 2's fade -- and each is clamped at 0x7F (0x0044D6AF, 0x0044D6CF). slack < 0: both fades = 1, then stage 1's start +1 and threshold -1 until fades + threshold - start <= T AND threshold - start <= 1 (0x0044D706..0x0044D754), and if threshold - start < 1 the start comes back 1 (0x0044D772). [proved] from the listing; web/src/game/class31/arc.ts.

(obj, dest, script, step). [proved] from the listing: character type 0x19 ActorArcBeginToAtSpeed(obj+0x40.., dest..), every other type ActorArcBeginTo(obj+0x40.., dest.., step). Then, if script != &DAT_007DCC70 (CMP at 0x0044D7E0), InstallArcMotionScript(script) and obj+0x1360 = 0. With the sentinel it draws the attack itself: obj+0x131A = g_class31_attack_picks[obj+0x130C][(rand() >> 4) % 10 + (obj+0x1318 & 7) * 10] (the byte at *4), overwritten with 3 for character type 0x18 AFTER the draw (0x0044D83B), then ThrowerLoadAttackArcScript(obj) and obj+0x1360 = 0. ThrowerStatePathFollow passes a waypoint's script, ThrowerStateLeapAside a state script, ThrowerStateLeapDown the sentinel.

One frame of an arc begun by ActorArcBegin, with its three-stage motion script. The phase at obj+0x1360 is a five-way jump table (0x0044DA4C) whose arms fall into each other, each incrementing the phase and running on. 0: for types 0x16..0x19 outside state 10 (the leap aside) raise obj+0x34 bit 0x100 -- the actor cannot be shot in the windup -- noting in obj+0x136C bit 0x200 that it was already up; fit the script (FitArcScriptByStartFrame for type 0x19, FitArcScriptByFadeLength otherwise); play stage 0. 1: wait for obj+0x19C >= stage0.until; play stage 1; for 0x16..0x19 drop bit 0x100 unless 0x200 said it was up before, and drop 0x200. 2: ActorArcInterpolate(step) with its result IGNORED, so an arc that lands first waits for the clip; wait for obj+0x19C >= stage1.until; play stage 2; obj+0x1330 -= step, because phase 3 flies the same frame again. 3: wait for ActorArcInterpolate to return 0, then ThrowerEmitGroundDust(0x50). 4: wait for obj+0x19C >= stage2.until; for 0x16..0x19 obj+0x136C |= 0x180000; return 0. A phase past 4 returns 1. Every stage is played by CALL 0x004119a0 directly (0x0044D901, 0x0044D94D, 0x0044D9C9) -- ActorSetMotionBlended(obj+0x194, motion, start, fade), not the SetCurrentActorMotionBlended thunk -- so each stage's start frame is written to obj+0x19C and held there for the fade by SkeletonAdvancePlayCursor, and the thresholds are measured against that held cursor. It returns 0 when the landing clip reaches stage 2's threshold, not when the arc lands. [proved]

Copies a 12-dword three-stage arc motion script -- {s32 motion, s32 start frame, s32 fade, s32 threshold} x 3 -- into g_arc_scripts at 0x009C8AA0, stride 0x30, indexed by the actor's enemy slot obj+0x3C. ActorArcStep plays stage 0 at the start of the arc, stage 1 once the clip frame reaches threshold [3], stage 2 once it reaches [7], and reports the arc finished at [11]. A script is mostly one clip cut into windup, flight and landing, but not always: zslman's aside in stances 1 and 3 (504 then 506, 494 then 496) and set 3's attack 3 in all five stances end on a different clip, and ThrowerStatePathFollow's style-2 script flies on 300 between two stages of 301. Every start and threshold of every script classes 0x30 and 0x31 can install lies inside its own stage's g_motion_play_length, and tools/verify_combat.py check 16 counts them. [proved]

ActorArcBegin whose duration it works out itself: the horizontal distance at a fixed 30 world units per minFrames, where minFrames is 10 when obj+0x136C bit 0x2000000 is set and obj+0x34 bits 0x44000000 are not, else 15 -- so 2.0 or 3.0 units a frame -- clamped up to minFrames. ActorArcBeginToWaypoint uses this instead of ActorArcBeginTo for character type 0x19.

Record a ballistic arc: source in obj+0x13C0/C4/C8, destination in obj+0x13CC/D0/D4, duration in obj+0x1334, frame counter obj+0x1330 reset. ActorArcVelocity then rebuilds the velocity every frame from those.

Begin an arc from the actor's position to a named point. Records src in obj+0x13C0..C8 and dst in obj+0x13CC..D4, zeroes the frame counter, and sets the duration at obj+0x1334 to n - n%step where n = (int)(dist2d * step) -- the **2D** distance, x and z only, y is not in it (FSQRT of dx*dx + dz*dz at 0x0044DC88..0x0044DCB1, FIMUL [ESP+0x20] = the 7th argument at 0x0044DCDD, CDQ/IDIV/SUB at 0x0044DCE8). The duration is in PARAMETER frames: every caller that begins with this steps the arc with ActorArcStep(obj, step), whose ActorArcInterpolate advances obj+0x1330 by step a call, so a leg lasts about dist2d frames -- one unit of ground a frame -- whatever the step; a bigger step only raises the apex, since the parabola is solved over T = dist*step. It is NOT the arc kind (that is obj+0x1354, SelectActorGravityAxis's, read by ActorArcVelocity); an older note here said both. No floor: a leg under one unit gives T = 0 and a 0/0 position in ActorArcInterpolate. Ghidra drops the FPU argument to __ftol here and shows the distance as nothing at all. [proved]

Advances g_cur_actor's ballistic arc by param_1 frames and writes obj+0x40/0x44/0x48. Reads the six-float arc record ActorArcBeginTo laid down -- obj+0x13C0/13C4/13C8 the start, obj+0x13CC/13D0/13D4 the destination -- with obj+0x1330 as the elapsed frame count and obj+0x1334 as the total. Gravity is 0.027222222 on the Y term. Returns 0 once elapsed reaches the total. Only two callers (FUN_0044D780, FUN_0045E010), but classes 0x2D, 0x30, 0x31 and 0x40 all re-implement the same maths on the same offsets, so those offsets are a convention the whole game shares rather than one routine's private state.

ActorArcVelocity (FUN_0044DE80) case 0 with the axis selector taken out: one frame of the shared arc record as a velocity, the parabola on y. Advances obj+0x1330, returns 0 once it has reached obj+0x1334, and computes the velocity for frame t+1 while testing with t. Two callers: ThrowerStateFallAndLand (0x0044A561) and ZombieStateDeathKnockbackArc (0x0045534C).

The arc itself, and it is exact projectile motion: vel.xz = (dst - src)/T flat, and vel.y = -0.027222222*n + (T*T*0.027222222 + 2*dy)/(2*T) for frame n of T. The 0.027222222 is half the 0.05444444 gravity ThrowerStateFallAndLand uses, which is what a discrete `pos += vel; vel -= g` integrator needs. The six cases select which axis carries the arc.
Zeroes the current actor's acceleration (+0x58/5C/60) and then its velocity (+0x4C/50/54).

The fit for character type 0x19, chosen by ActorArcStep's CMP CX,0x19 at 0x0044D8C1; it moves start frames rather than fades. slack = duration - script[10] - script[6] - script[7] + script[5] (0x0044E170..0x0044E17A) and k = __ftol(|slack * 0.5|): a positive slack adds k to both fade lengths and puts the remainder slack - fades on stage 1's, with NO clamp at 0x7F (unlike FitArcScriptByFadeLength); a slack <= 0 advances stage 1's and stage 2's start frames (indices 5 and 9) by k, each clamped at its own threshold, and puts the remainder |slack| - both starts on stage 1's, clamped again -- so a short leap skips into the middle of the clip rather than playing it slowly. Ghidra drops the FPU argument to __ftol; the 0.5 is float ptr 0x004C43AC = 0x3F000000 and the sign flip 0x004C4C64 = -1.0. [proved]

Class 0x31 state 18, an entrance. Plays the walk variant from g_class31_motion_sets[set] chosen by obj+0x34 bit 27, records the start position in obj+0x13C0..C8, and hands to state 7 once the 2D distance travelled reaches the float at descriptor tail +0x04. Stage 2 block 17 step 5 spawns two zstin this way with a distance of 15.0. Raises obj+0x136C bit 0x1000 on entry (OR CH, 0x10 -- 80cd10 at 0x0044E32E) and clears it on the way out (0x0044E3DE). Nothing in the program tests that bit. [open]

Class 0x31 state 19, an entrance. Plays the motion named by the int at descriptor tail +0x04 once -- 296 for every stage-2 zstin that uses it -- then plays sound 0x2916A9, sets obj+0x136C bit 0x80000 and hands to state 7.

Class 0x31 state 20, and how a spawn placed in the air reaches the ground. Sub 0 hands the actor's position and the descriptor's destination (float x,y,z at +0x04/08/0C) and duration (s32 at +0x10) to ActorArcBegin; each frame ActorArcStep integrates the arc, and when it ends the actor drops into state 7 to stand and throw. Stage 2 block 5 spawns two zsass at y = 87 whose descriptors name the street at y = 37, 50 units down over 30 and 35 frames.

Class 0x31 state 21, an entrance no shipped spawn uses and no state can reach -- cut content. Rides object path 0x14F (op_st2 local 7) at g_cam_path_frame for 0xC4 frames; both the slot and the count are immediates, not descriptor fields. Copies position and all three BAMS angles out of CamEvalObjectPath6 -- which returns three floats then three ints, whatever Ghidra's signature says. Sub 0 raises obj+0x34 bit 0x100 (OR AH, 1 at 0x0044E603), and the frame the count runs out lowers it (AND DH, 0xfe at 0x0044E67D) BEFORE claiming an attack permit (0x0044E683), discards the answer and goes to state 9. [proved]

Class 0x31 state 22, an entrance no shipped spawn uses and no state can reach -- dead code. When ThrowerTryClaimAttackSlot fails it forces obj+0x121 from g_active_player -- 1 gives player 1, 2 a coin flip, 0 or -1 player 0 -- and attacks with no permit actually held. Draws obj+0x131A from g_class31_attack_picks, installs the arc script with ThrowerLoadAttackArcScript, and arcs to ThrowerPickLandingPoint over the s32 frame count at descriptor tail +0x04, calling ThrowerStrikeConnect every frame IsPlayerAttackable allows. Class 0x31 state 23, both an entrance and an attack; three subs that fall into each other (SUB EAX,0/JZ, DEC/JZ, DEC/JZ at 0x0044E846; any other sub returns). Sub 0: obj+0x1F8 |= 0x10 (model+0x64 RootMotionY -- its only writer found), ActorSetMotionBlended(obj+0x194, desc+4, 0, 5) called directly (0x0044E879), obj+0x34 |= 0x100 (ShotImmune), obj+0x1330 = desc+8. Sub 1: --obj+0x1330 > 0 returns; else clears both bits, claims with ThrowerTryClaimAttackSlot (0xFF into obj+0x121 on failure), obj+0x34 |= 0x10000000 and obj+0x136C |= 0x20000, draws obj+0x131A from g_class31_attack_picks by (rand() >> 4) % 10 + (obj+0x1318 & 7)*10, ThrowerLoadAttackArcScript, ThrowerPickLandingPoint (its state-0x17 arm: -6.0 deep, -350px), ActorArcBegin from obj+0x40..0x48 to (p.x, g_camera_eye_y, p.z) over desc+8, obj+0x1360 = 0. Sub 2: obj+0x6C = TurnAngleToward(obj+0x6C, 0, 0xCCC); ThrowerStrikeConnect if obj+0x121 != 0xFF; obj+0x34 |= 0x2000 once obj+0x19C > g_class31_melee_attacks[set][attack + stance*4].+4 with the LIVE stance (pounce bit included, 0x0044E9A6..0x0044E9FE), where the connect reads obj+0x1364 instead; ActorArcStep(obj, 1) != 1 clears 0x10000000 and 0x20000 and goes to state 0x19. Stage 2 block 21 step 2 spawns two zstin this way, motion 310 over 45 and 60 frames. [proved]

Class 0x31 state 24. Takes ThrowerPickLandingPoint as its target, draws an attack index, plays the g_class31_throws entry's approach clip until it is within that entry's own distance of the point, then plays its strike clip and calls ThrowerStrikeConnect on the frame the entry names. Ends in state 25.

Class 0x31 state 25, the retreat the two scripted attacks end in. Plays the motion set's landing clip and returns to state 7 once 0x5A frames have passed or the actor is more than 50 units from the camera -- 30 units and no clip test for character type 0x17, which also faces away from its strike anchor while it goes. Releases the permit with ThrowerReleaseAttackPermit on the way out.

Class 0x31 state 26: follow a predefined path -- two shipped spawns, both zsass in stage 2 (block 3's climb, block 14's rooftop route). Jump table 0x0044EF7C; the arms fall into each other. Sub 0 (0x0044EE29) points obj+0x1394 at the waypoint list, which starts at descriptor +0x08 and runs in **16-byte entries** -- {s16 step, s16 style, f32 x, f32 y, f32 z} -- terminated by a step of -1, puts the delay from descriptor +0x04 in obj+0x1330 and raises obj+0x34 bit 0x100 (OR AH,1). Sub 1 (0x0044EE52) decrements it and goes on at <= 0. Sub 2 (0x0044EE70) begins the leg with ActorArcBeginToWaypoint(obj, wp+4, script, wp.step): character type 0x17 takes g_class31_arc_path_c17 (0x00565E28) directly, every other type copies g_class31_arc_path_style1 (0x00565E58) for style 1, _style2 (0x00565E88) for style 2 and _style0 (0x00565EB8) otherwise onto the stack. Sub 3 (0x0044EEE8) runs ActorArcStep(obj, wp.step) -- the same step, so the leg is flown step parameter frames a frame -- and, when it returns 0, plays sound 0x2916A9 and advances the cursor by 0x10. At the terminator it clears obj+0x34 bit 0x100; character type 0x17 goes to state 7 and everything else calls ThrowerTryClaimAttackSlot (result untested) and goes to state 9. [proved]; ported as web/src/game/class31/path.ts.

Class 0x31 state 27, an entrance; four shipped spawns, all zslman in st5evtbl. Six sub-states over an 0x18-byte tail: three floats at +0x04 are the destination camera-relative offset of which only +0x08, the Y, is ever read; s16 +0x10 the camera path frame to drop on, matched against g_cam_path_frame or camera block 2's frame at 0x009A6458; s16 +0x12 the descent frames; s16 +0x14 the hold frames; s8 +0x16 the player to grab, -1 meaning at random. It anchors to the camera every frame, drops on the cue at obj+0x50 = dY/frames, blinks for the first fifteen hold frames, then takes g_attack_permits[p] outright with a two-player fallback, plays 0x1E5 or 0x1E7 at random and damages on obj+0x19C == 30. Subs 2 to 4 ride MatrixTranslate(camera eye) then MatrixRotateY(g_camera_yaw_bams + 0x8000) and write only X and Z; sub 5 tracks the camera by delta through obj+0x137C..0x1384. Sounds 0x2516A9 ENE_WALK2 on the cue frame and again at half the finish clip, 0x2916A9 ENE_WALK6 on landing, 0x1F23A9 LASER_SWORD on as the hold begins and 0x2023A9 LASER_SWORD off on every frame of the solid phase. The last pair is a looping pair from g_looping_se_ids / g_looping_se_stop_ids, so the off id calls SoundStopAllLoopingSe before playing; it still fires once per solid frame, which is the engine's own behaviour and not a dedupe.

Class 0x31 state 28, an entrance; six shipped spawns, all in trnevtbl. The tail is 0x0C bytes: s32 +0x04 the motion, played from rand() modulo its own length with a 4-frame blend; s16 +0x08 the condition -- 0 a frame count in obj+0x1330, 1 g_cam_path_frame, 2 g_script_flags -- and s16 +0x0A the operand. Then it jumps to the signed byte at tail +0x03, which is 7 in every shipped record. Any selector above 2 waits for ever.
True when character 0x16 or 0x18 still holds a weapon in either hand -- the gate on state 0x1F, the throw. Character types 0x17 and 0x19 always fail it, which is why zstin never throws.

Returns the bone index of the hand still holding a weapon: 5 for the right (draw slot obj+0x4DC) or 8 for the left (obj+0x68C), 0 if neither. The armed part ids are 0x1FA2 and 0x1F9E for character type 0x16 and 0x1FF3 and 0x1FEF for 0x18; every other type returns 0 without a test. The rand() parity picks which hand is PREFERRED, not which one throws: parity 0 tests bone 8 then bone 5 and parity 1 tests bone 5 then bone 8, each later test overwriting the earlier, so a bare preferred hand falls through to the other one and only two bare hands give 0. [proved]

True when one of character 0x16's or 0x18's hands has thrown its weapon and the other has not been restored -- the gate on states 0x1D and 0x1E, the re-arm. Character types 0x17 and 0x19 have no weapon and always fail it.

Class 0x31 state 29, character type 0x16's re-arm and its only caller-visible effect. Plays motion **5** -- 0044f7b9 6a05 / 0044f7c6 6a05, SetCurrentActorMotionBlended(obj+0x194, 5, 0, 5), the id and the fade both 5 -- and at the clip's exact MIDPOINT (obj+0x19C == g_motion_play_length[obj+0x1B4] / 2) swaps each bare hand model back to its armed one: obj+0x4DC 0x1F9F -> 0x1FA2 with bone 5's hit sphere at 0x554..0x560 (radius, then centre) and obj+0x1318 &= ~2, and obj+0x68C 0x1F9B -> 0x1F9E with bone 8's at 0x704..0x710 and obj+0x1318 &= ~4. The spheres are g_character_part_tables[0x16] rows 4 and 7, read by name: MOV ECX,[0x004D0384] at 0x0044F822 then [ECX+0x60] and +0x54..+0x5C, and MOV EAX,[0x004D0384] at 0x0044F880 then [EAX+0x9C] and +0x90..+0x98 -- unscaled and with no slot test. Ghidra's pseudocode shows all eight words as float literals (0x3FE00000 ...) because it folds the load through that initialised pointer into the values it points at; they are the table's rows bit for bit (verify_combat check 17). Both tests are sequential, not exclusive, so a zsass that has thrown twice gets both weapons back on one frame. Exits to state 7 at play_length - 1 and clears obj+0x34 bit 0x2000. Those two hand slots are exactly what ThrowerHasBareHand (FUN_0044F720) reads, so this routine failing to run is self-perpetuating: state 7 offers 0x1D to ThrowerTryEnterState BEFORE it asks ThrowerPickNextState, so a thrower whose hands never re-arm re-enters this state every frame and the router -- the only route to state 8 and therefore to any attack at close range -- is never reached.

Class 0x31 state 30. Sub 0 raises obj+0x34 0x2000 (the no-hit-reaction latch), blends to the stance's idle (0x208/0x1FD/0x1F3/0x205) over 5 frames through SetCurrentActorMotionBlended when it is not already playing, zeroes obj+0x1384 and raises obj+0x136C bit 0x8000000, then falls into sub 1, which waits for that bit to clear -- which only ThrowerDrawBonePart does, from the draw. Then it puts back each of character 0x18's weapons that is still bare -- bone 5's draw slot 0x1FF1 becomes 0x1FF3 and bone 8's 0x1FED becomes 0x1FEF, two independent tests, each with its hit sphere restored from PTR_DAT_004D032C -- clears that arm's destroyed-zone bit, and falls into sub 2, which returns to state 7 on the idle's last frame and clears 0x2000. [proved]

Takes an attack permit, picks a hand with ThrowerPickThrowingHand (FUN_0044F630), reads its entry from g_class31_throws[obj+0x130C] at index obj+0x131A<<4, plays the throw clip and calls SpawnThrownWeapon on the frame the entry names. Then hands to state 7. The three sub-states at obj+0x1312 FALL THROUGH into each other -- SUB EAX,0/JZ then DEC EAX/JZ twice at 0x0044FB16..0x0044FB23, each arm ending in INC word [ESI+0x1312] and running straight on -- so a throw can start and release on the same frame. Sub 0 also passes a START CURSOR to ActorSetMotionBlended, not frame zero: PUSH 0x4/PUSH 0x1a (6a04 6a1a) at 0x0044FB87 for every type but 0x18 and PUSH 0x4/PUSH 0x0 (6a04 6a00) at 0x0044FC68 for 0x18, both into the one CALL 0x004119a0 at 0x0044FC74, and FUN_004119A0 writes that third argument into obj+0x19C outright (param_1[2] = param_3; param_1[6] = param_3/2). So a zsass throw is 22 cursor ticks of wind-up against its entry's release frame of 48. Sub 2 is the exit: g_motion_play_length[obj+0x1B4] - 1 <= obj+0x19C plays sound 0x2916A9 and writes obj+0x1310 = 7, obj+0x1312 = 0 (66c786101300000700 at 0x0044FCE1). It re-arms NOTHING and releases NOTHING -- state 7 offers 0x1D (0x1E for type 0x18) to ThrowerTryEnterState before it asks the router, and the permit rides the projectile out of SpawnThrownWeapon; FUN_0044CFB0 has eight call sites and this is not one. Character type 0x18 is diverted out of that path TWICE, by two copies of CMP word ptr [ESI+0x1f4], 0x18 (6683bef401000018). At 0x0044FB7A it picks the CLIP: other types take it from the entry's +0x00 (MOVSX EDX, word ptr [EDI] -- 0fbf17 at 0x0044FB84), 0x18 jumps to 0x0044FB98 and indexes the 32-byte selector table at 0x0044FD1C by handIdx + 10*stance, stance = 3*bit8 + 2*bit7 + bit6 of obj+0x136C, bounded by CMP EAX,0x1f/JA at 0x0044FBC4, out through the nine-entry jump table at 0x0044FCF8 to motions 0x1F7/0x1F6/0x1FC/0x1FB/0x1F2/0x1F1/0x204/0x203 plus a default that plays the actor pointer itself as a motion id. At 0x0044FC83 it picks the RELEASE FRAME: other types compare obj+0x19C against the entry's +0x08 at 0x0044FC8D, 0x18 compares it against obj+0x1350, into which all eight arms have written the constant 0x19 = 25 (c7865013000019000000). That is the SAME word states 2 and 33 use for the landing surface -- one address, two readings, both inside class 0x31. The table at 0x0044FD1C is .text, not .rdata: one xref (the MOV CL at 0x0044FBCF), nine jump targets all inside this function, 24 of its 32 bytes unreachable dense-switch padding, and the clip ids MOV immediates in the arms. So it is NOT exportable as data; it is transcribed in web/src/game/class31/thrower.ts as THROW_BY_STANCE_ZSLMAN and ZSLMAN_RELEASE_FRAME under the .rdata/.text rule in docs/formats/bundle.md. [proved]

Class 0x31 projectile state 0; five subs off the jump table at 0x00450030, each running on into the next. Sub 0: ttl = |target - pos| * [0x00565EE8] (0x3F555555, 0.8333), velocity = difference / ttl, KNIFE2_44 (0x5117A9). Sub 1, the flight: obj+0x68 += obj+0x135C when obj+0x1358 is bone 5, -= otherwise (0x0044FDE1..0x0044FE04) -- the Y term of ThrownWeaponUpdate's draw, at the 0x2400 BAMS a frame SpawnThrownWeapon writes -- then pos += vel, ttl -= 1.0; at ttl <= 0 PlayerTakeDamage(obj+0x121, 1, 6): the hit is TIMED, not tested. Sub 2, the landing (0x0044FE59): obj+0x34 |= 0x400C000, VecToAngles(eye.x - x, 0, eye.z - z) into obj+0x64/+0x68 with obj+0x64 then zeroed; zslman's 0x1FE1/0x1FE2 take a half turn for the other player's blade in a two-permit game and a yaw kick of -(rand()&5) for bone 5, +(rand()&5) otherwise; every other weapon gets obj+0x64 += (1-2*(rand()%2))*(rand()&2)*0x100 and the same kick; obj+0x68 += kick*0x100; obj+0x1330 = 0x1E; KNIFE2_44_OFF (0x5217A9). Sub 3: AimThrownWeapon, pos = target, 0x1E frames. Sub 4: the same and 0x3C frames blinking obj+0x1F8 bit 0 on the counter's parity; at the end CALL 0x0044cfb0 (e88ccfffff at 0x0045001F) gives the permit SpawnThrownWeapon handed over back, then ActorDespawn. [proved]

Class 0x31 projectile state 1, entered when the weapon is shot out of the air; four subs off 0x004503B8, the first three falling through. Sub 0: SpawnSpriteEffect(pos, kind 3 for zsass's 0x1F90/0x1F91 else 0x51, 1, -1), obj+0x34 |= 0x4008000, ThrowerReleaseAttackPermit(obj) -- the permit goes back at once. Sub 1: obj+0x13C0 = the view point obj+0x70 offset (rand()%10+1)*10*(1-2*(rand()%2)) on x and then y, sign drawn before magnitude, at obj+0x78's depth, through g_camera_blocks+0x40; then -- past the MatrixStackPop the decompilation stops at (0x004501D1..0x0045022D) -- obj+0x135C = ftol(obj+0x135C * 1.3 [0x00565EEC] * (1-2*(rand()%2))), obj+0x1330 = 5, KNIFE2_44_OFF (0x5217A9) and BULLET_MET3 (0x1116A9). Sub 2: hang until --obj+0x1330 reaches 0. Sub 3: Vec3Normalize(target - pos) * 1.2 [0x00564708] into the velocity and the step, obj+0x64 -= obj+0x135C for bone 5 and += otherwise (the X term now: a cartwheel), gone at 0xB4 frames or once the pre-step difference is within 1.2 on all three axes. [proved]

The WEAPON's target (ESI is the projectile at its 0x00450750 call and in ThrownWeaponFlyToTarget's subs 3 and 4): p = (0, 0, -4) in camera space with one permit (g_max_attackers == 1), ((1 - 2*obj+0x121) * [0x00565EF0] = -0.6, 0, -4) with two, through g_camera_blocks + idx*0x1A4 + 0x40 into obj+0x13C0..0x13C8. The stores are past the MatrixStackPop the decompilation stops at (0x004504B5..0x004504D0). No height of its own: a pitched camera puts the point off the eye's height. [proved]

Allocates the projectile (ActorAlloc(ThrownWeaponUpdate, 0x13F4), then ActorClearGameFields and ActorClaimHitSlot), switches on the thrower's character type: zsass (0x16) hand 5 -> +0x4DC = 0x1F9F, model 0x1F91, hand 8 -> +0x68C = 0x1F9B, model 0x1F90, obj+0x1364 = 0x600; zslman (0x18) hand 5 -> 0x1FF1 and 0x1FE2, hand 8 -> 0x1FED and 0x1FE1, obj+0x1364 = 0; both zero the bone record's +0x78 (the hit-sphere radius). Marks the arm's destroyed zone and puts the weapon at the hand's bone position through the camera block's +0x40 matrix. EVERYTHING AFTER THE MatrixStackPop AT 0x0045069E IS OUT OF THE DECOMPILATION (L35): obj+0x34 = 0x80000001, obj+0x124 = obj+0x128 = 2.0, the permit hand-off -- MOV AL, [EDI+0x121] (8a8721010000 at 0x004506BB), MOV [ESI+0x121], AL (888621010000 at 0x004506C4), MOV [EDI+0x121], BL (889f21010000 at 0x004506D5) with BL zero from 0x0045050A, so the thrower is left holding 0, NOT -1 -- the off-screen latch obj+0x136C bit 0x8000 moving across (TEST EAX,ECX/JZ at 0x004506DB), obj+0x1F8 = 5, obj+0x1F4 = the thrower's type, obj+0x1390 = the thrower, obj+0x1358 = the hand, obj+0x135C = 0x2400 (c7865c13000000240000 at 0x0045072C -- THE TUMBLE RATE, 50 degrees a frame), obj+0x133C = obj+0x1338 = 4, state and sub zeroed at 0x00450742, AimThrownWeapon(weapon), and obj+0x100 = pos for RegisterForCameraTracking. [proved]

Class 0x31's projectile task. A mark (obj+0x34 bit 8) not already spent (bit 0x4000000) bumps g_player_hit_count[obj+0x34 & 0x10 ? 1 : 0] -- always player 0, since MarkActorShot writes 0x2/0x4 -- and switches to state 1 at sub 0. Then g_thrown_weapon_states[state], and while obj+0x1F8 bit 0 is up the draw: Rz(obj+0x6C) * Ry(obj+0x68) * Rx(obj+0x1364 + obj+0x64) under the camera; the decompilation returns at the MatrixStackPop, but 0x00450840..0x004508BF go on to obj+0x70..0x78 = the view-space position through g_camera_world_to_view, RegisterForShotTest(obj) -- which is what makes a thrown knife shootable, as a whole 2.0 sphere -- and ActorDrawGroundShadowWithSize(obj, 5.0, 5.0). Both paths then run ZslmanBladeEmitAfterimage for a type-0x18 weapon in state 0 sub < 2 or state 1, and in state 0 set obj+0x100 = pos and RegisterForCameraTracking. [proved]

Called by ThrownWeaponUpdate for a weapon whose obj+0x1F4 is 0x18 (zslman) while it is launching or flying (state 0, sub < 2, read after the state ran) or deflected (state 1). DEC obj+0x1338 then JNS (0x0045093B/0x00450942), so the launcher's 4 makes the first afterimage on the FIFTH call and every fifth after, reloading from obj+0x133C. While fewer than 10 are out (obj+0x1368, CMP/JGE at 0x00450948): ActorAlloc(ZslmanBladeAfterimageFade, 0x13F4) + ActorClearGameFields, REP MOVSD of obj+0x40..0x6C (position, velocity, acceleration, the three angles), +0x1390 = the weapon, obj+0x135C and obj+0x1364 copied, life +0x1330 = 15, light +0x1384 = 1.0 fading by +0x1388 = 0x3D888889 (1/15 as an f32) a frame, +0x3C = -1 (no hit slot, and ActorDespawn's clear is gated on +0x38 bit 0x40 first), model obj+0x13F0 -- then 0x1FE1 becomes 0x1FE4 and 0x1FE2 becomes 0x1FE5 (zslman.bin parts 13 and 14, single additive meshes), each at a starting light of 0.75; the second test reads the already-rewritten slot. The afterimage's +0x1368 is the weapon's count as it stood (written, never read) and the weapon's count goes up one. ActorAlloc links it at the tail of the running task's list, so it runs and draws on the frame it is made. Ported in web/src/game/class31/projectile.ts. [proved]

The afterimage ZslmanBladeEmitAfterimage allocates: while --obj+0x1330 >= 0 (JS at 0x00450A48) and the weapon's obj+0x34 bit 0x4000 (raised only by ThrownWeaponFlyToTarget's landing) is clear, light -= step (FLD/FSUB/FSTP f32), and the copied pose is drawn Rz * Ry * Rx(obj+0x1364 + obj+0x64) under SetRenderLightColour(0, 0, light) for 0x1FE1/0x1FE2 or (light, light, light) otherwise -- and since the emitter has already swapped those two models for 0x1FE4/0x1FE5, the blue arm is unreachable: every afterimage is lit grey. It never moves. Fifteen draws take 0.75 below zero, so the last few add nothing. Then, unless the weapon is spent (0x4000000, which both the landing and the shot-down arm raise), the weapon's count obj+0x1368 goes down one, and ActorDespawn. A shot-down blade that despawns leaves its afterimages reading its freed block, whose +0x34 ActorKill does not touch. The light colour is global and is not put back. Ported in web/src/game/class31/projectile.ts. [proved]

Class 0x31 state 32. Plays motion 0x1B8, pins itself to where that clip ended, then loops: claim a permit if it has none, draw an attack index, play its strike clip calling ThrowerStrikeConnect, then the motion set's second idle for 0x78 frames, and strike again. It never leaves the state.

Sets obj+0x1354, the arc kind ActorArcVelocity switches on: 0 floor, 1 ceiling, 2 wall at +X, 3 wall at -X, 4 wall at -Z, 5 wall at +Z. Derived from the cardinal-snapped yaw and obj+0x136C bits 0x40, 0x80 and 0x100, and it agrees with the acceleration ThrowerStateKnockedTumbling writes on the same axis.

Class 0x31 state 33, the shot reaction character type 0x18 takes instead of the stumble. Sub 0 picks the knock clip by stance -- 0x215 ground, 0x1FE and 0x1F4 the two walls, 0x206 ceiling -- fades it over 5 frames on a fresh knock or hard-cuts it on a re-entry (obj+0x136C bit 0x400000, which also skips the velocity clear and counts obj+0x1328 up), launches ThrowerBeginKnockbackArc while obj+0x1328 is under 2, and calls SelectActorGravityAxis. Then it rides the arc and bounces off whichever of the six axes obj+0x1354 names, standing 4.5 units off a wall, negating that axis by -0.5 and halving the other two, playing sound 0x2716A9 each time, until the speed on that axis drops to 0.15 or obj+0x1338 reaches 0x78. Landing waits (rand()%10+1)*3 frames, plays the stance's get-up clip -- 0x216 / 0x1FF / 0x1F5 / 0x207 -- and returns to state 7 with obj+0x133C = 0x14, a 20-frame window in which shots do nothing. A dead actor, or surface 0x5A under it, goes to ThrowerEnterCorpseState instead.

Class 0x31 state 34, an entrance; eight shipped spawns, all zslman in st6evtbl, covering all four surface stances. A three-hop blinking materialisation, not a retreat -- the earlier name ThrowerStateBackAwayThreeUnits was wrong. Called for bone 2 only, by ZombieDrawBonePart (at 0x004534EA) while obj+0x34 bit 0x40000 is clear, and by ThrowerDrawBonePart (at 0x00449FD9) while bit 0x40000 is clear AND (obj+0x136C bit 0x100 is set OR bit 0x20 is clear) -- a thrower on a wall does not aim, one on the ceiling does. [proved]

(pt) -- ActorAimHeadAtCamera's target. pt is {f32 x,y,z; s32 pitch; s32 yaw}; writes VecToAngles(target - pt) into pt+0x0C/+0x10. The target is (g_camera_eye_x, g_camera_eye_y + 15.0, g_camera_eye_z) -- FADD double [0x00565DD8] = 15.0 -- the point EnemyZombieInit and EnemyThrowerInit also seed the angles toward.
