[proved]

Class 0x30's per-frame shot drain, run before the state dispatch -- the mirror of ThrowerOnShot. Gated on obj+0x34 bit 8 (a shot the update has not drained); calls DispatchHit FIRST, so the damage lands either way, and only then refuses on obj+0x34 bit 0x100 (ShotImmune). Per player in g_hit_player_order it writes the hit result to obj+0x1364, clears obj+0x136C bit 0x400, RAISES obj+0x34 bit 0x8000000 -- 00453f17 81c900000008 OR ECX,0x8000000, the same sprint bit ZombieStateAttackRun indexes its motion pair with, so a zombie that has been shot switches to the run of the pair -- and runs ActorShotFeedback. Then obj+0x136C bit 0x80000000 latches the death once; a live actor takes ActorReactToHit plus FUN_0040A6F0(obj,0) unless the result is 5, and a dead one latches 0x80000000, plays the death voice and picks the state: bit 0x4000 (mid-leap) vetoes everything, else sub = 0 and state 9 when the state is 0x34, obj+0x136C bit 0x100000 is set, or the body condition is 5 or 6 -- with obj+0x136C bit 8 raised first when the state is 0x1B or 0x1C and the actor is within 18.0 of obj+0x13CC/0x13D4 -- and state 6 otherwise.  THE DEAD ARM'S VOICE KIND IS THE SHOT BONE, THE LIVE ARM'S THE RESULT. The loop holds two pointers from its head: LEA EBP,[EDI*4+0x9a2d88] (8d2cbd882d9a00 at 00453eee, &g_shot_bone[p]) and LEA EBX,[EDI*4+0x9a58f8] (00453f0d, &g_hit_result[p]). Dead path: 00453f68 MOV EAX,[EBP]; 00453f6e CMP EAX,0x2 -- kind 2 when the shot bone is 2, the head, kind 1 otherwise (EBP is callee-saved across ActorShotFeedback and NoOpStub). Live path: 00454020 MOV EAX,[EBX]; 00454025 CMP EAX,0x5 -- ActorPlayHitVoice(obj, 0) unless the result is 5 (NoEffect). An earlier note here read [EBP] as the hit result and called kind 2 'result 2'; that was the other of the two pointers. The latch test (00453f3b) precedes both arms, so a latched corpse is silent. Kind 2's two ids in g_hit_voice_table are the SAME PAIR as kind 1's, so the only audible difference is the impact -- two head impacts against the five body ones. The two loop-head writes (0x400 cleared at 00453f14, 0x8000000 raised at 00453f17, stored at 00453f24/00453f2a) are made for every landed shot that ShotImmune has not refused, before the latch test. Ported in web/src/game/class30/on_shot.ts and combat/feedback.ts. [proved]

Draws the hit: blood at the bone scaled by g_hit_result, or -- on result 5 -- an impact sprite and a metal ricochet, because the shot did nothing.  It also holds ONE of ActorPlayHitVoice's twenty-three sites, and it is kind 3, not one of the shot kinds: 00454105 loads g_hit_result[player], DECs it and jumps the five-arm table at 0x00454248, and result 1's arm tests 0045411d CMP [ESI*4+0x9a2d88],0x2 (g_shot_bone == the head) and 00454127 CMP [EDI+0x32c],0x1dc2 (bone 2's draw slot is that one head prop) before 00454133 PUSH 0x3 / 00454136 CALL 0x0040a6f0 and then 0045413b PUSH 0x1dc1 / CALL 0x0040a130 to swap the stump in. So the bursting head SHOUTS -- kind 3, the same cry the strike plays -- and kinds 0, 1 and 2 are NOT played from here at all: they are ZombieOnShot's (00453F7A, 0045402D) and ThrowerOnShot's (00449A7E, 00449A8B) plus ThrowerShotFeedback's unguarded 00449D11.

Derives obj+0x130C, the body condition, from which parts are gone, and is ActorShotFeedback's (FUN_00454050) only caller -- the sibling of ActorBodyConditionFromHands (0x00455920), which runs from the hub state instead. Switches on obj+0x1F4 and counts how many of the two hand slots (obj+0x4DC left, obj+0x68C right) still hold their authored prop: type 1 wants 0x1BA9/0x1BA5, type 2 wants 0x1BD2/0x1BCC, types 0x13/0x14 want 0x1ECE/0x1ECA or 0x1EF9/0x1EF5, type 0xE wants 0x1E55; none left means condition 0, and for type 2 one armed hand gives 1 and two gives 2. For TYPE 2 with NEITHER hand armed it also calls ZombieReleaseWeaponLoopSe (FUN_00456600): shoot the chainsaw out of its hands and the looping CHAIN_SAW_22 stops, which is the second proof that that loop belongs to the weapon and not to the actor's voice. Types 0x13 and 0x14 refuse to touch conditions 7 and 5, as 0x00455920 does. Last, obj+0x136C bit 0x40 with condition 0 and both obj+0x1318 bits 1 and 2 (both arm zones destroyed) forces condition 5, which ChooseDeathMotion reads, and clears the bit.

Records the last-hit zone in obj+0x1319 (1 torso, 2 head) and decides whether the hit interrupts what the actor is doing. Results 1 and 3 always react; 2 and 5 only for character types 3 and 0x12. AND IT IS THE ONE PLACE IN THE IMAGE THAT TESTS A CHARACTER TYPE AGAINST 0x0A: result 1 on character type 10 (znjoe) in zone 1, with obj+0x34 bit 0x400 still clear, raises 0x4000400 as a once-only latch, pays ScoreAddForPlayer(player, 0x50), records the shooter at obj+0x131C and drops the actor into STATE 0x19 sub 0 -- ZombieStateReleaseBodyCreature -- instead of staggering. Result 4 with zone 1 or 9 calls FUN_0045D9F0 instead.

The stumble. g_pHitReactionMotions[char][obj+0x130C][g_bone_reaction_group[bone]] cross-faded onto track 1 -- or hard-set with no fade when the bone is 9 or above, the pelvis and legs. It opens with two refusals and the second is the one that matters: 004544cc TEST EDX,EDX / JZ (bone 0) and then 004544d8 f7463400200010 TEST dword ptr [ESI+0x34], 0x10002000 / JNZ -- so an actor holding bit 0x2000 or bit 0x10000000 plays NO reaction at all. 0x2000 is the no-hit-reaction latch: eight routines raise it while something else owns the body (ZombieStateEmerge 0x00458532 OR DH,0x21, ZombieStateDelayedLeap, ZombieStateArcScriptedEntrance, ThrowerStateFallToSurface, ZombieApplyScriptMode's 0x2400, and this routine's own alt arm at 004545f5 OR CH,0x20) and each clears it on the way out. ThrowerOnShot is the only other reader -- 00449a95 f6c420 TEST AH,0x20 / JNZ skips the stumble, the knockdown and the tumble -- so the bit is read in exactly two places and both refuse a reaction.

Runs every frame from EnemyZombieUpdate while obj+0x34 bit 0x40000000 is up (a hit reaction is playing) and takes it back down. obj+0x136C bit 0x1000 marks the overlay track (motion obj+0x1B8, cursor obj+0x1A0) as busy and bit 0x2000 the base track (obj+0x1B4 / obj+0x19C); each is cleared when its own byte flag says so (obj+0x1CA == 0 for the overlay, obj+0x1F1 != 0 for the base -- [open] what those two bytes are) or -- unless obj+0x1364 == 3 -- once the cursor has passed a QUARTER of g_motion_play_length for that clip. When obj+0x136C & 0x3000 is zero it clears obj+0x34 bit 0x40000000. So those two bits, not a timer, are what ends a stumble.

Start a motion unless obj+0x136C bit 0x2000 holds the current one, the motion is already playing, or bit 0x1000 asks for the track to be stopped instead. The states call this rather than ActorSetMotion so a reaction in progress is not cut off.

Runs every frame from EnemyZombieUpdate. When obj+0x136C bits 0x100 AND 0x200 are both set and obj+0x34 & 0x50000000 is clear, cross-fades onto track 1 (FUN_00411B20, layer 1, fade 5) the motion at PTR_PTR_00592CBC[charType][obj+0x130C] + 0x10 + (s8)obj+0x1319 * 4 -- the row slot indexed by the LAST-HIT ZONE. If that clip is already on obj+0x1B8 and obj+0x1CA != 0 it instead waits for the base cursor obj+0x19C to reach half of g_motion_play_length[obj+0x1B4] and then clears obj+0x34 bit 0x2000. This closes the [open] on globals.tsv's 0x00592CBC row: the gate is 0x100 AND 0x200 together, not 0x100 alone.

Class 0x30's post-state motion step: draws the skinned model and then advances the motion frame counters at obj+0x194 and obj+0x198. Gated off by obj+0x34 bit 0x4000, which is how a state freezes a pose -- the gate is on the counters only, so the model is still drawn, but root motion is a frame-to-frame delta and a frozen counter therefore also stops the actor moving. ZombieStateMotionCue21 is the only thing that clears the bit for a spawn record that sets it. In g_GameMode 2 the advance additionally needs DAT_009c72f1 == 1 and DAT_009c72f3 == 0, and swaps the hook at obj+0x12EC between FUN_004534A0 and LAB_00453B30.

The per-frame hook EnemyZombieInit installs at obj+0x12F0 (00452E4A). NOT called by EnemyZombieUpdate directly: it is model+0x115C (obj+0x194 + 0x115C), called by SkeletonApplyRootMotion at 0x00410E93 inside ZombieAdvanceMotion's draw, after the frame's root motion and before the nodes -- so after the state and the velocity, and before RegisterForDistanceRank and ActorRegisterCameraPoint, which publishes the sphere this leaves. Every update, no visibility gate. In order: clear obj+0x136C 0x800000; ActorUpdateBoundingSphere; if obj+0x136C & 0x40000000 { if obj+0x138 (the recorded pusher) { f = obj+0x13C * 0.1 (0x004C4CC8), *1.8 (0x0055DD48) if the PUSHER's obj+0x34 & 0x18000000; obj+0x40..0x48 += f * obj+0x140..0x148, all three axes; sphere; obj+0x138 = 0 } if ColiTestSphereAgainstActors(obj+0x12C, obj+0x128) { f = g_coli_hit_depth * 0.1, *1.8 if THIS obj+0x34 & 0x18000000; x and z only, the normal not renormalised; raise 0x800000; sphere } } if obj+0x136C & 0x20000000 and ColiTestSphereAgainstFullSet(obj+0x12C, obj+0x128): += normal * depth on all three axes, raise 0x800000, sphere; unless obj+0x34 & 0x20000 ActorSnapToGroundHeight; sphere; DEC obj+0x1338 and when it goes negative with 0x800000 up, reset it to 0x3C and flip obj+0x136C 0x400000 (ZombieStateBackOff's turn). 0x18000000 is Committed (0x10000000, ZombieStateStrike) | 0x8000000, the spawn's sprint bit (ZOMBIE_SPRINTS, which ZombieStateAttackRun reads). Neither is the airborne bit 0x20000. [proved]

Rebuilds the actor's body sphere each frame: centre (x, y + obj+0x128 + 1, z) into obj+0x12C/130/134, with obj+0x124 -- g_actor_radius_by_char -- as the radius. The +1 becomes +0.5 when obj+0x136C bit 0x2000000 is set. That centre is what RegisterForShotTest publishes into the dynamic list, so it is read by the gunshot test, by the frustum test at FUN_0045CA60 AND -- via FUN_00405360's copy to 0x005A30A0 -- by ColiTestSphereAgainstActors. An earlier note here said the last of those was not a reader; it is.
Called by ZombiePushOutOfWorldAndActors unless obj+0x34 bit 0x20000 (airborne) is set.

Class 0x30 state 11, the drop. Where ActorSnapToGroundHeight sends an actor more than ten units above the floor that carries obj+0x136C bit 0x4000000. Gravity -0.16333 on obj+0x50, or -0.08167 with clip 0x41D for body condition 4, which bounces at -0.25 of the impact speed until it is under 0.15. Probes the ground at obj+0x104, the TRACKED point, not the feet. A live actor plays 0x3BA from frame 15 on landing; then state 1.

Class 0x30 state 6. sub 0 chooses the death motion; sub 1 raises obj+0x34 bits 0x22000, sets obj+0x136C 0x60000000, plays the death voice (FUN_00456600, which also counts down DAT_009C8A74) and runs ZombieReleasePermitAndUntrack (FUN_004565A0) -- so the permit and the commit latch are freed on death, by the state machine, not by the shot. sub 2 waits for the clip: at g_motion_play_length - 1 it hands to FUN_00456740, or to state 12 when obj+0x34 bit 0x1000000 is set.

The pose pin both class-0x30 corpse states call every frame: writes obj+0x194 -- the base track's frame counter -- from a table chosen by obj+0x1B4, picking between each table's two entries with rand() %% 17 >> 4, so the second comes up once in seventeen. DAT_0059301C is the general table for the eight directional deaths 0x3D9..0x3E0; the special cases are DAT_0059305C (clip 0x3F8), DAT_00593064 (0x1DF), DAT_0059306C (0x41A), DAT_00593074 (0x404) and DAT_0059307C (0x3F7). The class-0x31 twin is ThrowerCorpsePoseFrame's table at 0x00592AC0.

Class 0x30 state 7, the corpse. Sub 0 spawns the ground ring effect, clears obj+0x136C bits 0x20000000 and 0x200 (AND EDX, 0xdffffdff -- NOT bit 0x100, whose only clue this instruction used to be), raises obj+0x34 bits 0xA0000 (Airborne, so the ground snap lets it sink, and 0x80000 which FUN_0040A590 reads before it draws the ground decal), arms obj+0x1330 = 0x78 and stashes the spawn yaw obj+0x68 at obj+0x1350. Then each frame: the timer down one, obj+0x44 down 0.04, and the pose pin FUN_00454E00. At zero it raises obj+0x34 bit 0x10000, zeroes g_enemy_slots[obj+0x120*8] and calls ActorDespawn -- so a class-0x30 corpse leaves the pool on its own after two seconds and no sweep has to remove it.

Class 0x30 state 8, the corpse that flickers instead of sinking -- character types 0x12 and 3, which is the test ZombieEnterCorpseState makes. Identical to ZombieStateCorpseSink except that the countdown's parity drives obj+0x1F8 bit 0 (the skeleton's draw gate) and ActorSetPartVisibility(obj+0x194, even) (every vertex-blended part's byte), and the body does not move; on the way out it closes both before the despawn. Not an alpha: the class-0x31 twin, ThrowerStateCorpseBlink (FUN_0044AB70), blinks through obj+0x138C instead. [proved]

Class 0x30 state 9, the *other* death -- ZombieOnShot picks it over state 6 when the actor is in state 0x34, carries obj+0x136C bit 0x100000, or has body condition 5 or 6. Sub 0 raises obj+0x34 bit 0x20000, runs ZombieReleasePermitAndUntrack, builds a landing point in the camera's own matrix (g_camera_matrices + DAT_009C6F00 * 0x1A4) whose offsets and scale come from the body condition -- condition 4 also jitters obj+0x64 by rand()%%5 * 0x100 -- overrides it with obj+0x13CC..0x13D4 when obj+0x136C bit 8 is set and bit 0x10 is not, calls ActorArcBeginToAtSpeed, then ChooseDeathMotion. Sub 1 rides the arc through FUN_0044DDE0. Sub 2 falls under gravity (0xBD16872B, or 0xBCDF0123 for conditions 4 and 5), treating surfaces 5 and 0x37 as g_camera_fixed_eye_y, bouncing at -0.25 until it settles or 0x78 frames pass, and ends in ZombieEnterCorpseState.

ReleaseEnemyAliveCount, ReleaseEnemyPresentCount and ReleaseAttackSlot, then clears g_attack_permits[obj+0x120] and ActorDespawns. The terminal arm of ZombieStateWalkDistance, taken when obj+0x34 bit 0x20000000 is set -- which no class-0x30 spawn record does.

Class-0x30 state 1. Plays the run motion, closes on the camera, and switches to state 2 when TestApproachRing returns 1. The motion is row[2 + ((obj+0x34 >> 0x1B) & 1)] from a RANDOM start frame -- rand() %% g_motion_play_length[motion], fade 10 -- and the pair is a jog and a sprint, not two takes of one gait: measured on the shipped banks, 0.30 units an authored frame against 1.29 for char_adv02 and 0.32 against 1.00 for char_adv01. Bit 0x08000000 of obj+0x34 is never ORed anywhere in the image; it arrives from the spawn record's own flags word through ActorInitFlags, so which gait a zombie uses is placement data. 192 of the 402 class-0x30 spawns in the shipped stages set it. Every frame it also rolls rand() & 0xFF < 4 and, when obj+0x136C has both 0x2000000 and 0x1000000, clears 0x1000000 and calls ActorAbortAttackAndLeave (FUN_0045D9F0). Then by band: 1 -> state 2; outside 2..4 -> TurnActorTowardCamera and return; 2..4 -> TurnActorTowardCamera, then if (s8)obj+0x131D >= obj+0x1358 state 5 with obj+0x136C |= g_wait_turn_variant[(rand() >> 4) %% 10] << 21 (and the frame goes on), then for bands 3 and 4 only ZombieShouldStandAndThrow -> state 0x21. The turn rate is ftol((bit27 * 1.5 + 1.0) * 416.0) from 1.5 at 0x004C4CB8, 1.0 at 0x004C4380 and 416.0 at 0x00567890: 0x1A0 jogging, 0x410 sprinting. [proved]

Class 0x30 state 5, and the way back into the attack loop. Plays row[(obj+0x136C >> 0x15) & 1] -- the in-place walk ZombieStateAttackRun chose with g_wait_turn_variant -- through ActorSetMotionBlended(rand() %% 5, 10) when it is not already on it, turns to the camera at 0x40 a frame, and returns to state 1 the moment (s8)obj+0x131D < obj+0x1358 -- its rank in the distance queue is inside the allowance again. ZombieStateAttackRun sends an actor here when it drops out of that slice, so the queue throttle is a round trip and not a one-way exit. Note the **signed** read: EnemyZombieInit writes 0xFF to obj+0x131D, which is -1, so an actor that has not been ranked yet passes the test rather than failing it. [proved]

Class-0x30 state 2, and WHERE THE STANDING GROAN COMES FROM. Calls TestApproachRing and then ActorBodyConditionFromHands -- it is the only call site of the latter in the whole binary, so the body condition is refreshed exactly once per frame an actor spends at the ring and never while it is walking in. Then, at 0x00455748..0x0045576D: if obj+0x136C bit 0x20000 (its own off-screen latch bit) is set and ActorIsOnScreen returns 0, clears the bit and g_attack_committed -- an actor back in the hub still off screen gives the latch up; on screen it keeps it. Then: holds inside the inner ring, and on the frame the in-range idle STARTS -- 004558B0 CMP EAX,EDI / 004558B2 JZ, the one gate, obj+0x1B4 against row[0] -- it calls ActorSetMotionBlended(obj+0x194, row[0], rand() %% 5, 10) and immediately PlaySoundId(0x1917A9) at 004558D6, which is COMMON2\ZOMBIE_041_16.wav. That PUSH at 004558D2 is the ONLY occurrence of 0x1917A9 anywhere in .text, so this state is the whole of the zombie idle voice: one shot per entry into the idle clip, not periodic, not random, and not one of ActorPlayHitVoice's five kinds. The claim gate is four inline tests only -- obj+0x136C bit 0x400 clear, (s8)obj+0x131D < obj+0x1358, obj+0x131E < 3, obj+0x133C < 1 (0x0045580F..0x00455838) -- and then CALL TryClaimAttackSlot whatever the permit table holds; success moves to state 3, the strike (0x34 for body condition 4). Drops back to state 4 if the actor has drifted inside inner-1. [proved]

Derives obj+0x130C from whether bones 5 and 8 -- the hands, at obj+0x4DC and obj+0x68C, which are 0x20C + bone*0x90 -- still hold their original draw slots, and sets the matching destroyed-zone bits via g_bone_damage_zone. Character type 1 only ever falls to 0; types 0x13 and 0x14 write the armed-hand count (0, 1 or 2) but REFUSE to touch conditions 7 and 5, which are the stationary thrower's own row and the row it leaves behind. That refusal is what makes 7 sticky, and the write is what takes a condition-8 walker off the throw row (attacks[7] and attacks[8] are the throw: reach 99, clip 1005/1004) before ZombieStateStrike can read it as a melee. ZombieStateHoldAtRange (0x00455720) is its only caller. Engine bug at 0x0045599C: the left-hand test is CMP EDI,0x1EF5 with EDI still holding [EAX+0x4DC], the RIGHT hand's slot -- so a znonoopa's left hand can never count as armed and every one of them lands on condition 1 with the left-arm zone bit set.

Class-0x30 state 3. Sub 0 draws an attack from g_class30_attack_picks by (rand%10 + destroyed_zones*10) and indexes g_class30_attacks BLIND -- obj+0x131A = picks[...] and the entry pointer is base + index*0x10 with no validity test of any kind; sub 1 plays the lunge until inside the attack's own distance -- SetCurrentActorMotionBlended(obj+0x194, entry+0x02, 0, 10) at 0x00455B49, SKIPPED while the track's own motion already is the lunge (00455b31 CMP [ESI+0x1b4],EAX / 00455b37 JZ to the RET), so in the 155 of 311 shipped entries whose lunge is the actor's run clip (row[2] or row[3]) an actor that runs straight into its attack keeps the run playing as the lunge with no restart -- then starts the strike with ActorSetMotionBlended(obj+0x194, entry+0x00, 0, 5) at 0x00455B63, which writes the play cursor obj+0x19C = 0 and raises the fade bit track+0x37 & 1, and shouts (ActorPlayHitVoice kind 3); sub 2 runs the clip. The fade HOLDS that cursor: EnemyZombieUpdate runs this state (0x00453434) before ZombieAdvanceMotion (0x00453457) draws -- DrawSkinnedModelAndShadow -> SkeletonDrawWalk, whose first act is SkeletonAdvancePlayCursor at 0x004110F3 -- and only then increments the clock obj+0x194, and SkeletonAdvancePlayCursor leaves obj+0x19C alone until clock - track+0x28 reaches fade + 2. So the start frame is drawn fade + 1 = 6 times and this state reads obj+0x19C = 0 on fade + 2 = 7 consecutive frames, the one that set it included; the hit lands fade + 1 + entry+0x08 frames after the swing starts, and the lunge's clip is held 11 draws the same way. [proved] Sub 2 is two independent tests in one pass, and the order and the operators are the whole behaviour: the strike is 00455bdf CMP ECX,EAX / 00455be1 JNZ over CALL 0x00456490, i.e. obj+0x19C == entry+0x08 EXACTLY, and the exit is 00455c02 MOVSX EDX,[ECX*2 + 0x4e07d0] / 4a DEC / 3bc2 CMP EAX,EDX / 7c12 JL, i.e. g_motion_play_length[obj+0x1B4] - 1 <= obj+0x19C -> obj+0x1310 = 4, obj+0x1312 = 0. So a hit frame at or past the strike clip's play length fires NOTHING: the equality is never reached, the state is not aborted and nothing is retried, the clip simply runs to its end and hands to ZombieStateBackOff. The shipped tables use that: character types 0x07, 0x0B and 0x0C share a body-condition-4 entry 2 of clip 997 at hit frame 40 where g_motion_play_length[997] is 20, and their cond-4 pick rows are ten 2s then ten 3s per zone combo, so an UNDAMAGED crawler always draws that entry and always misses, while one with its head shot off draws entry 3 (clip 1018, hit frame 3) and connects. THE FIRST WRITE OF SUB 0, before the draw: 00455a82 MOV ECX,[ESI+0x34] / 00455a93 AND CH,0xfe / 00455a96 OR ECX,0x10000000 / 00455a9c MOV [ESI+0x34],ECX -- obj+0x34 bit 0x100 down and bit 0x10000000 (Committed) up. Nothing on the melee path lowers 0x10000000 until ZombieStateBackOff's first frame (00455ca1), so it spans pick, lunge and swing, and ActorPlayHitReaction's 004544d8 TEST [ESI+0x34],0x10002000 refuses every stumble in between: a zombie cannot be staggered out of its attack. The same bit is half of ZombiePushOutOfWorldAndActors' 0x18000000 test, so a striking zombie is shoved 1.8x as hard. At the swing start (sub 1 -> 2) it also does obj+0x136C = obj+0x136C & ~0x10000 | 0x80000 (00455b77/00455b7e) between the two effect hooks CALL [0x00592bcc] (ZombieStrikeStartSplash, 0x00455B69) and, every frame of sub 2, CALL [0x00592bd0] (ZombieStrikeFrameSplash, 0x00455BED). Sub 1 falls straight through into sub 2 on the frame the clip starts (00455bc5 INC sub, no RET).

Class-0x30 state 4, entered after a strike. Sub 0: obj+0x1338 = 0x3C, obj+0x1334 = 0, obj+0x34 = (obj+0x34 & ~0x10000000) | 0x20000000, obj+0x136C &= ~0x400000. Plays the back-away walk from g_class30_motion_rows[cond][4] (rand() %% 5, fade 10), turns with TurnActorAwayFromPoint relative to the position recorded when the strike began at -0x40 -- the long way, so away -- or +0x40 while obj+0x136C bit 0x400000 is up (the shove timer flips it), and KEEPS the attack permit until the actor is back outside the inner approach ring (0.7 of it for body condition 4) or 240 frames have passed, and not while motion 0x100 is at frame 0x43 or less -- only then does it release and hand to state 2. That retreat is the pause between attacks; there is no cooldown timer for an ordinary zombie. [proved] The 0x10000000 it clears is Committed, which ZombieStateStrike's sub 0 raises before its draw (00455a96); between the two, ActorPlayHitReaction refuses every stumble.

An enemy asks permission to attack, and is offered ONE player's permit. Read in full, 0x00455DE0..0x00455F39 [proved]: FIRST writes obj+0x121 = 0xFF (0x00455DE5), before any test, so a refused claim always leaves the actor holding no index. Gives up at once if g_attack_committed (0x00455DEC). Then picks on the s16 g_max_attackers: 1 -> g_active_player's permit if it is free (0 or 1; a taken one or g_active_player 2 offers nothing, and nothing falls back to the other player); 2 with the s16 g_players_in_play == 1 -> rand() %% 2's (CRT rand 0x004ABE60, sign-corrected AND 0x80000001), if free; 2 with the s16 g_enemies_present == 1 -> rand() %% 2, and if that permit is taken the pick is NOT'd (0x00455E69) -- -1 or -2, never the other player; otherwise ActorScreenHalfSign (0x00409C90): -1 -> player 0's, 1 -> player 1's, each only if free; any other g_max_attackers offers nothing. Then IsPlayerAttackable((s8)obj+0x121) voids the pick (0x00455ED5), and only 0xFF fails (0x00455EF0 CMP 0xFF) -- a -2 that IsPlayerAttackable passes (attract mode) goes on to claim g_attack_permits[-2], i.e. writes 1 to 0x009A2B98. On success: off screen (ActorIsOnScreen == 0) raises obj+0x136C bit 0x20000 and g_attack_committed; g_attack_permits[obj+0x121] = 1 (0 is free, the claim stores 1); returns 1. Writes nothing else -- in particular NOT obj+0x34: NoCameraTrack is each caller's to clear (ZombieStateApproach 0x00457A4E after a grant, ZombieStateWaitForCameraFrame 0x004576E5 before its claim, ZombieStateHoldForCameraCue 0x0045C00C at its cue; the hub, ZombieShouldStandAndThrow, ZombieStateStandAndThrow, ZombieStateScriptedGrabAndDespawn and state 28 have none). No queue-rank test: that lives in the callers. Nine call sites: 0x0045583B ZombieStateHoldAtRange, 0x004576FB ZombieStateWaitForCameraFrame, 0x00457A39 ZombieStateApproach, 0x00457C18 ZombieStateScriptedGrabAndDespawn, 0x004587C4 class-0x30 state 28 (0x004586E0, not ported), 0x00458EB0/0x00458EC3 ZombieShouldStandAndThrow, 0x0045920C/0x004592EE ZombieStateStandAndThrow. Ported in game/combat/permits.ts.

Class 0x30: snap the yaw at obj+0x68 straight to the player and record that player's position in obj+0x13E4/E8/EC. With one attacker the target is the camera eye; with two it is a point (+/-1.2, 0, -1.5) in front of the camera per permit index, so the two zombies converge on different shoulders. ZombieStateStrike measures its lunge distance against the recorded point, not against the camera.

special deaths for a destroyed part (obj+0x1368 bits 0x8/0x10/0x40/0x80 -> motions 0x1AC/0x1A5/0x279/0x229, set by ZombieStateTargetMotionScript and ZombieStateDragTarget from the kill-move clip id), else falls through to the directional pick. Also: condition 4 with obj+0x136C bits 0x2000000 AND 0x8000000 gives 0x3DA, character type 10 with obj+0x136C bit 0x8000 and character types 0xF-0x11 with bit 0x100000 give 0x3DB, obj+0x34 bit 0x1000000 gives 0x3F9, and conditions 5-6 fall through only when obj+0x136C & 7 is zero. Called only from ZombieStateDeath6 (0x00454D3A) and FUN_004550E0 (0x00455304), so every bit it reads is a class-0x30 bit -- including 0x8000, which ThrowerFlag calls the thrower's off-screen permit latch. The 0x3F9 arm is tested at 004560DD (f7463400000001) and has NO character-type guard; obj+0x34 bit 0x1000000 comes from the spawn record's +0x04 init flags through ActorInitFlags (0x00408970), and every shipped record that sets it is class 0x30. ZombieStateDeath6 reads the same bit to send the actor to state 12 instead of the corpse, so 0x3F9 and state 12's landing clip 0x3F8 are the pair any class-0x30 character type can need.

ChooseDeathMotion's directional pick (its only caller, 0x00456197). rel = (g_camera_block_yaw_bams[g_camera_index] - obj+0x68) & 0xFFFF (0x00456248), then FOUR tests in a row through AngleWithinTolerance(rel, centre, 0x2000), each setting obj's motion (FUN_004119A0(obj+0x194, m, 0, 5)) so a boundary heading takes the later arc: 0x4000 -> 0x3E0, 0xC000 -> 0x3DF, 0x0000 -> g_pDeathMotionsArc0[rand() % 4] (0x0059309C), 0x8000 -> g_pDeathMotionsArc8000[rand() % 6] (0x00593084). Then the obj+0x136C remaps: bit 4 re-draws a 0x3DF/0x3E0 from the 0x8000 table; bit 1 maps 0x3D9/0x3DA/0x3DE to 0x3DB/0x3DC/0x3DD; bit 2 maps 0x3DB/0x3DC/0x3DD to 0x3D9/0x3DA/0x3DE. An actor facing the camera has rel 0x8000 and falls back. [proved]

ChooseDeathMotion's tail: points obj+0x13A0 at the dust/splash cue list for the death clip it just chose -- DAT_005930AC..DAT_00593100 for motions 0x3D9..0x3E0 and DAT_00593124 for everything else. ZombieDeathEffectCueTick (FUN_004569B0) is what walks it.

Lands the strike on the player named by the attack permit (obj+0x121). The whole routine is one guard: (obj+0x121 == 0 || == 1) && ((s16)(char)(obj+0x1318 & 7) & entry+0x0C) != entry+0x0C, then FUN_00415300(player, 1, entry+0x0A) -- or FUN_00415300(player, 0, ...) plus ZombieReleaseAndDespawn when obj+0x34 bit 0x2000000 is up. So it whiffs when every zone in the entry's cancel mask has been shot off -- blowing an arm off stops the attack that swings it -- and a cancel mask of ZERO whiffs unconditionally, because 0 != 0 is false. The ten zeroed attack entries the shipped tables carry (types 0x00 cond 0/1, 0x01 and 0x13/0x14 cond 4, 0x07 cond 6, 0x09/0x0F/0x10/0x11 cond 3) therefore deal no damage even though ZombieStateStrike does call this on their frame 0.
Frees the attack permit at obj+0x121 and clears the global commit latch.
Decrements g_enemies_alive exactly once, guarded by obj+0x38 bit 1. This is what opens wait_enemies_alive.
Decrements g_enemies_present exactly once, guarded by obj+0x38 bit 2. This is what opens wait_enemies_present, and it is separate from the alive count.

ZombieStateDeath6's sub-1 teardown, and the only thing that takes a dead class-0x30 zombie out of the attack system. Calls ReleaseAttackSlot (FUN_00456520) first -- which frees obj+0x121 AND clears the g_attack_committed latch when the actor held an off-screen permit -- then, unless obj+0x38 bit 0 is set, raises obj+0x34 bit 0x10000 to drop it from camera tracking and zeroes its camera slot at DAT_009a5ec0 + obj+0x120 * 8, skipping that arm for the last enemy alive when obj+0x34 bit 0x800000 is set. A port that clears the permit array without clearing the latch stalls every remaining enemy: TryClaimAttackSlot reads the latch on its first line and gives up before a player is picked.

Releases the one looping held-weapon SE a class-0x30 actor may hold, and it is NOT a death scream -- the ids prove it. Does nothing unless obj+0x131B is 1, the latch EnemyZombieInitByCharType raises at 0x00453164 when it takes the loop. Then, only while g_weapon_loop_holders is exactly 1 -- this actor is the last holder -- it plays 0x4E17A9 for character type 2 and 0x2025A9 otherwise, which are COMMON2\CHAIN_SAW_22_OFF.wav and STAGE6_SE\LASER_SWORD_22_OFF.wav and are entries 4 and 34 of g_looping_se_stop_ids, so PlaySoundId calls SoundStopAllLoopingSe before playing them (and the _OFF wavs are among the 36 the game never ships). Then it clears the latch and counts g_weapon_loop_holders down. Two callers: ZombieStateDeath6 sub 1, and ZombieRefreshBodyConditionAfterShot (FUN_00454270) when a type-2 actor has lost both hand props.
Returns which advance ring the actor is in -- 1 inside the inner radius (strike range), 2, 3, 4 outward -- and sets obj+0x1358 to the step count that band allows.

Class 0x30 state 6 sub 2 hands here when the death clip ends: the twin of ThrowerEnterCorpseState. Clears obj+0x136C bits 0x60000000 (out of both pushes), sets obj+0x34 bits 0xC000 and clears 0x20001, and -- unless obj+0x38 bit 0 is set -- calls ReleaseEnemyPresentCount. **That is the second half of the enemy accounting**: ReleaseEnemyAliveCount runs at death, in ZombieReleasePermitAndUntrack, and the present count only falls here, when the corpse is finished. A corpse still on stage is present and not alive, which is exactly what separates wait_enemies_present (0x43) from wait_enemies_alive (0x44). Then it steps obj+0x194 back one frame and enters state 7, or state 8 for character types 0x12 and 3.

SpawnWaterRing(params, scale): ActorAlloc(WaterRingUpdate, 0x13F4) at params[0..2] (params[3..5] copied to +0x64..+0x6C and read by nothing), +0x13F0 = 0xE23 (common.bin 181), +0x1370 = 0.02, +0x1374 = 1.0, +0x1330 = 0, +0x118 = scale + (rand() % 3) * 0.1 * (1 - 2 * (rand() & 1)) -- the sign's draw first. Six callers, twelve call sites, always in pairs at 1.0 and 0.5, every block {x, traced floor, z}: four (ZombieDeathEffectCueTick, ZombieDeathLandingEffect, ZombieStrikeStartSplash, ZombieStrikeFrameSplash) reach it only on surfaces 5 and 0x37; the other two (ZombieStateSurfaceOnCameraCue at 0x00457050, ZombieStateTargetMotionScript at 0x0045AC79) on the wading clip 0xB8's play frame 0x1B, with no surface test. [proved]; that it is a water ripple is [likely].

SpawnWaterRing's task: T(+0x40..+0x48) Scale(+0x118, 0.2, +0x118) AssetDrawSlotWithAlpha(+0x13F0, +0x1374), then +0x118 += +0x1370, +0x1330 += 1, +0x1374 -= 1/60 and ActorKill once +0x1330 >= 0x3C -- sixty frames. Draws BEFORE it steps; the step is past the no-return MatrixStackPop (L35). [proved]

Runs every class-0x30 frame unless obj+0x1368 bit 1 is already set. Queries the ground at y+20 and, if the surface underneath is 5 or 0x37 -- the two WET_SURFACES -- and the actor has fallen below it, calls FUN_00408740 to put it in the water and latches bit 1 so it only happens once.

g_class30_states[0x37], called every frame of ZombieStateDeath6 sub 2 (the entry frame included) through PTR_FUN_00592BC4. When obj+0x19C equals the cue at obj+0x13A0 it traces the ground at y+20 and: dry and no rain -- SpawnSpriteEffectFromParamsThunk kind 0x46 at the TRACED height, scale override (0.5, 1.5, 1.5), yaw-only billboard; for character types 0xF..0x11 kind 0x61 at obj+0x44, scale (1.0, 0.3, 1.0), full billboard. Wet (surfaces 5, 0x37) or rain -- on a wet surface with obj+0x136C bit 0x10000 down, SpawnWaterRing twice at the traced height and the bit raised; then SpawnSpriteEffect kind 0x61 at the traced height if the rings went down this call, else at obj+0x44. Either way the cue pointer steps 4 bytes. [proved]

g_class30_states[0x38], reached through PTR_FUN_00592BC8 from ZombieStateDeathKnockbackArc, ZombieStateDeathFallAndBounce, ZombieStateDelayedLeap and ZombieStateArcScriptedEntrance. Nothing while obj+0x136C bit 0x10000 is up; else traces the ground at y+20 (which moves g_coli_hit_surface -- state 9 reads it again straight after) and at the traced height: surfaces 5/0x37 -- SpawnWaterRing(1.0), SpawnWaterRing(0.5), sprite kind 0x61; rain -- sprite kind 0x61; otherwise sprite kind 0x46 billboarded by yaw only. Raises the bit on every arm. Kind 0x61 is a sprite, not a sound. [proved]

g_class30_states[0x39] (0x00592BCC), called through the table by ZombieStateStrike (0x00455B69, after the strike clip is set) and ZombieStateScriptedGrabAndDespawn (0x00457C2D, on its cue). In body condition 6 -- wading -- it traces QueryGroundHeightAt(x, y + 20, z) and, if g_coli_hit_surface is 5 or 0x37: PlaySoundId(0x4116A9), SpawnWaterRing({x, floor, z}, 1.0) and (.., 0.5), SpawnSpriteEffect({x, floor, z}, 0x61, or 0x62 in state 0x17, 1, -1). [proved]

g_class30_states[0x3A] (0x00592BD0), called through the table by ZombieStateStrike every frame of its swing (0x00455BED, between the hit test and the end test). Unless obj+0x136C bit 0x10000 is up: body condition 6, obj+0x19C == g_motion_play_length[obj+0x1B4] - 0x14, trace from y + 20, and on surface 5 or 0x37 SpawnWaterRing({x, floor, z}) at 1.0 and 0.5, SpawnSpriteEffect(.., 0x61, 1, -1), raise the bit, PlaySoundId(0x4116A9). [proved]

Class 0x30 state 12, where ZombieStateDeath6 sends an actor that dies still holding something (obj+0x34 bit 0x1000000, which is also why ChooseDeathMotion gave it clip 0x3F9). Sub 0 drops obj+0x136C bit 0x20000000, clears obj+0x34 bit 0x4000 and sets obj+0x5C = 0xBD16872B (-0.03675f). Sub 1 holds until obj+0x19C reaches 0x3C, then clears obj+0x136C bit 0x10000 and puts 0x20000000 back. Sub 2 freezes the pose once clip 0x3F9 is spent, integrates the fall, and on hitting the ground bounces at -0.25, fires the landing effect through PTR_FUN_00592BC8 once, cuts to clip 0x3F8 at rand()%10 over a 10-frame fade, and enters ZombieEnterCorpseState once |vel.y| <= 0.15.

Class 0x30 state 13 -- 16 spawns, the come-up-out-of-the-water entrance that waits on the CAMERA rather than on a delay (contrast ZombieStateEmerge, state 27, which counts a descriptor delay down). Sub 0 raises obj+0x34 bits 0x4100 (freeze the pose, and the no-ricochet bit) and plays clip 0xB8 for character types 0xF/0x10/0x11 and 0x3D8 for every other, with ActorSetMotion and no fade. Sub 1 waits for g_cam_path_frame >= (u32)tail+0x04 -- a >=, not the == states 18 and 19 use -- then clears both bits. Sub 2 plays it out, and while the clip is 0xB8 throws splash effect 0x62 at play-clock 0x15 and 0x1B, the second preceded by two FUN_004567C0 ripples at 1.0 and 0.5. Exit at g_motion_play_length[motion] - 1 <= obj+0x19C: to state 15 with obj+0x1370 = (float)(u32)tail+0x08 when tail+0x03 is 15, else to state 1. The +0x08 walk distance is only meaningful on that arm -- for the other 13 spawns those bytes are the next descriptor.

Class 0x30 state 14 -- 2 spawns. Runs on the spot for a fixed number of frames and then joins the attack run. Sub 0 latches obj+0x1330 = tail+0x04 (30 frames in stage 1, 5 in stage 2). Sub 1 plays row[2 + ((obj+0x34 >> 0x1B) & 1)] -- the same run pair ZombieStateAttackRun and ZombieStateWalkDistance pick between -- from a random start frame rand() %% g_motion_play_length[motion], fade 5, and counts the timer down. At zero it records obj+0x13D8/DC/E0 = position (the same three words ZombieStateWalkDistance writes when it arrives) and hands to state 1. Like state 15 it never moves the actor itself: SkeletonApplyRootMotion does, out of the clip.

Class-0x30 state 15, the commonest scripted entrance after the attack run: 50 spawns across the game. sub 0 latches obj+0x1370 from the FLOAT at descriptor tail +0x04 and falls through into sub 1, which records the start point at obj+0x13C0/C4/C8 and parks sub at 2. Every frame after that it plays row[2 + ((obj+0x34 >> 0x1B) & 1)] from a random start frame -- row[4] instead when obj+0x34 bit 0x20000000 is set -- and writes the 2D distance from the start point to obj+0x1374. Reaching obj+0x1370 records obj+0x13D8/DC/E0 and hands to state 1, or to ZombieReleaseAndDespawn on the 0x20000000 arm. It never moves the actor: SkeletonApplyRootMotion does, out of the clip. There is no destination and no route -- class 0x30 has no path-following state at all (PATH_STATES is class 0x31 only), so everything past tail+0x08 belongs to the next descriptor, not to this one.

Class 0x30 state 17 -- 38 spawns, the commonest unported entrance and the second commonest of all after the attack run. Plays one clip for a fixed count and then branches to the state the descriptor names. Sub 0 latches obj+0x1330 = tail+0x08. Both subs then, unless obj+0x34 bit 0x40000000 is set, ActorSetMotion(tail+0x04) whenever obj+0x1B4 is not already it -- so the clip is re-asserted every frame rather than started once. At the countdowns end: to state 15 with obj+0x1370 = (float)(u32)tail+0x0C when tail+0x03 is 15 (and sub 1, skipping ZombieStateWalkDistances own latch), else to (s8)tail+0x03 with sub 0. Shipped values are motion at +0x04, 14 to 420 frames at +0x08 and a 1-to-10 unit walk distance at +0x0C.

Class 0x30 state 18 -- 39 spawns. Holds a clip until the camera path reaches an exact frame, then branches. Sub 0, unless obj+0x34 bit 0x40000000 is set, ActorSetMotion(tail+0x04) whenever obj+0x1B4 is not already it, and returns while neither g_cam_path_frame nor g_cam_path_frame_2 EQUALS (s32)tail+0x08 -- an equality, so the frame must be hit exactly, and the actor waits for ever on a path that skips it. On the match sub goes to 1 and falls straight through to the branch: state = (s8)tail+0x03, sub = 0. Same shape as ZombieStateWaitScriptFlagThenBranch (state 20) with a different gate, and as ZombieStateWaitForCameraFrame (state 19) without the freeze and the permit claim.

Class 0x30 state 19. Holds the actor -- HIDDEN when tail+0x0C is 0: ActorSetPartVisibility(model, 0) at 0x00457653, obj+0x34 |= 0x90100 and obj+0x1F8 &= ~1 (the skeleton's draw gate), none of which touches the clock -- and plays tail+0x04 unless obj+0x34 has 0x40000000, until g_cam_path_frame or g_cam_path_frame_2 equals (s16)tail+0x08. Sub 0 runs on into sub 1. On the cue ActorSetPartVisibility(model, 1) at 0x004576CA unconditionally, and for the hidden kind obj+0x1F8 |= 1 and obj+0x34 &= 0xfff6feff; then optionally claims an attack slot (tail+0x0D) and counts (s16)tail+0x0E frames down at obj+0x1330, or takes the descriptor's state (tail+0x03). **This is the only place in class 0x30 that arms the attack cooldown**: it sets obj+0x1368 bit 0 and obj+0x133C = (s16)tail+0x10, then enters the strike. Every other zombie has obj+0x1368 bit 0 clear, so ZombieStateHoldAtRange forces obj+0x133C to zero and there is no wait between swings beyond the strike clip and the retreat. [proved]

Class 0x30 state 20 -- 2 spawns, both stage 2. Byte-for-byte ZombieStateWaitCameraFrameThenBranch with the camera gate replaced by g_script_flags[(s32)tail+0x08] == 1: it holds ActorSetMotion(tail+0x04) until the evt script raises that flag, then hands to (s8)tail+0x03. Both shipped spawns wait on flag 53 playing clip 198.

Class 0x30 state 21, the entrance that arrives on a clip -- the stage-2 van zombies and four more in stage 5, all six playing motion 923. sub 0 sets the descriptor's clip (params+0x04) with ActorSetMotion, no fade, and arms params+0x08 frames at obj+0x1330; it falls straight into sub 1, which counts that down and then **clears obj+0x34 bit 0x4000**; sub 2 plays the clip out. This state is the ONLY thing in the game that clears the three bits the spawn record sets to park the actor inside the vehicle: 0x4000 when the delay expires, 0x100 at obj+0x19C == 0x26 of clip 0x39B (the landing, so it stops ricocheting), and 0x2000 as it hands over. Exit is g_motion_play_length[motion] - 1 <= obj+0x19C -- the play clock, not the authored frame count -- to descriptor byte 3, substituting state 1 if that byte names 21 again; on the byte-3 == 4 arm it inlines TestApproachRing to seed obj+0x1358 first, an arm no shipped record takes. Skipping this state leaves the freeze bit on for ever: ZombieAdvanceMotion then never advances obj+0x194/0x198, and since a zombie is carried only by its clip's root motion it can never close either.

Class 0x30 state 22. Sub 0 measures the actor's distance to the CAMERA (not to a player) against g_enemy_approach_rings' three radii and latches obj+0x1358 from it (the same band test TestApproachRing makes, inlined), raises obj+0x34 bit 0x10000 (NoCameraTrack, 0x00457B32) and goes to sub 1. Sub 1 plays row[(obj+0x136C >> 21) & 1] from rand() %% play_length when it is not already playing, and when (s8)obj+0x131D < obj+0x1358 and obj+0x131E < 3 calls TryClaimAttackSlot (0x00457A39); on a grant it clears NoCameraTrack ITSELF (AND EAX, 0xfffeffff at 0x00457A4E -- the claim writes no obj+0x34) and takes the descriptor tail's byte 3 as its state, sub 0. [proved]

Class 0x30 state 23 -- 6 spawns. A one-shot scripted kill: the actor plays a grab clip, takes the player on an exact frame and then removes itself. Sub 0 latches obj+0x1330 = tail+0x04 and, when tail+0x08 is 0xBA, plays 0xBB with only bit 0x100 raised, else plays tail+0x08 with 0x4100 (pose frozen); obj+0x136C |= 0x100000. Sub 1 waits until obj+0x1330 is -1 (fire at once, which two stage-1 spawns take) or either camera path frame equals it, then blends 0xBA on the 0xBA arm, calls TryClaimAttackSlot and ActorFacePlayerTarget, clears 0x4100, runs the per-class hook at PTR_FUN_00592BCC and records obj+0x13C4 = y. Sub 2 calls PlayerTakeDamage(obj+0x121, 1, kind) at obj+0x19C == tail+0x0C, the kind being 9 unless the clip is 0xB1, in which case 0. Sub 3 waits out g_motion_play_length[motion] - 1, throws effect 0x62 at the actor and calls ZombieReleaseAndDespawn. This is the only class-0x30 entrance that ends in a despawn rather than in a state.

Class 0x30 state 24. Sub 0 reads a destination (float x,y,z at descriptor +0x04/08/0C) and a frame count (s16 at +0x10) and sets obj+0x4C velocity = (dest - pos)/frames, which EnemyZombieUpdate then integrates -- a scripted leap or drop, not gravity. On arrival it parks the position in obj+0x13C0..C8, claims a permit, plays the clip at descriptor +0x18 and calls PlayerTakeDamage on the frame at descriptor +0x1C.

Class 0x30 state 0x19 -- g_class30_states[0x19] is 0x00457FB0, with 0x18 LeapToPoint and 0x1A DelayedLeap either side of it -- reached only from ActorReactToHit's znjoe arm; no spawn record sets it. Sub 0 zeroes obj+0x11C (the actor is DEAD from here), raises obj+0x34 0x3500 (ShotImmune 0x100, NoDismember 0x400, 0x1000, no-hit-reaction 0x2000) and obj+0x136C 0x80000000, the death latch. Subs 0 and 1 both fall into the range test: while the xz distance to g_camera_eye_x/z is LESS than g_enemy_approach_rings[obj+0x131F].INNER -- 0045802D FCOMP [EAX*4 + 0x9A2BE0] with EAX = ringSet*3, so the inner radius of the set and not the outer -- it plays motion 0x1E3 at a random phase with blend 5 and returns, so the actor backs out to the inner ring before it opens. Sub 2 plays motion 0x1DF at a random phase with blend 10 and arms a countdown of rand()%10 + 0x5F, i.e. 95..104 frames. Sub 3 counts it down once, and on the frame it lands it applies the torso's FIRST damage step by hand rather than through ActorSwapDamagedPart: obj+0x328 = 1 is bone record 1's hit count (obj+0x298 + bone*0x90) and obj+0x29C = g_pBoneEffectSlots[obj+0x1F4][1*6+1] is bone record 1's draw slot (obj+0x20C + bone*0x90), the same index and the same table a first hit on bone 1 would have used -- so no zone bit is set and nothing is severed. Then SpawnBoneHitSprite(obj,1), a call to the empty function at 0x0041EBB0, SpawnBodyCreature, obj+0x136C |= 0x8000 so it happens once, ReleaseAttackSlot and obj+0x1328 = -1. The clip ending (obj+0x19C >= g_motion_play_length[obj+0x1B4] - 1) hands over to state 6.

Class 0x30 state 26, the burst-out entrance -- fourteen spawns. Sub 0 raises obj+0x34 bit 0x2000 and copies the tail into obj+0x1334 (delay, tail+0x04), obj+0x1374..0x137C (destination, tail+0x08..0x10) and obj+0x1380 (gravity, tail+0x14). Sub 1 counts the delay down and calls ActorArcBeginFalling, which solves the parabola and writes its frame count to obj+0x1330; the clip is 0x3BB at fade 1, or 0x399 at fade 5 when obj+0x34 bit 0x1000000 is set -- three stage-1 spawns. It then clears obj+0x136C bits 0x20000000 and 0x10000, sets bit 0x4000, and clears obj+0x34 bit 0x1000000. Sub 2 is the 0x399 wind-up ONLY: it holds in place to play frame 0x1A, integrates from 0x1A to 0x23, and at 0x23 cross-fades 0x3BB and advances -- obj+0x1330 is NOT decremented there, so that arm falls about 0x23 frames further than the solution and does not land on its point. Any other clip falls straight through to sub 3. Sub 3 integrates obj+0x4C += obj+0x58 each frame and, crucially, holds obj+0x34 bit 0x4000 -- THE POSE FREEZE -- for the whole flight except before the clip has started and for the last 0x15 frames, so the jump clip contributes no root motion while the arc owns the position; a port without that freeze applies both and sinks through the floor. While frozen, an actor whose hit points have gone below 1 switches to clip 0x3F7, which is the limp of a corpse shot out of the air and NOT a landing animation -- a live actor plays no landing clip at all. On the last frame it restores obj+0x136C bit 0x20000000, clears the velocity, sets obj+0x1350 = g_motion_play_length[current clip] - rand() %% 30 - 1, clears obj+0x34 bit 0x20000 unless obj+0x136C bit 0x10000000 is set, plays sound 0x1C16A9 with DAT_009C8E8C = 0x20 for body condition 5 or the per-class hook and 0x2A16A9 otherwise, and shouts. Sub 4 hands a dead actor to state 6 with obj+0x136C bit 0x80000000, and a live one to state 1 once obj+0x1350 <= obj+0x19C.

Class 0x30 state 27, the come-out-of-the-water entrance -- eighteen spawns, and the reason a spawn's y is where the entrance STARTS rather than where the actor stands. Sub 0 cuts to motion 0xB9 (ActorSetMotion, not blended, and nothing freezes the clock) and arms tail+0x04 as a delay; when tail+0x03 is 1 it also HIDES the actor: ActorSetPartVisibility(model, 0) at 0x0045855A, obj+0x34 |= 0x90000 and obj+0x1F8 &= ~1 (AND AL,0xfe at 0x00458571, model+0x64 bit 0, the skeleton's draw gate -- not root motion, which is bit 1). Sub 1 counts the delay down, then ActorSetPartVisibility(model, 1) at 0x004585DC and obj+0x1F8 |= 1 unconditionally and plays the clip at tail+0x08 -- 178 for the water spawns, 183 for the ground ones -- whose own translation lifts the actor out; sub 2 plays it through, throwing effect 0x62 at frame 0x16 and 0x61 at frame 0x23 when the clip is 178, then goes to state 1. Three writes to obj+0x34 span the state and they are what makes an emerging zombie unstaggerable: 00458532 80ce21 OR DH,0x21 raises 0x2100 in sub 0 -- 0x100 ShotImmune, which makes ZombieOnShot return before it can pick a death state, and 0x2000 the no-hit-reaction latch ActorPlayHitReaction tests at 004544d8; 004585ec 81e2fffef6ff AND EDX,0xfff6feff drops 0x90100 as the emerge clip starts, so the actor becomes shootable again while still holding 0x2000; and 0045869f 80e6df AND DH,0xdf clears 0x2000 on the same instruction pair that writes state 1. So the whole emerge plays no stagger, and the first half of it takes no death state either. [proved] Two writes to obj+0x136C as well: sub 0 raises 0x100002 (OR EAX,0x100002 -- 0d02001000 at 00458528) or, when obj+0x34 has 0x200000 (TEST EAX,0x200000 at 00458509), clears that bit (00458510) and raises 0x10 instead (OR AL,0x10 -- 0c10 at 0045851E), and the hand-over drops 0x100000 and restores 0x20000000 (AND EDX,0xffefffff / OR EDX,0x20000000 at 004586B4). The OR AL,0x10 is the only class-0x30 writer of obj+0x136C bit 0x10, the arc-target veto ZombieStateDeathKnockbackArc reads at 004552BA. [proved]

Class 0x30 state 29 -- 6 spawns, all stage 2. The actor is a PASSENGER: it stores its own spawn position at obj+0x13E4/E8/EC (x, y, z -- note 0x13E8 is y and 0x13EC z, written out of order) and every frame sets its position to that offset PLUS g_carrier_objects own, so it rides the rideable and moves with it. Plays row[0] from rand() %% 5, fade 10, and raises obj+0x136C bit 0x100000 for as long as it rides. It reads NOTHING from the descriptor tail but byte 3: the tail belongs to the state it hands over to, which is why the three spawns whose byte 3 is 26 carry a ZombieStateDelayedLeap tail and the three whose byte 3 is 30 carry a ZombieStateArcScriptedEntrance one. The ride ends when the carrier raises its own obj+0x34 bit 0x10000000.

Class 0x30 state 30 -- 3 spawns, all stage 4, all reached from ZombieStateRideCarrier. Waits, plays a crouch, then rides a scripted ballistic arc to a world point. Sub 0 latches obj+0x1330 = tail+0x18. Sub 1 either waits for a camera frame (when the descriptors own byte +2 is 0x16, an arm no shipped record takes) or counts the timer down, then plays 0x10C for character type 0 and 0x39F for every other, arms obj+0x1330 = 0x21 or 0x2C respectively, and raises obj+0x34 bit 0x2000. Sub 2 holds until obj+0x19C reaches that. Sub 3 calls ActorArcBegin(pos, tail+0x04..0x0C, tail+0x10) and InstallArcMotionScript with DAT_00567898 for type 0 and DAT_00567958 otherwise, then resets obj+0x1360 = 0. Sub 4 runs ActorArcStep(tail+0x14) to completion, mapping its five phases onto obj+0x136C bits 0x100000 (in flight) and 0x10000, playing the landing thud through PTR_FUN_00592BC8 and sound 0x2A16A9 -- or, for body condition 5, sound 0x1C16A9 with DAT_009C8E8C = 0x20. When the step reports done it clears 0x2000 and goes to state 1, or to state 3 keeping the permit when obj+0x121 is not -1.

Class 0x30 state 31 -- 4 spawns, all stage 2 and all with the same shape. Unlike state 20 this one is not counted as an enemy until its flag comes up. Sub 0 raises obj+0x34 bit 0x100 and plays tail+0x08 (919 for all four) from rand() %% g_motion_play_length, fade 5. Sub 1 waits for g_script_flags[(u8)tail+0x04] -- flag 129 -- to equal 1, then clears obj+0x34 bit 0x10000, INCREMENTS g_enemies_present and g_enemies_alive, and latches obj+0x1330 = tail+0x0C (0, 50, 70 or 100 frames). Sub 2 counts that down then plays tail+0x10 (920) from rand() %% 10. Sub 3 hands to state 1 and clears bit 0x100 as soon as the clip is not 920 or the play clock has passed 0x4D. The two counter increments are the point: these four are invisible to wait_enemies_alive until the script lets them in.

ZombieStateAttackRun's router into state 33 (bands 3 and 4 only), read in full (0x00458E10..0x00458EF1) [proved]. Requires body condition 8 and AngleWithinTolerance((g_camera_block_yaw_bams[g_camera_index] - 0x8000) & 0xFFFF, obj+0x68 & 0xFFFF, 0x400) (FUN_0040A040) -- the CAMERA BLOCK's yaw, read at 0x00458E48 (index * 0x69 dwords), turned half round, which is the heading of an actor facing the camera; then by character type: 1 (znassb) calls TryClaimAttackSlot FIRST (0x00458EC3) and only then tests its hands (obj+0x4DC == 0x1BA9 or obj+0x68C == 0x1BA5), so an unarmed znassb takes the permit and is answered 0; 0x13 and 0x14 test their hands first (0x1ECE/0x1ECA, 0x1EF9/0x1EF5) and claim only if one is armed (0x00458EB0); any other type answers 0 without claiming. Returns 1 only on a grant with a hand armed. No obj+0x34 write. Fourteen shipped spawns are condition 8: ten znassb in stage 4, one in stage 5, the axe walkers 0x14 x2 in stage 2 and 0x13 in stage 3. The port read g_camera_yaw_bams (0x009C71F0) here, half a turn out, and none of them ever threw.

Chooses which hand throws and writes the attack index at obj+0x131A: 0 for bone 5, 1 for bone 8. Tosses a coin for which to prefer and falls back to whichever hand still holds its original draw slot -- 0x1BA9/0x1BA5 for char type 1, 0x1ECE/0x1ECA for 0x13, 0x1EF9/0x1EF5 for 0x14. Returns the bone number, 5 or 8, or 0 when both hands are empty.

Class 0x30 state 33 (0x21), the stationary thrower -- char types 1 (znassb), 0x13 (tutorial) and 0x14 (znonoopa), and the only state that never moves the actor at all. Seven shipped spawns start here, every one of them body condition 7. Subs: 0 latches the idle delay from the descriptor tail by how many hands still hold a weapon (tail+0x04 for two, tail+0x08 for one, ZombieReleaseAndDespawn for none); 1 plays row[0] and counts that delay down; 2 waits for TryClaimAttackSlot, then takes the permit, picks a hand with ZombiePickThrowingHand, plays g_class30_attacks[type][cond][obj+0x131A]'s strike motion from frame 0 and shouts; 3 waits for obj+0x19C to reach the entry's hit frame (+0x08) and calls ZombieThrowHandWeapon; 4 waits out the clip, drops the commit flag, and goes back to sub 0 while a hand is still armed -- or, for condition != 7, straight back to state 1; 5 idles tail+0x0C frames and then TAKES ONE OF TWO ENDINGS, chosen at 0045945C by obj+0x38 bit 0x10 (TEST byte ptr [ESI+0x38],0x10 -- f6463810). Bit CLEAR: state 15 with obj+0x1370 = tail+0x10 when tail+0x03 is 0, or state 26 with the point at tail+0x10..0x18 and the gravity at tail+0x20 otherwise; the state 15 exit is what raises obj+0x34 bit 0x20000000, the arm of ZombieStateWalkDistance that retires the actor instead of attacking. Bit SET: it never moves again -- ReleaseEnemyAliveCount, ReleaseEnemyPresentCount and ReleaseAttackSlot on the spot, g_enemy_slots[obj+0x120*8] and the hit slot cleared, obj+0x1330 = tail+0x1C, obj+0x34 |= 0x10100 (NoCameraTrack | ShotImmune), sub 6. Sub 6 (LAB_00459562, which the retire arm falls into on the same frame) plays row[0] and despawns once g_enemies_present < 1 AND g_players_in_play != 0 AND --obj+0x1330 < 1, so the wait_enemies_alive this actor was holding opens the moment it stops rather than at the end of a walk. EnemyZombieInitByCharType is what puts that bit there, from obj+0x34 bit 1; two spawn records in the game set it and both are stage 3 block 2 step 4's axe men. CORRECTION: obj+0x34 bit 0x1000000 is NOT unwritten. Sub 0 only TESTS it (TEST ECX,0x1000000 at 004590E6, f7c100000001, JNE past the writes), and when it is CLEAR the arm writes obj+0x136C |= 1 at 004590F4 and, if obj+0x34 bit 0x20000 is also set, obj+0x136C |= 0x100000 at 00459104. The bit itself is SEEDED FROM THE SPAWN RECORD: the record's +0x04 u32 is OR'd with 1 into obj+0x34 by ActorInitFlags (0x00408970), and every shipped record that sets bit 0x1000000 is class 0x30 -- stage 1's state-26 leapers, stage 3's two state-33 axe men, and twelve state-37 ZombieStateCarryProp spawns, which is the corroboration that the bit means the actor has hold of something. tools/verify_death_clips.py counts them out of the bundles. So the test is usually FALSE, and the clear in the walk arm at 00459466..0045946F is what takes the bit off an actor that leaves alive. A sweep of .text for every encoding of the immediate (81 /1 imm32 OR forms, 0D, byte/word/bts forms at +0x37/+0x36, and B8+r MOV) finds no instruction anywhere in the image that raises it. RELEASE ARM (sub 3, 0x004592C3..0x00459319): ZombieThrowHandWeapon(obj, obj+0x135C); then for character type 1 ONLY (CMP word [ESI+0x1f4], DI with EDI=1 at 0x004592E4) TryClaimAttackSlot (answer unused), ZombiePickThrowingHand into obj+0x135C and a second ZombieThrowHandWeapon -- znassb throws both blades on one frame; then ZombieRetireThrowConditionIfUnarmed (0x004595F0), INC sub and JMP 0x00459320 straight into sub 4's clip-end test. SUB 4 RELEASES NO PERMIT: 0x0045933D..0x00459361 clears obj+0x34 bit 0x10000000 and, if obj+0x136C bit 0x20000 is up, clears it and g_attack_committed -- the permit itself went with the weapon.

Called once, from ZombieStateStandAndThrow's release arm after the throw (0x0045930A). If body condition obj+0x130C is 8 and no hand still holds its weapon -- draw slots +0x4DC/+0x68C against 0x1BA9/0x1BA5 (type 1), 0x1ECE/0x1ECA (0x13), 0x1EF9/0x1EF5 (0x14); any other type skips the test -- it writes obj+0x130C = 0 and obj+0x34 |= 0x8000000 (OR ECX, 0x8000000 -- 81c900000008 at 0x00459682), the sprint bit ZombieStateAttackRun reads: a walker that has thrown its last weapon comes on at a run. [proved]

Class 0x30's straight flight, slot 1 of g_zombie_thrown_weapon_states: the axe. Sub 0: ttl = |target - pos| / obj+0x1370, velocity from it, KNIFE1_44 (0x4F17A9). Sub 1: pos += vel with obj+0x64 += obj+0x135C at 0x00459731 -- the X term, NO sign test on the hand, at the 0xB00 ZombieThrowHandWeapon writes -- ttl -= 1.0, and at ttl <= 0 PlayerTakeDamage(obj+0x121, 1, 4). Sub 2 (0x00459792): obj+0x34 |= 0x4008000, VecToAngles(target.x - x, 0, target.z - z) into obj+0x64/+0x68, obj+0x68 += 0x8000, obj+0x64 += (1-2*(rand()%2))*(rand()&2)*0x100, obj+0x1330 = 0x1E, KNIFE1_44_OFF (0x5017A9). Subs 3 and 4: ZombieThrownWeaponAimAtCamera, pos = target, 0x1E stuck, 0x3C blinking on the counter's parity, then ReleaseAttackSlot (FUN_00456520, CALL at 0x004598C0) and ActorDespawn. An older note here said nothing writes obj+0x135C; ZombieThrowHandWeapon does, at 0x0045A427. [proved]

Thrown-weapon state 2, znassb's blades. Sub 0: ZombieThrownWeaponBeginArc(obj, pos, target, +0.009 for bone 5 / -0.009 otherwise (0x3C1374BC), speed a literal 1.0 (PUSH 0x3F800000 at 0x00459968), &ttl), KNIFE1_44. Sub 1: velocity += acceleration, obj+0x68 += obj+0x135C at 0x00459998 -- the Y term, unsigned, at 0x1600 -- pos += velocity, ttl -= 1.0, and on arrival PlayerTakeDamage(obj+0x121, 1, 6). Subs 2 to 4 are the straight state's landing, stick and blink byte for byte. [proved]

Solves the lob. The heading is VecToAngles from the THROWER's position (obj+0x1390 -> +0x40/+0x48) to the target; of four AngleWithinTolerance calls only the 0 and 0x8000 windows (+-0x2000) are used -- the 0x4000 answer goes to a JZ onto the next line and the 0xC000 one XORs an EDI that is already 0. Heading down Z: t = |(dy, dz)| / speed, acceleration (g, 0, 0), vel = ((2dx - g t^2)/2t, dy/t, dz/t). Otherwise: t = |(dx, dy)| / speed, acceleration (0, 0, g), vel = (dx/t, dy/t, (2dz - g t^2)/2t). So the curve bends ACROSS the throw. [proved]

Thrown-weapon state 3: the player shot it out of the air. Four subs off 0x0045A060. Sub 0: SpawnSpriteEffect(pos, 0x52, 1, -1), obj+0x34 |= 0x4008000, ReleaseAttackSlot (FUN_00456520). Sub 1: obj+0x13C0 = the view point obj+0x70 offset up to 100 on x and y (sign before magnitude, rand()%10+1 times 10), through the camera block's +0x40; then past the MatrixStackPop (0x00459E7D..0x00459ED9) obj+0x135C = ftol(obj+0x135C * 1.3 * (1-2*(rand()%2))), obj+0x1330 = 5, KNIFE1_44_OFF and BULLET_MET3. Sub 2: hang the five. Sub 3: Vec3Normalize(target - pos) * obj+0x1370 -- the throw's own speed, which is also the arrival box -- obj+0x64 += obj+0x135C (no hand test), gone at 0xB4 frames or inside the box. [proved]

Writes the projectile's target at obj+0x13C0..0x13C8: a CAMERA-SPACE point through g_camera_blocks + idx*0x1A4 + 0x40. obj+0x1360 == 1 (g_max_attackers latched at the throw): (0, -1.5, -4) for the axe 0x249, (0, 0, -4) otherwise; with two permits the x is (1 - 2*obj+0x121) * -0.6 [0x00565EF0]. The drop is along the camera's own Y, not the world's. [proved]

Throws the weapon out of bone hand. ActorAlloc(ZombieThrownWeaponUpdate, 0x13F4) + ActorClearGameFields + ActorClaimHitSlot; the char-type switch swaps the hand to its bare slot, zeroes that bone record's +0x78 (MOV [EDI+0x554],EBX -- 899f54050000 at 0045A2B2 for bone 5, MOV [EDI+0x704],EBX -- 899f04070000 at 0045A2DB for bone 8; the hit-sphere radius) and names the model: 0x249 (znonoo.bin 0, the axe) for 0x13 and 0x14, 0x1B8D / 0x1B8C (znassb.bin 3 and 2) for type 1; a hand that is neither 5 nor 8 falls out with no model and the weapon is still made. Position from the bone record through the camera block's +0x40; obj+0x34 = 0x80000001, obj+0x124 = obj+0x128 = 2.0; the permit moves to the weapon and the thrower keeps 0 (MOV [EDI+0x121], BL at 0x0045A3EC) -- no latch moves; obj+0x1F8 = 5, +0x1390 = thrower, +0x1358 = hand, +0x133C = +0x1338 = 7. The axe gets obj+0x135C = 0xB00 and state 1 (0x0045A427), anything else 0x1600 and state 2 (0x0045A43C); obj+0x1370 = 1.5 for a thrower in body condition 7 else 1.0; obj+0x1360 = g_max_attackers; ZombieThrownWeaponAimAtCamera; VecToAngles(target - pos, flat) into obj+0x64/+0x68 and obj+0x6C = 0x800 (0x0045A4C4) -- it leaves the hand facing its target, rolled; then obj+0x100 = pos lifted 1.5 [0x004C4CB8] and RegisterForCameraTracking. [proved]

The class 0x30 thrown weapon's per-frame entry, and it has no class id at all: its only reference in the binary is the allocation in ZombieThrowHandWeapon. A mark not already spent bumps g_player_hit_count[obj+0x34 & 0x10 ? 1 : 0] and jumps to state 3. Dispatches g_zombie_thrown_weapon_states[obj+0x1310], then while obj+0x1F8 bit 0 is up draws Rz(obj+0x6C) * Ry(obj+0x68) * Rx(obj+0x64) -- NO obj+0x1364 term, unlike class 0x31's (MOV EAX,[ESI+0x64]; PUSH EAX; CALL MatrixRotateX at 0x0045A58C) -- and writes obj+0x70..0x78, RegisterForShotTest(obj) and ActorDrawGroundShadowWithSize(obj, 5.0, 5.0) at 0x0045A5A8..0x0045A622. In states 1 and 2: obj+0x100 = pos (y + 1.5 for the axe) and RegisterForCameraTracking. [proved]

Class 0x30 state 34 (0x22), and the whole reason obj+0x1394 exists on a zombie: the actor walks at the object at obj+0x1394 -- for the 47 class-0x10 captors that is the civilian CivilianInit built them for -- and NOT at the camera. Sub 0/1 take a {f32 arrive_dist; u16 loops; u16 motion; u16 frame} header from ZombieScriptForState and leave the cursor at header+10; sub 2 turns toward the target with TurnActorAwayFromPoint at 0x1A0 each frame and, once the 2D distance is inside arrive_dist, switches to state 35 sub 1 and raises 0x800 in the civilian's OWN wait word (sub+0x00), which is what releases the civilian's script. If the target dies it parks in state 45. Every one of the 23 spawns in the game that starts here is a civilian's captor.

Class 0x30 state 35 (0x23), the scripted attack the walk hands over to. Steps a list of s16[4] {motion, frame, loops, mode} through the cursor at obj+0x1398, advancing it by one entry each time. sub 0 selects the blob with ZombieScriptForState and points the cursor past the first entry; sub 1 loads the entry the cursor already points at -- it does NOT re-select -- and advances it; sub 2 plays, fires the kill cue when obj+0x19C reaches the entry's mode (raising 0x4000000 on the target's obj+0x34, the same bit a killing shot raises), and on g_motion_play_length - 1 counts the loop down. At zero it takes the next entry, or ZombieScriptEnded when the cursor's motion short is below 1. A negative mode clears obj+0x34 bit 0x10000000; a non-negative one sets it, so an entry with a kill cue is also the one that will not be re-ranked out of its swing.

Class 0x30 state 36 (0x24). ZombieStateTargetMotionScript with a fifth short per entry: a g_script_flags index raised on the cue frame, which is how a set piece's zombie tells the evt it has finished.

Class 0x30 state 37 (0x25), the prop carrier -- stage 3's drum-throwers on the bridge. Sub 0: ActorAlloc(CarriedPropInit, 0x19C) into obj+0x139C with +0x198 = this, +0x194 = the state-37 script, +0x3C = -1; takes the script HEADER's own entry at +0x30 {motion, frame, loops, mode} (not the list's first), obj+0x1358 = script +0x08 (the release behaviour), cursor = +0x38. Subs 1/3 take the next list entry. Sub 2: prop hp < 1 -> civilian wait |= 0x800, drop HoldingWeapon (obj+0x34 &= ~0x1000000, obj+0x136C |= 1), obj+0x130C = 0, sub 4; else on frame == entry mode with no fade pending (track+0x37 bit 0) prop sub+0x10 = obj+0x1358 -- the throw -- with the same flag pair. Tail: TurnActorAwayFromPoint(eye, 0x34 while mode < 0 else 0xD0); on the last frame of the last loop, mode < 0: release mode != 4 steps to the next entry (Training + DAT_009A2234 == 1 replays 0x10F instead); mode 4 picks the player (g_active_player in 1P; a free permit or the side of the screen in 2P) into the prop's +0x121 and claims g_attack_permits[p], or replays 0x10F one loop while it is taken. mode >= 0: next entry -> state 35 sub 1, none -> ZombieScriptEnded. [proved]

Class 0x30 state 38 (0x26), the commonest attack state of the captor family. Header is {f32 x, y, z; s16 motion, frame; s16 loops, mode} and then s16[4] entries. The per-frame arm switches on the mode: 0 and 1 retire through ZombieRetireAndCredit as soon as ActorBoundsOnScreen says the actor has left the frame, 1 and 2 also turn toward the header's point, 3 retires when the loop count runs out.

Raises 0x4008001 on obj+0x34, credits obj+0x131C to the player named by the target civilian's sub+0x6C (or a random one when that is -1), runs the two count releases and parks sub at 4. This is how a captor leaves once its script is done -- and obj+0x131C is exactly the byte CivilianPruneDeadChildren reads back to decide who is paid the 400.

Class 0x30 state 39 (0x27). Reads the CIVILIAN's own sub-block and waits on the pair op 0x1A writes there: sub+0x2E is a COUNT of captors still to order (each one parked here consumes one, so op 0x1A(35,1) raises exactly one and a script that wants two issues it twice) and sub+0x2C the order. 0x31 means die -- obj+0x34 |= 0x4000000, the killer from the civilian's sub+0x6C, or when that is -1 g_active_player while g_players_in_play is 1 and rand() % 2 otherwise, then ReleaseEnemyAliveCount and ReleaseEnemyPresentCount on the spot -- anything else is a class-0x30 state id it switches to and dispatches immediately, a tail call through g_class30_states so the new state runs on the same frame. This is the civilian script driving its own captors. Sub 0 also HIDES the actor and falls straight into sub 1 on the same frame (no RET after the INC at 0x0045BB3A): obj+0x1350 = obj+0x34; obj+0x34 |= 0x18000; obj+0x1F8 &= ~1 (model+0x64 bit 0, the skeleton's draw gate and ActorDrawShadow's); and 0045bb31 MOV EAX,[ESI+0x1d4] / 0045bb37 MOV byte ptr [EAX+1],DL with DL=0 -- model+0x40 is the parts' record array and +1 of the first record is part 0's draw byte SkeletonDrawWalk (FUN_004110D0) reads. Part 0 ONLY: a second vertex-blended part is left drawn. The order arm puts both back (obj+0x1F8 |= 1, [ECX+1] = 1 at 0x0045BBF3). So stage 2 block 16's two znebi2 are invisible in the water until their civilian's killed script calls them up. [proved]

Rotates a world point into the actor's own frame by the inverse of its yaw/roll/pitch and returns whether the local z is positive. The arrival test for the states that walk PAST a point rather than up to it.
Class 0x30 state 40 (0x28). Header {f32 x, y, z; s16 motion, frame}; walks until ActorPointIsAhead says the point is behind, then either ends the script or hands over to state 35.
Class 0x30 state 41 (0x29). The same header, but the arrival test is a 2D distance of 5.0 and the actor turns toward the point at 0x1A0 while it closes.

Class 0x30 state 42 (0x2A), reached only from ZombieScriptEnded when a captor's exit lands on AttackRun and its descriptor tail+0x0C is not -1. Runs g_class30_states[obj+0x132C] every frame as a delegate, re-captures whatever state the delegate asked for, forbids it reaching Strike (bounces to HoldAtRange and frees the permit at g_attack_permits[obj+0x121] -- that table entry ONLY: 0x0045C049 MOV [ECX*4 + 0x9A2BA0], 0, with obj+0x121 and the off-screen latch left as they are), and graduates to the delegate only when g_active_cam_path == (s16)tail+0x0C and g_cam_path_frame == (s16)tail+0x0E. The graduation arm tests the cue BEFORE the Strike bounce, so a captor that reached HoldAtRange before the camera claims on the cue frame too and graduates into HoldAtRange STILL OWNING the permit; its next TryClaimAttackSlot fails on it. Nothing in class 0x30 frees it -- the finish_sequence queued after each held cue does (EvtActionFinishSequence21 zeroes both permits). 3 of the 69 captor spawns pass through it. The only captor-family code that touches g_attack_permits. [proved]

Class 0x30 state 43 (0x2B) -- g_class30_states[43] = 0x0045C080, with [42] 0x0045BFD0 and [44] 0x0045C2E0 either side, both agreeing with the port (L38). FIVE sub-states at obj+0x1312 off the jump table at 0x0045C2C0: {0x45C0B1, 0x45C113, 0x45C212, 0x45C27E, 0x45C29C}, and anything above 4 falls straight to the tail (JA at 0x0045C0A4).
