Otherwise records pc in the 16-entry ring at 0x009C9060 (index 0x009CA108, & 0xF), and -- if the selector dword at pc+4 is 0x21, finish_sequence (CMP EDX,0x21 at 0x0045F82E) -- sets g_attack_committed = 0 at 0x0045F833, AT QUEUE TIME, before the action runs; then g_queued_events_pending++ and pc advances. [proved]

Opcode 0x45. if (g_evt_yield == 0) { g_evt_yield = 1; return; } else if (g_script_flags[pc[1]] != 0 && g_evt_gameplay_live != 0) { g_evt_yield = 0; pc += 8; }. So: the first visit costs a frame without reading the condition, and the gate is a plain byte test on the SAME g_script_flags (0x009C7200) that EvtOpSetScriptFlag48 writes -- there is no second array. Sixteen of the shipped waits name a flag no set_script_flag anywhere in their stage raises: those are raised by gameplay -- CivilianRunScript op 0x1C, ZombieStateTargetScriptWithFlag (class 0x30 state 36), FUN_00433f40 (a class-0x33 cue prop) and class 0x32 state 4 (FUN_00480470) -- which is what makes this opcode the script's one way to wait on an actor finishing.

evt 0x46. The EvtOpWaitEnemiesPresent43 handler with g_civilians_alive (0x009CA0E8) in place of g_enemies_present: same DAT_009C8EA0 yield latch, same DAT_007DCCA4 gameplay-live gate, same DAT_009C6F2D side condition. All 68 sites in the shipped scripts pass operand 0, so in practice it waits for the last civilian to leave play.

Opcode 0x48, and the whole handler: pc += 8; g_script_flags[pc_old[1]] = 1. No yield, no test, no clear -- there is no clear_script_flag opcode anywhere in the dispatch table, so a flag stays up until ResetSceneOnEnter (FUN_0045EDD0) zeroes all 0x100 bytes on the next scene.

evt opcode 0x2C, set_skippable_region. Opens or closes the window in which the player may skip a cutscene.    operand != 0 -> DAT_009A2230 = 0; g_nEvtSkippableRegion = 1   operand == 0 -> g_nEvtSkippableRegion = 0; g_nEvtSkipFlag = 0  Closing always clears the skip flag, so a skip never carries past the region it was asked for -- and, conversely, one press skips every wait until the region closes, because the wait opcodes do not clear the flag themselves.  The six stage scripts contain 136 of these, always paired 1/0.  This opcode is live. What is dead is the flag it feeds: see g_nEvtSkipFlag.
evt 0x2E: if (g_nEvtSkipFlag) PlaySoundId(0x80000002) -- the VOICE channel's stop (PlaySoundControl). Formerly EvtOpResumeBgmIfSkipped2E, which it never did. [proved]

The run-phase dispatcher: one indirect call, (*g_pfnRunPhaseHandlers[g_nRunPhase])(). Thirteen handlers at 0x005679A8, and this is their only caller. Phase 0 ResetGameOnStart starts a run, 1 AdvanceToNextScene loads the next stage, 2-4 are the continue screen, 5 RunPhaseArmSceneAdvance and 6 RunPhaseStepToNextScene are the two-frame stage-to-stage step.

The new-game reset, one level above ResetSceneOnEnter (0x0045EDD0). Picks the opening scene and block by g_GameMode -- scene 6 / DAT_009A2BBC for mode 2, scene 0 / block 0x10 for mode 3, scene 0 / block 0 otherwise -- fills the 0x28-entry g_route_history with -1, zeroes the run totals g_civilians_seen_total and g_civilians_rescued_total and the first three dwords (six scenes) of both g_civilians_seen_by_scene and g_civilians_rescued_by_scene, clears the three-dword-stride block at DAT_009C8EC0, and ends by calling FUN_00460030, which loads the scene and calls ResetSceneOnEnter. So the per-scene tallies are zeroed here for the whole run and again per scene there.

The stage-to-stage transition. Walks the two players (stride 0x98 shorts = 0x130 bytes) and puts any whose g_player_state is 5 -- in play -- back to 2, then calls LoadSceneAndReset and steps the phase counter DAT_009C90A4. So a player is parked out of "in play" for the duration of the load, which is why IsPlayerAttackable refuses and no enemy commits an attack across a scene change.

Load the scene g_scene_index names and reset it -- the only caller of ResetSceneOnEnter (0x0045EDD0) in the playable path, and its last act. param_2 == 1 takes the attract path (a DAT_00598028-times preload loop through FUN_00437F90/SetupSceneProjection) and 0 the ordinary one; then per g_GameMode and g_wCaptionMode it queues the caption and title assets, drains the asset jobs, allocates the scene task at LAB_00460710, calls CameraClearHookAndPose, and finally ResetSceneOnEnter. Three callers, all of them "enter a scene": ResetGameOnStart (0x0045FEF0) for the first scene of a run, AdvanceToNextScene (0x0045FFF0) for each stage transition, and RunAttractDemo (0x00426800) for the demo playlist.

Run phase 2, a stage being played. When both players' states are 'out' (flag +0x04 of g_player_state_handlers: states 4 and 9), phase 3 -- or 0x0B in app state 6 when the mode is Training/Boss or CreditsAvailable is 0. Then RunSceneTasksAndTimers and g_screen_frames += 1. [proved]
Run phase 11: red fog (0x009A3564.. and the scene fog words), 0x007DCCD4 = 0, phase += 1 and falls into RunPhaseNoContinueWait. [proved]
Run phase 12: RunSceneTasksAndTimers, 0x007DCCD4 += 1, and past 1 stores g_max_attackers to 0x009C8E88 and RequestAppState(7). Created 2026-09-19. [proved]

Run phase 5, the frame before RunPhaseStepToNextScene. Sets g_nRunPhaseDelay = 1 and steps g_nRunPhase to 6, then falls into the same player-state test FUN_004601D0 runs: a player whose state has no row in the table at 0x00579CD4 sends the phase to 3 (the continue screen) or 0xB instead, so a stage only advances with a player still in play.

Run phase 6, and the one instruction that moves the game from one stage to the next: g_scene_index = g_scene_index + 1 for game modes 0 and 1, then phase 1 (AdvanceToNextScene) -- or phase 7 when the increment reaches 6, which is past the last stage. It does NOT choose the block: EvtAdvanceStepOrRoute already wrote g_evt_block_index from the terminal route record, and nothing between here and FUN_0045EBC0 touches it. Waits for g_nRunPhaseDelay to reach 0 first. Mode 2 goes to scene 6 instead; mode 3 reads the {scene, block} pair at 0x0055CBBC indexed by DAT_009A2268.
Run phase 3: RunSceneTasksAndTimers, continue timer 0x009A2BB8 = 0x9FFF, the credit counts it watches at 0x007DCCAC.., phase += 1. [proved]

Run phase 4, the run's CONTINUE? screen: RunSceneTasksAndTimers; a credit change restarts it; the continue buttons (g_pad_state 4 / 0x40000) of a player at 4 knock it to the bottom of its digit (below 0x8000 only); then DrawScreenSprite CONTINUE? 0x22C at (128, 200) and the 64x128 digit 0x4F + (timer >> 12) at (482, 188), both scale 1, flags 0, with the knocked timer and before the step; once anybody is back in play, phase 2 and PlayerResumeContinue for both; otherwise 0x2D a frame and at < 1 g_game_over_players = g_max_attackers and RequestAppState(7). [proved]
The scene's task list (FUN_004A7240), UpdateDamageRank, 0x009C8A7C += 1 while 0x009A2C30, then both players' g_player_invuln_frames -= 1 floored at 0. Every in-play run phase calls it. [proved]
Seeds g_damage_rank from g_initial_damage_rank[difficulty] when a game starts; forces difficulty 2 when FUN_00413280 is nonzero.
Adaptive difficulty. Re-derives g_damage_rank from lives lost since the last update and elapsed time (0x708 ticks per step), clamped to [0,15].

The top-level screen dispatcher: switch (g_app_state) with one routine per screen, then FUN_004067D0. PROVED table -- 3 FUN_00495EB0; 4 TitleMenuRunPhase, the title and mode-select screen; 5 RunAttractDemo; 6 RunPhaseDispatch, in play; 7 FUN_00460960; 8 FUN_0041A5E0, the RANKING row; 9 FUN_004996C0; 10 RunAttractScene10; 0x0B RunAttractScene11; 0x0C FUN_004869E0, the OPTION row; 0x0F NetworkModeRunPhase, the NETWORK row; 0x10 FUN_0041E1F0, boot. Every other value draws nothing. This is what fixes app state 4 as the screen g_GameMode is chosen on, and 0x0C and 0x0F as the two menu rows below it.

App state 7 in AppStateDispatch, the game-over screen: six run phases. 0 loads texbanks 0x155 (and 0x14F outside Training/Boss) and scene set 0x4D, zeroes the camera, task list GameOverBuildFlyTasks, players at 4 -> 6, g_game_over_timer = 200, furniture bit 1 off, PlaySoundId(0x10000009) (BGM 9 OVR_AR, unlooped). 1 the fly-over: the pad's 2/0x20000 cuts it once the timer is under 0xA5 (Original copies and saves the items on 0xC6). 2 task list GameOverBuildLogoTasks, timer 0xB4. 3 the logo, cut under 0xAF; then Training/Boss put players at 6 back to 0 and RequestAppState(6), others phase 4. 4 GameOverRouteMapArm. 5 GameOverRouteMapWait. [proved]
Phase 0's task list: GameOverSpawnCameraFly, FUN_00414F20 (the camera tasks), PlayerTasksCreate, SpawnAttackablePlayerTask. [proved]
Phase 2's task list: GameOverResetCamera and one GameOverLogoTask with its counter at 0. [proved]

The GAME OVER logo: a frame counter (+0x34) that spawns ScreenSpriteAnimSpawn records -- frame 0 plate 0x43A at (320,240) alpha 0 for 0x82 frames fading in (alpha mode 2); 0x78, 0x7D, 0x82, 0x87, 0x8C the 20-frame flashes 0x43B/0x43C/0x43D around it; 0x91 the plate again squashing (scale mode 1) and fading (alpha mode 1) over 20 -- and ActorKills itself at 0xA5. [proved]
The fly-over camera task: g_cam_path_frame = task+0x50, CamEvalPath7(0x1F, frame) into the camera block, frame += 1, the angles from the look-at, UpdateSceneViewAndLight. [proved]
Allocates GameOverCameraFlyTick, CameraBlocksReset, starts it at frame 10 and runs it once. [proved]
CameraBlocksReset then UpdateSceneViewAndLight. [proved]
Phase 4: seeds the route history (the default route from 0x0059351C when none was taken), the map's scroll state at 0x007DCCD8.., task list GameOverBuildRouteTasks, phase += 1. [proved]

Phase 4's task list: the camera, the player tasks, and one or two player figures (GameOverSpawnPlayerFigure with character 0x39/0x3A and motion 0x35B/0x358 -- who is at state 6 decides) plus RouteMapDrawTask; with both players out, GameOverSpawnPartnerFigure too. [proved]
The route list's first task: ActorAlloc(UpdateSceneViewAndLight, 0x34), CameraBlocksReset, and the camera block's eye z (0x009A60C8) = -7.0. [proved]
Phase 5: runs the task list and waits for the pad's 2/0x20000 (which writes g_game_over_route_done = -1) or for that word to be -1; then CreditsClear and AppStateAdvanceByTable (7 -> 3). [proved]
ActorAlloc(RouteMapDrawTask, 0x13F4). [proved]

The route map: walks g_route_history's blocks against the per-scene waypoint table at 0x00567A04 and draws the 5x15 map tiles from 0x005679FC with DrawScreenSprite, scrolling; sets g_game_over_route_done = 1 when the route is drawn. [proved]
A skinned player-character figure for the route screen: character from the argument (in Original Mode from the carried item), motion, and two anchor words. [proved]

The route map's player figure (GameOverSpawnPlayerFigure's task). By g_game_over_route_done: 0 picks the step toward the target (y then x, x winning) into 0x007DCCEA; 1 blends obj+0x1350 (the end clip) over 10 and sets 2; 2/3 count obj+0x1358 to 0x78 and set -1. The step moves the cursor 4 map px (2 up the map, growing the screen offset 0x007DCCFC; 4/6 x; 8 down, scrolling 0x007DCCD8 while the cursor is under 0x578 and the offset below 1) and turns obj+0x68; a step spawns RouteMarkSpawn. Then the figure's camera-space point ((obj+0x1354 + x) * -100 / d, offset * -100 / d, -100) through the camera block's matrix into obj+0x40, the disc 0x145B at -99.5 turned 0x4000 about X and scaled 3, DrawSkinnedModelAndShadow, model[0]++. Ghidra's body stops at the matrix pop; the draw tail is 0x0046171F..0x004617BE. [proved]
The second figure: character 0x3A (Original: from 0x009A2256), motion 0x358. [proved]

The route map's partner figure (GameOverSpawnPartnerFigure's task): on g_game_over_route_done 2 blends 0x339 over 10 and sets 3; turns by the player figure's step; stands at ((x - 0x18) * -100 / d, (offset + 0x18) * -100 / d, -100) and draws as the player figure does (disc 0x145B, DrawSkinnedModelAndShadow, model[0]++; tail 0x004619E2..0x00461A73). [proved]
RouteMarkSpawn(x, y, mode): ActorAlloc(RouteMarkTick, 0x48) with +0x34 x, +0x38 y, +0x40 mode -- a footprint on the route map. [proved]

One footprint, every frame: AssetDrawSlot(g_route_mark_slot) at the camera-space point (x * -101 / d, y' * -101 / d, -101) scaled 0.2 with the stack loaded with the identity -- mode 0 y' = y + scroll, mode 1 y' = scroll - y, mode 2 as spawned; any other mode counts +0x3C to 1000 and kills itself. [proved]

Takes the largest of its three float arguments and passes it to FUN_0041EBB0, the empty stub -- so the whole call is dead. PropDrawOnlyType12 (FUN_00467E50) is the only caller, right after MatrixScale with the same three values, which is what it was presumably meant to report.

Does a live player currently carry Original Mode item id N? Reads the two-slot per-player inventory at g_original_item_slots (0x009A2240, stride 0x14): with one player in play it checks g_active_player's two slots, with two it checks player 0 slot 0 and player 1 slot 0. Returns 1 or 0. Called by the branch triggers that only open a route once you are carrying the key -- PropUpdateType73, PropUpdateType76 and StoryModeSwitchUpdate.

Class 0x41's handler. A transient stub: dispatches obj+0x130C through the 79-entry g_class41_constructors, then falls into ActorKill so the placer never survives its first frame. It is never drawn and never damaged -- what the script places is the constructor call, not an object.

g_class41_constructors[5..14, 18..21, 25, 27, 28, 30..36, 41, 43, 45, 49, 51, 53, 54, 56..60, 62..64, 67, 69..77] -- 44 of the 79 types and 173 of the class's 316 spawns. Allocates a 0x378 object whose update routine comes from the SECOND 79-entry table, g_class41_updates at 0x005936BC, which is how one constructor serves thirty different objects. The prologue copies the position, all three orientation words as real angles, and -- the trap -- obj+0x11C into obj+0x28C, so for this family the hp word is the ASSET SLOT. Then a switch on the type applies that object's own setup: a slot override (6, 10, 0x0D, 0x13, 0x38), a hit radius, a shot count, an effect id, or a whole sub-object list (8, 0x43, 0x2B). Case 0x22 builds a falling container -- the same object class 0x44 selector 16 places, item countdown and all. Cases 0x13 and 0x19 increment g_enemies_present and 0x0E g_enemies_alive, so some of what this places is not a prop at all.

Six callers: PlaceGenericProp cases 0x46/0x47/0x48 (types 70, 71, 72) with the placer's desc+0x24 byte as the row, SpawnStoryModeItem with the dropping prop's +0x2A0, SpawnOriginalItemDrop (type 7's drop, row 0) and PropUpdateType43's Original Mode break (0x0046D035, row 0). r = rand() % (s8)row[7]; walk the cumulative s8 weights row[4..7] while weight <= r and i < 3; obj+0x290 = (s8)row[i] out of g_original_item_tables[g_scene_index]. For -1: obj+0x28C = obj+0x28E = 0 and obj+0x2C4 = 1.0; otherwise the three from g_original_item_records[id] +0/+2/+4. THE CALL OVERWRITES obj+0x28C: the collectibles' descriptor word is a lifetime (70, 71) or nothing (72), never their model.

g_class41_constructors[0]. Builds one BreakablePropUpdate child per member of breakable group obj+0x11C, from the 10-byte records at g_breakable_group_ptrs. x/z are the record's s16 tenths; y is g_camera_fixed_eye_y - 0.1 + level*7.540296, except group 7 which uses level*7.540296 - 14.9 off its own pointer. Each child gets +0x11C = 2 (two shots), asset 0x19E8, the placer's evt-block lifetime in +0x199, and its member index in +0x290. In g_GameMode 2 the members g_prop_target_set selects get +0x11C = 1 and asset 0x1A0F instead. Finally it seeds g_item_set_countdown for the group's item set with rand()%n + 1 -- so the hidden item drops on a RANDOM one of that set's props, not the last.

g_class41_constructors[4], the most-placed type (70 spawns). Builds one prop with update FUN_00465fb0 from the *orientation* words: obj+0x6C is the object kind and obj+0x64 the item-set size, which is why the class-0x41 orientation triple must never be read as angles. The kind indexes g_prop_kind_params (stride 0xC) for the break effect and radius, and picks the asset slot: 2 -> 0x17A9, 3 -> 0x19E8, 8 -> 0x17AA, 9 -> 0x17AB, else none.

g_class41_constructors[1] -- class 0x41 type 1, the canal's water tiles. ActorAlloc(WaterSurfaceUpdate, 0x44) + ActorClearGameFields, then task+0x34 = (u8)placer+0x1F4 (the index), +0x35 = (u8)placer+0x11C (lifetime in evt-step changes), +0x40 = g_water_surface_slots[(s16)placer+0x1F4], +0x36 = (u8)g_evt_step_index, +0x37 = 0, and only when g_scene_index == 2 (stage 3) +0x38 = index + 0x0B, the script flag that kills it. 15 shipped spawns: 5 stage 2, 7 stage 3, 3 training; every one at (0,0,0) with no angle. [proved]

g_class41_constructors[24]. Builds a TWENTY-segment chain: twenty 0x200-byte objects running ChainSegmentUpdate, each carrying the placer's +0x1F4 as a group id at +0x1AC and its own index 0..19 at +0x1AD, all registered in g_chain_segments (0x007DCD18) at [group * 0x14 + index]. Every segment takes the placer's position, its +0x11C as a step lifetime, a hit radius of 2.0 and a starting yaw of index << 14. Despawns without building anything when g_GameMode is not 1 and the group id is 1, so the branch-carrying group is Original Mode only. Four shipped spawns: stage 2 blocks 22 and 23, stage 4 block 3.

g_class41_constructors[38]. Builds NINE 0x378 objects running PropUpdateType38 (0x0046BCC0), one per row of g_prop_table38: position from the row, rotations = __ftol(row degrees * 182.0444) into obj+0x1CC/1D0/1D4, obj+0x11C copied from the placer (the step lifetime), obj+0x290 = row index, obj+0x1B8 = the row y (the rest height), obj+0x124 = 3.0, obj+0x34 = 0x80000001, obj+0x28C = 0x1237 (komono_st1.bin[3]). Stage 1 only (evt 0x1994, block 1 step 2 op 16), the church.

g_class41_constructors[39]. Builds EIGHT 0x378 objects running PropUpdateType39, one per row of g_prop_table39, each a STACK of up to eight copies of slot 0x1237: sub-position i at (x, y + i*0.926, z) in obj+0x22C+12i, and a random X-rotation offset rand()%0x1001-0x800 in the s16 at obj+0x1FC+6i. obj+0x124 = 5.0, obj+0x34 = 0x80000001, obj+0x1B8 = y. Stage 1 only (evt 0x19BC), the church.

Sets all twelve bytes of g_fragment_subkind1_intact to 1 (three dword stores of 0x01010101). Called by ResetGameOnStart, RunAttractDemo, RunAttractScene10/11 and two others -- a per-game reset, not a per-scene one.

g_class41_constructors[40] -- 28 spawns, and the constructor behind the most-placed branch trigger. Builds g_class41_fragment_counts[placer+0x1F4] objects running PropUpdateType40, each carrying its index at obj+0x1B8 and the placer's +0x1F4 as a sub-kind at obj+0x1BA, with obj+0x11C copied from the placer, a 5.5 hit radius and flags 0x80000001. The position, draw slot and scale come from per-sub-kind tables -- sub-kind 0 from 0x00594158 through a fixed transform, 1 from 0x00594038 with its own draw slot decided by g_original_items_taken and g_GameMode, and 6 and up from the pointer table at 0x005945EC with slots from 0x00594648. The switch arm for sub-kind 9 (iVar5 == 3) ZEROES g_branch_prop_shot_count, which is what makes PropUpdateType40's -both broken- test mean both of the two this placement built.

g_class41_constructors[44]. Builds SEVEN 0x378 objects running PropUpdateType44 from g_prop_table44: position = the row's s16 x/y/z * 0.01, rotations the row's three BAMS dwords, obj+0x290 = row index, obj+0x124 = 5.0, obj+0x34 = 0x80000001, and the effect state block obj+0x324 = {0x13, 0x1D4 (motion 468), 0, 0}. Stage 1 only (evt 0x1B48), the church.

g_class41_constructors[48]. ActorAlloc(PropUpdateType48FlickerLight, 0xD14); step latch obj+0x1BB = g_evt_step_index, counter +0x1BC = 0; lifetime +0x11C from the placer's +0x11C (the descriptor's hit-point word); position +0x194..0x19C from the placer's +0x40..0x48; yaw +0x1B0 from +0x68; shot radius +0x124 = 3.0; obj+0x1C4 = EntityLightAcquireSlot(). One shipped spawn: stage 2 block 26 step 1 (evt 0x11EF0).

The node draw hook SpawnGoldenFrog (0x0047238B) and FUN_00463E50 (0x00463F28) install at obj+0x12EC for the golden frog (character type 0x1C). obj+0x1350 < 25 (CMP EAX, 0x19): AssetDrawSlot(record slot); otherwise AssetDrawSlotWithAlpha(slot, 1.0 - obj+0x1350 * 0.02) -- FILD, FMUL [0x004E3100] = 0x3CA3D70A = 0.02, FSUBR [0x004C4380] = 1.0 -- so the shot frog fades from 0.5 at n = 25 to 0 at 50. [proved]. Not ported: the port releases the golden frog as an item.released event and has no actor for it.

The breakable prop placed by PlaceBreakableGroup. Despawns once g_evt_step_index has changed more than its +0x199 lifetime times -- a lifetime in event STEPS, not blocks. On a shot: +0x11C 2 -> 1 cracks it, plays 0x1D16A9 and sets +0x2C0 = 1.0 so it shakes, and marks every member it supports to shake too; +0x11C 1 -> 0 destroys it, plays 0x1A16A9, awards through BreakablePropAwardHit, clears its slot in g_breakable_members and decrements g_item_set_countdown -- releasing the set's item when that reaches zero. Destroying and toppling are DIFFERENT: a destroyed prop at stack level 0 has its object entry point overwritten with BreakableEffectUpdate and becomes a puff for 0x48 frames, and one above level 0 shatters through BreakablePropSpawnShatter -- neither falls. Falling (state 1 -> 2, settled by BreakablePropGroundContact) happens only to a prop whose supporting members have all gone, which is what makes a stack collapse from the bottom. Note also that only the destroying shot pays: the crack calls BreakablePropAwardHit with award=0.

Resolves which player's shot landed from obj+0x34 bits 1 and 2 -- both set means rand() picks -- then awards 10 points unless the caller passes 0 or g_GameMode is 2, and counts the hit into g_player_hit_count for the accuracy grade.

Breaks a stacked prop into one 0x2B4 object running BreakablePropShatterUpdate (0x004653B0) that carries all 15 pieces. Each piece is placed by MatrixInvert(0) * prop+0x2E4 (the matrix the prop's last draw stored) * Translate(g_shatter_fragment_offsets[i] * 0.001) * Rz Ry Rx(g_shatter_fragment_angles[i]), read back with MatrixGetTranslation and MatrixToEulerZYX; its velocity is (sin b, 1.0, cos b) with b = i * 0x1000 and a horizontal speed of rand() % 0x15 * 0.01 + 0.1 (x and z drawn separately), and its spin is three rand() % 0x801 - 0x400. 75 rand() calls per shatter. obj+0x34/0x35/0x36 take the prop's member, group and +0x324. [proved]

The shatter object's frame: while the pre-increment count at obj+0x2B0 is <= 0x48 it steps all 15 pieces -- vy -= 0.06805, position += velocity, the three s16 angles += their spins, and below g_camera_fixed_eye_y + 1.0 (unless obj+0x35, the group, is 0x63) it is put back on that plane with vy *= -0.8 -- and draws each under Translate; Rz Ry Rx with slot g_shatter_fragment_slots_a[i] when obj+0x36 is 0, else g_shatter_fragment_slots_b[i]. At 0x49 it ActorKills itself. No rand(), no shot test. [proved]
The break puff. Draws the effect record at +0x324 for 0x48 frames and then kills itself.

Transforms the 96 points of g_breakable_hull_points by the prop's Ry*Rz*Rx and reports whether any of them is below the floor (g_camera_fixed_eye_y - 0.1). In the falling state it records the first such point in +0x198; in the toppling state it keeps the lowest and re-seats the prop's origin on it, which is how a broken prop comes to rest leaning on a corner. Also clamps z into [-1325, -1265.8] while g_scene is 1.
The impact spark on a prop hit. Allocates a 0x50 object with effect id 0x904 at the shot's screen point unprojected to the prop's depth.

The per-frame body of the 0x50-byte spark SpawnPropHitSpark and SpawnScaledPropSpark allocate: obj+0x48 += 1, ActorKill once it passes 0x919, else Translate(+0x34/38/3C) MatrixClearRotation RotZ(+0x44) Scale(+0x4C x3) AssetDrawSlot(+0x48). Steps before it draws, so 0x905..0x919 are the frames seen.

The prop PlaceKindedProp builds -- class 0x41 type 4, 70 spawns and the most-placed constructor in the game. Shot handling depends on the model: a 0x19E8 crate takes two (the first cracks it, pays nothing and hides the model behind 0xFFFF), every other kind takes one. The destroying shot pays 10 through BreakablePropAwardHit, plays g_prop_kind_params[kind]+4, runs the break effect at +0x324 for DAT_004E07D0[effect]-2 frames and then despawns -- and releases the item set in +0x194 through the SAME g_item_set_countdown and the same switch BreakablePropUpdate uses. 37 of the 70 hide an item, which is more than the group placer accounts for. Draw-time shake, ground shadow 0x10D0 or 0x10D1 by kind.

Class 0x41's shared prologue: 25 of the update routines open with it. Despawns the prop when g_evt_step_index has CHANGED more than obj+0x11C times -- the counter is the step index, so this is a lifetime in event STEPS, not blocks -- and immediately when g_scene_index==1 and g_script_flags[0x77] is set. So five of the nine are Original-Mode-only.
g_class44_subtypes[16]. Allocates a 0x378 object running FallingContainerUpdate. Two spawns, both stage 2.

g_class44_subtypes[17]. Allocates a 0x378-byte object running StoryModeSwitchUpdate. Twelve shipped spawns across stages 1, 2, 3 and 5, and it is the branch writer with the widest reach: five of them stand in branch blocks.

The object PropBuildScriptFlagEffect allocates, and the whole of what class 0x44 selector 0 is. Three script-flag rules and a draw: g_script_flags[0x13] despawns it (ActorDespawn, not ActorKill); g_script_flags[0x12] steps obj+0x32C while it is below g_motion_play_length[obj+0x328] - 2; and the frame it lands on is matched against a cue list -- g_script_flag_effect_cues_a for effect 2 through the cursor at obj+0x2A4, g_script_flag_effect_cues_b otherwise through obj+0x2A8 -- each hit playing PlaySoundId(0x1816A9) and wrapping the cursor at the list's -1. The draw is gated on g_motion_slots[471].state == 2 (the literal word at 0x009A469C, which is that record's state half) and is EffectDrawWithCapture(obj+0x324, obj+0x2A0, -1): the effect tree at its own world coordinates, with the captured bone's matrix landing in obj+0x338 and copied on to obj+0x150. The three writes to obj+0x64/+0x68/+0x6C afterwards read EffectFrameRotations at the RAW cursor rather than the half-rate key, so past key 100 they index outside the motion block; nothing in this routine or in RegisterForShotTest reads them back.

shared by class 0x44 selectors 1/2/4. Swings on g_script_flags[open_flag] through g_pHingeCurvesXYZ (selectors 0/2/3) / g_pHingeCurvesYaw; transform is RotY(base); RotZ(rz); RotY(swing); RotX(rx). obj+0x1DC is read for its SIGN only here (TEST/JLE at 0x473EE6: ADD vs SUB on rx, NEG on yaw) -- its magnitude is the shot-wobble amplitude at IMUL 0x473FB5, and 4 of 56 hinges carry +/-512 or +/-416. obj+0x2C0 (the FMUL on the yaw) is 1.0f from every constructor; obj+0x1CC/0x1D4 are never written. Frame stops at 60, 130 on curve 4.

The object PropBuildFlagLiftedProp allocates. g_script_flags[obj+0x2A4] == 1 kills it (ActorKill); while g_script_flags[obj+0x2A0] == 1 and obj+0x1A0 < 10.0 it rises 0.8 a frame; draws AssetDrawSlot(obj+0x28C) under MatrixTranslate(obj+0x19C..0x1A4). Nothing else: no shot test, no collision. Unported.

The object PlaceStoryModeSwitch builds, and the branch writer with the widest reach -- twelve spawns over four stages. THE HEAD IS NOT BEHIND THE MODE GATE, and that matters: (1) it despawns when the g_script_flags byte at obj+0x2A4 is raised; (2) in scene 1 it despawns when g_script_flags[0x77] is raised; (3) ELSE, in scene 2 with g_evt_block_index == 2 and obj+0x192 still 0, it writes g_script_flags[0x15] = 1 at 0x00474FA6 -- every frame, in Arcade as well as Original, because the CMP g_GameMode,1 / JNZ sits at 0x00474FB4, AFTER it. That write is the only thing that opens stage 3 block 2 step 3's wait_script_flag 0x15 on the block-7 -> block-8 route, where the script's own set_script_flag 0x15 (block 1 step 5, evt 0x001D00) never runs; stage 3's switch is the one spawned by block 7 step 8 (evt 0x3630, remove flag 0x16, which block 2 step 3 raises at its end and so takes the object away). THE REST is behind g_GameMode == 1. Once obj+0x192 has latched -- which a hit, or PlayerHoldsOriginalItem for any of the four ids at obj+0x1FC/0x202/0x208/0x20E, or DAT_009A26EC does -- it runs 60 frames of g_pHingeCurvesXYZ. THE BRANCH: while the g_script_flags byte named by obj+0x2A0 is raised, a SCENE AND BLOCK TABLE decides -- scene 0 block 4, scene 1 blocks 1, 3 and 0xC, and scene 4 block 4 all write g_script_branch_var = 2 and then clear obj+0x2A0 to -1 so it fires once. Those five (scene, block) pairs are exactly five of the branch records whose live alternate is slot 2: stage 1 block 4 {6,-1,13}, stage 2 blocks 1 {2,-1,29}, 3 {4,-1,30} and 12 {13,-1,31}, and stage 5 block 4 {5,-1,6}. In scene 2 blocks 2 and 4 it also spawns a story-mode item once through SpawnStoryModeItem, with obj+0x2B0 as the once-only latch; afterwards, in block 2, it waits for g_script_flags[0x18] (which block 2 step 3 op 1 sets) and raises g_script_flags[0x15] a SECOND time from 0x004751B1 once obj+0x2B0 has passed 0x4C. So one routine has two writers of flag 0x15 and only the first of them runs in Arcade.

The object PropBuildRisingDoor allocates, and the whole of class 0x44 selector 11: a door that slides straight UP when a script flag is raised. Per frame: g_script_flags[obj+0x2A4] == 1 -> ActorKill. Then, while g_script_flags[obj+0x2A0] is still clear AND (s16)obj+0x28C == 0xA58, it RATTLES -- if obj+0x2C0 < 0.001 it is reset to 1.0f (and PoseHookNone(2, 0x14) is called, a dead call to the empty stub), then the draw is offset by (rand() %% 0x191 - 200) * obj+0x2C0 * 0.01 in X and (rand() %% 0x65 - 50) * obj+0x2C0 * 0.01 in Z and obj+0x2C0 *= 0.95. The amplitude decays below 0.001 in about 135 frames and is then reseeded, so it rattles in bursts for as long as the flag is clear; the offsets are frame LOCALS, not state. When g_script_flags[obj+0x2A0] == 1: on the first such frame obj+0x2A8 = 1 and obj+0x1C4 = 0.5f, then while obj+0x1A0 is below its ceiling obj+0x1C4 += step and obj+0x1A0 += obj+0x1C4 -- ceiling 20.0 and step 0.1 for slot 0xA58, ceiling 35.0 and step 0.01 for everything else, so stage 3's door clears in about 26 frames and stage 5's takes far longer. Past the ceiling it stops writing y and holds. The draw is MatrixStackPush(0); MatrixTranslate(rattleX + obj+0x19C, obj+0x1A0, rattleZ + obj+0x1A4); MatrixRotateY(obj+0x1D0); AssetDrawSlot((s16)obj+0x28C); MatrixStackPop(1) -- ONE rotation only, no Z and no X. No hit test: the door cannot be shot.

CurlModelSlot3F7ByYaw(yaw): if asset slot 0x3F7's record has its resident bit (0x009AE58C & 0x8000 -- the slot table is 0x009A66A0 + slot*0x20, pointer at +4, flags at +0xC, as AssetDrawSlot reads it), walks that model's meshes (a negative first dword skips a 0x50 header) and strips, and for every full 32-byte vertex (x's bit 0 set) rewrites z (+0x08) = 4.8e-05 - 4.0 * sin(ftol(x * 2058.112) BAMS) * sin(yaw BAMS) -- a sine curl across the model's width, scaled by how far it has turned. Constants: 0x0055DD14 = 0x4500A1CB, 0x004C4CA8 = 4.0 (double), 0x00569190 (double). Called per card by BossIntroBannerUpdate (0x00437C7D) and by Boss3IntroCardUpdate (0x0042499F). Slot 0x3F7 is boss4_kls_hod1.bin[30], which no shipped stage script loads, so in the arcade and Original stages the routine changes nothing. [proved]

The banner's frame: ++obj+0x2A0; past 0x96, or in scene 5 with g_original_item_banner_count above 1, it decrements the count and ActorKills. Otherwise two SpriteDrawCheckedBank records under SetDrawLayerNibble(0xF): the item's sprite obj+0x28C at (320, 370), flags 0xB, and the frame sprite 0x5E0 at the same point, flags 9, both at alpha 1.0 until frame 0x87 and (0x96 - n) / 15 after (0x00569198).

SpawnOriginalItemBanner(sprite): the pickup banner an Original Mode collectible raises -- ActorAlloc(OriginalItemBannerUpdate, 0x378), ActorClearGameFields, obj+0x2A0 = 0, obj+0x28C = the sprite (g_original_item_records[id] +0x08), obj+0x2C0 = 1.0, g_original_item_banner_count++. Callers: OriginalItemPropUpdate, PropUpdateType72, FUN_00466BE0 and an unfunctioned site at 0x0048DE73.

Class 0x14's Init, per g_class_handler_pairs (0x14 -> 0x00475E90): the stage-2 boss, character type 0x47 = boss2.bin. Allocates the 0xBC-byte block with ActorAllocSub (zeroed, so the phase at +0x08 starts 0 and is never written here), stores it at obj+0x1310 and g_class14_state, raises obj+0x34 bit 0x8000 at 0x00475ECF -- RegisterForShotTest skips such an actor, so the boss cannot be shot until an entrance clears it at its hand-over --, seats char type/motion (anim slot 0xB), char+0x1158 = NoOpStub, char+0x68 = 1, obj+0x124 = 30.0 at 0x00475F4F, increments g_enemies_present and g_enemies_alive, obj+0x120/+0x121 = 0xFF, RegisterEnemySlot, state = tail+1, sub 0, state+0x0C = 6.0 (0x40C00000 at 0x00475F98, the camera-point rise Class14Update passes to ActorRegisterCameraPoint), flags = 1, dir = tail+4..+0xC, route x/z = tail+0x10..+0x2C into +0x28/+0x30.. +0x54, +0x64..+0x78 = 0, track A +0x7C/+0x7E = 0x2CB, +0x80 = 0x2ED, +0x84 = 1.0, +0x82 = 0, track B +0x88/+0x8A = 0x2EE, +0x8C = 0x315, +0x8E = 0, +0x94 = 0, +0x90 = g_class14_window_timing[0].open_rate, rank = GetDamageRank, +0x97 = 0, +0x98/+0x99 = both players' lives; installs Class14Update. See docs/re/boss-hierophant.md.

Class 0x14's per-frame update. Re-seats g_class14_char/state/xform and g_cur_actor, runs Class14ResolveShotBone, dispatches g_class14_states[state+0x04] (CALL [ECX*4 + 0x596218]), runs Class14AdvanceMotionAndPublishPoints (so the play cursor advances AFTER the state), steers along the route quad with three Class14FollowSegment calls unless state+0x00 bit 0, then Class14AdvancePhase, ActorRegisterCameraPoint(state+0x0C) and Class14TrackAdaptiveRank. On g_active_cam_path == tail+0x30 and g_cam_path_frame == tail+0x32 it clears g_hit_slots[obj+0x3C] and calls ActorDespawn.

Class 0x14's shot handler, first thing in Class14Update. Returns unless obj+0x34 bit 3; picks g_hit_player_order from bits 1/2 (rand() coin when both or neither), clears bits 1..3, then walks BOTH order entries (loop 0x004762E0..0x004763C6, past the MatrixStackPop Ghidra ends the body on -- L35): for each player whose obj+0x190 byte names a bone it takes that bone's view-space hit centre (char+0xE0 + bone*0x90) into world space, and if the bone is 1 and obj+0x34 bit 0x100 is clear it calls Class14ApplyBoneDamage(obj, bone, player) (0x00476391) and raises bit 0x100 if that killed the boss; any other bone, or bit 0x100 set, gets SpawnSpriteEffect(point, 2, 1, player) and no damage. ONLY BONE 1 CAN EVER DAMAGE THE BOSS.

Class14ApplyBoneDamage(obj, bone, player). Two geometric gates, then the damage. (1) RayTestSphere(player, bone 1's view matrix char+0x130 x Translate(0, 4.0, 1.0), radius 3.5 = 0x40600000) -- a miss calls Class14SpawnNoDamageHitEffect. (2) The cone g_class14_damage_cones[state+0x88 - state+0x8A]: entry +0 == 0 (window frames 0..18) means no damage; otherwise LineSphereIntersect(5.5 = 0x40B00000, world(bone1 x T(0,3,0)), g_ShotRecords[player] origin, origin+dir), the crossing nearer the origin taken into (bone1 x T(0,3,0) x RotX(cone.rotX))^-1, pitch = atan2(-y, z) and yaw = atan2(x, z) in BAMS, pass iff |yaw| <= cone+0 and cone+4 <= pitch <= cone+6. On a pass and not yet dead: dmg = g_class14_bone_damage[rank][players-1], multiplied ONLY in g_GameMode 1 (Original) -- x2 when g_original_item_slots[player]+0x0C is -1.0, else x that factor (0x00476772..0x00476795) -- Arcade Mode takes the table value unmultiplied; capped at g_boss_shot_damage_cap; hp = ftol(hp - dmg); +0x97++; PlaySoundId(0x316A9 BLOOD03). hp < 1: DAT_009C8E10 = 0.0 (0x004767F8), obj+0x34 = (& ~0x2000) | 0x4000000, g_enemies_alive--, ScoreAddForPlayer(player, 0x5DC), BossModeRecordGrade. Else DAT_009C8E10 = hp / maxhp (FIDIV, 0x0047684E) and obj+0x34 |= 0x100 once hp <= maxhp * g_class14_phase_hp_frac[phase]. ScoreAddForPlayer(player, 10). Then SpawnBloodSpray(obj, bone, 2.0); return if obj+0x34 bit 0x40000000; unless bit 0x2000: save state/sub to +0x06/+0x07 and enter 0x11 (Class14StateKnockedDown) when in state 12/14 above ground or state 9 more than 5.0 above it, else 0x10 (Class14StateCuedMotion, +0x0C = 6.0), PlaySoundId(0x1117A9 ZOMBIE_022). +0x94 += 2 capped at 7 whether or not bit 0x2000 is set. This is the only route into either reaction and so to the deaths and every flag write.

Class14SpawnNoDamageHitEffect(bone, player): the feedback for a shot that reached Class14ApplyBoneDamage but failed its weak-point sphere or cone. Takes the bone's view-space hit centre (char+0xE0 + bone*0x90) into world space through g_camera_blocks and calls SpawnSpriteEffect(point, 2, 1, player) -- the same call Class14ResolveShotBone makes for a non-damaging bone. No damage, no score, no sound. Callers: 0x0047644D and 0x00476A12, both in Class14ApplyBoneDamage.

Class 0x14's per-frame pose, clock and draw, run after the state. THE BODY RUNS 0x00476AD0..0x00477BC7, far past the 0x00476F6F Ghidra gives it (the contact-code switch at 0x00476D21 jumps through 0x00477BC8). LightsUseSecondarySet; DrawSkinnedModelAndShadow; char+0x00++ unless obj+0x34 bit 0x4000. Unless state+0x00 bit 1: the four g_class14_foot_contacts from bone 15 (char+0x910) and bone 12 (char+0x760), foot = bone x T(0,-1.25,0), contacts at z +2.5 and -5.0, strengths from the contact code the current anim slot's g_class14_anim_cues record gives at char+0x08 (0: all 75; 1: all 150; 2/4: bone 15's pair 150/300; 3/5: bone 12's; 6: none). Unless obj+0x34 bit 0x20000 or char+0x37 bit 0: obj y moves toward the ground under the planted foot (or under itself when no contact is live) by at most 0.3 a frame (0x00476F91..0x00477080), and two-bone leg IK (Class14IkJointAngle, 9.514/8.432) is eased into state+0x64..+0x78 by Class14EaseAngleToward(0.5). Then two asset-slot flipbooks on bone 1: track A +0x7C over [+0x7E,+0x80] = 0x2CB..0x2ED (boss2.bin 2..36), ping-pong at +0x84 with 30/|rate| holds in +0x82 -- the entrances play HERTBEAT_22 on its low end; track B +0x88 over [+0x8A,+0x8C] = 0x2EE..0x315 (boss2.bin 37..76), opening at +0x90 and holding +0x8E frames from g_class14_window_timing[+0x94], forced shut while obj+0x34 bit 0x100 -- the index into g_class14_damage_cones, so it gates all damage. Draw (char+0x64 bit 0): bones 1..9, both flipbooks at bone 1, then the legs with the IK angles; LightsRestore. The "points" are the foot contacts.

Class14IkJointAngle(d2, a2, b2, a, b): the law-of-cosines joint angle in BAMS for a two-segment limb -- c = (a2 + b2 - d2) / (2ab); c >= 1.0 -> 0, c <= -1.0 -> 0x8000, c == 0 -> 0x4000, else atan(sqrt(1-c^2)/c) (+0x8000 when c < 0). Class 0x14's leg IK passes a = 9.514 (0x41183958), b = 8.432 (0x4106E979) and their squares 90.52 (0x42B5084B), 71.10 (0x428E327F). Five call sites, all in Class14AdvanceMotionAndPublishPoints's body past 0x00476F6F.

Class14EaseAngleToward(int *angle, target, k): *angle += ftol(wrap16(target - *angle) * k), the difference taken as a signed BAMS half-turn. Class 0x14's leg IK eases state+0x64..+0x78 by 0.5 a frame with it (six calls at 0x004775E2..0x00477651).

Moves an x/z position toward the line through two points by a given step, and returns 1 when it is already on the far side. Class14Update calls it three times over the descriptor's route quad, which is what keeps the boss inside its patch of water.

Class 0x14's phase ladder, called every frame from Class14Update. When obj+0x11C <= obj+0x11E * g_class14_phase_hp_frac[phase] and the state is 5, 6 or 7, it advances state+0x08: 0 -> 1 (state 10), 3 -> 4, 5 -> 6, 6 -> 7 and 8 -> 9 (all state 6). Phases 1, 2, 4, 7 and 9 are advanced or ended elsewhere. The phase is what picks which of g_script_flags 10..17 and 31 the boss raises.

Class 0x14's adaptive rank, g_class14_state+0x96, 0..15. g_players_in_play == 1: +1 when +0x97 > 0 (then cleared), and -3 -- always 3 -- when the active player's life count (0x009A5C66 + player*0x130) has fallen below the copy at +0x98+player, which it then refreshes. Any other player count: the same +1, and for BOTH players -2 while the state is 10 or 11, -3 otherwise. Clamped to 0..15. The rank indexes g_class14_bone_damage, g_class14_summon_delays_a/b and g_class14_summon_counts.

g_class14_states[0] and [3]. Sub 0 calls BossIntroBannerSpawn(0x005966B8) at 0x00478181 -- record {flag 9, cam path 0x65, 300 frames, message 0x1821} -- and sets phase 0; state 3 plays anim slot 0xE, raises g_script_flags[9], clears obj+0x34 bit 0x20000, BOMB2 and goes to sub 3; state 0 plays slot 0x13 and waits frame 0x1E, then slot 0xE at the clip end raising flag 9. Sub 3 plays ZOMBIE_007 at frame 0x37 and slot 0xF at 0x5A, falling into sub 4 (ZOMBIE_002 at char+0x00 == 0x4B). When g_bHudShutterState == 1 -- which only the banner sets on stage 2, 300 frames after flag 9 -- it hands over: state 5, target = pos, obj+0x34 &= ~0x8000, state bit 0 cleared, g_script_flags[10], BossHpBarSpawn(320.0, 35.0) at 0x00478361 and g_boss_engaged = 1. Every frame: HERTBEAT_22 when track A sits at its low end with a zero hold.

g_class14_states[1] and [4] -- the long fight. Sub 0 calls BossIntroBannerSpawn(0x005966F8) at 0x004783D6 -- {flag 9, cam path 0x69, 300, 0x1821} -- and sets phase 3; state 4 plays motion 0x26 with flag 9 and ZOMBIE_007 (sub 4); state 1 plays 0x20, obj+0x34 |= 0x8C000 and HIDES the model (char+0x64 bit 0, and the byte at *(char+0x40)+1). Sub 1 waits on g_script_flags[0x5F], which block 37's own set_script_flag 0x5F (0x014F60) raises and 0x00468EE4 clears, then g_screen_shake_frames = 0x30 and +0x9C = 0x1E. Sub 2 post-decrements +0x9C and at 0 clears 0xC000 and shows the model. Sub 3 at the clip end plays 0x26, clears 0x80000, flag 9, ZOMBIE_007. Subs 4/5 as EntranceA's 3/4, and the hand-over raises flag 10, BossHpBarSpawn(320.0, 35.0) at 0x004785EA and g_boss_engaged = 1.

g_class14_states[2] -- stage 5 block 3's cameo. No banner (the block's own script sets the shutter to 1 at 0x002268). Sub 0 plays 0x20, obj+0x34 |= 0x8C000, hides the model, phase 8, and falls into sub 1, which waits on g_script_flags[11] (raised by the script before the spawn) and then shakes (0x30) and counts 0x1E. Subs 2..5 as EntranceB's without flag 9, and the hand-over raises no flag and writes no g_boss_engaged but does call BossHpBarSpawn(320.0, 35.0) at 0x0047881D. Stage 5 block 3 therefore gates on flag 31 alone.

g_class14_states[5] -- the fight hub. Sub 0 picks the swim slot from hp and rank and clears obj+0x34 bit 0x100; sub 1 turns to face the camera and chooses: phases 0/3/8 within 55 -> state 8; 2/9 within 135 and |heading| <= 0x1FFF -> 9; 5/6/7 on the same test -> 12; each exit calls ActorPickTargetPlayer. EVERY frame, while the motion is 0x19 or 0x1A, it drives track B's hold +0x8E: in state 5, 0 when the window is shut and -1 when it is fully open; on the frame it leaves, 10 when fully open.

g_class14_states[6] -- closes on the latched target point at state+0x10. With state+0x9C zero it swims in until the point is inside 5 units and enters state 7; with state+0x9C one it follows the route quad and enters state 15 the moment Class14FollowSegment says it has left the segment.
g_class14_states[7] -- plays anim slot 8 state+0x60 times, one sound each, then returns to state 5.

g_class14_states[8] -- the melee. Sub 0: anim slot 0x15, clears obj+0x34 bit 0x100. Frames 0x1E..0x37 TURN THE BOSS (obj+0x68 -= 0xC a frame; with two attackers -0x1C or +4 by obj+0x121) -- not a camera drag. Frame 0x37 raises bit 0x2000; frame 0x3C PlayerTakeDamage(obj+0x121, 1, 6), clears 0x2000 and takes one off +0x94; the clip's last frame returns to state 6 with +0x9C = 0 and 0x10002000 cleared.

g_class14_states[9] -- phases 2 and 9's leap. Launch at clip frame 0x23 with speed = xz-distance x -0.0074074073 (phase 9) or -0.0076923077, vel.y 4.0, gravity -0.068055555, PlaySoundId(0x2A16A9 ENE_WALK7). With two attackers it turns toward the camera-space point (+/-2, 0, 0) by obj+0x121 instead (continues past the MatrixStackPop, L35). Sub 2 calls rand() (its store is overwritten the same frame) and pins track B's hold to 1 when shut, 0 otherwise. Damage within 22 of the ground, bounce, settle, state 6.

g_class14_states[10] -- phase 1's round. Sub 0 (every frame of the approach) clears all four g_water_attack_slots and draws +0xA8 = rand()&1; on arrival (local z < 15, or < 5 when resumed at sub 1) slot 0x1B, 0x100 cleared, 0x2000 raised, +0x8E = 0, +0x9C = 3. Sub 4 places one fish when g_enemies_alive < 4 AND g_screen_shake_frames == 0: r = rand()%3; if +0xA8 < r then +0xA8 = 1, x = px + dz*30 - dx*40, t = dx*30, else +0xA8 = 0, x = px - dz*40 - dx*40, t = -dx*40; z = pz - t - dz*40; y = WaterFieldSampleHeight(point) - 1.0; SpawnWaterEnemyAt(x, y, z, 100, 1). +0xAC is cleared whenever a player's lives fell this frame and gates the rank bump at the round's end. ZOMBIE_035 at frame 0x2D. Ends to state 5, phase 2.

g_class14_states[11] -- phase 4's round; raises g_script_flags[11] (0x00479C78) and [12] (0x0047A264). Sub 0 clears the four g_water_attack_slots. Sub 2 on cam path 0x6A frame 0x5F clears 0x10100 and sets +0x8E = 0. Sub 6 places one fish when alive < 4 and g_screen_shake_frames == 0 with THREE rand() draws: a = rand()%11 + 15, b = (rand()&15) + 15, r = rand()%3; if +0xA8 < r then +0xA8 = 1, x = px + b*dx + a*dz, z = pz + b*dz - a*dx, else +0xA8 = 0, x = px + b*dx - a*dz, z = pz + b*dz + a*dx; y = WaterFieldSampleHeight - 10.0; SpawnWaterEnemyAt(x, y, z, 0x50, 2). Sub 9 swims to (270 or 190 by +0x9C, its own y, -2150), turning while ActorPointIsAhead is 0 and advancing (obj+0x34 |= 0x10000) once it is 1. Ends to state 13, phase 5 on path 0x6B frame 100.

g_class14_states[12] -- phases 5/6/7's leap. As Class14StateLungeAtCamera over motion 0x33 with one launch factor (-0.0076923077), ENE_WALK7 at launch, the two-attacker offset +/-3, the same rand() and track-B pin in sub 2, and state 6 at the end.

g_class14_states[13]. Puts the boss at x = (route1.x + route2.x)/2 -/+ 65 by +0x9C (motion 0x38/0x39), z = state+0x18 -- the LATCHED TARGET's z, not a route corner --, yaw from atan2(-dir.x, -dir.z), y on the ground; clears 0x84000. Class 0x25's bytecode VM, and the second-largest class in the game at 142 spawns. Walks 8-byte commands -- {s16 op, s16 mode, s16 a, s16 b}, or 16 bytes when the command carries a point -- running them until one blocks; a command that cannot proceed leaves the cursor where it is and falls through to the per-frame tail, so a run of setup commands all take effect in one frame and only a wait costs one. 19 opcodes: 0/1/4 wait on a condition (frame count, camera path+frame, motion frame, script flag, or the point test in mode 4) -- and 0 and 1 differ in what they leave behind: obj+0x1324 is set to the OPCODE, and that word is the freeze flag the draw routine tests, so op 0 lets the animation run and op 1 holds the pose. MODE 4 PROCEEDS WHEN THE ACTOR HAS MOVED AWAY FROM THE POINT, not toward it: 0x004845FD FCOMPP compares |prev-point| against |pos-point| and 0x00484601 TEST AH,1 / JZ 0x00484A7B blocks unless C0 is set, i.e. unless the PREVIOUS distance was the smaller one. Mode 2 on op 0 can never fire -- CMP BP,BX / JZ at 0x004843CD (the arm the mode table at 0x00484CF8 sends mode 2 to; 0x00484386 is the JMP through that table) tests the opcode itself and jumps to the blocked path when it is zero -- and no shipped command uses it. 2/3 set the motion (2 is ActorSetMotion plus a phase into obj+0x194, -1 meaning rand()%%10; 3 is ActorSetMotionBlended with b as the start cursor and MODE as the fade length), 5/6/7 turn, 8 sets the position, 9 and 16 swap models from per-character tables, 10 skips an arm to the next -2 unless the player count matches, 11 rides an op_ object path through CamEvalObjectPath6 on the CAMERA's frame, 13 plays a sound, 14 sets the hand-prop draw mode at obj+0x1330, 15 jumps, 18 is ActorKill and -1 falls into ScriptedHumanoidIdle. Op 17 is FIVE DIFFERENT THINGS and only three of them leave: mode 0 installs ScriptedHumanoidFallAndSplash (0x00484DF0), mode 1 ScriptedHumanoidLaunchAndDrop (0x00484EA0), mode 4 ScriptedHumanoidFallTimed (0x00484F90, after obj+0x50 = -0.408); mode 2 calls ScriptedHumanoidSpawnFixedImpact (0x00484F50) and mode 3 spawns sprite effect 0x41 sub-type 2 at a hardcoded point -- (-189.3, -24.9, -1505.0) in block 9, (-1264.0, -24.9, -1353.0) elsewhere, immediates c33d4ccd/c1c73333/c4bc2000 and c49e0000/c1c73333/c4a92000 at 0x00484A05 and 0x00484A1F -- and BOTH of those stay in the VM and run the next command; a mode above 4 (or negative -- JA at 0x004849D5 is unsigned) steps past the command and ends the frame (CL is cleared at the loop head 0x00484360). The per-frame tail runs the turn, the path follow and the draw.

It also draws a per-spawn decoration chosen by tail+0x06: 1 and 2 are fixed props at hardcoded points, 3 rides an op_ object path, and 4 draws only while g_active_cam_path is 0x93. The body and the decoration are both skipped while g_screen_furniture_flags bit 0x20 (the chapter card's) is set -- TEST AL,0x20 at 0x00484FF8, JNZ 0x0048523A -- but that target is the tick, not the RET, so the motion frame still advances behind a card. Every decoration arm reaches the same tick: 1, 2 and 4 through the shared draw at 0x0048522B, 3 by JMP at 0x004851F3. The pseudocode's returns after those MatrixStackPop calls are Ghidra's (L35), and its case 3 also drops the mirrored 0x24A flipbook pair at 0x0048515A..0x004851F0.

Class 0x25's per-bone draw callback, installed at obj+0x12EC by ScriptedHumanoidInit (0x004841AD writes 0x485260 into model+0x1158). Takes the skeleton node in EBX and switches on its bone index at node+0x14. obj+0x1364 non-zero with bone 2 calls ScriptedHumanoidAimHeadAtCamera (FUN_00485BA0); obj+0x1330 == 2 or == 1 select which hand prop to draw, each indexing a 13-byte cel table (g_class25_bone_prop_cels / _alt) by (obj+0x1334 %% 13), adding the cel to a per-character asset-slot base (0x14B3/0x14C3/0x14DA/0x14E1/0x1273/0xD28/0xC3A/0x149D by character type) and drawing it through FUN_00418560, then incrementing obj+0x1334. This is the reader that makes obj+0x1330 a DRAW MODE for class 0x25 -- ScriptedHumanoidDraw (0x00484FF0) never reads it, which had been taken to mean nothing did. It also reads byte obj+0x131B and word obj+0x1F4. op 12 mode 1 seeds the two angles through ScriptedHumanoidSeedHeadAim (FUN_00485D70) as it sets the flag. It also draws slot 0xE24 FADED on one bone for three frames through AssetDrawSlotWithAlpha (0x0048574F, 0x004857F9, 0x00485861, 0x004858D1): during clip 0x32D or 0x355 at play frames 1..3, and during 0x35D at 0x26..0x28, 0x40..0x42 and 0x58..0x5A, at alpha 1.0 - (frame - first) * 0.3 ([0x004C4D10] = 0x3E99999A, [0x004C4380] = 1.0), calling FUN_00485DE0 on each run's first frame. Not ported: the port draws none of this hook's extra models.

Class 0x25's twin of ActorAimHeadAtCamera, called by ScriptedHumanoidBoneDrawHook at 0x0048529C for bone 2 while obj+0x1364 != 0. The same stepping -- TurnAngleToward at 0xC0, kept inside AngleWithinTolerance 0x4000 of 0 (pitch) and of centre = (obj+0x68 - 0x8000) & 0xFFFF (yaw), stepped back toward them otherwise -- on DIFFERENT words: pitch obj+0x1368, yaw obj+0x136C. The point is the same (bone record +0x68 through the camera block's view-to-world), but the target is inline, with no two-attacker arm: VecToAngles(eye.x - pt.x, eye.y + 15.0 - pt.y, eye.z - pt.z), and its yaw is offset by -0x8000 (ADD ECX, 0xFFFF8000 at 0x00485C87) before the mask. And the rotation is ABSOLUTE: MatrixClearRotation (FUN_004A9F70) wipes the bone matrix's 3x3, then MatrixRotateY(obj+0x136C), MatrixRotateX(obj+0x1368) -- no MatrixRotateY(-centre). The same CALL_RETURN override sat on its MatrixStackPop call at 0x00485C38 and is cleared the same way. Seeded by ScriptedHumanoidSeedHeadAim. obj+0x1364 has three writers in class 0x25's code -- ScriptedHumanoidInit at 0x00484229 beside +0x1368 and +0x1360, and op 12's two arms at 0x004848BE (1) and 0x004848DE (0) -- and op 12 is in no exported class-0x25 program. Not ported. [proved]

(obj) -- class 0x25's head-aim seed, the twin of the two combat Inits' inline one: VecToAngles(g_camera_eye_x - obj.x, (g_camera_eye_y + 15.0) - obj.y, g_camera_eye_z - obj.z), then obj+0x1368 = pitch & 0xFFFF and obj+0x136C = (yaw - 0x8000) & 0xFFFF -- the same half-turn offset ScriptedHumanoidAimHeadAtCamera puts on its target. Its one caller is ScriptedHumanoidUpdate's op 12 at 0x004848C8, mode 1, beside setting obj+0x1364 = 1, which is the flag ScriptedHumanoidBoneDrawHook aims bone 2 under. op 12 is in none of the 274 class-0x25 programs the twelve exported bundles carry, so neither runs in the retail data as exported. [proved]

Zeroes the per-player Original Mode block at g_original_item_slots, stride 0x14: both item slots to -1, +0x02 the player index, +0x03 1, +0x04 3, +0x05 5, +0x06 0, +0x07 0, +0x08 the magazine size 6, +0x09 the weapon kind 0, +0x0C 1.0f. This is what proves +0x08 and +0x09 are fields of that block and not two loose bytes.

Class 0x10, the civilian. ActorAllocSub(0xC4) at obj+0x1310; the descriptor tail at obj+0x130C gives the character type (+0x00), the g_civilian_scripts index (+0x01), the removal cue (+0x02/+0x04/+0x06), a part list (+0x08) and a child count and array (+0x0C/+0x10). Every child is SpawnFromDescriptor'd and parented at child+0x1394, and its hit points are scaled by g_hp_percent_by_rank -- those children are the zombies holding the civilian, and nothing in the evt instruction stream points at their descriptors.

Class 0x10's per-frame entry. Prunes dead children, runs the sub+0x5C frame hook, turns toward the target, steps op 0x26's move, counts the clip's loops, calls CivilianStepScript and re-enters CivilianRunScript when it says so, then the shot branch, the queued sound and the removal countdown. The shot branch pays -100 to the shooter (or to both on a killing shot), calls PlayerTakeDamageTimed and switches to the sub+0x4C script. THEN, ON EVERY PATH THAT DOES NOT DESPAWN (all branches rejoin at 0x0048AD97), PUSH 0x40800000 / CALL ActorRegisterCameraPoint at 0x0048ADAB..0x0048ADB0 -- which tail-calls RegisterForCameraTracking at 0x00409C03 -- so a civilian is a CAMERA CANDIDATE whenever obj+0x34 bit 0x10000 is clear, i.e. in every block whose wait word carries 0x40000. While she holds a g_enemy_slots entry CameraDriverSelectMode stays in mode 3, g_camera_free stays 0 and wait ops 0x43/0x44/0x46/0x47 hold: this is how the room waits for a rescued civilian's lines (bug 18). [proved] THE REMOVAL ARMS, 0x0048AF8E..0x0048B0C8, in order [proved]: (1) g_cutscene_skipping && !(word & 0x20000000) -> sub+0x2A = 1; (2) else if sub+0x2A: count it down, and at zero despawn unless children remain (then sub+0x2A = 1); (3) else if g_active_cam_path == sub+0x26 && g_cam_path_frame == sub+0x28: sub+0x2A = tail+0x06; (4) else if word & 0x2000000 && !ActorBoundsOnScreen(obj) && g_scene_state_major_entered != 2 && no children: despawn now. Each despawn frees the hit slot, ActorReleasePartList, leaves g_civilians_alive unless sub+0x04 bit 0 says it already did, and ActorDespawn. THE SPHERE SWITCH, 0x0048ADB5..0x0048AF83, after ActorRegisterCameraPoint (which has already published last frame's obj+0x12C through RegisterForShotTest): MOVSX byte sub+0x80 (op 0x17; CivilianInit writes 2), CMP 3 / JA past, table 0x0048B12C. 0 (0x0048ADDB): obj+0x12C = obj+0x40. 1 (0x0048ADFC), 2 (0x0048AE60): MatrixStackSetTopFromArray(g_camera_blocks[g_camera_index]) (view to world), MatrixMultiply(model + 0x1C0 / 0x130), MatrixGetTranslation -> obj+0x12C. 3 (0x0048AEC4): the same for model+0x910 and model+0x760, obj+0x12C = (a + b) * 0.5 (0x004C43AC = 0x3F000000). model = g_cur_actor_model = obj+0x194, so the offsets are BYTE offsets model+0xA0+bone*0x90 = the matrix SkeletonEmitNode stores at record+0x28 (record = obj+0x20C+bone*0x90): bones 2, 1, 15 and 12. Each arm is therefore that bone's origin in the world, drawn by DrawSkinnedModelAndShadow at 0x0048AA02 earlier in this same routine. Ghidra's pseudocode shows the offsets as int* indices (0x70, 0x4C, 0x244, 0x1D8), which is how they were once misread as non-record matrices. Any other mode writes nothing. [proved]

Class 0x10's other entry, installed when the descriptor's +0x22 is non-zero. Pushes the carrier object's (sub+0x68) translate/rotate around a call to CivilianUpdate, so the civilian rides it; when the carrier dies it copies the position out and swaps itself for CivilianUpdate.

Decides whether class 0x10's parked wait command is over, and if so walks the cursor to the next one. Every bit of the wait word is a REASON TO KEEP WAITING, so the conjunction reads inverted: it breaks out when all the reasons still hold. **LAB_0048B52E is one label reached from three places** and holds the tail all the arrival arms share -- the in-front test (bit 0x40, against the RAW sub+0x30..0x38 target, not the mode-resolved point the reach and turn tests build), then the camera cue (0x80) and the in-play gate (0x40000000), then the timer at sub+0x14. A word with neither 0x10 nor 0x20 jumps straight there; the 0x20 arm goes there when the heading error is not yet zero; the 0x10 arm goes there while the actor is outside sub+0x3C. Splitting that tail per-arm is a bug: a word carrying 0x40 alone then runs no test at all and only its timer can release it. On success it zeroes the target mode at sub+0x40 (LAB_0048B67E) before advancing.  BIT 0x1000 IS THREE CONDITIONS, NOT ONE, and the whole arm is gated on the scene-state major: 0048b2f8 TEST BH,0x10 (f6c710) / 0048b2fb JZ 0048b320 -- bit clear, no arm / 0048b2fd CMP dword ptr [0x009c6f08],0x2 (833d086f9c0002) = g_scene_state_major_entered / 0048b304 JNZ 0048b320 -- not row 2, so the bit holds nothing / 0048b306 MOV AL,byte ptr [0x009c6f2f] = g_camera_settled / 0048b30b TEST AL,AL / 0048b30d JNZ 0048b621 -- resume the script / 0048b313 MOV AL,byte ptr [0x009c6f2d] = g_camera_free / 0048b318 TEST AL,AL / 0048b31a JNZ 0048b621 -- resume the script. So the bit releases on g_camera_settled OR g_camera_free -- the same pair EvtOpWaitTargetsClear47 accepts, which is what makes it a rule rather than one routine's habit -- and only while g_scene_state_major_entered is 2, the cam/ path camera row IsPlayerAttackable also demands. [proved] The browser port read g_camera_settled alone, and CameraTrackEnemiesTick only raises that while nothing is tracked, so a civilian whose room still held one g_enemy_slots entry could never be released: stage 2 block 9's wait_script_flag 3 is raised by such a civilian (class 0x10 stream 19, op 0x1C arg 3) and hung for ever. Bit 0x8000 is tested nowhere in this function, so it is not a wait condition here; [open] what reads it.

Walks class 0x10's stream from one wait command to the next, applying ONLY the opcodes a wait condition reads -- the clip and its loop count, the target point, the timer, the three count goals, the camera cue, the frame hook and the script-flag index. A block CivilianStepScript skips still has to leave those in place; its sounds, dialogue and score are not conditions and are not run.

Class 0x10's action VM. Dword commands, per-opcode length, opcodes 0x00-0x2C; stops before any opcode above 0x2B and parks the cursor at sub+0x48. Op 0x2C loads the wait word (masking off 0x04000000) and, when it carries 0x10000000, pays ScoreAddForPlayer 400 -- to sub+0x6C's player, or to both when that is -1. That is the rescue award. Op 0x10 installs a native per-frame hook which decides its own command length. OPS 0x00 AND 0x01 CARRY THE ROOT-MOTION SWITCH: inside their 'is this a different clip' test they write model+0x64 bit 1 from bit 0x00100000 of the wait word -- (*g_cur_civilian & 0x100000) ? (model+0x64 | 2) : (model+0x64 & 0xfffffffd) -- which is exactly the gate SkeletonApplyRootMotion (FUN_00410C50) tests. So a civilian's clip carries her only in the blocks whose wait word asks for it: 289 of the 596 shipped wait commands set the bit, 297 do not, and the write happens only on a clip CHANGE. Op 0x27 is the only command that touches model+0x116C, storing its operand verbatim into that float field (one instance in the shipped scripts, 0x42480000 = 50.0); ops 0x1B/0x23/0x24/0x25 do not touch it. [proved] OP 0x1B IS THE HUD SHUTTER, and through it the firing gate: 'CMP dword ptr [0x009c8e98],0xA / JZ / MOV DL,byte ptr [ESI+0x4] / MOV byte ptr [0x009ca0f4],DL' at 0x0048BF0A-0x0048BF16 -- a BYTE store of the low byte of a dword operand into g_bHudShutterState, skipped only while g_app_state is 10. HudDrawShutterState (0x00413970) picks the change up on its next draw and raises g_nFiringGate for a 1 or drops it at the end of a 3, so a CIVILIAN'S SCRIPT CAN GIVE THE PLAYER THE GUN BACK inside a letterboxed scene. 60 of the shared table's commands run it, 30 with 1 and 30 with 3. That is what makes stage 1 block 1 step 8's wait_enemies_alive clearable: the script closes the shutter at step 6 and never reopens it, and the mauled civilian's own killed script does. [proved]

Class 0x10's pose step: blends the clip, takes the root translation off the pol file's own frame, and turns the body by the difference between two bone directions. Driven by wait-word bits 0x8000/0x10000/0x18000/0x20000/0x200000.

Class 0x10's per-frame turn, run by CivilianUpdate whenever sub+0x40 (the target mode) is non-zero. Resolves the target the same way the wait tests do -- the camera for mode -1, the actor's position mirrored through the camera for any other negative, sub+0x30..0x38 for a positive one, and for a civilian riding a carrier it pulls the point into the carrier's frame first -- then calls ActorTurnTowardPoint with a **literal 0x100** cap. It does NOT read sub+0x0E: op 3 writes that field and nothing in the turn consults it, so a port that passes it instead turns every civilian at the op's default of ten, twenty-five times too slowly.

Turn an actor's yaw toward a point by at most cap BAMS. Builds the inverse of the actor's orientation (-ry, -rz, -rx), transforms actor MINUS target through it -- that order, not target minus actor -- takes fpatan of the transformed x and z as a s16, clamps it to +/-cap and adds it to xform+0x28. It also writes the transformed point back over its second argument, so the caller's local is clobbered; no shipped caller reads it afterwards.

Compacts class 0x10's child array, dropping every child whose obj+0x34 carries 0x4000000 and remembering that child's obj+0x131C in sub+0x6C -- which is the player the rescue pays. Wait bit 0x04 blocks until the array is shorter than sub+0x20.
Op 0x13: grow class 0x10's held-item array by one and append the command's two operands.
Op 0x14: the same, but the first operand is whatever CivilianPickHeldItem last chose (sub+0x74).
Op 0x15: walk a {weight, record} list terminated by weight -1, pick one with rand() %% total, store it at sub+0x74 and preload its two assets. The second comes from a per-kind table at 0x0056B0F4.
Draws class 0x10's held items, each on the bone the character type's attach set (sub+0x82) names. Compacts the array when an item raises the wait word's 0x400000.

The only other per-frame pose hook in the program. Ramps the actor's radius (obj+0x128) toward a target and pushes it out of world collision along the hit normal. It does NOT rotate any bone -- see the note on upper-body aim in docs/formats/combat.md. Installed at model+0x115C by CivilianInit (0x0048A61B) and called from SkeletonApplyRootMotion (CALL [ECX+0x115C] at 0x00410E93, which both of its arms reach -- the root-motion arm past a MatrixStackPop Ghidra marks no-return), i.e. inside the draw at the top of CivilianUpdate. The push traces obj+0x12C AS IT STANDS (LEA EDX,[ESI+0x12C] at 0x0048D0F8) with radius obj+0x128, so it measures the centre CivilianUpdate's switch wrote on the previous frame; nothing here derives one. [proved]

Plays the voice a shot civilian cries out. sub+0x81 selects directly; 0xFF picks by character type -- 0x24/0x25/0x2E/0x31-0x33 -> 0x2000001A, 0x21/0x22 -> 0x20000011, 0x26-0x2C -> 0x2000000B, 0x20/0x23/0x2D -> 0x2000000D, else 0x20000012. Those five ids are COM\\220_Y_M, COM\\209_M, COM\\190_Y_W, COM\\207_OLD_W and COM\\200_C -- which is what proves the class is civilians.
Op 0x10 hook: zero the y velocity, set obj+0x5C to -0.02722 and install CivilianHookFallStep. Consumes two dwords.

Per-frame: obj+0x50 += obj+0x5C, obj+0x44 += obj+0x50, and when QueryGroundHeightAt(x, y+100, z) is at or above the new height, snap to it, raise sub+0x18 (which wait bit 0x400 waits for) and uninstall.
Op 0x10 hook: install CivilianHookRideChildrenStep. Consumes two dwords.

Per-frame: averages the surviving children's positions and turns the civilian toward it with ActorTurnTowardPoint capped at 0x80 BAMS -- a facing, not a carry. Uninstalls itself once the object is flagged dead, and does NOT raise sub+0x18, so wait bit 0x400 never ends on this one.
Op 0x10 hook: take one dword as the launch y speed, raise obj+0x34 bit 0x80000 and install the fall step. Consumes three dwords.
Op 0x10 hook: take three dwords as a whole launch velocity and install the fall step. Consumes five dwords.
Builds the 0x1314-byte decal object a shot civilian leaves, scaled by how far below the camera plane the point is, and picks asset 0x132D or 0x132E by which player fired.

Class 0x26's handler. Switches on the s16 at obj+0x11C (0..7), calls the chosen update once and installs it at obj+0x00, so this runs exactly once per spawn. obj+0x11C is the subtype here, not hit points.

Stream: returns at once if already playing; else sets (loop == 1) or clears flags bit 0x08000000 -- the bit SoundStreamThread tests at end of file -- and Play(0, 0, DSBPLAY_LOOPING), the ring always looping.
