Stop a channel's buffer without rewinding it; channel state bits -> 0x20000. SoundCommand(_, 0x2A0) sends channel 0xF here and 0x3A0 restarts it with SoundChannelStartBuffer(0xF, 1). [likely] a pause: the pairing with 0x3A0 and the absence of any rewind are proved, the name is inference
Stop a channel and put it back at its start: static buffer Stop + SetCurrentPosition(0); stream SoundStreamRewind. Channel state bits -> 0x10000. [proved]
Stop the buffer if playing, seek the file to the channel's +0x3C (the first sample), refill the whole ring (SoundStreamFill) and SetCurrentPosition(0). [proved]

Lock a ring region and ReadFile into it; on a short read (end of FILE) either seek to +0x3C and read the rest (loop bit 0x08000000) or fill silence. Called by SoundChannelOpenWav for the first fill, while the loop bit is still clear. [proved]

SoundChannelOpenWav(ch, name, flags, ringMs): walks RIFF counting bytes into +0x3C (RIFF tag+size, bare WAVE, fmt tag+size+body, other chunks skipped by size with no pad, stops at data +4) -- so +0x3C is the file offset of the first sample. flags&1 streams: ring = nAvgBytesPerSec*ringMs/1000 rounded up to 64, notify at half and end-2, SoundStreamThread. Channel 0xF is opened (0xF, name, 1, 3000). [proved]

Streaming channel thread. On each half-ring notify: Lock the half just played, ReadFile half a ring. Short read = END OF FILE (not end of data chunk): if +0x40 & 0x08000000 (loop), SetFilePointer(+0x3C) and read the rest into the same lock -- a gapless wrap to the first sample, with any trailing chunk bytes played as PCM and no frame alignment; else silence, then after one more half SoundStreamRewind and stop. [proved] 0x004A4991 / 0x004A4AAF

Creates the D3DX context and device, then sets texture stage 0 once for the life of the device: MAGFILTER 1 (POINT), MIPFILTER 2, COLOROP 4 MODULATE, COLORARG1 2 TEXTURE, COLORARG2 0 DIFFUSE, ALPHAOP 4 MODULATE, ALPHAARG1 2 TEXTURE, ALPHAARG2 0 DIFFUSE; stage 1 COLOROP and ALPHAOP 1 DISABLE (the pushes at 0x004A4F20..0x004A4FDD). Nothing re-sets the six ARG states for meshes (DrawSpriteQuadCommand swaps ARG1 to TFACTOR only for an untextured quad and back), so a textured mesh's alpha is always TEXTURE alpha, alone (ALPHAOP SELECTARG1, mode 1) or times the material diffuse alpha (MODULATE). Then fog mode by caps (FOGTABLEMODE or FOGVERTEXMODE LINEAR), CULLMODE 3, ALPHAREF 1, ALPHAFUNC 7, ALPHATESTENABLE 1, ZWRITEENABLE 1, ZENABLE, TEXTUREFACTOR 0xFF000000, SHADEMODE 2, ALPHABLENDENABLE 1, and EnumerateDeviceTextureFormats. [proved]

The IDirect3DDevice7::EnumTextureFormats callback EnumerateDeviceTextureFormats installs. Files each DDPIXELFORMAT the device offers into one of the eight 0x20-byte slots of g_texture_formats (0x007DEBD0), and returns 1 (keep going), so the LAST match wins: PALETTEINDEXED4 -> 0, PALETTEINDEXED8 -> 1; then only DDPF_RGB with no FourCC and no LUMINANCE/BUMP bits: 16-bit F800/07E0/001F -> 2 (R5G6B5); 16-bit 7C00/03E0/001F -> 5 when DDPF_ALPHAPIXELS (TEST BL,1 at 0x004A5CD0) else 3 -- so A1R5G5B5 and X1R5G5B5 are kept apart; 16-bit 0F00/00F0/000F -> 6 with NO test of DDPF_ALPHAPIXELS; 32-bit FF0000/FF00/FF -> 7; 24-bit -> 4. Slot 6 carries alpha on any device that enumerates A4R4G4B4 as its 4:4:4 format [likely: DX7 drivers list A4R4G4B4; DecodeTextureToSurface's PAL4 arm writes an alpha nibble into this format]. [proved]
dev->EnumTextureFormats(EnumTextureFormatsCallback, 0): fills g_texture_formats once, from InitD3DDeviceAndTextureStages. [proved]

CreateSurfaceInTextureFormat(w, h, slot): a DDSURFACEDESC2 (0x7C, flags 0x111007) of w x h whose pixel format is g_texture_formats[slot] copied whole, created through FUN_004A5ED0 (a texture directly when w and h are powers of two, else a system-memory offscreen surface). Returns 0 when the device enumerated nothing for that slot. DecodeTextureToSurface's only surface maker. [proved]

PromoteSurfaceToTexture(surf, flags): returns surf as is when GetCaps says DDSCAPS_TEXTURE; otherwise reads its desc (Lock/Unlock), creates a power-of-two DDSCAPS_TEXTURE surface in the SAME DDPIXELFORMAT, Blts surf into it and releases surf unless flags & 1. The format is never changed, so what DecodeTextureToSurface wrote -- alpha bits included -- is what the device samples. [proved]

BindTextureStage(stage, tex): IDirect3DDevice7::SetTexture(stage, tex) unless tex is g_bound_texture (0x007DECD0), the one-entry cache of the last texture bound. Nothing else -- no stage state, no alpha. [proved]
sprintf("%s", name); CreateFileA(GENERIC_READ, FILE_SHARE_READ, OPEN_EXISTING). [proved]

Starts a new task list and calls the builder it is given, which allocates the tasks into it; returns the list. LoadSceneAndReset, the title, the attract scenes and each game-over phase build theirs through it. [proved]

Allocates an object of param_2 bytes running param_1 and links it into the task ring. It zeroes exactly the first 0xD dwords -- the task header -- and writes eight header fields; everything from obj+0x34 up is left as FUN_004A7400 returned it, a free-list split that does not clear. Every spawn allocator that builds a game object calls ActorClearGameFields (0x004A73D0) on the very next line, which zeroes that body: SpawnThrownWeapon at 0x004504F8 and ZombieThrowHandWeapon at 0x0045A259 are two. An older note here concluded that a thrown weapon's tumble rate obj+0x135C was the previous occupant's memory; it is cleared, and then written by both launchers.

unlinks the actor and longjmps; does not return. It rewrites its neighbours' links (prev +0x1C, next +0x18) and its parent's head/tail (+0x28/+0x2C) and pushes itself on the free list through +0x14, but it leaves its OWN next pointer (+0x1C) alone -- and TaskRunTree reads that pointer after the longjmp lands, so the walk carries on to whatever followed the killed task, including one it allocated in its last frame. That is why a class-0x41 placer's object runs on the frame the placer made it and died.

One frame of the task tree, depth first: the +0x28 child list (0x004A71AD), then this task's own handler through slot 0, then the +0x24 child list (0x004A7210) -- each walked from the head via +0x1c, the next pointer read AFTER the child's recursive call returns (0x004A71C3). An earlier reading had the two lists the other way round; the disassembly is unambiguous. The handler is skipped for one frame, and the flag cleared, when the low byte of +0x32 is 0xFF (0x004A71F5). ActorAlloc (0x004A6FA0) appends at the parent's tail (+0x2c; +0x28 is the head), so EXECUTION ORDER IS CREATION ORDER, and a task allocated during the walk is reached on the same frame -- even when its allocator then ActorKills itself, because ActorKill leaves the killed task's own +0x1c intact. That is what puts EvtInterpreterLoop before EvtRunQueuedActions every frame (created first and third by the scene task list at 0x00460710), and therefore what makes a camera action retired by CamAdvancePathFrame invisible to the script until the next frame.
Makes the given list current and runs TaskRunTree over it. [proved]

Zeroes the actor from obj+0x34 to the end of the allocation, taking the size from the heap block header (uVar1 = -*(int *)(obj - 0x10) - 0x44). Run immediately after ActorAlloc by all three spawn allocators, which is what divides the struct: obj+0x00..0x33 is ActorAlloc's own task control block (+0x00 the update function, +0x08 a serial, +0x0C alive, +0x14 the free-list link, +0x18/+0x1C/+0x20 next/prev/list head, +0x30 a u16) and obj+0x34 onward is the game struct. No class may use anything below 0x34.

Device state once: ZENABLE 1, ALPHAREF 1, ALPHAFUNC 7 GREATEREQUAL, ALPHATESTENABLE 1 (then per mesh by TranslatePvr2StateToD3D), DITHER 1, SPECULAR 1, COLORVERTEX 0, TEXTUREFACTOR 0xFF000000, COLORKEYBLEND 0, the four material sources 0 (D3DMCS_MATERIAL), CULLMODE 1 NONE, SHADEMODE 2 GOURAUD; SetTransform(2 VIEW, g_view_flip_z = diag(1,1,-1,1)) -- so eye space on the matrix stack looks down -z and a point in front of the camera has negative z; seeds the TranslatePvr2StateToD3D cache (ISP 0xD0000000, TSP 0x20800000), g_draw_layer_nibble = 8 and the sprite layer 0x007E78B8 = 0; stores the command-queue buffers (0x007E78C8 count, 0x007E78C4 base). [proved]

One mesh's PVR2 words (parameter_control, isp_tsp, tsp, texture_control) to D3D7 state, each change only when its bits differ from the previous mesh's (cache at 0x007E7928..34, seeded by RenderInitStates). ISP 31-29 -> ZFUNC (0x17) through g_ZFuncTable; ISP 26 inverted -> ZWRITEENABLE (0x0E); TSP 31-29 -> SRCBLEND (0x13) through g_SrcBlendTable; TSP 28-26 -> DESTBLEND (0x14) through g_DstBlendTable; TSP 23 inverted -> FOGENABLE (0x1C); (tsp & 0x180000) != 0x80000 -> state 0x0F, which is ALPHATESTENABLE (D3DRENDERSTATE 15), NOT ALPHABLENDENABLE (27) as this row used to say -- blending is switched per pass, by RenderBeginCommandList (off) and RenderFlushCommandList (on); TSP clamp/flip -> ADDRESSU/V through g_TexAddressModeTable; TSP 7-6 -> COLOROP MODULATE always, ALPHAOP SELECTARG1 for mode 1 else MODULATE; TSP 14-13 -> MAG/MINFILTER point or linear. Over all 82,494 meshes in pol/ ISP bit 26 is clear and the compare mode is 4 (LESSEQUAL), so every mesh, translucent ones included, writes depth. TSP bit 19 (IgnoreTexAlpha) is read here and in WalkMeshChainAndDraw only as half of the 0x180000 pair -- no other instruction in the D3D path tests it, and nothing reaches the texture: the texture's alpha goes into the alpha op in every pass, and only the pass's state (blend off, test off in pass 0) decides whether it shows. The mode jump table at 0x004A79C8 is {0x004A792E, 0x004A790F, 0x004A792E, 0x004A792E}. [proved]

Opens the frame's command list: the queue pointer DAT_007e78c0 = DAT_007e78c4 + ((DAT_007e78c8 + 3) & ~3) * 4 -- past the pointer array RenderInitStates was given -- and SetRenderState(0x1B ALPHABLENDENABLE, 0) (PUSH 0 / AND AL,0xFC / PUSH 0x1B at 0x004A7A1E), so every opaque-pass draw RenderEnqueueCommand makes during the frame is unblended. Called only from FUN_004ABF00, which runs before the scene draws. RenderFlushCommandList turns blending back on for the translucent pass. [proved]
A quad command with bit 31 of its first word is copied into the deferred list at 0x007E78C0; anything else goes straight to DrawSpriteQuadCommand. [proved]

One screen quad as a D3D TL triangle strip (DrawPrimitive 5, FVF 0x1C4). Half extents texW*sx/2, texH*sy/2; corners from g_sprite_quad_corners (1,3),(3,3),(1,1),(3,1) minus the anchor (1,1 by default), so (x,y) is the TOP-LEFT and y grows down; vertex 0 at (x, y+H) takes (u0,v0) and vertex 2 at (x, y) takes (u0,v1). So texture row 0 is drawn at the BOTTOM of the sprite: every screen texture is stored upside down relative to the image it shows, which is why a naive decode of tex/scr_common.bin reads 'RELOAD' inverted. [proved]

Submits one model command. Unless bit 31 of the key is set it draws the opaque part immediately (WalkMeshChainAndDraw(cmd, 0)) and returns if nothing translucent is left; otherwise copies the 0x1D-dword command into the queue with key |= the current draw layer nibble (DAT_007E78BC, SetDrawLayerNibble) | 0x40000000 and +4 = the sort depth DAT_007E7938. RenderFlushCommandList then sorts the queue by that nibble ascending, depth descending. [proved]

WalkMeshChainAndDraw(cmd, pass)  The NL1 mesh-chain renderer. cmd is a 0x1D-dword draw command; cmd[3] (+0x0C) is the model pointer and cmd+0x34 is a 4x4 world matrix, installed with SetTransform(D3DTRANSFORMSTATE_WORLD).  Called twice per command: pass 0 draws opaque meshes, pass 1 translucent. The selector is     is_translucent = (tsp_instruction & 0x180000) != 0x80000 i.e. a mesh is opaque only when IgnoreTexAlpha is set and UseAlpha is clear. DAT_007E7940 non-zero collapses both passes into one.  Per mesh: ComputeSphereVisibility on the mesh bounding sphere (dev+0x84); invisible or wrong-pass meshes are skipped with (mesh_data_size >> 2) + 0x14 dwords and only contribute their transformed Z to the sort key.  Per strip, from the strip control word (NOT parameter_control):     & 0x80  reuse previous global parameters -- skips the state change             entirely, so the strip's own bits 0-1 and 6 are IGNORED and the             previous strip's culling / shade mode stand     & 3     CULLMODE via g_CullModeTable = {NONE, NONE, CCW, CW}     & 0x40  SHADEMODE: 1 FLAT / 2 GOURAUD    <- per strip, not per mesh     & 8     triangle list (count is a triangle count) vs triangle strip     & 0x20  super index: records may be back-references, so each is copied             into a scratch buffer; without it the model's vertices are handed             to D3D directly as a contiguous array     & 4     sprite/quad -- NEVER TESTED. 23.5% of strips set it; it has no             effect in this port.  Submission is always     DrawPrimitive(D3DPT_TRIANGLESTRIP|LIST, 0x112, verts, count, 0) FVF 0x112 = XYZ | NORMAL | TEX1: 32 bytes, two f32 UVs at dwords 6-7, taken verbatim from the model file. There is no 16-bit UV path and no texture coordinate generation anywhere in this port.  The `global_flag & 0x10` branch (2-dword back-reference / 14-dword inline) is dead: no model in the game sets that bit.  The sort depth: DAT_007E7938 (g_render_sort_depth) is seeded from cmd+4 -- the modelview _43, the model origin's eye z -- and every mesh the pass skips (the wrong pass, or the right pass with ComputeSphereVisibility's clip-intersection bits & 0xFFF000 set, 0x004A7F81) lowers it to M[2]*cx + M[6]*cy + M[10]*cz + M[14] of its sphere centre when that is less (FCOMP / TEST AH,0x41 at 0x004A7FC4). Eye z is negative in front of the camera, so the least z is the farthest point. Returns non-zero when anything was skipped, which is when RenderEnqueueCommand queues the command. [proved]

RenderEnqueueCommand for a faded draw: (cmd, alpha). Pass 0 is DrawModelWithForcedAlphaBlend(cmd, 0), which draws nothing -- every mesh is skipped and lowers the sort depth -- so the command is always queued, with key |= g_draw_layer_nibble | 0x60000000 (bit 29 routes RenderFlushCommandList to DrawModelWithForcedAlphaBlend) and +0x10 = alpha. Callers: RenderSubmitModelFadedDefaultLight, RenderSubmitModelFadedSceneLights. [proved]

WalkMeshChainAndDraw for a command RenderEnqueueCommandFaded queued (key bit 29) -- every AssetDrawSlotWithAlpha draw, whatever its alpha, 1.0 included: the caller has no alpha test. Pass 0 draws nothing: every mesh, visible or not, is skipped and lowers the sort depth to its sphere centre's eye z when less. Pass 1 draws every visible mesh, opaque and translucent, with the TSP rewritten (tsp & 0x03FFFF7F) | 0x94000080 (0x004A863B / 0x004A8645) -- SRCBLEND SRCALPHA, DESTBLEND INVSRCALPHA, and bit 7 set so the shading mode is 2 or 3 and ALPHAOP is MODULATE: texture alpha times the material alpha, which is the mesh's base alpha times the command's +0x10. So an OPAQUE-pass mesh's texture alpha, which pass 0 ignores, blends here. TSP bits 19-20 are kept (so the alpha test stays the mesh's own pass's: off for an opaque-pass mesh) and the ISP word is untouched (so it still writes depth). [proved]

The translucent pass, at the end of the frame: qsort (FUN_004ADCF7) the queued command pointers with RenderCommandCompare, SetRenderState(0x1B ALPHABLENDENABLE, 1), then per command: a sprite quad (bit 30 clear) goes to DrawSpriteQuadCommand; a model re-installs its light block if the generation differs, then WalkMeshChainAndDraw(cmd, 1) -- or DrawModelWithForcedAlphaBlend for a faded command (key bit 29). Resets the queue count. Called only from FUN_004ABF30, before the frame is presented. [proved]

The qsort comparator behind the translucent draw order: (key & 0xF) ascending -- the draw layer SetDrawLayerNibble set -- then the float at +4 descending: FLD [b+4]; FSUB [a+4]; -1 when negative (0x004A8A3C). The float is eye z on the matrix stack, which looks down -z (RenderInitStates' VIEW is diag(1,1,-1,1) under a left-handed projection), so descending is NEAREST FIRST. This row said 'far first' until that sign was read. [proved]

The translation of the top of the matrix stack, read straight out of g_MatrixStackTop+0x30/0x34/0x38 into a vec3. BodyCreatureUpdate's state 0 uses it to read the host's bone position out of MatrixInvert(0) * host+0x2C4.
The general 4x4 inverse of the argument (the top when 0), by cofactors over the determinant (FUN_004A8B60); a singular matrix becomes sixteen 3.4e38. [proved]

SetMatrixMode(int mode)  OpenGL-style matrix mode selector over the stack at g_MatrixStackTop. DAT_007E7994 holds the current mode.      mode 3 = PROJECTION     mode 1 = WORLD / model  The commit happens on the 3 -> 1 transition:      if (mode == 1 && current == 3) {         SetTransform(D3DTRANSFORMSTATE_PROJECTION /* 3 */, g_MatrixStackTop);         memcpy(DAT_007E7948, g_MatrixStackTop, 64);   /* cached projection */     }     current = mode;  So the game builds its projection with the same push/identity/translate/ multiply API it uses for object transforms, then installs it by switching back to mode 1. This is the only place D3DTRANSFORMSTATE_PROJECTION is ever set.  The matrix API, all angles in BAMS (65536 = 360 degrees):      MatrixStackPush     0x004A9880   push (duplicates the top; NULL = copy top)     MatrixStackPop      0x004A9840     MatrixLoadIdentity  0x004A9E10   copies the identity at DAT_00571210     MatrixTranslate     0x004A9D80   row 3 += x*row0 + y*row1 + z*row2     MatrixRotateX       0x004A99F0   rows 1,2     MatrixRotateY       0x004A9AE0   rows 0,2     MatrixMultiply      0x004A92A0   top = top * M

The other order from MatrixMultiply (FUN_004A92A0): g_MatrixStackTop = arg x top, where MatrixMultiply is top x arg -- in the element layout both share (Matrix4.elements'), new[c*4+r] = sum_k arg[k*4+r] * top[c*4+k]. [proved] from the sixteen sums. Two callers: SkeletonEmitNode at 0x004115F7, which pre-multiplies the tracked node's view-space matrix by g_camera_blocks[g_camera_index] (view to world) to write obj+0x100 in the world, and BuildSceneLightDirection at 0x0040E117.
push(0) duplicates the top

Post-multiplies the top of the stack by a rotation of param_2 BAMS about the axis param_1 (a normalised copy, via Vec3ScaleToUnitLength), the Rodrigues matrix built in the scratch at 0x00598C18. [proved]

MatrixRotateZ(bams) -- rows 0 and 1 of g_MatrixStackTop, the member the SetMatrixMode note's matrix API table was missing. c = cos(bams * 9.58738e-05), s = sin: row0' = row0*c + s*row1, row1' = row1*c - row0*s. Same pre-multiplying, same BAMS scale (2*pi/65536) and the same four-wide rows as MatrixRotateX (0x004A99F0) and MatrixRotateY (0x004A9AE0). DrawBackdropDome's preset-5 arm and every class 0x41 draw-only prop call it.

MatrixScale(x, y, z) -- scales g_MatrixStackTop's three basis rows in place: row0 *= x, row1 *= y, row2 *= z, four floats each. No translation row is touched, so it scales about the current origin. The last member of the matrix API listed on SetMatrixMode.
Copies the stack top's rotation columns and translation -- elements 0,1,2 4,5,6 8,9,10 12,13,14 -- into a 12-float array. The inverse of MatrixSetTop3x4.
Writes a 12-float array into the stack top's elements 0,1,2 4,5,6 8,9,10 12,13,14, leaving 3, 7, 11 and 15 as they were.
wipes the top 3x3; a screen-axis billboard
Writes a vec3 into g_MatrixStackTop+0x30/0x34/0x38 -- the translation row -- and leaves the rotation alone. [proved]

SetLightingDefaultSingle() -- the ENTIRE fixed-function light setup, one directional light and the global ambient. The decompiler drops every FPU argument here (__ftol() with no args, unaff_EDI); this is from the disassembly. Constants read out of the image: 0x00570F5C = 255.0, 0x00565DE4 = 1.4, 0x004C4D10 = 0.3.  a = g_render_ambient (channel 10);  c = g_render_light_colour r/g/b (channels 6/7/8)  t = c * a                                    /* [esp+0xC/0x10/0x14] */  SetRenderState(0x8B D3DRENDERSTATE_AMBIENT, 0xFF000000 | pack(t * 255))  light.diffuse  = t * 1.4  light.specular = light.diffuse               /* copied dword-for-dword */  light.ambient  = c * 0.3                     /* NOT scaled by a */  light.direction = g_render_light_dir         /* view space, already negated */  SetLight(0, &light); LightEnable(0, TRUE); for (i=1;i<16;i++) LightEnable(i,FALSE)  **The ambient channel is a master brightness, not a separate ambient term.** It multiplies the light colour into BOTH the D3D ambient render state and the light's diffuse, so turning it down dims the directional light too; only light.ambient escapes it. And the render-state ambient is TINTED by the light colour -- it is c*a, never a neutral grey. The browser port had it as an untinted scalar plus c*0.3, which with the (1.0, 0.2, 0.1) light colour is nearly white where the engine is deep orange.  D3DLIGHT7 lives at 0x007E79C0: +0x04 diffuse, +0x14 specular, +0x24 ambient, +0x40 direction. The three ftol conversions truncate and are NOT clamped, so a colour*ambient product above 1.0 would carry into the next byte of the packed D3DCOLOR; no shipped script is known to do it. Called from the render command list (RenderEnqueueCommand / RenderFlushCommandList).

RenderSubmitModelDefaultLight(model): AssetDrawSlot's submit. Unless DAT_007DEBAC is non-zero (then nothing is drawn; that flag's meaning is open), builds the 0x1D-dword command -- key 0 (not faded, bit 26 clear so the single default light), +4 = g_MatrixStackTop[0xE] (the modelview _43, the sort depth's seed), +0xC the model, +0x14..+0x20 the light colour and g_render_ambient, +0x24 g_render_light_generation, +0x28..+0x30 the light direction, +0x34 the 4x4 modelview -- and hands it to RenderEnqueueCommand. No alpha field is written; RenderSubmitModelFadedDefaultLight (0x004AA350) is the twin that carries one. [proved]

RenderSubmitModelDefaultLight's twin for AssetDrawSlotWithAlpha: builds the same 0x1D-dword command (key 0, +4 = g_MatrixStackTop[0xE] the modelview _43, the light block, the 4x4 at +0x34) and hands it with the alpha to RenderEnqueueCommandFaded. [proved]

Walks the model's mesh chain (header word 0 ends it; bit 31 skips a mesh) and, unless the model's +4 word has 0x10, for each mesh whose header has bit 8 (TEST DH, 0x1) rewrites the UVs of every vertex whose flag bit 0 is set (0x20-byte entries; the others are 8) from that vertex's normal through the top of the matrix stack (0x007E7990): u = (1.0 - (n.x*M[0] + n.y*M[4] + n.z*M[8])) * 0.5, v = (1.0 + (n.x*M[1] + n.y*M[5] + n.z*M[9])) * 0.5 -- [0x004C4380] = 1.0, [0x004C43AC] = 0x3F000000 = 0.5 -- in place, in the model's own vertex data. Returns at once while 0x007DEBAC is set, as the submit routines do. Called only by AssetSlotUVsFromViewNormals (FUN_00418660). [proved]
RenderSubmitModelSceneLights' faded twin: key 0x4000000 (the scene light array), otherwise RenderSubmitModelFadedDefaultLight. Called by AssetDrawSlotWithAlphaSceneLights. [proved]

0x007E813C = (arg == 1). SetLightingSceneArray submits all 16 lights only while it is set, else light 0 alone. UpdateSceneViewAndLight calls it with 1 every frame, so the array path always has all 16.
0x007E8128[index] = (enabled != 0); marks the light state dirty (0x007E79B8 |= 0x8000000).
D3DRENDERSTATE_AMBIENT for the scene-array path: 0x007E8138 = 0xFF000000 | rgb(arg[1..3] * 255.0). Only SetLightingSceneArray reads it.
Copies one D3DLIGHT7 (0x1A dwords) into slot index of 0x007E7AA8 and transforms its position (point) and direction (vector) by the view matrix at 0x007E7A68, because D3D7 takes lights in view space.
All 16 render light slots: zeroed, type 3 (directional), diffuse (1,1,1), direction (0,0,1), disabled (0x007E8128[i] = 0 and LightEnable(i, FALSE)).
(a, b, out): out = a x b, the ordinary right-handed cross product.
In place, divide by the length; no zero test. Not 0x004AAA00, which already has the name Vec3Normalize. [proved]
Vec3Normalize(src, dst): dst = src / |src|, the length returned in ST0 (both shot-down arms pop it with FSTP ST0). No zero test. [proved]

ColiSegmentVsMesh(float x0,y0,z0, float x1,y1,z1, int *blob)  Segment-vs-quad test against one `coli/` collision blob. Returns the surface id of the nearest hit, or 0. This function *is* the coli/ format specification:      u32 group_count     repeat group_count:         u32 quad_count         f32 aabb_max[3]          <- MAX first, see below         f32 aabb_min[3]         repeat quad_count:       18 dwords = 72 bytes             f32 nx, ny, nz, d    plane             u32 axis             dominant axis: 0 = X, 1 = Y, 2 = Z             f32 v0[3] v1[3] v2[3] v3[3]             u32 surface          surface material id -- the return value  The AABB really is stored max-then-min. The reject test is      seg_min.x <= box[1] && seg_min.y <= box[2] && seg_min.z <= box[3] &&     box[4] <= seg_max.x && box[5] <= seg_max.y && box[6] <= seg_max.z  so `box[1..3]` is the upper corner and `box[4..6]` the lower one.  Per quad: signed plane distances at both segment ends; a hit needs opposite signs (a back-facing hit is allowed only when DAT_009CAC5C is set). The intersection point is the distance-weighted blend of the endpoints. The point-in-quad test is four 2D cross products taken in the plane that drops the dominant axis -- `axis` selects which pair of components to use, and it is an INTEGER in a float slot: the decompiler shows the comparisons against 1.4013e-45 and 2.8026e-45, the bit patterns of 1 and 2.  Nearest hit wins (squared distance from the segment start), reported in:      DAT_009CAC40  surface id (also the return value)     DAT_009CAC44  pointer to the winning quad     DAT_009CAC48  squared distance     DAT_009CAC54/58/50  hit point x / y / z     DAT_009CAC60  plane d,  DAT_009CAC64/68/6C  plane normal  Surface ids observed in the shipped data: 0, 2, 3, 5, 50, 52, 53, 55, 56, 60, 61, 90, 99. **5 and 55 are wet/water**: FUN_00456B70 spawns impact effect 0x61 with two extra ripple calls instead of 0x46, and FUN_0040A230 plays a different impact sound (0x4416A9 vs 0x2616A9) for a bouncing dropped object.  VALIDATED over all 8 loaded files (tools/verify_coli.py): the blob walk tiles every file to 100.00% with no slack; all 10,064 quad vertices lie inside their group's AABB; the stored plane fits its own vertices; normals are unit to 6.8e-07; and all 86 evt collision-set pointers land exactly on a blob header.

sphere vs one collision mesh. distance^2 <= radius^2 with NO sign test: a centre behind a quad is a hit exactly as one in front. g_coli_hit_depth is left as fVar6, the SIGNED unnormalised plane distance, and ColiTestSphereAgainstFullSet turns it into radius-dist in front and radius+dist behind. The normal is the quad's own nx/ny/nz on the face branch and centre-minus-closest only on the edge/vertex branches. Nearest dist^2 wins, not deepest

BuildPerspectiveProjection(int fov_bams, float aspect, float znear, float zfar)  Builds a left-handed D3D perspective matrix and MatrixMultiply()s it onto the top of the matrix stack.      half = (int)(fov_bams * 0.5)            /* 0x004C4C98 = 0.5, truncating  */     cot  = cos(a)/sin(a),  a = half * 2*PI/65536   /* 0x004C4370 = 2*PI/65536 */      m00 = cot / aspect     m11 = cot     m22 = zf / (zf - zn)     m23 = 1.0                                /* left-handed */     m32 = -zn * zf / (zf - zn)  fov_bams is therefore the FULL vertical field of view in BAMS (65536 = 360 degrees).  ONLY TWO CALL SITES, and both pass the same FOV and aspect:      SetupSceneProjection      (0x004184C0)  0x1D3B, 4/3, 0.8,   8000.0     SetProjectionNearPlane(zn)(0x004194C0)  0x1D3B, 4/3, <var>, 8000.0  So the field of view is a compile-time constant for the whole game:      0x1D3B = 7483 BAMS;  half = (int)3741.5 = 3741     fovY = 2 * 3741 * 2*PI/65536 = 0.7173277659 rad = 41.100 degrees     fovX = 2 * atan(tan(fovY/2) * 4/3)             = 53.127 degrees  Cross-checked independently: SetupSceneProjection also computes     DAT_009A2D70 = 240.0 / tan(0.35866388296751145)  = 640.16 which is the projection distance in pixels for a 480-tall viewport, and 0.35866388296751145 rad is exactly 3741 * 2*PI/65536. Two constants, one FOV.

SetFogColour(D3DCOLOR) -- D3DRENDERSTATE_FOGCOLOR (0x22), the sibling of SetFogRange.  MOV EAX,[0x007deb74] / PUSH [ESP+4] / PUSH 0x22 / CALL [ECX+0x50].  The argument is a plain 0x00RRGGBB D3DCOLOR, and D3D7 blends it against the framebuffer in the framebuffer's OWN encoding: fixed-function fog is C = f*C_pixel + (1-f)*C_fog evaluated on 8-bit gamma-encoded values, not light-linear ones. There is no sRGB write path in DX7 and no D3DRENDERSTATE_COLORVERTEX gamma stage. A renderer that blends fog in linear space and encodes afterwards is doing a different sum -- at f=0.5 over a dark surface it lands ~10/255 too bright. Sole caller PushSceneFogColour (FUN_0040D5B0). See docs/formats/materials.md.

SetFogRange(float near, float far) -- D3DRENDERSTATE_FOGSTART / FOGEND.  **Both values are DOUBLED before they reach the device.** From the disassembly, which is unambiguous where the decompiler's FPU tracking is not:      FLD  [esp+4]  FADD ST0,ST0  FST  [esp+4]     ; [esp+4] = near * 2     FLD  [esp+8]  FADD ST0,ST0  FSTP [esp+8]     ; [esp+8] = far  * 2     FCOMP [esp+8]                                ; compare near*2 : far*2     JZ   -> swapped      ordered:  SetRenderState(0x24 FOGSTART, near*2)               SetRenderState(0x25 FOGEND,   far*2)     swapped:  SetRenderState(0x24 FOGSTART, far*2)     ; guard for near >= far               SetRenderState(0x25 FOGEND,   near*2)  So a script's "near 21, far 507" is really a 42..1014 ramp. Rendering with the raw values halves the ramp and the fog comes out far too thick -- which is exactly what the browser player did until this was read.  FOGSTART/FOGEND mean this is D3DFOG_LINEAR: factor = (end - d) / (end - start), a straight ramp, not a curve.  Callers: FUN_0040C320, which is handed the scene light block's +0x30 (near) and +0x34 (far) -- the fields evt opcodes 0x20-0x27 channels 0 and 1 write. Whether an individual mesh is fogged is separate and per-mesh: TSP bit 23 maps to D3DRENDERSTATE_FOGENABLE **inverted**.  See docs/formats/materials.md.

Uploads one tex/ texture into a D3D surface made by CreateSurfaceInTextureFormat in slot g_pvr_pixfmt_texture_format[entry +0x04 & 7] -- ARGB1555 -> 5 (A1R5G5B5), RGB565 -> 2, ARGB4444 -> 6 -- then PromoteSurfaceToTexture. By data layout (+0x04 & 0xFF00): 0x100 twiddled 16-bit, 0x300 VQ, 0x500 PAL4 -- 4-bit twiddled indices into the palette g_texture_palettes + g_texture_palette_current*16, whose entries are ARGB1555 and are converted to the surface format (565, 1555 copied, or 4444 with the alpha nibble 0xF or 0 from bit 15) --, 0x900 linear, 0xD00 twiddled rectangle. The 16-bit layouts copy each texel verbatim, alpha bits included; nothing here drops or forces alpha. Rows go to the surface top-down in texture order. [proved]

BindModelTextureHandles(model, bank_descriptors, bank_data): for every mesh header whose +0x20 is still a bank-local texture index (top two bits clear), makes the bank entry's GLOBAL texture slot (entry +0x0C) resident -- DecodeTextureToSurface(entry, data) on first use, else a reference count -- and rewrites +0x20 to slot | 0x40000000. The decode takes the bank entry and its data and no mesh word, so one surface serves every mesh that names the texture, whatever each mesh's TSP says: IgnoreTexAlpha cannot reach it. [proved]

TextureSlotAcquire(_, tex, bank_descriptors, bank_data, palette): creates the D3D texture for a global slot on first use (FUN_004AC270 decodes it; a layout-5 PAL4 texture looks its colours up in g_texture_palettes + palette*16) and records its size at 0x00810A00; later calls only count references. palette is taken only when 0..0x3F. [proved]
Drops one reference to a global texture slot and frees the D3D texture at zero. [proved]

Copies the palette table's {s16 16, u32 ptr, u32 n} records (g_texture_palette_table + 2, stride 12) into g_texture_palettes, 16 u16 each, until a record is not 16 entries. Called once from the renderer's init FUN_00418150. [proved]

Builds the 15-dword quad command from a sprite record and the global texture slot (skips it if the slot has no texture in 0x00810A0C): x, y, depth, scale, BAMS rotation, the UV rect with flags 0x10/0x20 flipping U/V, colour alpha<<24|0xFFFFFF (or a full ARGB with flag 0x2000); then QueueOrDrawSpriteQuad. The C runtime's acos on ST0, and not asin: 0x004AD0E8..0x004AD0F6 is FLD1; FADD ST0,ST1; FLD1; FSUB ST0,ST2; FMULP; FSQRT; FXCH; FPATAN, which is atan2(sqrt((1+x)(1-x)), x) = acos(x); the |x| == 1 arm loads FLDZ for +1 (0x004AD136) and FLDPI for -1 (0x004AD132), acos's two ends. FrogStateHopWithinScreenWedge's two wedge clamps call it (0x0043AC25, 0x0043AC94) with perpendicular distance / 26.0, so a frog exactly on a screen-edge ray is clamped by a quarter turn and one 26 units off it by nothing. [proved]
